Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 49–50:

﴿And when We delivered you﴾: that is, your forefathers and grandfathers. He counted it as a favour upon them because they were saved by their deliverance, ﴿from the folk of Pharaoh﴾, his followers and the people of his religion. Pharaoh was al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan, and he was of the Amalekite Copts. He lived for more than four hundred years. ﴿They subjected you﴾, that is, they imposed upon you and made you taste [suffering]. ﴿Dreadful torment﴾, that is, the most severe and the worst torment. It was also said: they turned you about in torment, now this way and now that, like camels grazing in the wilderness. This was because Pharaoh made the Children of Israel servants and retainers [[Khadam and khawal: they are a man's dependants and followers; their singular is kha'il, derived either from takhwil, meaning ownership, or said to be from ri'ayah, meaning care.]] and divided them into occupations. One group built, another group ploughed and planted, another group served him, and whoever was not engaged in some work had the jizyah (poll tax) imposed upon him.

Wahb said: they were divided into categories in Pharaoh's works. The strong among them hewed pillars [[al-asawari: the columns.]] from the mountains until their necks and hands were wounded [[qaruha: wounded.]] and their backs were galled [[dabarat: galled their backs; from dabbarat al-dabbah, meaning the animal's back was sored.]] from cutting and carrying them. Another group carried stones, another built palaces for him, another group moulded bricks and fired baked bricks [[al-ajurr: baked bricks.]], and another group were carpenters and blacksmiths. As for the weak among them, a daily kharaj (tax) was imposed upon them which they had to pay each day. Whoever the sun set upon before paying his tax, his right hand was chained to his neck for a month. The women spun flax and wove.

It was also said: its explanation is what follows it: ﴿They slaughtered your sons﴾, mentioned as an apposition [badal] to His saying, ﴿they subjected you to dreadful torment﴾. ﴿And spared your women﴾, that is, they left them alive. This was because Pharaoh saw in his dream as if a fire had come from Bayt al-Maqdis, surrounded Egypt and burned every Copt in it, but did not touch the Children of Israel. This terrified him, and he asked the soothsayers about his vision. They said: a boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will be the cause of your destruction and the end of your kingdom. So Pharaoh ordered the killing of every boy born among the Children of Israel, and he gathered the midwives and said to them: let no boy of the Children of Israel fall into your hands except that he be killed, and no girl except that she be left. He appointed overseers over the midwives, and they continued doing this, until it was said that he killed twelve thousand children of the Children of Israel in pursuit of Moses. Wahb said: it reached me that he slaughtered ninety thousand newborns in pursuit of Moses, peace be upon him.

They said: death spread among the elders of the Children of Israel, so the chiefs of the Copts entered upon Pharaoh and said: death has fallen upon the Children of Israel; will you slaughter their young while their elders die, so that the labour will soon fall upon us? So Pharaoh ordered that they slaughter for one year and leave alone for one year. Thus Harun was born in the year in which they did not slaughter, and Musa was born in the year in which they did slaughter.

﴿And in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord﴾. It was said: al-bala' means ordeal (mihnah), that is, in their subjecting you to dreadful torment there was a great ordeal. It was also said: al-bala' means blessing, that is, in My rescuing you from them there was a great blessing. Thus al-bala' comes with the meaning of blessing and with the meaning of hardship. Allah, exalted is He, may test by blessing so that one gives thanks, and by hardship so that one is patient. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ (21:35).

﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾. It was said: its meaning is 'We parted it for you.' It was also said: We parted the sea by your entering it. The sea is called baḥr because of its vastness, and from this the horse is called baḥr when it extends its running stride. This was because when Pharaoh's destruction drew near, Allah, exalted is He, commanded Musa, peace be upon him, to set out with the Children of Israel from Egypt by night. Musa commanded his people to light lamps in their houses until morning. Allah, exalted is He, brought out every illegitimate child of the Copts to the Children of Israel, and every illegitimate child of the Children of Israel to the Copts, until each returned to his father. Allah cast death upon the Copts, so every firstborn of theirs died, and they were occupied with burying them until morning came and the sun rose. Musa, peace be upon him, set out with six hundred thousand and twenty thousand fighting men, not counting those aged twenty for their youth, nor those aged sixty for their old age. When they entered Egypt with Ya'qub they were seventy-two persons, men and women together.

It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the companions of Musa were six hundred thousand and seventy thousand [[Ibn Khaldun, in the introduction to his history, reports that al-Mas'udi and many historians mentioned that Musa, peace be upon him, counted the Children of Israel in the wilderness of wandering (al-tih), after permitting only those able to bear arms, from the age of twenty and upward, and they were six hundred thousand or more. Then he refuted that for several reasons: (a) it entails heedlessness of the capacity of Egypt and Syria and their ability to hold such a number of armies. Each kingdom has a share of garrison that it can contain and carry out its duties with, and which becomes too cramped for anything larger, as the familiar customs and well-known conditions attest. (b) Moreover, armies reaching such a number could hardly come into contact or fight, because the land is too narrow for them and, when they line up, they would stretch beyond the range of sight two or three times or more. How then would these two groups fight, or how could one line prevail? Would one side's flank not be aware of the other flank? (c) Also: if the Children of Israel had reached such a number, the extent of their realm would not have contained them, and the reach of their dominion would have been broken. (d) Also: the lineage between Musa and Isra'il consists, according to what the scholars have verified, of only four fathers, and the period between them, according to what al-Mas'udi transmitted, is two hundred and twenty years. It is unlikely that descendants would branch out in four generations into such a number. See: Muqaddimat Ibn Khaldun, 1/13–16, Dar al-Kitab al-Arabi edition.]].

And from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: they were six hundred thousand. When they wanted to move on, the wandering (al-tih) was imposed upon them, and they did not know where to go. Musa summoned the elders of the Children of Israel and asked them about this. They said: when Yusuf, peace be upon him, was approaching death, he took an oath from his brothers that they would not leave Egypt until they took him out with them, and therefore the way was closed to us. He asked them about the location of his grave, but they did not know. So Musa stood calling out: I adjure Allah every person who knows where the grave of Yusuf, peace be upon him, is, to tell me of it! Whoever does not know of it, may his ears be deafened to my words! He would pass between the two men calling out, but they did not hear his voice, until an old woman among them heard him and said: Tell me, if I guide you to his grave, will you give me whatever I ask of you? He refused her and said: Until I ask my Lord. Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to grant her request. She said: I am a very old woman and cannot walk, so carry me and take me out of Egypt. This is for this world; as for the Hereafter, I ask you that I not descend into any chamber of Paradise except that I descend into it with you. He said: Yes. She said: He is in the middle of the water in the Nile, so pray to Allah that the water recede from him. He prayed to Allah, exalted is He, and the water receded from him. He also prayed that the dawn be delayed until he finished with the matter of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Musa, peace be upon him, dug out that place and extracted him in a coffin of marble, and carried him until he buried him in al-Sham (Syria). Then the way was opened for them, and they travelled, with Musa, peace be upon him, at their rear [[ 'ala sawaqihim: at their rear, meaning he placed them in front of him and walked behind them out of humility.]] and Harun at their front. Pharaoh was informed about them, so he gathered his people and ordered them not to set out in pursuit of the Children of Israel until the rooster crowed. By Allah, no rooster crowed that night. Pharaoh set out in pursuit of the Children of Israel, and at the head of his vanguard was Haman, with one million and seven hundred thousand [men]. Among them were seventy thousand dark-coloured horses, besides the rest of the colours [[The plural of shiyah: every colour that differs from the main colour of a horse.]]. [Muhammad ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said: in Pharaoh's army there were one hundred thousand dark-coloured horses, besides the rest of the colours.] [[These reports are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin), on which one should not rely in explaining the Book of Allah, and whose understanding does not depend on them. It is better to set them aside entirely.]] [[Omitted in (A).]] Pharaoh would ride a dark horse [[al-duhm: the great number; it also means black horses.]]. It was said: Pharaoh was with seven thousand thousand [men]; before him were one hundred thousand archers, one hundred thousand spearmen, and one hundred thousand pikemen. The Children of Israel marched until they reached the sea, and the water was at its highest level. They looked, and behold, Pharaoh was upon them as the sun rose. They remained bewildered and said: O Musa, what shall we do, and where is what you promised us? This is Pharaoh behind us; if he overtakes us he will kill us! And the sea is before us; if we enter it we will drown! Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿When the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said: Indeed we are overtaken. He said: Never! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ (26:61–62).

Then Allah revealed to him: strike the sea with your staff. He struck it, but it did not obey him. Allah revealed to him: be gentle with it. He struck it again and said: Split, O Abu Khalid, by the permission of Allah, exalted is He. It split, and each part became like a great mountain. A path appeared in it, twelve paths, one for each tribe, and the water rose between every two paths like a mountain. Allah sent the wind and the sun upon the bed of the sea until it became dry. The Children of Israel crossed the sea, each tribe in its own path, with the water on either side of them like a huge mountain, and they could not see one another. They were afraid, and each tribe said: our brothers have been killed. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed to the mountains of water: interlace! So the water became interlaced layers, so that they could see one another and hear one another's speech, until they crossed the sea safely. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾.

﴿Then We rescued you﴾ from the folk of Pharaoh and from drowning, ﴿and We drowned the folk of Pharaoh﴾. This was because when Pharaoh reached the sea and saw it split, he said to his people: Look at the sea, it has split out of awe of me, so that I may overtake my slaves who fled. Enter the sea! His people were afraid to enter it. It was said: they said to him, if you are a lord, then enter the sea as Musa entered it. Pharaoh was on a dark horse, and among Pharaoh's horses there was no female horse. Then Jibril came on a female horse in heat [[Faras wadiq: a mare in heat, desiring the stallion. Al-Tabari recorded this report in his Tafsir and also in his History.]], went ahead of them and plunged into the sea. When Pharaoh's dark horse smelled her scent, it plunged into the sea after her, while they could not see him. Pharaoh had no control over his affair, and he could not see Jibril's mare. The horses plunged into the sea all together behind him. Mika'il came on a horse behind the people, urging them on and driving them so that no man would lag behind, and saying to them: Join your companions! Until they all plunged into the sea. Jibril came out of the sea, and when the first of them was about to come out, Allah, exalted is He, commanded the sea to seize them. It closed over them and drowned them all. The distance between the two shores of the sea was four farsakhs. It is the Gulf of Qulzum, an arm of the Persian Sea. Qatadah said: it is a sea behind Egypt called Isaf, and this took place in full view of the Children of Israel. This is His saying: ﴿while you were looking on﴾ at their downfall. It was also said: at their destruction.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 49–50:

﴿And when We delivered you﴾: that is, your forefathers and grandfathers. He counted it as a favour upon them because they were saved by their deliverance, ﴿from the folk of Pharaoh﴾, his followers and the people of his religion. Pharaoh was al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan, and he was of the Amalekite Copts. He lived for more than four hundred years. ﴿They subjected you﴾, that is, they imposed upon you and made you taste [suffering]. ﴿Dreadful torment﴾, that is, the most severe and the worst torment. It was also said: they turned you about in torment, now this way and now that, like camels grazing in the wilderness. This was because Pharaoh made the Children of Israel servants and retainers [[Khadam and khawal: they are a man's dependants and followers; their singular is kha'il, derived either from takhwil, meaning ownership, or said to be from ri'ayah, meaning care.]] and divided them into occupations. One group built, another group ploughed and planted, another group served him, and whoever was not engaged in some work had the jizyah (poll tax) imposed upon him.

Wahb said: they were divided into categories in Pharaoh's works. The strong among them hewed pillars [[al-asawari: the columns.]] from the mountains until their necks and hands were wounded [[qaruha: wounded.]] and their backs were galled [[dabarat: galled their backs; from dabbarat al-dabbah, meaning the animal's back was sored.]] from cutting and carrying them. Another group carried stones, another built palaces for him, another group moulded bricks and fired baked bricks [[al-ajurr: baked bricks.]], and another group were carpenters and blacksmiths. As for the weak among them, a daily kharaj (tax) was imposed upon them which they had to pay each day. Whoever the sun set upon before paying his tax, his right hand was chained to his neck for a month. The women spun flax and wove.

It was also said: its explanation is what follows it: ﴿They slaughtered your sons﴾, mentioned as an apposition [badal] to His saying, ﴿they subjected you to dreadful torment﴾. ﴿And spared your women﴾, that is, they left them alive. This was because Pharaoh saw in his dream as if a fire had come from Bayt al-Maqdis, surrounded Egypt and burned every Copt in it, but did not touch the Children of Israel. This terrified him, and he asked the soothsayers about his vision. They said: a boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will be the cause of your destruction and the end of your kingdom. So Pharaoh ordered the killing of every boy born among the Children of Israel, and he gathered the midwives and said to them: let no boy of the Children of Israel fall into your hands except that he be killed, and no girl except that she be left. He appointed overseers over the midwives, and they continued doing this, until it was said that he killed twelve thousand children of the Children of Israel in pursuit of Moses. Wahb said: it reached me that he slaughtered ninety thousand newborns in pursuit of Moses, peace be upon him.

They said: death spread among the elders of the Children of Israel, so the chiefs of the Copts entered upon Pharaoh and said: death has fallen upon the Children of Israel; will you slaughter their young while their elders die, so that the labour will soon fall upon us? So Pharaoh ordered that they slaughter for one year and leave alone for one year. Thus Harun was born in the year in which they did not slaughter, and Musa was born in the year in which they did slaughter.

﴿And in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord﴾. It was said: al-bala' means ordeal (mihnah), that is, in their subjecting you to dreadful torment there was a great ordeal. It was also said: al-bala' means blessing, that is, in My rescuing you from them there was a great blessing. Thus al-bala' comes with the meaning of blessing and with the meaning of hardship. Allah, exalted is He, may test by blessing so that one gives thanks, and by hardship so that one is patient. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ (21:35).

﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾. It was said: its meaning is 'We parted it for you.' It was also said: We parted the sea by your entering it. The sea is called baḥr because of its vastness, and from this the horse is called baḥr when it extends its running stride. This was because when Pharaoh's destruction drew near, Allah, exalted is He, commanded Musa, peace be upon him, to set out with the Children of Israel from Egypt by night. Musa commanded his people to light lamps in their houses until morning. Allah, exalted is He, brought out every illegitimate child of the Copts to the Children of Israel, and every illegitimate child of the Children of Israel to the Copts, until each returned to his father. Allah cast death upon the Copts, so every firstborn of theirs died, and they were occupied with burying them until morning came and the sun rose. Musa, peace be upon him, set out with six hundred thousand and twenty thousand fighting men, not counting those aged twenty for their youth, nor those aged sixty for their old age. When they entered Egypt with Ya'qub they were seventy-two persons, men and women together.

It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the companions of Musa were six hundred thousand and seventy thousand [[Ibn Khaldun, in the introduction to his history, reports that al-Mas'udi and many historians mentioned that Musa, peace be upon him, counted the Children of Israel in the wilderness of wandering (al-tih), after permitting only those able to bear arms, from the age of twenty and upward, and they were six hundred thousand or more. Then he refuted that for several reasons: (a) it entails heedlessness of the capacity of Egypt and Syria and their ability to hold such a number of armies. Each kingdom has a share of garrison that it can contain and carry out its duties with, and which becomes too cramped for anything larger, as the familiar customs and well-known conditions attest. (b) Moreover, armies reaching such a number could hardly come into contact or fight, because the land is too narrow for them and, when they line up, they would stretch beyond the range of sight two or three times or more. How then would these two groups fight, or how could one line prevail? Would one side's flank not be aware of the other flank? (c) Also: if the Children of Israel had reached such a number, the extent of their realm would not have contained them, and the reach of their dominion would have been broken. (d) Also: the lineage between Musa and Isra'il consists, according to what the scholars have verified, of only four fathers, and the period between them, according to what al-Mas'udi transmitted, is two hundred and twenty years. It is unlikely that descendants would branch out in four generations into such a number. See: Muqaddimat Ibn Khaldun, 1/13–16, Dar al-Kitab al-Arabi edition.]].

And from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: they were six hundred thousand. When they wanted to move on, the wandering (al-tih) was imposed upon them, and they did not know where to go. Musa summoned the elders of the Children of Israel and asked them about this. They said: when Yusuf, peace be upon him, was approaching death, he took an oath from his brothers that they would not leave Egypt until they took him out with them, and therefore the way was closed to us. He asked them about the location of his grave, but they did not know. So Musa stood calling out: I adjure Allah every person who knows where the grave of Yusuf, peace be upon him, is, to tell me of it! Whoever does not know of it, may his ears be deafened to my words! He would pass between the two men calling out, but they did not hear his voice, until an old woman among them heard him and said: Tell me, if I guide you to his grave, will you give me whatever I ask of you? He refused her and said: Until I ask my Lord. Then Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to grant her request. She said: I am a very old woman and cannot walk, so carry me and take me out of Egypt. This is for this world; as for the Hereafter, I ask you that I not descend into any chamber of Paradise except that I descend into it with you. He said: Yes. She said: He is in the middle of the water in the Nile, so pray to Allah that the water recede from him. He prayed to Allah, exalted is He, and the water receded from him. He also prayed that the dawn be delayed until he finished with the matter of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Musa, peace be upon him, dug out that place and extracted him in a coffin of marble, and carried him until he buried him in al-Sham (Syria). Then the way was opened for them, and they travelled, with Musa, peace be upon him, at their rear [[ 'ala sawaqihim: at their rear, meaning he placed them in front of him and walked behind them out of humility.]] and Harun at their front. Pharaoh was informed about them, so he gathered his people and ordered them not to set out in pursuit of the Children of Israel until the rooster crowed. By Allah, no rooster crowed that night. Pharaoh set out in pursuit of the Children of Israel, and at the head of his vanguard was Haman, with one million and seven hundred thousand [men]. Among them were seventy thousand dark-coloured horses, besides the rest of the colours [[The plural of shiyah: every colour that differs from the main colour of a horse.]]. [Muhammad ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said: in Pharaoh's army there were one hundred thousand dark-coloured horses, besides the rest of the colours.] [[These reports are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin), on which one should not rely in explaining the Book of Allah, and whose understanding does not depend on them. It is better to set them aside entirely.]] [[Omitted in (A).]] Pharaoh would ride a dark horse [[al-duhm: the great number; it also means black horses.]]. It was said: Pharaoh was with seven thousand thousand [men]; before him were one hundred thousand archers, one hundred thousand spearmen, and one hundred thousand pikemen. The Children of Israel marched until they reached the sea, and the water was at its highest level. They looked, and behold, Pharaoh was upon them as the sun rose. They remained bewildered and said: O Musa, what shall we do, and where is what you promised us? This is Pharaoh behind us; if he overtakes us he will kill us! And the sea is before us; if we enter it we will drown! Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿When the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said: Indeed we are overtaken. He said: Never! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ (26:61–62).

Then Allah revealed to him: strike the sea with your staff. He struck it, but it did not obey him. Allah revealed to him: be gentle with it. He struck it again and said: Split, O Abu Khalid, by the permission of Allah, exalted is He. It split, and each part became like a great mountain. A path appeared in it, twelve paths, one for each tribe, and the water rose between every two paths like a mountain. Allah sent the wind and the sun upon the bed of the sea until it became dry. The Children of Israel crossed the sea, each tribe in its own path, with the water on either side of them like a huge mountain, and they could not see one another. They were afraid, and each tribe said: our brothers have been killed. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed to the mountains of water: interlace! So the water became interlaced layers, so that they could see one another and hear one another's speech, until they crossed the sea safely. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾.

﴿Then We rescued you﴾ from the folk of Pharaoh and from drowning, ﴿and We drowned the folk of Pharaoh﴾. This was because when Pharaoh reached the sea and saw it split, he said to his people: Look at the sea, it has split out of awe of me, so that I may overtake my slaves who fled. Enter the sea! His people were afraid to enter it. It was said: they said to him, if you are a lord, then enter the sea as Musa entered it. Pharaoh was on a dark horse, and among Pharaoh's horses there was no female horse. Then Jibril came on a female horse in heat [[Faras wadiq: a mare in heat, desiring the stallion. Al-Tabari recorded this report in his Tafsir and also in his History.]], went ahead of them and plunged into the sea. When Pharaoh's dark horse smelled her scent, it plunged into the sea after her, while they could not see him. Pharaoh had no control over his affair, and he could not see Jibril's mare. The horses plunged into the sea all together behind him. Mika'il came on a horse behind the people, urging them on and driving them so that no man would lag behind, and saying to them: Join your companions! Until they all plunged into the sea. Jibril came out of the sea, and when the first of them was about to come out, Allah, exalted is He, commanded the sea to seize them. It closed over them and drowned them all. The distance between the two shores of the sea was four farsakhs. It is the Gulf of Qulzum, an arm of the Persian Sea. Qatadah said: it is a sea behind Egypt called Isaf, and this took place in full view of the Children of Israel. This is His saying: ﴿while you were looking on﴾ at their downfall. It was also said: at their destruction.

﴿وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا﴾ ("And when We appointed") is from the *mufa'alah* form (the form expressing mutual action, *al-mufa'alah*), which can also come from one party only, as in their saying ﻋَافَاكَ اللَّهُ ('afāka Allāh, "God granted you well-being"), ﻋَاقَبْتُ اللِّصَّ ('āqabtu al-liṣṣ, "I punished the thief"), and ﻃَارَقْتُ النَّعْلَ (ṭāraqtu al-na'l, "I put one sandal upon another"). Al-Zajjaj said: "The command came from God, and acceptance came from Musa. Therefore it is mentioned with the wording *al-muwā'adah* (mutual appointment)." The people of Basra recited ﴿وَإِذْ وَعَدْنَا﴾ (wa-idh wa'adnā), from *al-wa'd* (promise).

﴿مُوسَى﴾ (Mūsā, Moses) is a Hebrew name that was Arabicised. In Hebrew, "mū" means water and "shā" means tree. He was named this because he was taken from between water and trees. Then the *shīn* with a dot was changed to *sīn* in Arabic.

﴿أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً﴾ (forty nights) means their completion: thirty nights of Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten of Dhu al-Hijjah. The date is tied to the nights rather than the days, because the months of the Arabs were set according to the course of the moon, and the crescent appears at night. It was also said: because darkness is older than light, and the night was created before the day. God the Exalted says: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ﴾ ("And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day," Yā-Sīn 37).

This happened because the Children of Israel, once they were safe from their enemy and had entered Egypt [[The correct wording would be: and entered the Holy Land.]], had no book or law to which they could turn. So God promised Musa that He would send down the Torah to him. Musa said to his people: "I am going to the appointed time of your Lord; I will bring you a Book in which is an explanation of what you do and what you leave undone." He appointed them forty nights: thirty of Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten of Dhu al-Hijjah. He appointed his brother Hārūn (Aaron) as his successor over them.

When the promise came, Jibrīl (Gabriel) came on a horse called "the horse of life," which brings to life whatever it touches, in order to take Musa to his Lord. When al-Sāmirī saw him, he was a goldsmith from Bajarmā, and his name was Mīkhā. Sa'īd ibn Jubayr said: he was from Kirmān. Ibn 'Abbās said: his name was Mūsā ibn Muzaffar [[In B: Muzaffar.]]. Qatādah said: he was from the Children of Israel, from a tribe called Sāmirah. He was a hypocrite who showed Islam, and he came from a people who worshipped cows. When he saw Jibrīl on that horse, and saw that the places where the horse's hoof touched turned green at once, he said: "This has a special significance." So he took a handful of dust from the hoofprint of Jibrīl, peace be upon him.

ʿIkrimah said: it was put into his heart that whatever he cast it upon would be changed. The Children of Israel had borrowed many ornaments from the people of Pharaoh when they wanted to leave Egypt, on the pretext of a wedding for them. God destroyed Pharaoh, and those ornaments remained in the hands of the Children of Israel. When Musa set out, al-Sāmirī said to the Children of Israel: "The ornaments you borrowed from the people of Pharaoh are spoils that are not lawful for you. So dig a pit and bury them in it until Musa returns, and he will see his opinion regarding them."

Al-Suddī said: Hārūn, peace be upon him, ordered them to throw them into a hole until Musa returned, and they did so. [11/b] When the ornaments were gathered, al-Sāmirī fashioned them into a calf over three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the dust of Jibrīl's horse, peace be upon him, and a golden calf came out, studded with jewels, as beautiful as could be, and it lowed a lowing. Al-Suddī said: it used to low and walk. Al-Sāmirī said: ﴿هَذَا إِلَهُكُمْ وَإِلَهُ مُوسَى فَنَسِيَ﴾ ("This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot," Ṭā-Hā 88), meaning: he left it here and went out to seek it.

The Children of Israel had broken the promise, counting the day as two days from the night. When twenty days had passed and Musa had not returned, they fell into temptation.

It was also said: Musa had promised them thirty nights, then ten were added, and their trial took place during those ten. When the thirty passed and Musa had not returned, they thought he had died. They saw the calf and heard al-Sāmirī's words. Eight thousand men of them cloistered themselves around the calf, worshipping it. It was also said: all of them worshipped it except Hārūn, along with twelve thousand men, and this is the more sound view. Al-Ḥasan said: all of them worshipped it except Hārūn alone. This is the meaning of God the Exalted's words: ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ ("Then you took the calf," meaning as a god) ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ ("after him"). Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafs made the *dhāl* in *akhadhtu* and *ittakhadhtu* clear, while the others assimilate it. ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ ("while you were wrongdoers") means harming yourselves by disobedience, placing worship in other than its proper place.

﴿ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنْكُمْ﴾ ("Then We pardoned you") means We erased your sins ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ ("after that") after your worship of the calf ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ ("that you might be grateful"), so that you would be thankful for My pardon and My kindness to you. It was said: gratitude is obedience with all the limbs, in private and in public. Al-Ḥasan said: the gratitude for a blessing is to mention it. God the Exalted says: ﴿وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ﴾ ("As for the blessing of your Lord, speak of it," al-Ḍuḥā 11). Al-Fuḍayl said: the gratitude for every blessing is that God is not disobeyed after that blessing. It was also said: the true reality of gratitude is the inability to be grateful.

It is related that Musa, peace be upon him, said: "My God, You have bestowed upon me abundant blessings, and You have commanded me to be grateful, and my gratitude to You is itself a blessing from You." God the Exalted said: "O Musa, you have learned a knowledge than which no knowledge surpasses. It is enough for Me from My servant that he knows that whatever blessing he has is from Me." Dāwūd, peace be upon him, said: "Glory be to Him who made the servant's acknowledgment of his inability to thank Him a form of thanks, just as He made his acknowledgment of his inability to know Him a form of knowing Him."

God the Exalted says: ﴿وَإِذْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ﴾ ("And when We gave Musa the Book"), meaning the Torah, ﴿وَالْفُرْقَانَ﴾ ("and the Criterion"). Mujāhid said: it is also the Torah; He mentioned it by two names. Al-Kisā'ī said: *al-Furqān* is a description of *al-Kitāb*, and the *wāw* is superfluous, meaning: the Book that distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful. Yamān ibn Rabbān said: by *al-Furqān* He meant the parting of the sea, as He said: "And when We divided the sea for you and saved you" (al-Baqarah 50). ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("that you might be guided") by the Torah.

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ ("And when Musa said to his people"), those who worshipped the calf, ﴿يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ ("O my people, you have wronged yourselves"), meaning you harmed yourselves ﴿بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ ("by your taking the calf") as a god. They said: "What should we do?" He said: ﴿فَتُوبُوا﴾ ("So repent") meaning return ﴿إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ﴾ ("to your Creator"), your Maker. They said: "How do we repent?" He said: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ ("then kill yourselves"), meaning that the innocent among you should kill the guilty. ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ ("That") meaning the killing ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ عِنْدَ بَارِئِكُمْ﴾ ("is better for you with your Creator"). When Musa commanded them to kill, they said: "We will be patient with God's command." So they sat in the courtyards [[Plural of *fanā'*: the open space in front of a house; it was said: what extends from its sides.]] crouched [[*Al-iḥtibā'*: a man gathers his back and his shins with a garment or something else.]]. It was said to them: whoever stretches out his crouch, or lifts his gaze toward his killer, or shields himself with a hand or a foot, is cursed, and his repentance is rejected. The people drew daggers upon them. A man would see his son, his father, his brother, his relative, his friend, and his neighbour, and yet they could not carry out God the Exalted's command. They said: "O Musa, what shall we do?" So God sent upon them a fog and a black cloud, so that none could see another, and they kept killing one another until evening. When the killing increased, Musa and Hārūn, peace be upon them both, called out, wept, and entreated, and said: "O Lord, the Children of Israel are being destroyed; spare the remnant, spare the remnant!" God the Exalted then lifted the cloud, and commanded them to stop killing. The cloud cleared, revealing thousands of the slain.

It is narrated from ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The number of the slain was seventy thousand. This weighed heavily upon Musa, so God the Exalted revealed to him: "Would it not please you that I admit both the killer and the killed into Paradise?" Those among them who were killed were martyrs, and those who remained had their sins expiated. This is the meaning of God the Exalted's words: ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ ("So He turned to you in forgiveness"), meaning: when you did what you were commanded, He turned to you and pardoned you. ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ﴾ ("Indeed He is the Accepter of repentance") ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ ("the Most Merciful") toward His creation.

﴿وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا﴾ ("And when We appointed") is from the *mufa'alah* form (the form expressing mutual action, *al-mufa'alah*), which can also come from one party only, as in their saying ﻋَافَاكَ اللَّهُ ('afāka Allāh, "God granted you well-being"), ﻋَاقَبْتُ اللِّصَّ ('āqabtu al-liṣṣ, "I punished the thief"), and ﻃَارَقْتُ النَّعْلَ (ṭāraqtu al-na'l, "I put one sandal upon another"). Al-Zajjaj said: "The command came from God, and acceptance came from Musa. Therefore it is mentioned with the wording *al-muwā'adah* (mutual appointment)." The people of Basra recited ﴿وَإِذْ وَعَدْنَا﴾ (wa-idh wa'adnā), from *al-wa'd* (promise).

﴿مُوسَى﴾ (Mūsā, Moses) is a Hebrew name that was Arabicised. In Hebrew, "mū" means water and "shā" means tree. He was named this because he was taken from between water and trees. Then the *shīn* with a dot was changed to *sīn* in Arabic.

﴿أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً﴾ (forty nights) means their completion: thirty nights of Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten of Dhu al-Hijjah. The date is tied to the nights rather than the days, because the months of the Arabs were set according to the course of the moon, and the crescent appears at night. It was said: gratitude is obedience with all the limbs, in private and in public. Al-Ḥasan said: the gratitude for a blessing is to mention it. God the Exalted says: ﴿وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ﴾ ("As for the blessing of your Lord, speak of it," al-Ḍuḥā 11). Al-Fuḍayl said: the gratitude for every blessing is that God is not disobeyed after that blessing. It was also said: the true reality of gratitude is the inability to be grateful.

It is related that Musa, peace be upon him, said: "My God, You have bestowed upon me abundant blessings, and You have commanded me to be grateful, and my gratitude to You is itself a blessing from You." God the Exalted said: "O Musa, you have learned a knowledge than which no knowledge surpasses. It is enough for Me from My servant that he knows that whatever blessing he has is from Me." Dāwūd, peace be upon him, said: "Glory be to Him who made the servant's acknowledgment of his inability to thank Him a form of thanks, just as He made his acknowledgment of his inability to know Him a form of knowing Him."

God the Exalted says: ﴿وَإِذْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ﴾ ("And when We gave Musa the Book"), meaning the Torah, ﴿وَالْفُرْقَانَ﴾ ("and the Criterion"). Mujāhid said: it is also the Torah; He mentioned it by two names. Al-Kisā'ī said: *al-Furqān* is a description of *al-Kitāb*, and the *wāw* is superfluous, meaning: the Book that distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful. Yamān ibn Rabbān said: by *al-Furqān* He meant the parting of the sea, as He said: "And when We divided the sea for you and saved you" (al-Baqarah 50). ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("that you might be guided") by the Torah.

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ ("And when Musa said to his people"), those who worshipped the calf, ﴿يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ ("O my people, you have wronged yourselves"), meaning you harmed yourselves ﴿بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ﴾ ("by your taking the calf") as a god. They said: "What should we do?" He said: ﴿فَتُوبُوا﴾ ("So repent") meaning return ﴿إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ﴾ ("to your Creator"), your Maker. They said: "How do we repent?" He said: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ ("then kill yourselves"), meaning that the innocent among you should kill the guilty. ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ ("That") meaning the killing ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ عِنْدَ بَارِئِكُمْ﴾ ("is better for you with your Creator"). When Musa commanded them to kill, they said: "We will be patient with God's command." So they sat in the courtyards [[Plural of *fanā'*: the open space in front of a house; it was said: what extends from its sides.]] crouched [[*Al-iḥtibā'*: a man gathers his back and his shins with a garment or something else.]]. It was said to them: whoever stretches out his crouch, or lifts his gaze toward his killer, or shields himself with a hand or a foot, is cursed, and his repentance is rejected. The people drew daggers upon them. A man would see his son, his father, his brother, his relative, his friend, and his neighbour, and yet they could not carry out God the Exalted's command. They said: "O Musa, what shall we do?" So God sent upon them a fog and a black cloud, so that none could see another, and they kept killing one another until evening. When the killing increased, Musa and Hārūn, peace be upon them both, called out, wept, and entreated, and said: "O Lord, the Children of Israel are being destroyed; spare the remnant, spare the remnant!" God the Exalted then lifted the cloud, and commanded them to stop killing. The cloud cleared, revealing thousands of the slain.

It is narrated from ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The number of the slain was seventy thousand. This weighed heavily upon Musa, so God the Exalted revealed to him: "Would it not please you that I admit both the killer and the killed into Paradise?" Those among them who were killed were martyrs, and those who remained had their sins expiated. This is the meaning of God the Exalted's words: ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ ("So He turned to you in forgiveness"), meaning: when you did what you were commanded, He turned to you and pardoned you. ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ﴾ ("Indeed He is the Accepter of repentance") ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ ("the Most Merciful") toward His creation.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 55–57:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly"﴾. The reason was that Allah the Exalted commanded Musa, peace be upon him, to come to Him with some of the Children of Israel who would apologise to Him for worshipping the calf. Musa chose seventy men from his people, the best of them, and said to them: "Fast, purify yourselves, and wash your garments." They did so, and Musa set out with them to Mount Sinai (Tur Sina') for the appointed time with his Lord. They said to Musa: "Ask for us, that we may hear the speech of our Lord." He said: "I will do so." When Musa drew near to the mountain of Sinai, a column of cloud descended upon him and covered the whole mountain. He entered the cloud and said to the people: "Draw near." They drew near until they entered the cloud, and they fell down prostrate. Whenever his Lord spoke to Musa, a brilliant light would fall upon his face, such that no human being could look at it. A veil was drawn between them and him, and they heard Him speaking to Musa, commanding him and forbidding him. Allah made them hear: "Indeed I am Allah, there is no god but Me, the Possessor of Bakka [[Dhu Bakka: i.e., the Possessor of strength.]]. I brought you out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand. So worship Me and do not worship other than Me." When Musa had finished and the cloud had dispersed, he came back to them, and they said to him: "We will never believe you until we see Allah openly" — that is, face to face. This is because the Arabs use the word "knowledge" in the heart to mean "sight," so He said "openly" to make clear that what is meant is direct seeing. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized you﴾, that is, death. It was also said: a fire came down from the sky and burned them. ﴿While you were looking on﴾, that is, some of you were looking at others when death seized you. It was also said: "while you were knowing," and seeing can carry the meaning of knowing.

When they perished, Musa began to weep and supplicate, saying: "What shall I say to the Children of Israel when I come to them, after You have destroyed their best?" ﴿If You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?﴾ (7:155). He kept pleading with his Lord until Allah the Exalted brought them back to life, one man after another, after they had died for a day and a night, while they looked at one another, wondering how they would be revived. That is the meaning of His words:

﴿Then We raised you﴾, that is, We brought you back to life. Ba'th (resurrection) means stirring a thing from its place. It is said: "I raised the camel" and "I roused the sleeper, and he rose." ﴿after your death﴾. Qatadah said: He revived them so that they might complete the remainder of their lifespans and provisions; had they died at their appointed times, they would not have been raised again until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿So that perhaps you would be grateful. And We shaded you with the cloud﴾ in the wilderness (al-tih), protecting you from the heat of the sun. Al-ghamam (cloud) derives from al-ghamm, and its root meaning is covering and concealing. Clouds are called ghamam because they cover the face of the sun. They had no shelter in the wilderness to protect them, so they complained to Musa, and Allah the Exalted sent a white, thin cloud, more pleasant than rain-clouds, and made for them a pillar of light that illuminated the night for them, since they had no moon.

﴿And We sent down to you the manna and the quail﴾, that is, in the wilderness. Most scholars hold that al-manna is the terengabin (a sweet exudation). Mujahid said: it is a substance like gum that fell upon the trees, whose taste was like honey. Wahb said: it is thin bread (al-khubz al-raqaq). Al-Zajjaj said: the whole sense of al-mann is what Allah bestows without toil.

We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us [12/a]: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu Nu'aym informed us: Sufyan informed us, from Abd al-Malik — that is, Ibn Umayr — from Amr ibn Huraith, from Sa'id ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Mushrooms (kam'a) are of the manna, and their water is a cure for the eye." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of Surah al-Baqarah, chapter "And We shaded you with the cloud" (8/163), and in the Tafsir of Surah al-A'raf, and in the Book of Medicine. Muslim in the Book of Drinks, chapter on the excellence of mushrooms and treating the eye with them, no. 2049 (3/1619). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/332–333.]]

They said: This manna used to fall every night upon their trees like snow, a sa' for each person. They said: "O Musa, this manna has wearied us with its sweetness; ask your Lord to feed us meat." So Allah the Exalted sent down the quail (al-salwa) upon them. It is a bird resembling the quail (sumana). It was also said that it is the quail itself. Allah sent a cloud, and the quail rained down a mile wide and a spear's length high in the sky, piled upon one another. Al-salwa was also said to mean honey. Allah sent down the manna and the quail upon them every morning from the break of dawn until sunrise, and each of them would take what sufficed him for a day and a night. On Friday, each would take enough for two days, because it did not fall on Saturday.

﴿Eat﴾, that is, and We said to them: "Eat ﴿of the good things﴾, the lawful ones, ﴿that We have provided for you﴾, and do not store them up for tomorrow." They did so, but Allah cut this off from them, and what they had stored became infested with worms and spoiled. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves﴾, that is, they did not diminish Our right, but they wronged themselves by incurring My punishment, and by cutting off the source of provision that had been sent down upon them without effort in this world and without reckoning in the Hereafter.

We were informed by Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmish al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah informed us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Were it not for the Children of Israel, food would not spoil, and meat would not rot [[Yatanun: stink.]]; and were it not for Hawwa', no woman would ever betray her husband." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of the Prophets, chapter on the saying of Allah, "And We appointed for Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten" (6/430). Muslim in the Book of Suckling, chapter "Were it not for Hawwa', no woman would betray her husband forever," no. 1470 (2/1092). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/164.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 58–59:

﴿And when We said: "Enter this town"﴾ The town (*qaryah*) is so called because it gathers (*tajma'u*) its people. From the same root comes *al-miqrah* (the cistern), meaning the basin, because it gathers the water. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: It is Jericho (*Arihaʾ*), and it is the town of the giants (*al-Jabbarin*). In it lived a people from the remnant of 'Ad called the 'Amalaqah (Amalekites), whose chief was 'Uj ibn 'Unuq. It is also said: it is Balqa'. Mujahid said: it is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). al-Dahhak said: it is al-Ramlah, al-Urdunn (Jordan), Filastin (Palestine) and Tadmur (Palmyra). Muqatil said: it is Ilya' (Aelia). Ibn Kaysan said: it is al-Sham (Greater Syria).

﴿So eat from it wherever you wish, in abundance﴾, meaning, with plenty provided for you. ﴿And enter the gate﴾, meaning one of the gates of the town; it had seven gates. ﴿In prostration﴾, meaning bowing, humbling yourselves, and bending low. Wahb said: When you have entered it, prostrate in thanks to Allah, exalted is He.

﴿And say: "Ḥiṭṭah"﴾. Qatadah said: It means, "Remove from us our sins." They were commanded to seek forgiveness. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means "There is no god but Allah," because it removes sins. It is in the nominative (*raf'*) by implying the sense: "Say: our request is ḥiṭṭah."

﴿We will forgive you your sins﴾. The word *ghafr* means covering, so forgiveness (*maghfirah*) covers sins. Ahl al-Madinah and Nafi' [[Addition from manuscript B.]] read *naghfir* with a *yā'* (*yughfar*, the passive form) and a *ḍammah* on it, with a *fatḥah* on the *fā'*. Ibn 'Amir read *tughfar* with a *tā'* and a *ḍammah*, with a *fatḥah* on the *fā'*. In al-A'raf, all of them and Ya'qub read it with a *tā'* and a *ḍammah*, while the others read both places with a *fatḥah* on the *nūn* and a *kasrah* on the *fā'*. [These are variant readings (*qira'at*), that is, differing recitations of the Qur'an.] ﴿And We will increase the good-doers﴾ in reward, out of Our bounty.

﴿But those who did wrong substituted﴾, meaning they changed, ﴿a word other than that which had been said to them﴾. This was because they replaced the word *ḥiṭṭah* with *ḥinṭah* (wheat). They said with their tongues, "Ḥiṭānā simqāthā," meaning "a red wheat," out of contempt for the command of Allah, exalted is He. Mujahid said: The gate was lowered for them so that they would lower their heads, but they refused to enter in prostration. So they entered on their backsides, in opposition in deed, just as they had changed the word, and said a word other than what had been said to them.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Nasr informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It was said to the Children of Israel: 'Enter the gate in prostration and say ḥiṭṭah,' but they changed it. They entered crawling on their backsides and said, 'A grain in a hair.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of the Prophets, 6/436; and Muslim in the Book of Tafsir, no. 3015, 4/2312.]

﴿So We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from the heaven﴾. It is said: Allah sent upon them a plague (*ṭā'ūn*), and seventy thousand of them perished in a single hour. ﴿Because they were defiant﴾, meaning they disobeyed and departed from the command of Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 58–59:

﴿And when We said: "Enter this town"﴾ The town (*qaryah*) is so called because it gathers (*tajma'u*) its people. From the same root comes *al-miqrah* (the cistern), meaning the basin, because it gathers the water. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: It is Jericho (*Arihaʾ*), and it is the town of the giants (*al-Jabbarin*). In it lived a people from the remnant of 'Ad called the 'Amalaqah (Amalekites), whose chief was 'Uj ibn 'Unuq. It is also said: it is Balqa'. Mujahid said: it is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). al-Dahhak said: it is al-Ramlah, al-Urdunn (Jordan), Filastin (Palestine) and Tadmur (Palmyra). Muqatil said: it is Ilya' (Aelia). Ibn Kaysan said: it is al-Sham (Greater Syria).

﴿So eat from it wherever you wish, in abundance﴾, meaning, with plenty provided for you. ﴿And enter the gate﴾, meaning one of the gates of the town; it had seven gates. ﴿In prostration﴾, meaning bowing, humbling yourselves, and bending low. Wahb said: When you have entered it, prostrate in thanks to Allah, exalted is He.

﴿And say: "Ḥiṭṭah"﴾. Qatadah said: It means, "Remove from us our sins." They were commanded to seek forgiveness. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means "There is no god but Allah," because it removes sins. It is in the nominative (*raf'*) by implying the sense: "Say: our request is ḥiṭṭah."

[These are variant readings (*qira'at*), that is, differing recitations of the Qur'an.] ﴿And We will increase the good-doers﴾ in reward, out of Our bounty.

They said with their tongues, "Ḥiṭānā simqāthā," meaning "a red wheat," out of contempt for the command of Allah, exalted is He. So they entered on their backsides, in opposition in deed, just as they had changed the word, and said a word other than what had been said to them.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Nasr informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It was said to the Children of Israel: 'Enter the gate in prostration and say ḥiṭṭah,' but they changed it. They entered crawling on their backsides and said, 'A grain in a hair.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of the Prophets, 6/436; and Muslim in the Book of Tafsir, no. 3015, 4/2312.]

﴿So We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from the heaven﴾. It is said: Allah sent upon them a plague (*ṭā'ūn*), and seventy thousand of them perished in a single hour. ﴿Because they were defiant﴾, meaning they disobeyed and departed from the command of Allah, exalted is He.

﴿وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَى مُوسَى﴾ (And when Moses asked for water), meaning he sought water, ﴿لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ (for his people). This was because they became thirsty in the wilderness (al-tih), so they asked Moses to pray for rain/water for them, and he did. Then it was revealed to him, as He said: ﴿فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ﴾ (So We said: Strike the rock with your staff). The staff was from the trees of Paradise (aas al-jannah, myrtle). Its length was ten cubits (adhru') according to the height of Moses, peace be upon him. It had two prongs that shone with light in the darkness. Its name was ʿAlaq (or ʿAlliq), which Adam, peace be upon him, brought down from Paradise. The prophets inherited it until it reached Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, who gave it to Moses, peace be upon him.

Muqatil said: The name of the staff, by its description, is the Almighty's words ﴿الْحَجَرَ﴾ (the rock). The scholars differed about it. Wahb said: It was not a specific rock; rather, Moses would strike whatever rock was at hand among the stones, and it would gush forth springs, a spring for each tribe, and they were twelve tribes. Then each spring would flow in a stream to the tribe that had been commanded to drink from it. The others said: It was a specific rock, as evidenced by its being defined with the article "al" (alif and lam). Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was a light, square stone, the size of a man's head, which he would place in his bag (mikhlah); whenever they needed water, he would set it down and strike it with his staff. ʿAta said: The rock had four faces, and each face had three springs, one for each tribe. It was also said: The rock was marble. It was also said: It was of al-kadhdhan [[A soft rock, as if it were clay, and perhaps it was crumbly.]], in which there were twelve holes, and from each hole a spring of sweet water welled up. When they had finished and Moses wanted to carry it, he struck it with his staff and the water went away. It supplied six hundred thousand people each day. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: It is the rock on which Moses placed his garment in order to bathe, and it fled with his garment, and he passed by it over an assembly of the Children of Israel when they accused him of having a testicular swelling (al-udrah) [[Swelling of the testicle.]]. When he stopped, Jibril came to him and said: Indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: Lift this rock, for I have power in it, and for you there is a miracle in it. So he lifted it and placed it in his bag. ʿAta said: Moses would strike it twelve times, and at the place of each strike there would appear something like a woman's breast, which would sweat, and then the rivers would burst forth and flow.

Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) say: "inbajasat" and "infajarat" are one and the same. Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ said: "inbajasat" means it sweated, and "infajarat" means it flowed. This is the meaning of the Almighty's words:

﴿فَانْفَجَرَتْ﴾ (Then there gushed forth), meaning: he struck, and so it gushed forth, that is, it flowed from it. ﴿اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا﴾ (twelve springs), according to the number of the tribes. ﴿قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَشْرَبَهُمْ﴾ (Every people knew its drinking place), meaning the place where they drink, such that no tribe would enter upon another's drinking place. ﴿كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِنْ رِزْقِ اللَّهِ﴾ (Eat and drink from the provision of Allah), meaning: We said to them, "Eat from the manna and the quails, and drink from the water," for all of this is from the provision of Allah, coming to you without hardship. ﴿وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ﴾ (And do not commit corruption in the earth, spreading mischief). And al-ʿaith is the most extreme corruption. It is said: ʿathā yaʿthī ʿathyan, ʿathā yaʿthū ʿathwan, and ʿāba yaʿīthu ʿaythan.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 61:

His words, exalted is He, ﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will not endure one kind of food"﴾. The reason was that they united in complaint and grew weary of eating the manna (al-mann) and the quails (al-salwa). He said ﴿one kind of food﴾ although they were two, because the Arabs express the dual with the singular form, just as they express the singular with the dual form, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾ (55:22). In fact, they come forth only from the salt water and not the sweet. It is also said that they used to eat one of them with the other, so they were like one food. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: they used to knead the manna with the quails, so the two became one.

﴿So call upon your Lord for us﴾, meaning, ask on our behalf, ﴿that He bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: al-fum is bread. ʿAta' said: wheat. Al-Qutaybi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the grains that are all eaten. Al-Kalbi said: ﴿and its lentils and its onions.﴾

Musa, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿Would you exchange that which is lower﴾, meaning more base and worse, ﴿for that which is better﴾, meaning more noble and excellent. He regarded wheat as lower in value, though it is better than the manna and the quails. Or he meant that it is easier to obtain in the usual way. It is also possible that "better" refers to Allah's choice for them and their own choice for themselves.

﴿Go down to a city﴾, meaning: if you refuse anything other than this, then descend to one of the cities. Al-Dahhak said: it is the Egypt of Musa and Pharaoh. The first view is more sound, because if He had intended that, He would not have made it indeclinable (ghayr munsarif). ﴿For you will have what you ask.﴾ The vegetation of the earth. ﴿And they were struck with humiliation﴾, meaning they were placed under and obliged to bear abasement and disgrace. ﴿Ruin [al-dhilla]﴾, meaning humiliation and degradation. It is said: this refers to the poll tax (al-jizya). ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib said: it is the kustij and the zunnar, the distinctive dress of Judaism. ﴿And poverty [al-maskana]﴾, meaning neediness. The poor person is called miskin because poverty made him still and kept him from movement. Thus you see the Jews, even when they are wealthy, appearing as if they were poor. It is also said: al-dhilla is poverty of the heart, so you will not find among the followers of the religions anyone more abject or more avid for wealth than the Jews.

﴿And they returned with wrath from Allah﴾. Baa'u means they returned, and it is not said "baa'u" except with evil. Abu ʿUbayda said: they bore it and acknowledged it. From this comes the supplication: "abu'u laka bi-ni'matika ʿalayya wa abu'u bi-dhanbi," meaning: I acknowledge to You Your blessing upon me and I acknowledge my sin. ﴿That﴾, i.e., the wrath, ﴿is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, namely the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the verse of stoning in the Torah, and they disbelieved in the Gospel and the Qur'an. ﴿And they killed the prophets﴾. Nafi' alone read the hamza in "al-nabiyyin" and its derivatives, so its meaning would be "the one who informs," from anba'a yunbi'u. The well-known reading omits the hamza, and it has two aspects: first, it is also from al-inba' (informing), with the hamza dropped for lightness due to frequent use; second, it means "elevated," derived from al-nubuwwa, which is an elevated place, and on this view "al-nabiyyin" stands in its original form. ﴿Without right﴾, i.e., without any crime. If it is asked: why did He say "without right," since killing the prophets can only be without right? It is answered: He mentioned it as a qualifier of the killing, and killing is sometimes described as "without right." It is like His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge with truth"﴾ (21:112), where "truth" is mentioned as a qualifier of the judgment, not because His judgment is divided into injustice and truth. It is narrated that the Jews killed seventy prophets in the early part of the day, and a market was held for their killing at the end of the day. ﴿That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress﴾, i.e., they exceed My command and commit My prohibitions.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 62–64:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews﴾: "those who were Jews" means the Jews. They were named this for their saying, "We have turned (hudna) to You," that is, "We have inclined (milna) to You." It is also said that they were named this because they repented (hadu) from worshipping the calf. It is also said that they were named this because they deviated from the religion of Islam and from the religion of Musa, upon him be peace. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: they were named this because they "yatahawwadun," that is, they move when reciting the Torah and say, "The heavens and the earth moved when Allah gave Musa the Torah."

﴿and the Christians﴾: they were named this for the saying of the Hawariyyun (the disciples of 'Isa): "We are the helpers (ansar) of Allah." Muqatil said: they were named this because they settled in a town called Nasirah. It is also said: they were named this for their affiliation to Nasirah, a town where 'Isa, upon him be peace, used to stay.

﴿and the Sabians﴾: Ahl al-Madinah read "wal-Sabiyyin" and "wal-Sabbun" without the hamzah, while the rest read it with the hamzah. Its original root meaning is "to exit." It is said: "Sabaa fulan," meaning he left one religion for another. "Sabaat al-nujum" means the stars emerged from their risings, and "sabaa naab al-ba'ir" means the camel's tooth came out. They were named this because they exited from one religion to another. 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas said: they are a people from among the People of the Book. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: their slaughtered animals are the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book. Ibn 'Abbas said: their slaughtered animals are not lawful, nor is marriage to them. Mujahid said: they are a tribe toward Syria, between the Jews and the Magians. Al-Kalbi said: they are a people between the Jews and the Christians who shave the middles of their heads and castrate their male members. Qatadah said: they are a people who recite the Zabur (Psalms), worship the angels, pray toward the Ka'bah, and affirm Allah, the Exalted; they took a bit from every religion. 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: they have become extinct.

[[In Iraq at the present time there is a minority of Sabians. They believe in the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, and believe in the Last Day. They claim that they follow the teachings of Adam, upon him be peace, and that their prophet Yahya came to purify the religion of Adam of what had clung to it. They have a book they call "al-Kanzabra," meaning the scrolls of Adam. Among their acts of worship is prayer, which is limited to standing, bowing, and sitting on the ground without prostration. They perform it three times a day: before sunrise, at its decline, and shortly before sunset, and they face the Pole Star in their prayer. Source: Ahkam al-Dhimmiyyin wal-Musta'manin fi Dar al-Islam, Dr. 'Abd al-Karim Zaydan, pp. 14–15. See also the opinions of the jurists on the ruling concerning the Sabians in Ibn Kathir, 1/189–190, and Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas, 3/91.]].

﴿Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾: If it is asked, how does His saying "whoever believes in Allah" fit, when at the beginning of the verse He mentioned "those who believed"? It is answered: they differed regarding the ruling of the verse. Some of them said: by His saying "those who believed," He meant those who believed in truth. Then they differed about these believers. A group said: they are those who believed before the mission (of the Prophet), who were seekers of the religion, such as Habib al-Najjar, Qiss ibn Sa'idah, Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqah ibn Nawfal, al-Bara' al-Sinni, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Salman al-Farisi, Bahira the monk, and the delegation of al-Najashi. Among them are those who met the Prophet ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him [[In b: "followed him."]], and among them are those who did not meet him. It is also said: they are the believers from the previous nations. It is also said: they are the believers from this Ummah.

﴿and those who were Jews﴾: those who were upon the religion of Musa, upon him be peace, and did not change it. And the Christians: those who were upon the religion of 'Isa, upon him be peace, and did not alter it, and died upon that. They said: these two names clung to them during the times of Musa and 'Isa, upon them both be peace, when they were upon the truth, just as "Islam" belongs to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. The Sabians (were so named) during the time when their affair was upright.

﴿man amana﴾ means: whoever among them died while a believer, because the reality of faith is by continuing in it until death. It is permissible that the conjunction (wa) be understood as implied, meaning: "and whoever believes after you, O Muhammad, until the Day of Resurrection." Some of them said: those mentioned with belief at the beginning of the verse are meant in a figurative sense, not literally. Then they differed about them. Some of them said: those who believed in the prophets who passed away but did not believe in you. It is also said: He meant the hypocrites who believed with their tongues but did not believe in their hearts, and the Jews and Christians who adhered to Judaism and Christianity after their alteration, and the Sabians, who are some categories of disbelievers.

﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾: these categories, with the heart and the tongue. ﴿and does righteousness, they will have their reward with their Lord﴾. It was mentioned in the plural form because ﴿man﴾ is suitable for the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine, and the feminine. ﴿No fear will there be concerning them﴾ in this world, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ in the Hereafter.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when We took your covenant﴾, that is, your pledge, O company of Jews, ﴿and raised above you the mount﴾, the mountain. In the Syriac language, according to some of them, and this is the saying of Mujahid, "Tur" is the word for mountain. It was said: there is no language in the world that is not found in the Qur'an. Most scholars said: there is no language in the Qur'an other than the language of the Arabs, due to His saying, ﴿an Arabic Qur'an﴾. These words and their like occurred by agreement between the two languages [[See the opinions of scholars on what occurred in the Qur'an in a language other than Arabic, al-Itqan by al-Suyuti, 2/125, edited by Muhammad Abu al-Fadl Ibrahim.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah commanded a mountain from the mountains of Palestine, and it was uprooted from its base until it stood over their heads. That was because Allah sent down the Torah to Musa, upon him be peace, and Musa commanded his people to accept it and act upon its rulings, but they refused to accept it because of the burdens (asar) [[Plural of isr: here meaning covenant and pledge, and it may also mean sin and punishment.]] and heavy obligations contained in it, for it was a heavy law. So Allah commanded Jibril, upon him be peace, and he uprooted a mountain the size of their army, which was a farsakh by a farsakh, and raised it above their heads like a canopy, the height of a man's stature. He said to them: "If you do not accept the Torah, I will drop this mountain upon you." 'Ata' reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: Allah raised the Tur above their heads, sent a fire toward their faces, and the salt sea came to them from behind. ﴿Take﴾, that is, We said to them: take ﴿what We have given you﴾, what We have bestowed upon you, ﴿with strength﴾, with earnestness, striving, and perseverance. ﴿And remember﴾ and study ﴿what is in it﴾. It is also said: memorize it and act upon it, ﴿so that you may be righteous﴾, in order that you may be saved from destruction in this world and from punishment in the Hereafter. If you accept, well and good; otherwise I will crush you with this mountain, drown you in this sea, and burn you with this fire. When they saw that there was no escape for them from it, they accepted, prostrated, and began to glance upward at the mountain while prostrating. This became a tradition for the Jews: they do not prostrate except on the sides of their faces, and they say: "By this prostration the punishment was lifted from us."

﴿Then you turned away﴾, that is, you turned away ﴿after that﴾, after you had accepted the Torah, ﴿and were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾, meaning by respite, delay, and postponement of punishment from you, ﴿you would have been﴾, you would have become ﴿among the losers﴾, among those defrauded by punishment and the loss of this world and the Hereafter. It is also said: among those punished immediately, because He showed you mercy by granting respite.

It is also said: they are the believers from the previous nations. It is also said: they are the believers from this Ummah.

﴿and those who were Jews﴾: those who were upon the religion of Musa, upon him be peace, and did not change it. And the Christians: those who were upon the religion of 'Isa, upon him be peace, and did not alter it, and died upon that. They said: these two names clung to them during the times of Musa and 'Isa, upon them both be peace, when they were upon the truth, just as "Islam" belongs to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. The Sabians (were so named) during the time when their affair was upright.

﴿man amana﴾ means: whoever among them died while a believer, because the reality of faith is by continuing in it until death. It is permissible that the conjunction (wa) be understood as implied, meaning: "and whoever believes after you, O Muhammad, until the Day of Resurrection." Some of them said: those mentioned with belief at the beginning of the verse are meant in a figurative sense, not literally. Then they differed about them. Some of them said: those who believed in the prophets who passed away but did not believe in you. It is also said: He meant the hypocrites who believed with their tongues but did not believe in their hearts, and the Jews and Christians who adhered to Judaism and Christianity after their alteration, and the Sabians, who are some categories of disbelievers.

﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾: these categories, with the heart and the tongue. ﴿and does righteousness, they will have their reward with their Lord﴾. It was mentioned in the plural form because ﴿man﴾ is suitable for the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine, and the feminine. ﴿No fear will there be concerning them﴾ in this world, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ in the Hereafter.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when We took your covenant﴾, that is, your pledge, O company of Jews, ﴿and raised above you the mount﴾, the mountain. In the Syriac language, according to some of them, and this is the saying of Mujahid, "Tur" is the word for mountain. It was said: there is no language in the world that is not found in the Qur'an. Most scholars said: there is no language in the Qur'an other than the language of the Arabs, due to His saying, ﴿an Arabic Qur'an﴾. These words and their like occurred by agreement between the two languages [[See the opinions of scholars on what occurred in the Qur'an in a language other than Arabic, al-Itqan by al-Suyuti, 2/125, edited by Muhammad Abu al-Fadl Ibrahim.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah commanded a mountain from the mountains of Palestine, and it was uprooted from its base until it stood over their heads. That was because Allah sent down the Torah to Musa, upon him be peace, and Musa commanded his people to accept it and act upon its rulings, but they refused to accept it because of the burdens (asar) [[Plural of isr: here meaning covenant and pledge, and it may also mean sin and punishment.]] and heavy obligations contained in it, for it was a heavy law. So Allah commanded Jibril, upon him be peace, and he uprooted a mountain the size of their army, which was a farsakh by a farsakh, and raised it above their heads like a canopy, the height of a man's stature. He said to them: "If you do not accept the Torah, I will drop this mountain upon you." 'Ata' reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: Allah raised the Tur above their heads, sent a fire toward their faces, and the salt sea came to them from behind. ﴿Take﴾, that is, We said to them: take ﴿what We have given you﴾, what We have bestowed upon you, ﴿with strength﴾, with earnestness, striving, and perseverance. ﴿And remember﴾ and study ﴿what is in it﴾. It is also said: memorize it and act upon it, ﴿so that you may be righteous﴾, in order that you may be saved from destruction in this world and from punishment in the Hereafter. If you accept, well and good; otherwise I will crush you with this mountain, drown you in this sea, and burn you with this fire. When they saw that there was no escape for them from it, they accepted, prostrated, and began to glance upward at the mountain while prostrating. This became a tradition for the Jews: they do not prostrate except on the sides of their faces, and they say: "By this prostration the punishment was lifted from us."

﴿Then you turned away﴾, that is, you turned away ﴿after that﴾, after you had accepted the Torah, ﴿and were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾, meaning by respite, delay, and postponement of punishment from you, ﴿you would have been﴾, you would have become ﴿among the losers﴾, among those defrauded by punishment and the loss of this world and the Hereafter. It is also said: among those punished immediately, because He showed you mercy by granting respite.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 62–64:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews﴾: "those who were Jews" means the Jews. They were named this for their saying, "We have turned (hudna) to You," that is, "We have inclined (milna) to You." It is also said that they were named this because they repented (hadu) from worshipping the calf. It is also said that they were named this because they deviated from the religion of Islam and from the religion of Musa, upon him be peace. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: they were named this because they "yatahawwadun," that is, they move when reciting the Torah and say, "The heavens and the earth moved when Allah gave Musa the Torah."

﴿and the Christians﴾: they were named this for the saying of the Hawariyyun (the disciples of 'Isa): "We are the helpers (ansar) of Allah." Muqatil said: they were named this because they settled in a town called Nasirah. It is also said: they were named this for their affiliation to Nasirah, a town where 'Isa, upon him be peace, used to stay.

﴿and the Sabians﴾: Ahl al-Madinah read "wal-Sabiyyin" and "wal-Sabbun" without the hamzah, while the rest read it with the hamzah. Its original root meaning is "to exit." It is said: "Sabaa fulan," meaning he left one religion for another. "Sabaat al-nujum" means the stars emerged from their risings, and "sabaa naab al-ba'ir" means the camel's tooth came out. They were named this because they exited from one religion to another. 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas said: they are a people from among the People of the Book. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: their slaughtered animals are the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book. Ibn 'Abbas said: their slaughtered animals are not lawful, nor is marriage to them. Mujahid said: they are a tribe toward Syria, between the Jews and the Magians. Al-Kalbi said: they are a people between the Jews and the Christians who shave the middles of their heads and castrate their male members. Qatadah said: they are a people who recite the Zabur (Psalms), worship the angels, pray toward the Ka'bah, and affirm Allah, the Exalted; they took a bit from every religion. 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: they have become extinct.

[[In Iraq at the present time there is a minority of Sabians. They believe in the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, and believe in the Last Day.
