**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 65–67:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you certainly knew those among you who transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath﴾. That is, they exceeded the limit. The root of *sabt* (Sabbath) is *al-qat'* (cutting off). It is said that the day of the Sabbath was named so because Allah, may He be exalted, ceased (*qata'a*) creation on it. It is also said that it was because the Jews were commanded to cease (*qat'*) their work on it. The story concerning it is that during the time of Dawud, peace be upon him, they were in a land called Aylah. Allah forbade them to hunt fish on the Sabbath day. Whenever the Sabbath came, no fish remained in the sea without gathering there, so that they would thrust their snouts out of the water in their safety, until the water could not be seen because of their multitude. When the Sabbath had passed, they would sink and settle at the bottom (*maqal*) of the sea, so that none of them could be seen. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, appearing openly, but on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾ (7:163).

Then Satan whispered to them and said: "You have only been forbidden from taking them on the Sabbath day." So some men set about digging pools around the sea and channelled rivers from it to them. When it was the evening of Friday, they opened those channels, and the waves brought the fish to the pools. They could not get out again because of the depth of the pools and the scarcity of their water. When Sunday came, they took them. It is also said that they would drive the fish into the pools on the Sabbath day without taking them, and then take them on Sunday. It is also said that they would set up nets and traps on Friday and take them out on Sunday. They did this for a time, and no punishment descended upon them, so they grew bold in sin and said: "We see that the prohibition has only been lifted for us." So they took them, ate them, salted them, sold them and bought with them, and their wealth increased. When they did this, the people of the town, who numbered about seventy thousand, became three groups: one group refrained and forbade (the sin); one group refrained but did not forbid; and one group violated the sanctity (of the Sabbath). Those who forbade numbered twelve thousand. When the wrongdoers refused to accept their advice, they said: "By Allah, we will not live with you in one town." So they divided the town with a wall, and they passed two years in this state. Then Dawud, peace be upon him, cursed them, and Allah became angry with them for their persistence in disobedience. One day, those who had forbidden (the sin) came out through their gate, but none of the wrongdoers came out, and they did not open their gate. When they were slow in coming out, (the others) climbed over the wall, and behold, they were all apes with tails, swarming about. Qatadah said: "The young men became apes and the elders became swine." They remained (in that state) for three days, then they perished. No transformation lasts longer than three days, and they did not reproduce.

Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So We said to them: Be apes, despised﴾. This is a command of transformation and bringing into being. ﴿Despised﴾ means removed and expelled. It is said that there is an inversion (*taqdim wa ta'khir*) here, meaning: "Be despised apes," and for this reason it did not say *khasi'atin* (feminine). *Al-khasa'* means expulsion and banishment. It is both intransitive and transitive: one says *khasa'tuhu khas'an fa-khasa'a khusu'an*, like *raja'tuhu raj'an fa-raja'a ruju'an*.

﴿So We made it﴾, that is, We made their punishment by transformation into apes, ﴿a deterrent﴾, that is, a punishment and a lesson. *Al-nakal* is the name for any punishment by which the onlooker is deterred from doing the act for which the punishment was made a requital. From it comes *al-nukul* (refusal) concerning an oath, which means abstention. Its root is *al-nikl*, which means a fetter, and its plural is *ankal*. ﴿For what was before it﴾: Qatadah said: "He meant by what was before it, that is, the sins that had preceded (it)." That is, We made that punishment a requital for their sins committed before they were forbidden to take the game. ﴿And what was after it﴾: what was present of the sins for which they were seized, namely disobedience by taking the fish. Abu al-Aliyah and al-Rabi' said: (it was) a punishment for their past sins and a lesson for those after them, so that they would follow their example. The second *ma* (in *wa ma khalfaha*) is in the sense of *man* (those who). It is also said: ﴿We made it﴾ means We made the town of the people of the Sabbath a lesson for what was before it, that is, the towns that were built at the time; ﴿and what was after it﴾, that is, the towns that would arise afterwards, so that they might take warning. It is also said that there is an inversion here, the sense being: "So We made it and what was after it," meaning what was prepared for them of punishment in the Hereafter; and a requital for what was before it, that is, for their past sins in transgressing on the Sabbath. ﴿And an admonition to the God-fearing﴾, that is, to the believers of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, so that they do not do the like of what they did.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Musa said to his people: Indeed Allah commands you to slaughter a cow﴾. *Al-baqarah* (the cow) is the female of the bovine species. It is said that it is derived from *al-baqr*, which means splitting, and it was so named because it splits the earth for ploughing.

The story [[The story is from the Isra'iliyyat, as is evident, and nothing is accepted in the exegesis of the Book of Allah except what comes through a firm transmission. Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said after relating the story of the cow: "These narrations from 'Ubaydah, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Suddi and others contain disagreement, and it is apparent that they are taken from the books of the Children of Israel. They are among the things whose transmission is permissible, but they are neither to be affirmed nor denied. Therefore nothing is relied upon from them except what agrees with the truth as we know it, and Allah knows best." Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/197. See also: al-Isra'iliyyat fi al-tafsir wa al-hadith by Dr. Muhammad Husayn al-Dhahabi.]] concerning it is that among the Children of Israel there was a wealthy man who had a poor paternal cousin, who had no heir other than him. When his death was prolonged, the cousin killed him in order to inherit from him. He carried him to another town and left him at their outskirts. Then in the morning he began demanding vengeance for him and brought some people to Musa, accusing them of the killing. Musa questioned them, but they denied it, and the matter of the slain man became unclear to Musa. Al-Kalbi said: "This was before the revelation of the *qasamah* in the Torah [[The oaths are sworn by the heirs of the slain who make the claim of blood.]]." So they asked Musa to invoke Allah so that He might make the matter clear to them through his supplication. Allah then commanded them to slaughter a cow, and Musa said to them: "Indeed Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." ﴿They said: Do you make a mockery of us?﴾, that is, do you mock us? We ask you about the matter of the slain man, and you command us to slaughter a cow!? They said this only because of the great distance between the two matters in appearance, and they did not know the wisdom in it. Hamzah read *huzuwan* and *kufuwan* with lightening (*takhfif*), while the others read them with doubling (*tathqil*), and Hafs read them without the hamzah.

﴿He said: I seek refuge in Allah﴾, that is, I hold myself back by Allah, ﴿from being among the ignorant﴾, that is, among those who mock the believers. It is also said: among the ignorant regarding the answer, not in accordance with the question, for an answer not in accordance with the question is ignorance. When the people [[In the original: "the people" (al-nas) in the text.]] knew that slaughtering the cow was a firm command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, they began to inquire about its description. Had they gone to any ordinary cow and slaughtered it, it would have sufficed them. But they made it hard upon themselves, so Allah made it hard upon them, and there was a wisdom in that. The story is that among the Children of Israel there was a righteous man who had a young son and a heifer. He brought the heifer to a thicket [[Dense growth of trees.]] and said: "O Allah, I entrust this heifer to You for my son until he grows up." Then the man died, and the heifer remained in the thicket as an *awan* [[Of middle age between youth and maturity.]]. It would flee from everyone who saw it. When the son grew up, and he was dutiful to his mother, and he divided the night into three parts: he prayed one third, slept one third, and sat at the head of his mother for one third. When morning came, he set off and gathered firewood on his back, then brought it to the market and sold it for whatever Allah willed. Then he gave away a third in charity, ate a third, and gave his mother a third. One day his mother said to him: "Your father left you a heifer which he entrusted to Allah in such-and-such a thicket. So go and call upon the God of Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq to return it to you. Its sign is that when you look at it, it will seem to you that the rays of the sun are coming out of its skin. It was called *al-Mudhahhabah* (the Gilded) because of its beauty and yellowness." The youth came to the thicket and saw it grazing. He called out to it and said: "I adjure you by the God of Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq and Ya'qub to come to me." So it came running until it stood before him, and he seized its neck, leading it. Then the heifer spoke by the permission of Allah, the Exalted, saying: "O youth, dutiful to your mother, ride me, for that is easier for you." The youth said: "My mother did not command me to do that, but she said: 'Take hold of its neck.'" The heifer said: "By the God of the Children of Israel, if you had ridden me, you would never have been able to control me. Go, for if you commanded the mountain to uproot itself from its base and go with you, it would do so, because of your dutifulness to your mother." So the youth went with it to his mother. She said to him: "You are poor and have no wealth, so gathering firewood by day and standing in prayer by night will be hard for you. Go and sell this heifer." He said: "For how much shall I sell it?" She said: "For three dinars, and do not sell it without consulting me." The price of a heifer at that time was three dinars. So he set off with it to the market. Allah sent an angel to show His creatures His power, and to test the youth to see how he would be dutiful to his mother, and Allah was ever aware of him. The angel said to him: "For how much will you sell this heifer?" He said: "For three dinars, and I stipulate upon you the consent of my mother." The angel said: "You shall have six dinars, and do not consult your mother." The youth said: "Even if you gave me its weight in gold, I would not take it except with my mother's consent." He returned it to his mother and informed her of the price. She said: "Go back and sell it for six dinars, with my consent." He set off with it to the market, and came to the angel, who said: "Have you consulted your mother?" The youth said: "She commanded me not to reduce it below six, on condition that I consult her." The angel said: "I will give you twelve, on condition that you do not consult her." The youth refused. He went back to his mother and informed her, and she said: "The one who comes to you is an angel in human form, testing you. When he comes to you, say to him: 'Do you command us to sell this heifer or not?'" He did so, and the angel said to him: "Go to your mother and tell her: 'Keep this heifer, for Musa son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, is going to buy it from you for a murdered man who will be slain among the Children of Israel. So do not sell it except for its hide filled with dinars.'" So they kept it. Allah, the Exalted, decreed upon the Children of Israel the slaughter of that very heifer. They kept asking Musa to describe it to them until he described that heifer for them, as a reward to him for his dutifulness to his mother, out of His grace and mercy. ﴿That﴾ [[From B.]]

The story is that among the Children of Israel there was a righteous man who had a young son and a heifer. He brought the heifer to a thicket [[Dense growth of trees.]] and said: "O Allah, I entrust this heifer to You for my son until he grows up." Then the man died, and the heifer remained in the thicket as an *awan* [[Of middle age between youth and maturity.]]. It would flee from everyone who saw it. When the son grew up, and he was dutiful to his mother, and he divided the night into three parts: he prayed one third, slept one third, and sat at the head of his mother for one third. When morning came, he set off and gathered firewood on his back, then brought it to the market and sold it for whatever Allah willed. Then he gave away a third in charity, ate a third, and gave his mother a third. One day his mother said to him: "Your father left you a heifer which he entrusted to Allah in such-and-such a thicket. So go and call upon the God of Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq to return it to you. Its sign is that when you look at it, it will seem to you that the rays of the sun are coming out of its skin. He called out to it and said: "I adjure you by the God of Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq and Ya'qub to come to me." So it came running until it stood before him, and he seized its neck, leading it. Then the heifer spoke by the permission of Allah, the Exalted, saying: "O youth, dutiful to your mother, ride me, for that is easier for you." The heifer said: "By the God of the Children of Israel, if you had ridden me, you would never have been able to control me. Go, for if you commanded the mountain to uproot itself from its base and go with you, it would do so, because of your dutifulness to your mother." So the youth went with it to his mother. He said: "For how much shall I sell it?" She said: "For three dinars, and do not sell it without consulting me." The price of a heifer at that time was three dinars. So he set off with it to the market. Allah sent an angel to show His creatures His power, and to test the youth to see how he would be dutiful to his mother, and Allah was ever aware of him. The angel said to him: "For how much will you sell this heifer?" He said: "For three dinars, and I stipulate upon you the consent of my mother." The angel said: "You shall have six dinars, and do not consult your mother." The youth said: "Even if you gave me its weight in gold, I would not take it except with my mother's consent." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 68–69:

Allah's words, ﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what she is."﴾ That is, what is her description (ṣifatuhā) [[In B: her age (sinnuhā).]] ﴿He said﴾ Moses, ﴿"Indeed, He says"﴾ meaning he asked Allah, the Exalted, and said: "Indeed," meaning that Allah, the Exalted, says ﴿"She is a cow neither old (fāriḍ) nor virgin (bikr)"﴾ that is, neither elderly nor young. Al-fāriḍ is the aged one that no longer bears young. It is said of it: faraḍat, tafriḍu, furūḍan. Al-bikr is the young female who has never given birth at all. The (hā') [[From B.]] is dropped from both words because they apply specifically to females, like ḥā'iḍ (menstruating). ﴿'Awān﴾ means intermediate, middle, ﴿between that﴾ meaning between the two ages. It is said: ʿawwanat al-mar'ah taʿwīnan, when the woman exceeds thirty. Al-Akhfash said: (al-ʿawān is the one that has never given birth at all; and it was said:) [[Omitted in the printed B.]] al-ʿawān is the one that has calved several times, and its plural is ʿawn. ﴿So do what you are commanded﴾: slaughter the cow, and do not overburden yourselves with questions.

﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what her color is." He said: "Indeed, He says she is a yellow cow, intensely yellow in color."﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: intensely yellow. Qatadah said: pure (ṣāf). Al-Hasan said: yellow-black (al-ṣafrāʾ al-sawdāʾ). The first view is the most sound, because one does not say "black intensely" (aswad fāqiʿ); rather one says "intensely yellow" (aṣfar fāqiʿ), while black is ḥālik, red is qāniʾ, green is nāḍir, and white is baqaq, for emphasis. ﴿It pleases the onlookers﴾: its beauty and the purity of its color delight those who look upon it.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 70–73:**

﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what she is."﴾ [Is she a cow that has been pastured or one that has been worked?] ﴿Indeed, cattle have become confused to us.﴾ He did not say "tashabahat" (feminine) because the word "baqar" (cattle) is treated as masculine, as in His saying, ﴿palm trunks uprooted﴾ [al-Qamar 54:20]. Al-Zajjaj said: "That is, the species of cattle has become confused, meaning its matter has become ambiguous and unclear to us, so we are not guided to it." ﴿And we, if Allah wills, will surely be guided﴾ to its description. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah (in B: and by Allah), had they not made the exception (of the will of Allah), it would never have been made clear to them until the end of time."[[Al-Tabari: 2/205; Ibn Kathir: 1/199, where he said: "This is a strange hadith from this route, and at best it may be a statement of Abu Hurayra." Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 8: "Ibn Jarir narrated it through Ibn Jurayj as a marfu' report, and it is mu'dal (having two or more consecutive missing links)."]]

﴿He said: "Indeed, He says she is a cow neither broken to plough﴾ (dhalul), meaning tamed through work. It is said: "a man is dhalul" meaning clearly humbled, and "an animal is dhalul" meaning clearly tame. ﴿who plows the earth﴾ by turning it for cultivation, ﴿and does not irrigate the field﴾ — that is, she is not one that draws water. ﴿Sound, with no defect﴾ — free from faults. ﴿No color in her except one﴾ — she has no color other than the color of her whole skin. ʿAtaʾ said: "No blemish in her." It is said: "a man is dhalul" meaning clearly humbled, and "an animal is dhalul" meaning clearly tame. ﴿who plows the earth﴾ by turning it for cultivation, ﴿and does not irrigate the field﴾ — that is, she is not one that draws water. ﴿Sound, with no defect﴾ — free from faults. ﴿No color in her except one﴾ — she has no color other than the color of her whole skin. ʿAtaʾ said: "No blemish in her." Mujahid said: "No white and no black in her."

﴿They said: "Now you have brought the truth﴾ — that is, the complete and sufficient clarification that leaves no ambiguity. They searched for her, and they did not find her with the perfection of her description except with a young man, so they bought her for her hide filled with gold. ﴿So they slaughtered her, but they nearly did not do it﴾ because of the high price of her. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "They nearly did not find her with the combination of her attributes." It was also said: ﴿they nearly did not do it﴾ because of the extreme confusion and disagreement among them about her.

**His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:** ﴿And [recall] when you killed a soul﴾. This is the beginning of the story, although it comes later in the recitation. The name of the slain man is ʿAmmiyl [[Knowing his name has no proof behind it, its knowledge brings no benefit, and ignorance of it does no harm.]]. ﴿And you disputed over it﴾ — its origin is "tadara'tum," so the taʾ was assimilated into the dal and an alif was inserted, like His saying "ithaqqaltum" (you grew heavy). Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said: its meaning is "fa-ikhtalaftum" (you differed). Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "tadafaʿtum" (you pushed one another away), that is, each of you shifts the blame onto another, from al-dar' (repelling), which is pushing away; so each one pushed away from himself. ﴿And Allah will bring out﴾ — that is, will make manifest — ﴿what you were concealing,﴾ for the killer was concealing the killing.

﴿So We said: "Strike him with part of it"﴾ — meaning the slain man — "with part of it" — that is, with part of the cow. They differed about which part. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and most of the exegetes said: they struck him with the bone that is adjacent to the cartilage, which is the vital spot. Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: with the tailbone (ʿajb al-dhanab), because it is the first part created and the last part to decay, and the creation is assembled upon it. Al-Dahhak said: with its tongue. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this is because it is the instrument of speech. Al-Kalbi and ʿIkrima said: with its right thigh. It was also said: with a part of it, not specified. So they did that, and the slain man rose alive by Allah's permission, and his jugular veins — that is, the veins of the neck — were gushing blood, and he said, "So-and-so killed me," then he fell and died on the spot. Therefore his killer was deprived of inheritance. In a report: "No killer inherits after the companion of the cow."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 2/184; Ibn Kathir mentioned it: 1/194, edited by al-Wadiʿi.]] There is an implied omission in it, its estimate being: "so he was struck and he came to life." ﴿Thus Allah brings the dead to life﴾ as He brought ʿAmmiyl to life, ﴿and shows you His signs that you might reason.﴾ It was said: "that you might restrain yourselves from sins."

**As for the ruling on this matter in Islam:** If a slain person is found in a place and his killer is not known, then if there is a *lawth* (circumstantial indication, a presumptive sign) against a particular person — and *lawth* means that the truthfulness of the claimant becomes dominant in the heart, such as when a group of people gathered in a house or open field and then dispersed leaving a slain person, such that it becomes dominant in the heart that the killer is among them; or a slain person was found in a neighborhood or village whose inhabitants are all enemies of the slain man and no one else mixes with them, so it becomes dominant in the heart that they killed him — and the guardian (*wali*) makes a claim against some of them, the claimant swears fifty oaths (*qasama*) against the one he accuses. If the heirs are a group, the oaths are distributed among them. After they have sworn, they take the blood money (*diyah*) from the *ʿaqila* (the paternal kin who bear the obligation) of the accused if they claim it was an accidental killing; and if they claim it was intentional killing, then it is from his own wealth. There is no retaliation (*qawad*) according to the majority, but some scholars held that retaliation is obligatory; this is the view of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, and Malik and Ahmad also said so. If there is no *lawth* against the accused, then the statement of the accused is accepted with his oath. Then, does he swear one oath or fifty oaths? There are two opinions: first, one oath, as in all other claims; second, he swears fifty oaths, to emphasize the seriousness of the matter of blood. According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, there is no effect for *lawth*, and [the oath does not begin with the claimant's oath][[In B: "the oath does not begin with the oath of the claimant."]]. He said: if a slain person is found in a neighborhood, the ruler selects fifty men from its righteous people and makes them swear that they did not kill him and did not know of a killer; then he takes the blood money from its residents.

The evidence that the beginning is with the claimant's oath when *lawth* exists is:

[We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib: Abd al-ʿAziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabiʿ informed us: al-Shafiʿi informed us: ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn ʿAbd al-Majid al-Thaqafi informed us, from Yahya ibn Saʿid, from Bashir ibn Yasar] [[Missing from the original; it is in (B).]] from Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, that ʿAbdullah ibn Sahl and Muhayyisa ibn Masʿud went out to Khaybar, and they separated for their needs. ʿAbdullah ibn Sahl was killed. So he (Muhayyisa) and ʿAbd al-Rahman — the brother of the slain man — and Huwayyisa ibn Masʿud went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned to him the killing of ʿAbdullah ibn Sahl. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You shall swear fifty oaths, and you will be entitled to the blood of your companion or your killer." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we did not witness it and we were not present." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then the Jews shall clear themselves with fifty oaths." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we accept the oaths of a people who are disbelievers?" So the Prophet (ﷺ) paid the blood money himself from his own property.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari, in Jizya and Muwada'a, chapter: Truce and reconciliation with the polytheists with wealth and other things: 6/275. And Muslim, in Qasama, Muharibin, Qisas and Diyat, chapter: Qasama, no. (1669), 3/1291. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 10/211 onwards, without the addition "so the Prophet (ﷺ) paid his blood money from his own property."]] [In another wording: "He claimed that the Prophet (ﷺ) paid his blood money from his own property."][[Addition from (B).]] Bashir ibn Yasar said: Sahl said: "A she-camel of those camels struck me in a pen of ours," and in another narration: "A red she-camel of those camels kicked me in a pen of ours." Muslim narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from ʿAbd al-Wahhab.[[Muslim narrated it through other chains from Yahya ibn Saʿid, in Qasama and Muharibin, 3/1292.]]

**Aspect of the evidence from the report:** The Prophet (ﷺ) began with the oaths of the claimants in order to strengthen their side through the *lawth*, since ʿAbdullah ibn Sahl was found slain in Khaybar, the enmity was evident between the Ansar and the people of Khaybar, and it was dominant in the heart that they had killed him. An oath is always a proof for the party whose side is strengthened. When there is no *lawth*, the side of the accused is strengthened, since the original state is the freedom of his liability, and his statement is accepted with his oath.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verse 74:**

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Then your hearts hardened﴾: they became dry and parched. The dryness of the heart is the departure of mercy and softness from it. It is said: they became harsh. It is said: they became black. ﴿After that﴾: after the signs had become manifest. Al-Kalbi said: They said after that, "We did not kill him." They were never more blind of heart, nor more intense in denying their Prophet, than they were at that time. ﴿Then they are﴾, that is, in hardness and severity, ﴿like stones, or even harder in hardness﴾. It is said: "aw" here means "bal" (rather). It is also said: it means "wa" (and), as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿a hundred thousand or they increase﴾ (37:147, al-Saffat), that is, "rather they increase" or "and they increase."

He did not liken them to iron, even though iron is harder than stone, because iron is receptive to softening: it softens by fire, and it was softened for Dawud, peace be upon him. Stone never softens at all. Then He preferred stone over the hardened heart, saying: ﴿And indeed among stones are those from which rivers gush forth﴾. It is said: He meant by this all stones. It is said: He meant the stone which Musa struck for the tribes (al-Asbat). ﴿And indeed among them are those that split open, so water comes out from them﴾. He meant by this springs, not rivers. ﴿And indeed among them are those that fall down﴾, that is, descend from the top of the mountain to its base, ﴿out of fear of God﴾, while your hearts do not soften and do not humble themselves, O assembly of the Jews.

If it is said: a stone is inanimate and does not understand, so how can it fear (yakhsha)? It is said: God makes it understand and inspires it, so it fears by His inspiration.

The doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) is that God, Exalted is He, has a knowledge in inanimate objects and all other living beings apart from reason, which no one other than Him comprehends. So for them there is prayer, glorification, and fear, as the One whose remembrance is exalted said: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies Him with His praise﴾ (17:44, al-Isra'), and He said: ﴿Every one knows its prayer and its glorification﴾ (24:41, al-Nur), and He said: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon﴾ (22:18, al-Hajj), to the end of the verse. It is obligatory upon the believer to have faith in this and to entrust its knowledge to God, Glorified and Exalted is He.

It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ was on Thabir, and the disbelievers were pursuing him. The mountain said: "Get down from me, for I fear that you will be seized upon me, and God will punish me for that." Then Mount Hira said to him: "Come to me, O Messenger of God."

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: al-Sayyid Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-'Alawi related to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Naysaburi related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh related to us: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr related to us: Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samura, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed I know a stone in Mecca which used to greet me with peace before I was sent as a prophet, and indeed I know it now."¹ This is a sound hadith, related by Muslim from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from Yahya ibn Abi Bakr.

It is authentically related from Anas that the Messenger of God ﷺ looked over Uhud and said: "This is a mountain which loves us, and we love it."² It is also narrated from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer, then turned to the people with his face and said: "While a man was driving a cow, he became tired, so he mounted it and struck it. It said: 'We were not created for this; we were only created for plowing the earth.'" The people said: "Glory be to God! A cow speaks?!" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed, I believe in this, I and Abu Bakr and 'Umar," and they were not there. And he said: "While a man was with his sheep, a wolf attacked one of his sheep, and its owner pursued it and rescued it. The wolf said: 'Who will protect it on the day of the beast of prey?' That is, on the Day of Resurrection, the day when it will have no shepherd except me." The people said: "Glory be to God! A wolf speaks?!" He said: "I believe in this, I and Abu Bakr and 'Umar," and they were not there.³ It is also authentically related from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was on Hira, and with him were Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talha, and al-Zubayr, when the rock moved. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Be still (ihda'), that is, be calm. There is upon you only a prophet, or a truthful one (siddiq), or a martyr." This is sound; it is related by Muslim.⁴

Al-Imam Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Sa'id Yahya ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Sani' related to us: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Ishaq ibn Hisham al-Razi related to us: Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Duraysa al-Bajali al-Razi related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, from al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr, from al-Suddi, from 'Ubada ibn Abi Yazid, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ in Mecca. We went out into its outskirts, away from Mecca, among the mountains and trees. He did not pass by any tree or mountain without it saying: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God.'"⁵

Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: 'Abd al-Majid ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may God be pleased with him, say: "When the Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon, he would lean against the trunk of a palm tree from among the pillars of the mosque. When a pulpit was made for him and he sat upon it, that pillar shook and moaned like the moaning of a she-camel, until the people of the mosque heard it. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ came down, embraced it, and it became calm."⁶

Mujahid said: No stone descends from the top to the bottom except out of fear of God. What supports what we have said is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of God. And these are the parables which We strike for the people, that perhaps they will reflect﴾ (59:21, al-Hashr).

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And God is not unaware﴾ (heedless) ﴿of what you do﴾. It is a warning and a threat. It is also said: He will not abandon punishing what you do, but will recompense you for it. Ibn Kathir recited ya'malun (with the "ya") and the others recited ta'malun (with the "ta").

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 75–76:

His words, Exalted is He, ﴿Do you hope﴾: "Do you expect?" He means Muhammad and his Companions, ﴿that they will believe you﴾: that the Jews will believe you, in what you tell them, ﴿when a party of them used to hear the Speech of Allah﴾: meaning the Torah, ﴿then distort it﴾: they change its rulings, ﴿after they had understood it﴾: after they had known it, just as they changed the description of Muhammad ﷺ and the verse of stoning, ﴿while they know﴾ that they are liars. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah, al-Suddi and a group [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 63.]]. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning the seventy whom Musa chose for the appointed time of his Lord. When they returned to their people, after they had heard the Speech of Allah, the people returned to their words. As for the truthful among them, they conveyed what they had heard. But a group of them said: "We heard Allah say at the end of His speech: 'If you are able to do it, then do it, and if you wish, do not do it.'" This is their distortion, while they know that it is the truth [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 63.]].

﴿And when they meet those who believe﴾: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: this refers to the hypocritical Jews, who professed faith with their tongues, when they meet the sincere believers. ﴿They say: "We believe"﴾: like your belief. ﴿And when they are alone﴾: they return ﴿to one another﴾: Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Ka'b ibn Asad, Wahb ibn Yahuda and others of the Jewish leaders, to take counsel on this matter. ﴿They say: "Do you tell them what Allah has opened up to you?"﴾: what Allah has related to you in your Book, that Muhammad is true and that his word is truth. Al-Fattah (the judge) [the word al-Fattah, "the Opener," here means the judge].

Al-Kisa'i said: what Allah has made clear to you [of the knowledge of the description and attributes of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ], and he said: [al-Waqidi said:] what Allah has sent down upon you. Its parallel is: ﴿We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven﴾ (6:44), meaning, We sent down. Abu Ubaydah said: what Allah has bestowed upon you and given you. ﴿That they may argue with you by it﴾: that they may dispute with you, meaning the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, and argue using your words [upon you] [[Addition from (B).]], so that they say: "You have acknowledged that he is a true prophet in your Book, and then you do not follow him!" This is because they said to the people of Madinah, when they consulted them about following Muhammad ﷺ: "Believe in him, for he is true." Then some of them said to others: "Do you tell them what Allah has sent down to you, so that it becomes their proof against you ﴿before your Lord﴾," in this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: they informed the believers of what Allah had punished them for, namely their crimes. Some of them said to others: [Do you tell them what Allah has sent down to you of punishment, that they may argue with you by it before your Lord, so that they may see honour for themselves over you before Allah]. Mujahid said: this is the statement of the Jews of Qurayzah, when some of them said to others, when the Prophet ﷺ had said to them: "O brothers of the apes and the pigs!" They said: "Who told Muhammad this? It did not come out except from you" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 2/252, edition of Shaykh Shakir, and mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 1/207, edition of al-Wad'i.]]. ﴿Do you not then reason?﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 77–79:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal﴾ (yukhfuna) ﴿and what they reveal﴾ (yubdun), meaning the Jews.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾, i.e., among the Jews there are unlettered people (ummiyyun) who do not know how to read or write. Ummiyy (unlettered) is the plural form, derived from umm (mother), as if he remains in the state in which his mother bore him, having learned neither writing nor reading.

[It is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "We are an unlettered nation (ummiyya), meaning we do not write and we do not calculate."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in Fasting, chapter: the saying of the Prophet ﷺ "We do not write nor calculate," 4/136. And Muslim: in Fasting, chapter: the obligation of fasting Ramadan upon sighting the crescent, no. (1080), 2/761. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/228.]]] [[An addition from manuscript B, which contained some transposition of phrases that changed the meaning; we have corrected it.]] It has also been said: it is derived from Umm al-Qura, which is Makkah.

﴿They know not the Scripture except wishful thinking (amani)﴾. Abu Ja'far recited amani with the yā' lightened throughout the Qur'an, dropping one of the two yā's for lightness (takhfifan). [[In the two manuscripts: istikhfaf.]] The common reading is with the shaddah (tashdid). It is the plural of umniyya, which means recitation (tilawa). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Except when he recites (tamanna), Satan casts into his recitation (umniyyatihi)﴾ [al-Hajj: 52], meaning into his recitation. Abu Ubaydah said: they recite it from memory, not from a book. It has also been said: they know it by memorization and recitation, without understanding its meaning. Ibn Abbas said: meaning, they do not understand the meanings of the Book. Mujahid and Qatadah said: except lies and falsehood. Al-Farra' said: the amani are fabricated sayings. Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I have not made a wish (tamannaytu) since I embraced Islam" (i.e., I have not lied). [[An addition from (B).]] By this he meant the things their scholars wrote from their own selves and then attributed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such as altering the description of the Prophet ﷺ and other matters. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 80–83:**

﴿And they said﴾ — meaning the Jews — ﴿"The Fire will not touch us except for a few days"﴾ [lan tuṣībanā al-nār] [[Omitted in manuscript A.]] — a counted number of days, after which the punishment will leave us and bliss will follow it. The scholars differed concerning this verse. Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said: The Jews used to say, "This world is seven thousand years, and we will only be punished one day for every thousand years, then the punishment will end after seven days." Qatadah and ʿAtaʾ said: They meant forty days, the days in which their fathers worshipped the calf. Al-Hasan and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: The Jews said, "Indeed our Lord was angry with us regarding our affair, so He swore that He would punish us forty days, so the Fire will not touch us except for forty days, a fulfilment of the oath (taḥillat al-qasam)." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, rejecting them: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿"Have you taken a covenant with Allah"﴾ — the alif here is an interrogative alif that entered upon the alif of connection (alif al-waṣl) — ﴿a covenant﴾ confirmed that He will not punish you except for this period — ﴿then Allah will not break His covenant﴾ and His promise. Ibn Masʿud said: a covenant concerning monotheism (tawhid), as indicated by the words of the Exalted: ﴿Except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾ (19:87), meaning his saying "There is no god but Allah." ﴿Or do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Yes (balā)﴾. Bal and balā are two particles of correction (istidrak), and their meaning is the negation of a past statement and the affirmation of a future statement. ﴿Whoever earns an evil deed﴾ — meaning shirk — ﴿and his sin encompasses him﴾. The people of Madinah read khaṭīʾātuhu in the plural. Iḥāṭah (encompassment) is surrounding a thing from all its sides. Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ, al-Dahhak, Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Rabiʿ and a group said: It is shirk, dying upon it. It was also said: it is a great sin. Encompassment by it means that one persists in it and dies without repenting; this was said by ʿIkrimah and al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym. Mujahid said: These are sins that surround the heart; whenever one commits a sin, it rises until it covers (until it veils) the heart, and that is the rayn (rust). Al-Kalbi said: His sins have destroyed him. Its proof is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Unless you are encompassed (by misfortune)﴾ (12:66), meaning that you perish. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

The Exalted said: ﴿And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ in the Torah. The mithaq is a firm covenant. ﴿"Do not worship except Allah"﴾ — Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ya'budūna﴾ with yā' (third person), while the others read it with tā' (second person), in agreement with the Exalted's words: ﴿And speak to people good words﴾. Its meaning is "that you not worship," and when "an" (that) is omitted the verb becomes marfūʿ (nominative). Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read: "Do not worship except Allah," as a prohibition. ﴿And to parents, good treatment﴾ — meaning, and We enjoined upon them good treatment of parents, kindness toward them, tenderness toward them, and compliance with their command in matters that do not oppose the command of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿And to relatives﴾ — meaning and to kin; al-qurbā is a verbal noun like al-ḥusnā. ﴿And orphans﴾ — plural of yatīm, the child who has no father. ﴿And the needy﴾ — meaning the poor. ﴿And speak to people good words﴾ — truthfully and rightly concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ): whoever asks you about him, then tell him the truth, explain his description, and do not conceal his affair. This is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Command them with what is right and forbid them from what is wrong. It was also said: it is gentleness in speech and good conduct in companionship. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Yaʿqub read ḥasanan with a fatḥah on the ḥā' and sīn, meaning "a good word." ﴿And establish prayer and give zakat; then you turned away﴾ — you withdrew from the covenant and the pact — ﴿except a few of you﴾. That was because a group of them believed — ﴿and you are persistent in refusal﴾, like the aversion of your fathers.

Mujahid said: These are sins that surround the heart; whenever one commits a sin, it rises until it covers (until it veils) the heart, and that is the rayn (rust). The mithaq is a firm covenant. ﴿"Do not worship except Allah"﴾ — Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ya'budūna﴾ with yā' (third person), while the others read it with tā' (second person), in agreement with the Exalted's words: ﴿And speak to people good words﴾. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 84–86:**

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿And when We took your covenant: that you shall not shed your blood﴾, meaning: do not spill your blood, i.e., none of you shall shed the blood of another. It is also said: do not shed the blood of others, lest you shed your own blood, so that it is as if you had shed your own blood. ﴿Nor shall you expel yourselves from your homes﴾, meaning: none of you shall expel another from his home. It is also said: do not mistreat those who are your neighbors, lest you drive them to leave because of your bad neighborliness.

﴿Then you acknowledged﴾ this covenant as true and accepted it, ﴿and you were witnesses﴾ to it today, O assembly of the Jews, and you affirm your acceptance.

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿Yet here you are, killing yourselves﴾. ﴿Here you are﴾ means: O you (these people), and "hā' ulā'" is for alerting attention. ﴿Killing yourselves﴾, i.e., (one) of you kills another. ﴿And expelling a group of you from their homes, backing one another against them﴾. It is read with the shaddah on the zā' (ẓ), i.e., "tatẓāharūna" (you back one another), the tā' being assimilated into the ẓā' (idgham, assimilation of consonants). ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read it with a light zā', deleting the tā' of the reciprocal form (tafā'ul) and keeping the tā' of address, as in His words, "﴿And do not cooperate﴾" (5:2), both meaning: you cooperate (tata'āwanūna). Al-ẓahīr means the helper. ﴿In sin and aggression﴾, i.e., disobedience and injustice. ﴿And if they come to you as captives﴾. Ḥamzah reads "asrā" (captives), and both are the plural of "asīr" (captive), with the same meaning. ﴿You ransom them﴾ with wealth and rescue them. The people of Madina, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisā'ī and Yaʿqūb read "tufādūhum" (you exchange them), meaning: the ransoming of a captive by a captive (exchange). It is also said that the meaning of the two readings is one.

As for the meaning of the verse: al-Suddī said: Indeed God, Exalted is He, took a covenant from the Children of Israel in the Torah that none of them would kill another, nor expel another from his home. Whichever slave, male or female, you found from the Children of Israel, you were to buy him with what it cost and free him. Qurayẓa were allies of the Aws, and al-Naḍīr were allies of the Khazraj, and they used to fight one another in a war [called] Sumayr?. So the Banū Qurayẓa and their allies would fight, and the Banū al-Naḍīr and their allies. When they prevailed, they would ruin their homes and expel them from them. And if a man from either of the two parties was taken captive, they would gather to ransom him, even if the captive was from their enemy. So the Arabs would reproach them and say: How do you fight them and then ransom them? They said: We have been commanded to ransom them. They said: Then why do you fight them? They said: We are ashamed that our allies be humiliated. So God, Exalted is He, reproached them for that, saying: ﴿Yet here you are, killing yourselves﴾.

In the verse there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr), and its order is: ﴿And expelling a group of you from their homes, backing one another against them in sin and aggression﴾, ﴿while it is forbidden to you to expel them﴾, and ﴿if they come to you as captives, you ransom them﴾. So it is as if God, Exalted is He, took four covenants from them: to abstain from fighting, to abstain from expulsion, to abstain from backing their enemies against them, and to ransom their captives. They turned away from all of them except ransoming.

God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ Mujāhid said: It means: if you find him in the hand of another, you ransom him, while you yourselves kill him with your own hand. ﴿So what is the recompense of those among you who do that?﴾, O assembly of the Jews, ﴿but disgrace﴾, i.e., punishment and humiliation, ﴿in the life of this world﴾. So the disgrace of Qurayẓa was killing and captivity, and the disgrace of al-Naḍīr was exile and banishment from their dwellings to Adhraʿāt and Arīḥā in Syria. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment﴾, the punishment of the Fire. ﴿And God is not unaware of what you do﴾. Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ and (Abū Bakr) read it with the yā' (they), and the rest with the tā' (you).

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Those are the ones who bought﴾, i.e., exchanged ﴿the life of this world for the Hereafter. So the punishment will not be lightened﴾, i.e., made easier, ﴿for them, nor will they be helped﴾, i.e., they will not be protected from the punishment of God, Mighty and Majestic is He.
