Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 102–103 (part 1 of 2):

﴿When there came to them a Messenger from Allah﴾, meaning Muhammad, ﴿confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs﴾, meaning the Torah. It is also said: the Qur'an. ﴿As if they did not know.﴾ Al-Sha'bi said: They would recite the Torah but would not act upon it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: They wrapped it in silk and brocade, adorned it with gold and silver, and did not act upon it. That is their "throwing it away" of it. [[Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/163; al-Qurtubi 1/16; al-Qurtubi 2/41; al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/325.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they followed﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿what the devils recited﴾, i.e., what they recited. The Arabs place the future tense in the place of the past and the past in the place of the future. It is also said: "what you were reciting", i.e., reading. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "They followed it and acted upon it." 'Ata' said: "They spoke of it and discussed it." ﴿Over the kingdom of Sulayman﴾, i.e., during his rule and reign.

The story of the verse [[Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, cited a number of reports in explaining the verse, then said: "The story of Harut and Marut has been related from a group of the Successors (tabi'un): such as Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and others. Many exegetes, early and late, have recounted it, and its substance, in its details, traces back to the reports of the Children of Israel, for there is no sound, connected, marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith to the Truthful and Believed One, the infallible, who does not speak from desire. The apparent context of the Qur'an is a general outline of the story without elaboration or lengthy detail. So we believe in what has come in the Qur'an, in the sense Allah intended, and Allah knows best the reality of the matter." Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/249–250. Qadi 'Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said concerning Harut and Marut: "What the reporters and transmitters of exegesis have mentioned, and what has been related from 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas about their choice and their trial by love for a woman and their punishment for what they did, and what occurred of sorcery: know, may Allah honour you, that none of these reports has been transmitted, whether weak or sound, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it is not something that can be established by analogy. As for what is in the Qur'an about it, the exegetes have differed over its meaning, and many of the early generation rejected what some of them said. These reports come from Jewish books and their fabrications, as Allah indicated at the beginning of these verses, and their fabrication thereby against Sulayman and their declaring him a disbeliever. The story contains great abominations, and here we shall set forth what removes the veil from these difficulties, Allah willing." He then mentioned what refutes and nullifies the story in several respects. See al-Shifa bi-Ta'rif Huquq al-Mustafa by Qadi 'Iyad 2/853–859. Ibn 'Atiyya, after mentioning the reports about the story in his exegesis, said: "All of this is weak, and far-fetched from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both." See al-Muharrar al-Wajiz of Ibn 'Atiyya 1/420. See also what Shaykh Jamal al-Din al-Qasimi, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his exegesis; and Ibn al-'Arabi in Ahkam al-Qur'an 1/27–30; and al-Qurtubi in al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an 2/52. Although some reports appear in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad or elsewhere, they are weak reports, and they do not contradict the sound reports and the established principles concerning the infallibility of the angels, peace be upon them, even though Imam al-Tabari, al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi remained silent about them. See also Lubab al-Tafsir by Mahmud ibn Hamza al-Kirmani 1/369, edited by Dr. Nasir ibn Sulayman al-'Umar.]] is that the devils wrote down sorcery and magical charms [[This is a kind of sorcery in the sense of trickery, though not true sorcery; it is imitation and deception. (al-Qamus)]] in the name of Asaf ibn Barkhiya, [saying]: "This is what Asaf ibn Barkhiya taught King Sulayman." Then they buried it beneath his prayer mat, until Allah removed the kingdom from him, and Sulayman did not perceive this. When he died, they dug it up and said to the people: "Sulayman ruled them only by this, so learn it." As for the scholars of the Children of Israel and their righteous ones, they said: "God forbid that this should be from the knowledge of Allah." [[So it is in manuscript (a); in (b) it reads "Sulayman", as in the printed edition, and that is the correct reading.]] As for the base people, they said: "This is the knowledge of Sulayman," and they turned to learning it and abandoned the books of their prophets. Blame fell upon Sulayman, and this remained their condition and their deed until Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and sent down to him the exoneration of Sulayman. This is the saying of al-Kalbi.

Al-Suddi said: The devils used to ascend to the heaven and hear the speech of the angels about what would occur on earth, such as death and other things. They would come to the soothsayers and mix into what they had heard, seventy lies for every word, and inform them of it. [So this was written down] [[In (b): "So the people wrote that down."]], and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn know the unseen. So Sulayman sent for the people, gathered those books, placed them in a chest and buried it beneath his throne, and said: "I will not hear anyone say that the devil knows the unseen except that I will strike off his neck." When Sulayman died, and the scholars who knew the matter of Sulayman and the burial of the books had departed, a later generation succeeded them. The devil took the form of a man and came to a group of the Children of Israel and said: "Shall I show you a treasure that you will never eat away?" They said: "Yes." So he went with them and showed them the place beneath his throne. They dug, while he stood at a distance, and they said to him: "Come near." He said: "I will not come near. If you do not find it, then kill me." This was because none of the devils could approach the throne without being burned. They dug and brought out those books. The devil, may Allah curse him, said: "Sulayman used to control the jinn, the humans, the devils and the birds by this." Then the devil flew away from them, and it spread among the people that Sulayman had been a sorcerer. They took those books and used them. For this reason sorcery is found most among the Jews. When Muhammad ﷺ came, Allah cleared Sulayman of that, and sent down in exoneration of Sulayman: ﴿Sulayman did not disbelieve﴾ by means of sorcery. It is also said: Sulayman was not a disbeliever through sorcery, nor did he practise it. ﴿But the devils disbelieved﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Kisa'i and Hamza read "lakin" with a light nun, and "al-shayatin" in the nominative. The rest read "lakinna" with a heavy nun, and "al-shayatin" in the accusative, and likewise ﴿but Allah slew them﴾ (8:17). The meaning of "lakin" is negation of a past report and affirmation of what follows.

﴿They taught people﴾. It is said: The meaning of sorcery is knowledge and skill in a thing. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they said, "O sorcerer, call upon your Lord for us"﴾ (43:49), meaning the knowing one. The correct view is that sorcery is an expression for deception and imagination. The existence of sorcery in reality is affirmed by the People of the Sunna, and most nations hold this view. But practising it is kufr (disbelief). It is related from al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Sorcery causes imagination, causes illness, and may kill, so much so that he made retaliation (qisas) obligatory upon one who kills by it. It is from the work of the devil, which the sorcerer receives from him by his teaching. When he receives it from him, he uses it against others." It is also said that it affects the nature of things, so that it makes a human into the form of a donkey and makes a donkey into the form of a dog. The more correct view is that this is imagination. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿It is imagined to him, because of their sorcery, that they were moving﴾ (20:66). However, it does affect bodies with illnesses, death and madness. Speech has an influence on dispositions and souls: a person may hear what he dislikes and become heated and angry, and perhaps a fever comes upon him from it. Some people have died from words they heard. It is then like the afflictions and ailments that affect bodies. [[For the detailed treatment of this, see what Ibn Kathir expounded regarding the nature of sorcery and the ruling on practising and learning it, in al-Tafsir 1/252–261; and Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 1/50–72.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon﴾, i.e., and they taught what was sent down upon the two angels [i.e., by inspiration and knowledge; so "sending down" here means inspiration and teaching. It is also said: "and they followed what was sent down upon the two angels"] [[Addition from (b).]]. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan read "al-malikayn" with a kasra on the lam. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They were two men, sorcerers, who were in Babylon." Al-Hasan said: "Two 'ilj" [[al-'Ilj: a large man among the non-Arab unbelievers.]], because the angels do not teach sorcery. Babylon is the Babylon of Iraq. It was named Babil because of the confusion of tongues there (tabalbul al-alsina) when the palace of Nimrod fell, i.e., their dispersal. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Babil is the land of Kufa." It is also said: it is the mountain of Damawand. The well-known reading is "al-malakayn" with a fatha. If it is asked: how is it permissible for angels to teach sorcery? It is answered: there are two interpretations. The first: they did not intentionally teach it, but they described sorcery, mentioned its falsehood, and commanded people to avoid it. Teaching here means informing. The wretched one would abandon their advice and learn sorcery from their practice. The second interpretation, which is the more correct: Allah, may He be exalted, tested people through the two angels at that time. Whoever was wretched would learn sorcery from them [and take it from them and practise it], and thereby disbelieve; whoever was blessed would leave it and remain upon faith. The two teachers would increase in punishment because of the teaching. So there is a trial in this for the teacher [and the learner] [[Omitted in (b).]]. Allah may test His servants with whatever He wills, for command and judgment belong to Him.

His saying, may He be mighty and majestic: ﴿Harut and Marut﴾. They are two Syriac names, and they stand in the genitive position as an explanation of "the two angels," but they are given the accusative because of their foreignness and definiteness. The story of the two, according to what Ibn 'Abbas and the exegetes mentioned [[See the previous footnote (1) on page (127), and what the research scholars among the exegetes said in refuting these Israelite reports.]], is that the angels saw the evil deeds of the children of Adam ascending to heaven in the time of Idris, peace be upon him. So they reproached them and said: "These are the ones You made vicegerents on the earth and chose, yet they disobey You." Allah, may He be exalted, said: "If I were to send you down to earth and place in you what I placed in them, you would ride as they rode." They said: "Glory be to You, it was not fitting for us to disobey You." Allah, may He be exalted, said to them: "Choose two angels from among your best, and I will send them down to earth." They chose Harut and Marut, who were among the most righteous and most devout angels. Al-Kalbi said: Allah, may He be exalted, said to them: "Choose three." They chose 'Azza, who is Harut, and 'Azaya, who is Marut [their names were changed when they committed the sin] and 'Aza'il. So Allah placed desire in them and sent them down to earth, and commanded them to judge between people with truth, and forbade them from shirk, unjust killing, fornication and drinking wine. As for 'Aza'il, when desire fell into his heart, he turned to his Lord and asked Him to raise him up to heaven, and He returned him. So he prostrated for forty years without raising his head, and thereafter remained with his head bowed out of shame before Allah, may He be exalted.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 102–103 (part 2 of 2):

As for the other two, they remained steadfast in that and used to judge between people during the day. When evening came, they would mention the Greatest Name of God (ism Allah al-a'zam, the Greatest Name) and ascend to the sky. Qatada said: "Not a month had passed over them before they were seduced." They all said: "One day Zuhrah (Venus) came to them for judgment, and she was one of the most beautiful women." Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "She was from the people of Persia and was a queen in her land. When they saw her, she captivated their hearts, and they solicited her, but she refused and departed. Then she came back the next day, and they did the same, but she refused and said: 'No, unless you worship what I worship, pray to this idol, kill a soul, and drink wine.' They said: 'There is no way to these things, for Allah the Exalted has forbidden us from them.' So she departed, then came back on the third day, with a cup of wine, and there was in their hearts the inclination toward her that there was. They solicited her, but she presented to them what she had said the day before. They said: 'Prayer to other than Allah is a grave matter, and killing a soul is a grave matter, and the least of the three is drinking wine.' So they drank wine, became intoxicated, and had relations with the woman, and they committed fornication. When they had finished, a man saw them, so they killed him." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "They also prostrated to the idol, so Allah transformed Zuhrah into a star." Others said: "A woman of the most beautiful of people came to them, disputing with her husband. One of them said to the other: 'Has there fallen into your soul the same as what has fallen into mine (from love of this woman)?' [Omitted in manuscript B.] He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Would you like to judge in her favor against her husband according to what she says?' His companion said to him: 'Do you not know what is with Allah of punishment and torment?' His companion said to him: 'Do you not know what is with Allah of pardon and mercy?' So they asked her for herself. She said: 'No, unless you kill him.' One of them said: 'Do you not know what is with Allah of punishment and torment?' His companion said: 'Do you not know what is with Allah of pardon and mercy?' So they killed him. Then they asked her for herself again, and she said: 'No, for I have an idol that I worship. If you both pray with me to it, I will comply.' One of them said to his companion the same first statement, and his companion said the same. So they prayed with her to it, and she was transformed into a meteor (shihab)."

Ibn Abi Talib, al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: When they asked her for herself, she said to them: "You will not reach me until you tell me the means by which you ascend to the sky." They said: "By the Greatest Name of Allah." She said: "You will not reach me until you teach it to me." One of them said to his companion: "Teach it to her." He said: "I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds." The other said: "Then where is the mercy of Allah the Exalted?" So they taught her that, and she spoke it, ascended to the sky, and Allah transformed her into a star. Some of them held that she was Zuhrah herself, but others denied this and said: "Zuhrah is among the seven wandering stars by which Allah swore, when He said: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede, that run and hide﴾ (Qur'an 81:15-16)." And the one who tempted Harut and Marut was a woman called Zuhrah for her beauty. When she transgressed, Allah the Exalted transformed her into a meteor.

They said: When Harut and Marut had evening come after committing the sin, they intended to ascend to the sky, but their wings would not obey them. They realized what had befallen them (of the wrath), so they went to Idris the Prophet, peace be upon him. They informed him of their matter and asked him to intercede for them with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and said to him: "We have seen that there ascends for you of worship the same as what ascends for all the people of the earth, so intercede for us with your Lord." Idris, peace be upon him, did so, and Allah gave them the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. They chose the punishment of this world, knowing that it would come to an end. So they are in Babylon, being punished.

They differed about the manner of their punishment. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "They are suspended by their hair until the Hour arises." Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "Their heads are turned downward beneath their wings." Qatada said: "They are bound (kubbila) from their feet to the roots of their thighs." Mujahid said: "They were placed in a well filled with fire." Umar ibn Sa'd said: "They are upside down and are struck with whips of iron."

It is narrated that a man went to Harut and Marut to learn magic, and he found them suspended by their feet, their eyes blue, their skins blackened, and there was between their tongues and the water only four fingers' width, and they were being tormented with thirst. When the man saw that, the state of their place terrified him, so he said: "There is no god but Allah." When they heard his words, they said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "A man from among the people." They said: "From what community are you?" He said: "From the community of Muhammad (ﷺ)." They said: "Has Muhammad (ﷺ) been sent?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Praise be to Allah," and they showed joy. The man said: "Why is your joy?" They said: "He is the Prophet of the Hour, and the end of our punishment has drawn near."

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they do not teach anyone﴾, meaning anyone at all, and "min" is a redundant particle (silah), ﴿until they have advised him first and said: "We are only a trial"﴾, a test and an ordeal, ﴿so do not disbelieve﴾, meaning: do not learn magic and act upon it, lest you disbelieve. The root of fitnah (trial) is testing and examination, from the saying: "I smelted the gold and silver" when I melted them with fire, so that the good is distinguished from the bad. He used the singular "fitnah" though they are two, because fitnah is a masdar (verbal noun), and verbal nouns are neither dualized nor pluralized. It was also said: they would say "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve" seven times.

Ata' and al-Suddi said: If he refuses except to learn, they say to him: "Go to this ash and turn toward it," and a bright light will come out of it into the sky, and that is the light of knowledge. A black thing resembling smoke will descend until it enters his ears, and that is the wrath of Allah the Exalted. Mujahid said: No one reaches them, and between them a devil goes back and forth, once for each question.

﴿So they learn from them that by which they cause division between a man and his wife﴾, meaning that each one is taken away from his companion, and each is made hateful to his companion. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But they cannot harm anyone thereby﴾, it was said: meaning the sorcerers, and it was said: the devils, ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning by His knowledge and His decree. So the sorcerer performs sorcery, and Allah brings it into being.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Its meaning is except by His decree, His power and His will. ﴿And they learn that which harms them and does not benefit them﴾, meaning that magic harms them. ﴿And they certainly knew that whoever purchases it﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿has no share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning no portion in Paradise. ﴿And wretched is that for which they sold themselves﴾, they sold by it their own souls' portion, in that they chose magic and disbelief over the religion and the truth. ﴿If only they knew.﴾ If it is said: Did He not say: "And they certainly knew that whoever purchases it..."? So what is the meaning of His saying ﴿If only they knew﴾ after He informed that they knew? It is answered: By His saying "And they certainly knew" He meant the devils, and His saying ﴿If only they knew﴾ means the Jews. It was also said: both refer to the Jews, meaning: but since they did not act upon what they knew, it is as if they did not know.

﴿And if they had believed﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, ﴿and had feared Allah﴾, by avoiding Judaism and magic, ﴿the reward from Allah would have been better﴾, meaning the reward of Allah to them would have been better for them, ﴿if only they knew.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 102–103 (part 1 of 2):

﴿When there came to them a Messenger from Allah﴾, meaning Muhammad, ﴿confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs﴾, meaning the Torah. It is also said: the Qur'an. ﴿As if they did not know.﴾ Al-Sha'bi said: They would recite the Torah but would not act upon it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: They wrapped it in silk and brocade, adorned it with gold and silver, and did not act upon it. That is their "throwing it away" of it. [[Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/163; al-Qurtubi 1/16; al-Qurtubi 2/41; al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/325.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they followed﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿what the devils recited﴾, i.e., what they recited. The Arabs place the future tense in the place of the past and the past in the place of the future. It is also said: "what you were reciting", i.e., reading. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "They followed it and acted upon it." 'Ata' said: "They spoke of it and discussed it." ﴿Over the kingdom of Sulayman﴾, i.e., during his rule and reign.

The story of the verse [[Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, cited a number of reports in explaining the verse, then said: "The story of Harut and Marut has been related from a group of the Successors (tabi'un): such as Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and others. Many exegetes, early and late, have recounted it, and its substance, in its details, traces back to the reports of the Children of Israel, for there is no sound, connected, marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith to the Truthful and Believed One, the infallible, who does not speak from desire. The apparent context of the Qur'an is a general outline of the story without elaboration or lengthy detail. So we believe in what has come in the Qur'an, in the sense Allah intended, and Allah knows best the reality of the matter." Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/249–250. Qadi 'Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, said concerning Harut and Marut: "What the reporters and transmitters of exegesis have mentioned, and what has been related from 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas about their choice and their trial by love for a woman and their punishment for what they did, and what occurred of sorcery: know, may Allah honour you, that none of these reports has been transmitted, whether weak or sound, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it is not something that can be established by analogy. As for what is in the Qur'an about it, the exegetes have differed over its meaning, and many of the early generation rejected what some of them said. These reports come from Jewish books and their fabrications, as Allah indicated at the beginning of these verses, and their fabrication thereby against Sulayman and their declaring him a disbeliever. The story contains great abominations, and here we shall set forth what removes the veil from these difficulties, Allah willing." He then mentioned what refutes and nullifies the story in several respects. See al-Shifa bi-Ta'rif Huquq al-Mustafa by Qadi 'Iyad 2/853–859. Ibn 'Atiyya, after mentioning the reports about the story in his exegesis, said: "All of this is weak, and far-fetched from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both." See al-Muharrar al-Wajiz of Ibn 'Atiyya 1/420. See also what Shaykh Jamal al-Din al-Qasimi, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his exegesis; and Ibn al-'Arabi in Ahkam al-Qur'an 1/27–30; and al-Qurtubi in al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an 2/52. Although some reports appear in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad or elsewhere, they are weak reports, and they do not contradict the sound reports and the established principles concerning the infallibility of the angels, peace be upon them, even though Imam al-Tabari, al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi remained silent about them. See also Lubab al-Tafsir by Mahmud ibn Hamza al-Kirmani 1/369, edited by Dr. Nasir ibn Sulayman al-'Umar.]] is that the devils wrote down sorcery and magical charms [[This is a kind of sorcery in the sense of trickery, though not true sorcery; it is imitation and deception. (al-Qamus)]] in the name of Asaf ibn Barkhiya, [saying]: "This is what Asaf ibn Barkhiya taught King Sulayman." Then they buried it beneath his prayer mat, until Allah removed the kingdom from him, and Sulayman did not perceive this. When he died, they dug it up and said to the people: "Sulayman ruled them only by this, so learn it." As for the scholars of the Children of Israel and their righteous ones, they said: "God forbid that this should be from the knowledge of Allah." [[So it is in manuscript (a); in (b) it reads "Sulayman", as in the printed edition, and that is the correct reading.]] As for the base people, they said: "This is the knowledge of Sulayman," and they turned to learning it and abandoned the books of their prophets. Blame fell upon Sulayman, and this remained their condition and their deed until Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and sent down to him the exoneration of Sulayman. This is the saying of al-Kalbi.

Al-Suddi said: The devils used to ascend to the heaven and hear the speech of the angels about what would occur on earth, such as death and other things. They would come to the soothsayers and mix into what they had heard, seventy lies for every word, and inform them of it. [So this was written down] [[In (b): "So the people wrote that down."]], and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn know the unseen. So Sulayman sent for the people, gathered those books, placed them in a chest and buried it beneath his throne, and said: "I will not hear anyone say that the devil knows the unseen except that I will strike off his neck." When Sulayman died, and the scholars who knew the matter of Sulayman and the burial of the books had departed, a later generation succeeded them. The devil took the form of a man and came to a group of the Children of Israel and said: "Shall I show you a treasure that you will never eat away?" They said: "Yes." So he went with them and showed them the place beneath his throne. They dug, while he stood at a distance, and they said to him: "Come near." He said: "I will not come near. If you do not find it, then kill me." This was because none of the devils could approach the throne without being burned. They dug and brought out those books. The devil, may Allah curse him, said: "Sulayman used to control the jinn, the humans, the devils and the birds by this." Then the devil flew away from them, and it spread among the people that Sulayman had been a sorcerer. They took those books and used them. For this reason sorcery is found most among the Jews. When Muhammad ﷺ came, Allah cleared Sulayman of that, and sent down in exoneration of Sulayman: ﴿Sulayman did not disbelieve﴾ by means of sorcery. It is also said: Sulayman was not a disbeliever through sorcery, nor did he practise it. ﴿But the devils disbelieved﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Kisa'i and Hamza read "lakin" with a light nun, and "al-shayatin" in the nominative. The rest read "lakinna" with a heavy nun, and "al-shayatin" in the accusative, and likewise ﴿but Allah slew them﴾ (8:17). The meaning of "lakin" is negation of a past report and affirmation of what follows.

﴿They taught people﴾. It is said: The meaning of sorcery is knowledge and skill in a thing. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they said, "O sorcerer, call upon your Lord for us"﴾ (43:49), meaning the knowing one. The correct view is that sorcery is an expression for deception and imagination. The existence of sorcery in reality is affirmed by the People of the Sunna, and most nations hold this view. But practising it is kufr (disbelief). It is related from al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Sorcery causes imagination, causes illness, and may kill, so much so that he made retaliation (qisas) obligatory upon one who kills by it. It is from the work of the devil, which the sorcerer receives from him by his teaching. When he receives it from him, he uses it against others." It is also said that it affects the nature of things, so that it makes a human into the form of a donkey and makes a donkey into the form of a dog. The more correct view is that this is imagination. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿It is imagined to him, because of their sorcery, that they were moving﴾ (20:66). However, it does affect bodies with illnesses, death and madness. Speech has an influence on dispositions and souls: a person may hear what he dislikes and become heated and angry, and perhaps a fever comes upon him from it. Some people have died from words they heard. It is then like the afflictions and ailments that affect bodies. [[For the detailed treatment of this, see what Ibn Kathir expounded regarding the nature of sorcery and the ruling on practising and learning it, in al-Tafsir 1/252–261; and Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 1/50–72.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon﴾, i.e., and they taught what was sent down upon the two angels [i.e., by inspiration and knowledge; so "sending down" here means inspiration and teaching. It is also said: "and they followed what was sent down upon the two angels"] [[Addition from (b).]]. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan read "al-malikayn" with a kasra on the lam. Ibn 'Abbas said: "They were two men, sorcerers, who were in Babylon." Al-Hasan said: "Two 'ilj" [[al-'Ilj: a large man among the non-Arab unbelievers.]], because the angels do not teach sorcery. Babylon is the Babylon of Iraq. It was named Babil because of the confusion of tongues there (tabalbul al-alsina) when the palace of Nimrod fell, i.e., their dispersal. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Babil is the land of Kufa." It is also said: it is the mountain of Damawand. The well-known reading is "al-malakayn" with a fatha. If it is asked: how is it permissible for angels to teach sorcery? It is answered: there are two interpretations. The first: they did not intentionally teach it, but they described sorcery, mentioned its falsehood, and commanded people to avoid it. Teaching here means informing. The wretched one would abandon their advice and learn sorcery from their practice. The second interpretation, which is the more correct: Allah, may He be exalted, tested people through the two angels at that time. Whoever was wretched would learn sorcery from them [and take it from them and practise it], and thereby disbelieve; whoever was blessed would leave it and remain upon faith. The two teachers would increase in punishment because of the teaching. So there is a trial in this for the teacher [and the learner] [[Omitted in (b).]]. Allah may test His servants with whatever He wills, for command and judgment belong to Him.

﴿So they learn from them that by which they cause division between a man and his wife﴾, meaning that each one is taken away from his companion, and each is made hateful to his companion. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But they cannot harm anyone thereby﴾, it was said: meaning the sorcerers, and it was said: the devils, ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning by His knowledge and His decree. So the sorcerer performs sorcery, and Allah brings it into being.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Its meaning is except by His decree, His power and His will. ﴿And they learn that which harms them and does not benefit them﴾, meaning that magic harms them. ﴿And they certainly knew that whoever purchases it﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿has no share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning no portion in Paradise. ﴿And wretched is that for which they sold themselves﴾, they sold by it their own souls' portion, in that they chose magic and disbelief over the religion and the truth. ﴿If only they knew.﴾ If it is said: Did He not say: "And they certainly knew that whoever purchases it..."? Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 104–105:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not say, "Ra'ina"﴾. This was because the Muslims used to say, "Ra'ina, O Messenger of Allah," from al-murasha (ر ا ع ن ا, "to attend to"), meaning: "Give heed to us (arina sam'aka)," i.e., empty your hearing for our speech. It is said: "ar'a ila al-shay'," "ra'aahu," and "ra'aahu," meaning he inclined to it and listened to it. This expression, however, was an ugly one in the language of the Jews. It is also said that its meaning among them was: "Listen, may you not hear."

It is also said: it derives from ru'ūna (foolishness). When they wanted to make a person appear a fool, they would say to him, "Ra'ina," meaning, "O fool!" When the Jews heard this expression from the Muslims, they said among themselves: "We used to curse Muhammad in secret, so now openly do so." They would come to him and say, "Ra'ina, O Muhammad," and laugh among themselves. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (in the reports on the occasions of revelation: Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah) heard it and grasped its meaning, and he knew their language. He said to the Jews: "If I hear any of you say it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I will surely strike his neck." They said: "Do you not say it yourselves?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Do not say, "Ra'ina"﴾,

so that the Jews would find no way to revile the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (see: Tafsir al-Qurtubi 2/75; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 31). ﴿But say, "Unzurna"﴾, i.e., look at us. It is also said: wait for us and be patient with us. It is said: "nazartu fulanan" and "intaẓartuhu" (I looked at so-and-so and I waited for him). From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light﴾ (57:13). Mujahid said: its meaning is (fahhimnahu, "make us understand"). ﴿And listen﴾ to what you are commanded and obey. ﴿And for the disbelievers﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿is a painful punishment﴾.

This was because when the Muslims said to their allies among the Jews, "Believe in Muhammad (ﷺ)," they said: "This that you call us to is not better than what we are upon, and we would wish that it were good." Min here is an added particle (ṣilah). ﴿But Allah specifies for His mercy﴾, that is, His prophethood, ﴿whom He wills; and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾. Fadl (bounty) is the beginning of kindness without a cause.

It is also said: the mercy refers to Islam and guidance. It is also said: the meaning of the verse is that Allah, exalted is He, sent the prophets from the descendants of Isaac; when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent from the descendants of Ishmael, that did not happen with the love and desire of the Jews, and so the verse was revealed. As for the polytheists, it did not come about by their love because he came to refute them and to disparage their gods.

[Ibn Kathir attributed it to al-Tabarani with its chain from Salim from his father, and said: Sulayman ibn al-Arqam is weak. One night they stood to pray and recite it, but they could not recall a single letter of it. In the morning they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is among what was abrogated or forgotten, so disregard it." Al-Zuhri used to recite it as ﴿ma nasikh min ayatin aw nansaha﴾ with a light nun and a damma. Narrated by al-Tabarani, and in its chain is Sulayman ibn al-Arqam, who is abandoned (matruk) [al-Majma' 6/315]. Al-Wahidi also narrated the hadith of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl in al-Tafsir 1/172; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 32, Tafsir al-Qurtubi 2/63, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1/256.]

It was also said: Surat al-Ahzab was like Surat al-Baqarah, then most of it was lifted in both recitation and ruling. Then, among the abrogation of rulings is that a ruling is removed and something else is put in its place, just as the qiblah was abrogated from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah, the bequest to relatives was abrogated by inheritance, the waiting period of widowhood was abrogated from a year to four months and ten days, and the obligation of one to stand against ten in fighting was abrogated by standing against two. Abrogation applies only to commands and prohibitions, not to reports (akhbar).

As for the meaning of the verse, His words ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾ are read by the majority with a fatha on the nun and a kasra on the sin, from naskh, meaning: We remove it. Ibn 'Amir read it with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the sin, from al-insakh, and this has two possible meanings:

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿or cause it to be deferred (aw nansaha)﴾ with a fatha on the first nun and the sin, hamzated, meaning: We postpone it, so We do not replace it. It was also said: a ruler, the one who manages affairs ﴿nor a helper﴾, a supporter who prevents you from punishment.

It was also said: "Rather, do you wish to question your Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿as Moses was questioned before﴾." His people asked him: "Show us Allah plainly." It was also said: they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We will not believe you until you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group" [Allah the Exalted says: "And they say, 'We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to flow through it in force, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. One is that the text remains while the ruling is abrogated, like the verse of bequest to relatives, the verse of the waiting period of widowhood lasting a year, the verse of relief in fighting, the verse of al-Mumtahanah, and similar verses [see the detailed rulings on naskh and related matters in al-Risala by Imam al-Shafi'i, p. 137 onwards; al-Idah li-Nasikh al-Qur'an wa-Mansukhihi; Lubab al-Tafsir 1/382-386; and most books of usul al-fiqh].

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said regarding His words ﴿Whatever verse﴾: "We confirm its writing and change its ruling." Among these forms is that its recitation is lifted while its ruling remains, like the verse of stoning. Another form is that its recitation is lifted entirely from the mushaf and from hearts. This is what was narrated from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf: that some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, stood one night to recite a sura, but they could not recall any of it except "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." They went in the morning to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is a sura whose recitation and rulings were lifted."

[Ibn Kathir attributed it to al-Tabarani with its chain from Salim from his father, and said: Sulayman ibn al-Arqam is weak. He said: Abu Bakr al-Anbari also narrated something similar from Abu Umamah, raised to the Prophet: Tafsir 1/151, Beirut edition. In the hadith of Abu Umamah is 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Laith, who is weak. And from Umar, who said: Two men from the Ansar recited a sura that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had taught them, and they used to recite it. One night they stood to pray and recite it, but they could not recall a single letter of it. In the morning they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is among what was abrogated or forgotten, so disregard it." Al-Zuhri used to recite it as ﴿ma nasikh min ayatin aw nansaha﴾ with a light nun and a damma. Narrated by al-Tabarani, and in its chain is Sulayman ibn al-Arqam, who is abandoned (matruk) [al-Majma' 6/315]. Al-Wahidi also narrated the hadith of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl in al-Tafsir 1/172; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 32, Tafsir al-Qurtubi 2/63, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1/256.]

It was also said: Surat al-Ahzab was like Surat al-Baqarah, then most of it was lifted in both recitation and ruling. Then, among the abrogation of rulings is that a ruling is removed and something else is put in its place, just as the qiblah was abrogated from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah, the bequest to relatives was abrogated by inheritance, the waiting period of widowhood was abrogated from a year to four months and ten days, and the obligation of one to stand against ten in fighting was abrogated by standing against two. Among them is what is removed without anything else being put in its place, like the examination of women.

Abrogation applies only to commands and prohibitions, not to reports (akhbar).

As for the meaning of the verse, His words ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾ are read by the majority with a fatha on the nun and a kasra on the sin, from naskh, meaning: We remove it. Ibn 'Amir read it with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the sin, from al-insakh, and this has two possible meanings:

One is that We make it like the abrogated.

The other is that We make it a copy of it [it is said: "I copied the book" (nasakhtu al-kitab), meaning I wrote it, and "I had it copied by another" (ansakhtuhu ghayri) when I made it a copy for him] [addition in B] ﴿or cause to be forgotten﴾, meaning: cause it to be forgotten upon your heart.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "We leave it, we do not abrogate it." Allah, may He be exalted, says ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ (9:67), meaning they abandoned Him, so He abandoned them. It was also said: ﴿cause to be forgotten﴾ means: We command its abandonment. It is said: "I caused the thing to be forgotten" when I commanded its abandonment. So the first abrogation involves lifting a ruling and putting something else in its place, while causing to be forgotten is abrogation without putting anything else in its place.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿or cause it to be deferred (aw nansaha)﴾ with a fatha on the first nun and the sin, hamzated, meaning: We postpone it, so We do not replace it. It is said: "Allah postponed (nasa'a) his term" and "Allah deferred (ansa'a) his term." Regarding its meaning there are two views. One is: We lift its recitation and postpone its ruling, as was done with the verse of stoning. In this case, the first abrogation means the lifting of both recitation and ruling. The second view is that of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ata': as for what is abrogated from a verse, it is what has already been revealed of the Qur'an, and they took it as from naskha (copying), or ﴿nansaha﴾ means: We postpone it and leave it in the Preserved Tablet, and it is not sent down.

﴿We bring a better one than it﴾, meaning: something more beneficial for you, easier for you, and greater in reward for you. It does not mean that one verse is better than another, because the speech of Allah is one, and all of it is good. ﴿Or its like﴾ in benefit and reward. So whatever is abrogated to something easier is easier in practice, and whatever is abrogated to something harder is greater in reward. ﴿Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?﴾ regarding abrogation and substitution. Its wording is a question, but its meaning is affirmation, that is: you know this.

﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have, O disbelievers, when the punishment descends, ﴾ apart from Allah ﴿﴾ of anything other than Allah ﴿a protector﴾ a close relative or friend. It was also said: a ruler, the one who manages affairs ﴿nor a helper﴾, a supporter who prevents you from punishment.

His words: ﴿Or do you wish to question your Messenger﴾. It was revealed concerning the Jews when they said: "O Muhammad, bring us a book from the heaven all at once, as Moses brought the Torah." So He, may He be exalted, said ﴿Or do you wish﴾, meaning: "Do you wish?" The mim here is a connective particle. It was also said: "Rather, do you wish to question your Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿as Moses was questioned before﴾." His people asked him: "Show us Allah plainly." It was also said: they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We will not believe you until you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group" [Allah the Exalted says: "And they say, 'We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to flow through it in force, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read.' Say, 'Exalted is my Lord! Was I but a human messenger?'" Surat al-Isra' 17:90-93. See also Lubab al-Tafsir by Mahmud ibn Hamzah 1/390-391.] just as Moses' people asked him, saying: "Show us Allah plainly." In this is their prohibition from shameful questions after the proofs and evidences have become manifest. ﴿And whoever exchanges disbelief for faith﴾ takes disbelief in exchange for faith ﴿has strayed from the sound way﴾, erred from the middle of the path. It was also said: ﴿he has strayed from the sound way﴾ means he aimed at the way.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 109:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish﴾ The verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews who said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and Ammar ibn Yasir after the Battle of Uhud: "If you were upon the truth, you would not have been defeated. So return to our religion, for we are better guided in the way than you." Ammar said to them: "How would the breaking of the covenant be against you?" They said: "It is severe." He said: "Then I have covenanted that I will not disbelieve in Muhammad (ﷺ) as long as I live." The Jews said: "As for this one, he has indeed turned away (ṣabaʾa)." Hudhayfah said: "As for me, I am content with Allah as Lord, with Muhammad as Prophet, with Islam as religion, with the Qur'an as leader, with the Ka'bah as qiblah, and with the believers as brothers." Then the two of them came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of that. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have both attained the good and succeeded." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish﴾ [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "I have not found it with a chain of narration (musnad). It is in the Tafsir of al-Tha'labi likewise, without any chain or narrator." See al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 10. Al-Wahidi also mentioned it briefly in his Tafsir, from Ibn Abbas: 1/174.]] That is, they desire and wish. ﴿Many of the People of the Book﴾, namely the Jews, ﴿would that they could turn you back﴾, O assembly of believers, ﴿after your faith into disbelievers, out of envy﴾. The word ḥasadan (envy) is in the accusative (naṣb) as a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning: they envy you with envy. ﴿from themselves﴾, that is, from their own selves, and Allah did not command them to do so. ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾ in the Torah, that the saying of Muhammad (ﷺ) is true and his religion is the truth. ﴿So pardon﴾, that is, leave them alone, ﴿and overlook﴾, and pass over. Al-ʿAfw is erasure (al-maḥw), and al-ṣafḥ is turning away (al-iʿrāḍ). This was before the verse of fighting. ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾, that is, His punishment: killing and taking captive of the Banu Qurayzah, and expulsion and exile of the Banu al-Nadir [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit, 1/348.]]. This was said by Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. Qatadah said: it is His command to fight them, in His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day ... and they are humbled﴾ (9:29). Ibn Kaysan said: by His knowledge and His judgment concerning them; He ruled for some of them to embrace Islam, and for some to be killed, taken captive, or pay the jizyah. ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾.

Wa-aqīmū al-ṣalāh wa-ātū al-zakāh, wa-mā tuqaddimū (tuslifū) li-anfusikum min khayr (ṭā'ah wa-'amal ṣāliḥ) tajidūhu 'inda Allāh.

And establish prayer and give zakah, and whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah.

[The words "(tuslifū)" and "(ṭā'ah wa-'amal ṣāliḥ)" are glosses in the commentary text, and the bracketed gloss is shown as it appears in the source.]

It was said: by "good" He meant wealth, as in His saying, ﴿If he leaves behind wealth (khayr)﴾ [2:180], and He meant zakah or ṣadaqah. ﴿You will find it with Allah﴾, even a date (al-thamrah) and a morsel (al-luqmah) the size of Uhud. ﴿Indeed Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 111–113:

﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians.﴾ That is, Hud means Jews (yahud). Al-Farra' said: "He dropped the extra ya' and returned to the verb from al-Yahudiyyah (Judaism)." Al-Akhfash said: "Hud is the plural of ha'id, like a'id and ud, and ha'il and hul." [[Al-ha'il: a she-camel that has been mounted by a stallion but has not conceived.]] ﴿or Christians﴾. This is because the Jews said: "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew, and there is no religion but the religion of Judaism," and the Christians said: "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Christian, and there is no religion but the religion of Christianity."

It was also said: it was revealed concerning the delegation of Najran, who were Christians, who gathered in the assembly of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ together with the Jews, and some of them denied the others. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿These are their wishful beliefs.﴾ That is, their false desires, which they wished upon Allah without right. ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿"Produce your proof"﴾ — its origin is "ātū" — ﴿your evidence﴾ for what you claim, ﴿if you are truthful.﴾ Then He said, refuting them:

﴿Rather, whoever submits his face to Allah﴾ That is, the matter is not as they said; rather, the ruling belongs to Islam, and only one who submits his face enters Paradise. ﴿to Allah﴾ That is, he sincerely devotes his religion to Allah. It was also said: he sincerely devotes his worship to Allah. It was also said: he humbles himself and submits to Allah. The origin of Islam is surrender and submission. He specified the face because when one gives his face in prostration, he will not withhold the rest of his limbs. ﴿and he is a doer of good﴾ in his deed. It was also said: a believer. It was also said: sincere. ﴿For him is his reward with his Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾

His saying: ﴿And the Jews say: The Christians are not on anything;﴾ it was revealed concerning the Jews of Madinah and the Christians of Najran. [[Al-Tabari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When the Christians of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the rabbis of the Jews came to them, and they disputed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Rafi' ibn Harmalah said: "You are not upon anything!" and he disbelieved in 'Isa ibn Maryam and the Injil. A man from the Christians of Najran said: "You are not upon anything!" and he denied the prophethood of Musa and disbelieved in the Torah. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed concerning that, from their two statements: "The Jews say the Christians are not upon anything, and the Christians say the Jews are not upon anything" up to His saying "concerning that in which they used to differ." Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/513-514; see also Tafsir al-Wahidi: 1/176, Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 33, Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/273, where it says: Rafi' ibn Harmalah.]] That is because when the delegation of Najran came to the Prophet ﷺ, the rabbis of the Jews came to them, and they debated until their voices rose. The Jews said to them: "You are not upon anything of the religion," and they disbelieved in 'Isa and the Injil. The Christians said to them: "You are not upon anything of the religion," and they disbelieved in Musa and the Torah. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And the Christians say: The Jews are not upon anything, while they recite the Book.﴾ [Both groups read the Book. It was said: its meaning is that this disagreement is not in their books, so their recitation of the Book and their opposition to what is in it indicate that they are upon falsehood.] [[Addition from (b).]] ﴿Thus say those who have no knowledge﴾ — meaning their forefathers who passed away — ﴿the like of their statement.﴾ Mujahid said: it means the common Christians. Muqatil said: it means the polytheists of the Arabs, who said the same about their Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions: that they are not upon anything of the religion.

'Ata' said: they are nations that existed before the Jews and Christians, such as the people of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them, who said to their prophets: "He is not upon anything." [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 2/517; Ibn Kathir 1/273; al-Wahidi 1/176. Al-Tabari chose that the verse is general and suitable for all of them, and there is no decisive proof specifying one of these sayings, so applying it to all is preferable.]] ﴿So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ He will decide between the truthful and the falsifier ﴿concerning that in which they used to differ﴾ — the religion.

He said, ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them﴾, and the rest of the verse. It was revealed concerning Taytus ibn Isbisyanus al-Rumi (Titus) and his companions. They attacked the Children of Israel, killed their fighting men, took their offspring captive, burned the Torah, destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), threw carrion into it, and slaughtered pigs in it. It remained in ruins until the Muslims rebuilt it in the days of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: It was Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his companions who attacked the Jews and destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Christians aided them in that, Taytus al-Rumi and his companions from among the people of Rome. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/264-265, Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/274, and al-Tabari: 2/520-521.]] Al-Suddi said: It was because they killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya. Qatadah said: Some of the Jews induced them to assist Bukhtnassar al-Babili (the Magian). [[Addition from manuscript B.]] So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿And who is more unjust﴾, meaning, more disbelieving and more insolent, ﴿than one who prevents the mosques of Allah﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis and those who fight against it. [[Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that the Quraysh prevented the Prophet ﷺ from praying near the Ka'bah in the Masjid al-Haram, and so Allah revealed: "And who is more unjust..." See: Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyuti: p. 438, in the margin of al-Jalalayn, and Ibn Kathir preferred this view. Ibn Jarir also narrated from Abu Zayd, who said: These were the polytheists, when they prevented the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah from entering Mecca. He said: The most preferred interpretation is the view of the one who said that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, meant by "And who is more unjust..." the Christians. See: Tafsir al-Tabari 2/521.]]

﴿from having His name mentioned in them and striving﴾ to ruin them ﴿for their destruction. Those would not have entered them except in fear﴾. That is because Bayt al-Maqdis is the place of pilgrimage and visitation for the Christians. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: No Roman entered Bayt al-Maqdis after it was rebuilt, meaning, except in fear, for if he were known he would be killed. Qatadah and Muqatil said: No Christian enters Bayt al-Maqdis except in disguise, and if he were caught he would be punished. Al-Suddi said: They were made to fear through the jizyah (the poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects). It was also said: This is a report with the meaning of a command, that is, subdue them through jihad so that none of them enters it except in fear of being killed or taken captive. That is, it is not befitting for them. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾, meaning punishment and humiliation. Qatadah said: It is killing for the enemy combatant (harbi) and the jizyah for the protected dhimmi (dhimmi, a non-Muslim under Muslim protection). Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: Their three cities will be conquered: Qustantiniyya (Constantinople), Rumiyya, and Amuriyya. [[Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad: 2/176, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who was asked: Which of the two cities will be conquered first, Qustantiniyya or Rumiyya? He called for a chest of his with rings, and said: He took out a book from it. Abdullah said: While we were around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ writing, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: Which of the two cities will be conquered first, Qustantiniyya or Rumiyya? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The city of Heraclius will be conquered first," meaning Qustantiniyya. Al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 4/508, 555, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/219: Ahmad narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the authentic collections except Abu Qabil, who is trustworthy. Rumiyya, with the letter ya lightly pronounced and dotted from below, is the capital and seat of learning of the Romans. It is one of the wonders of the world in its construction, vastness, and large population. Strange accounts have been related about it which reason rejects and finds unlikely. See: Maraṣid al-Ittila' by al-Baghdadi: 2/642. Amuriyya, with the first letter vowelled with a fatha and the second letter doubled, is a town in the land of the Romans, which al-Mu'tasim attacked and conquered. It was among the greatest conquests of Islam. See: Maraṣid al-Ittila': 2/963. Qustantiniyya, also called Qustantina with the nisba ya dropped, was formerly called Byzantium. Constantine the Great settled there, built a wall around it, and it became the seat of the Roman kingdom and their capital. See: Maraṣid al-Ittila': 3/1092. Allah the Exalted decreed its conquest for the Muslims at the hands of the Ottoman Sultan Muhammad al-Fatih, who was given that title for his conquest of Qustantiniyya, in the year 857 AH (1453 CE).]] ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾, which is the Fire. Ata and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Mecca, and by "the mosques" he meant the Masjid al-Haram. They prevented the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions from performing the pilgrimage to it and from praying in it in the year of Hudaybiyyah. When they were prevented from building it up with remembrance, they strove to ruin it. ﴿Those would not have entered them except in fear﴾, meaning the people of Mecca. It is as if Allah says: I will open it for you until you enter it and become more entitled to it than they are. So He opened it for them, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded a caller to proclaim: "Let no polytheist perform the pilgrimage after this year." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Salah, chapter: What is covered of the awrah, 1/477, and in Hajj, Maghazi, Jihad, and Tafsir. Also by Muslim in Hajj, chapter: No polytheist shall perform pilgrimage to the House, nor circumambulate it naked, no. 1347, 2/982. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/121.]] This was their fear. It is established in the Shari'ah that a polytheist is not to be allowed to enter the Haram. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾, meaning abasement, humiliation, killing, captivity, and exile.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 115–116:**

God Most High said: ﴿To God belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of God﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: A group of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out on a journey before the qibla was changed to the Ka'bah. A fog came upon them, the time for prayer arrived, and they sought the direction of the qibla (*tahharri*, striving to determine the qibla by reasoning) and prayed. When the fog cleared, it became clear to them that they had not hit the direction and had erred in their *tahharri*. When they returned, they asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about that, and this verse was revealed. [[Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh through the chain of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, with a similar meaning. See: Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyuti, in the margin of al-Jalalayn, p. (45). Ibn Kathir said, after citing a number of reports in his tafsir (1/279): "These chains contain weakness, but perhaps some of them strengthen others." See also: Nasb al-Raya by al-Zayla'i: 1/305.]]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, said: It was revealed concerning the traveller who performs voluntary prayer wherever his mount turns.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih al-Sarakhsi informed us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to pray on his mount while travelling, wherever it turned." [[Narrated by Malik in the Muwatta', chapter: Voluntary prayer while travelling, no. (28). Al-Bukhari: in Prayer, chapter: Facing the qibla wherever one is, 1/503, from Jabir. Muslim: in the Prayer of the Traveller, chapter: Permissibility of voluntary prayer on a beast, no. (700), 1/487, from Ibn 'Umar. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/188, from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar. See also: Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/530.]]

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning the changing of the qibla. Abu al-'Aliyah said: When the qibla was turned to the Ka'bah, the Jews reproached the believers and said: "They have no fixed qibla; sometimes they face this way and sometimes that way." So God Most High revealed this verse. [[See Tafsir al-Wahidi: 1/177.]] Mujahid and al-Hasan said: When God's words were revealed, ﴿Your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will answer you﴾ (40:60), they said: "Where should we call upon Him?" So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿To God belong the east and the west﴾, in dominion and creation, ﴿wherever you turn, there is the Face of God﴾, meaning: wherever you turn your faces, there is *thamma*, that is, there (*hunak*), ﴿the mercy of God﴾. [[The phrase "wajh Allah" (Face of God) appears in manuscript B, and it is the more accurate reading, because it contains no ta'wil (figurative interpretation). This is the methodology of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah regarding God's names and attributes. Al-Baghawi, may God have mercy on him, followed the method of not interpreting figuratively. It appears that this is from the copyist, since he wrote "the Face" in his copy (B). And God knows best.]] Al-Kalbi said: *Thamma* is God: He knows and sees. The word "Face" (*wajh*) is a connecting element (*silah*), like His saying: ﴿Everything perishes except His Face﴾ (28:88), meaning: except Him. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: *Thamma* is the qibla of God. *Al-wajh*, *al-wujhah* and *al-jihah* mean the qibla. It is also said: it means the good pleasure of God Most High.

﴿Indeed God is All-Encompassing﴾, meaning: rich, who gives out of abundance. Al-Farra' said: *al-Wasi'* is the generous one whose giving embraces everything. Al-Kalbi said: All-Encompassing in forgiveness. ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their intentions, wherever they pray and call upon Him.

God Most High said: ﴿And they say: God has taken a son﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited "qalu ittakhadha Allah" without the waw, and the others recited it with the waw [[the words "wa qalu ittakhadha Allah wa lada" are omitted from manuscript A]]. It was revealed concerning the Jews of Madinah, who said: "'Uzayr is the son of God"; concerning the Christians of Najran, who said: "The Messiah is the son of God"; and concerning the polytheist Arabs, who said: the angels are the daughters of God. [[See: al-Wasit by al-Wahidi, 1/178, 179.]] ﴿Glory be to Him﴾: He declared Himself free of imperfection and magnified Himself.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Na'imi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hasan Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "God Most High said: The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so; and he reviled Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, he claims that I cannot bring him back as he was. As for his reviling Me, he says: 'God has a son.' Glory be to Me; I am too exalted to take a spouse or a son." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, in Tafsir, chapter: "And they say: God has taken a son," 8/168, and in the Beginning of Creation. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/81, through the chain of Hammam ibn Munabbih from Abu Hurayrah, similar in meaning. See also: Ibn Kathir: 1/282.]]

God Most High said: ﴿Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, as servants and as dominion. ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ (*qanitun*). Mujahid, 'Ata' and al-Suddi said: obedient. Ikrimah and Muqatil said: acknowledging His lordship in servitude. Ibn Kaysan said: standing firm in witness. The root meaning of *qunut* is standing. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best prayer is the one with the long *qunut*." [[Narrated by Muslim, in the Prayer of Travellers, chapter: The best prayer is the one with long qunut, nos. (756, 757), 1/520.]]

The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse. A group held that its ruling is specific. Muqatil said: it refers to 'Uzayr, the Messiah and the angels. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: it refers to those who obey Him, excluding the rest of mankind. Another group held that the ruling of the verse is general, encompassing all creation, because "all" (*kull*) requires comprehensiveness with respect to a thing, so that nothing is excluded from it. [[The Imam al-Tabari said in his tafsir: "Some whose knowledge fell short of grasping the meaning of speech have claimed that His words, 'all are devoutly obedient to Him,' refer only to the people of obedience and are not general. It is not permissible to claim a particular sense for a verse whose apparent meaning is general, except with a proof that must be accepted, as we have shown in our book 'The Book of Clarification of the Foundations of Rulings.' This is a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, that the Messiah, whom the Christians claimed to be the son of God, refutes them—he and the heavens and the earth and what is in them—either by speech or by indication. God, may His praise be exalted, informed about all of them, of their obedience to Him and their acknowledgment of servitude to Him, immediately after His words, 'and they say: God has taken a son.' This indicates the soundness of what we have said." Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/539–540.]] Then they took two approaches regarding the disbelievers. Mujahid said: their shadows prostrate to God against their will. God Most High said: ﴿And their shadows at morning and evening﴾ (13:15). Al-Suddi said: this is on the Day of Resurrection; its evidence is ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾ (20:111). It is also said: ﴿qanitun﴾ means subjugated and made to serve for what they were created for. [[Addition from manuscript B.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 117–119:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: its Innovator (mubdi'uha) and Creator (munshi'uha) without any prior pattern. ﴿And when He decrees a matter﴾, meaning: He determines it. It is said: He judges it, determines it, and perfects it [and the root of qada' (decree) is "completion" (al-faragh); from it comes the saying about one who has died: "qudiya 'alayhi" (his end has been decreed), because he has completed (faraga) the world; and from it comes "qada' Allah wa qadaruhu" (the decree and predestination of Allah)] [[Addition from manuscript B.]], because He has completed it in measure and arrangement.

﴿Then He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited "kun fa-yakuna" with a fathah on the nun in all places except in Al 'Imran, "kun fa-yakuna, al-haqqu min rabbika" and in Surat al-An'am, "kun fa-yakuna, qawluhu al-haqq." He gave it the fathah because the response to a command introduced by the fa' (fa-) is put in the subjunctive (mansub). [Al-Kisa'i agreed with him in al-Nahl and Ya-Sin [[Addition from manuscript B.]].] The others recited it with the damma (raf'), on the meaning of "fa-huwa yakunu" (so it is, and it comes to be). If it is asked: how can He say "Then He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is," when the non-existent is not addressed? Ibn al-Anbari said: its meaning is "fa-innama yaqulu lahu," that is, for the sake of its bringing into being, and so the sense of address is removed. It is also said: although it is non-existent, since its existence has been decreed and it will certainly come to be, it is as though it were existent, so the address is valid.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who have no knowledge say﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: they are the Jews. Mujahid said: the Christians. Qatadah said: the polytheists of the Arabs. ﴿Why does not Allah speak to us﴾ (lawla), meaning: why not (halla), ﴿directly﴾, [informing us] that you are His Messenger? Every "lawla" in the Qur'an has the meaning of "halla" except one, which is His saying: ﴿Had he not been of those who glorify [Allah]﴾ (37:143), meaning: "fa-law lam yakun" (had he not been). ﴿Or a sign comes to us﴾, a proof and evidence of the truth of your claim to prophethood.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus said those before them﴾, meaning: the disbelievers of the earlier nations, ﴿the like of their words. Their hearts are alike﴾, meaning: some of them resembled others in disbelief, hardness, and seeking the impossible. ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain.﴾

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾, meaning: with the sincere (bi-al-sidq), like His saying: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?"﴾ (10:53), meaning: is it sincere? Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: with the Qur'an as its evidence, as in ﴿But they denied the truth when it came to them﴾ (50:5). Ibn Kaysan said: with Islam and its laws, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾ (17:81). Muqatil said: its meaning is that We did not send you in vain; rather, We sent you with the truth, just as He said: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ (15:85).

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿as a bringer of good news﴾, meaning: giving good tidings to My allies and the people of My obedience of the noble reward; ﴿and a warner﴾, meaning: warning and frightening My enemies and the people of My disobedience of the painful punishment. Nafi' and Ya'qub recited ﴿And you will not be asked﴾ as a prohibition (nahy). 'Ata' reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: this is because the Prophet ﷺ said one day: "Would that I knew what became of my parents," and then this verse was revealed. [[Reported by Ibn Kathir from 'Abd al-Razzaq with his chain from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and he said: Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb from Waki' from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, and they have spoken about it. Ibn Kathir: 1/285, Dar al-Arqam. Ibn Hajar said in al-Taqrib: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi is weak. Shaykh Ahmad Shakir commented on the two narrations of al-Tabari: "These are two mursal reports, for Muhammad ibn Ka'b ibn Sulaym al-Qurazi is a Successor (tabi'i), and a mursal report does not establish proof. Moreover, they are both weak chains because of the weakness of their narrators: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi is very weak..." (see Tafsir al-Tabari 2/558–559 with Shakir's commentary). al-Suyuti attributed it also to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir and said: "This is a mursal report of weak chain." al-Durr al-Manthur 1/271.]] It is also said that it is in the sense of their saying, "Do not ask about the evil of so-and-so, for it is beyond what you imagine," and it is not a prohibition. The others recited ﴿And you will not be asked﴾ with the damma (raf') as a negation, meaning: "wa lastu bi-mas'ulin 'anhum" (and you will not be questioned about them). [[This is what Imam al-Tabari preferred, and he gave it a precise explanation with a strong argument. See: al-Tafsir 2/559–561 with Shakir's commentary; and compare Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/285, Dar al-Arqam edition.]] As Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and Ours is the reckoning﴾ (3:20), and ﴿about the companions of the Hellfire﴾. Al-Jahim is the greatest part of the Fire.

It is said: He judges it, determines it, and perfects it [and the root of qada' (decree) is "completion" (al-faragh); from it comes the saying about one who has died: "qudiya 'alayhi" (his end has been decreed), because he has completed (faraga) the world; and from it comes "qada' Allah wa qadaruhu" (the decree and predestination of Allah)] [[Addition from manuscript B.]], because He has completed it in measure and arrangement.

﴿Then He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. See: al-Tafsir 2/559–561 with Shakir's commentary; and compare Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/285, Dar al-Arqam edition.]] As Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and Ours is the reckoning﴾ (3:20), and ﴿about the companions of the Hellfire﴾.
