Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 120:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Neither will the Jews be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion. Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (true) guidance.﴾ The reason for this is that they used to ask the Prophet ﷺ for a truce (al-hudnah), and they would raise his hopes that if he gave them respite, they would follow him. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit by Abu Hayyan: 1/368.]] Its meaning: if you make a truce with them, they will not be pleased with it; they only seek it as a pretext, and they will not be pleased with you except by following their religion. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: This concerns the qiblah. The Jews of Medina and the Christians of Najran used to hope that the Prophet ﷺ would pray facing their qiblah. When Allah turned the qiblah to the Kaaba, they despaired of him agreeing with their religion. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Neither will the Jews be pleased with you﴾ unless you adopt Judaism, ﴿nor the Christians﴾ unless you adopt Christianity. [[See: Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyuti, in the margin of al-Jalalayn, pp. 48-49; he attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur to al-Tha'labi.]] Al-millah means the path (al-tariqah). ﴿And if you were to follow their desires﴾. It is said the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is the community (ummah), as in His saying: ﴿If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ (39:65). ﴿After the knowledge that has come to you﴾ — the clarification that the religion of Allah is Islam, and that the qiblah is the qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him, which is the Kaaba. ﴿You will have no protector or helper against Allah.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 121–124:**

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: It was revealed concerning the people of the ship who came with Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). They were forty men: thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight monks from al-Sham, among them Bahira[[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/369; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 37; al-Wasit 1/184.]]. Al-Dahhak said: They are those Jews who believed: ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, Saʿiya ibn ʿAmr, Tamam ibn Yahuda, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Kaʿb, Ibn Yamin, and ʿAbdullah ibn Suriya[[Al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/369; al-Tabari 2/564, which he preferred, may Allah have mercy on him.]]. Qatada and Ikrima said: They are the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: They are all the believers[[Al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/369; al-Tabari 2/564.]]. ﴿They recite it as it should be recited﴾. Al-Kalbi said: They describe him in their books as he truly is, to anyone among the people who asks them. The pronoun ("it") refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). Others said: It refers to the Book. They differed about its meaning. Ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They read it as it was revealed and do not distort it, they make lawful what it makes lawful and unlawful what it makes unlawful. Al-Hasan said: They act upon its clear verses (muhkam), they believe in its ambiguous verses (mutashabih), and they leave the knowledge of what is unclear to them to its Knower. Mujahid said: They follow it as it truly should be followed.

His saying: ﴿Those are the ones who believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers. O Children of Israel, remember My blessing which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds. And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will ransom be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped﴾. 18/a

His exalted saying: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾. Ibn ʿAmir recited "Ibrahaam" with an alif in most places. It is a non-Arabic name, which is why it is not declined. He is Ibrahim ibn Tarikh ibn Nakhur. His birthplace was al-Sus in the land of al-Ahwaz, and it was said Babil, and it was said Kufa, and it was said [Lashkar][[In b: Kaskar.]], and it was said Harran. His father moved him to the land of Babil, the land of Nimrod ibn Kanaan. The meaning of ibtila' (testing) is examination, trial, and command. Allah's testing of His servants is not so that He may know their conditions through the testing, for He already knows them, but so that the servants may know their own conditions and thus some of them may come to know others.

They differed about the "words" with which Allah tested Abraham, peace be upon him. Ikrima and Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: They are thirty, which they named as the laws of Islam, and no one was tested with them and fulfilled them all except Abraham, so acquittal was written for him. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And Abraham who fulfilled﴾ (53:37). Ten are in Surat al-Tawba, "the repentant, the worshippers" to the end; ten are in al-Ahzab, "Indeed the Muslim men and Muslim women"; and ten are in Surat al-Mu'minun, in His saying: "The believers have certainly succeeded," the verses; and His saying ﴿except those who pray﴾ in "A questioner asked"[[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/375.]].

Tawus said, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): Allah tested him with ten things, which are: five pertaining to the head: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, the siwak (tooth-cleaning stick), and parting the hair; and five pertaining to the body: cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, and cleaning with water after relieving oneself[[See Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/289; al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/375.]].

It is reported in a narration: "Indeed Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to trim his moustache, the first to be circumcised, the first to cut his nails, and the first to see gray hair. When he saw it he said: 'O Lord, what is this?' He said: 'The mark of dignity.' He said: 'O Lord, increase me in dignity.'"[[Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir 2/98, and in the Muwatta' and others, from Yahya ibn Saʿid, that he heard Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab say: Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to be circumcised... etc. See also al-Durr al-Manthur 1/281.]]

Mujahid said: They are the verses that follow in His exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾ (2:124), to the end of the story. Al-Rabi' and Qatada said: They are the rites of Hajj. Al-Hasan said: Allah tested him with seven things: with the stars, the moon, and the sun, and he contemplated them well and knew that his Lord is eternal and does not cease; with the fire, and he endured it; with migration; with the sacrifice of his son; and with circumcision, and he endured it. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: They are the words of Abraham and Ishmael when they raised the House: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾ (2:127), the verse. They raised it with "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, [and Allah is the Greatest]"[[In b: Yaman.]]. Yaman ibn Rabab said: They are his argument with his people. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And his people argued with him﴾, up to His saying, exalted: ﴿And that is Our argument which We gave to Abraham﴾ (6:83). It was also said: They are His saying: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ (26:78), up to the end of the verses.

﴿And fulfilled them﴾. Qatada said: He discharged them. Al-Dahhak said: He stood by them. And [Nuʿman][[Omitted in b.]] said: He acted upon them. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾, one who is followed in good. ﴿He said﴾, meaning Abraham: ﴿And from my offspring﴾, meaning also from my children, so appoint from them leaders who are followed in good. ﴿He said﴾, Allah, exalted: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾. Hamza and Hafs recited it with the yaʾ sukun (ʿahdi), and the rest with fath. The meaning: whoever among them is a wrongdoer, it will not reach him. ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah said: "My covenant" means My mercy. Al-Suddi said: My prophethood. It was also said: The leadership. Mujahid said: No wrongdoer is to be obeyed in his wrongdoing. The meaning of the verse: What I have covenanted to you of prophethood and leadership will not reach those among your descendants who are wrongdoers. It was also said: By "covenant" He meant security from the Fire, and by "wrongdoer" the polytheist, as in His saying: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their faith with wrongdoing, those will have security﴾ (6:82).

It was also said: By "covenant" He meant security from the Fire, and by "wrongdoer" the polytheist, as in His saying: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their faith with wrongdoing, those will have security﴾ (6:82).

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 121–124:**

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: It was revealed concerning the people of the ship who came with Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). They were forty men: thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight monks from al-Sham, among them Bahira[[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/369; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 37; al-Wasit 1/184.]]. Al-Dahhak said: They are those Jews who believed: ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, Saʿiya ibn ʿAmr, Tamam ibn Yahuda, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Kaʿb, Ibn Yamin, and ʿAbdullah ibn Suriya[[Al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/369; al-Tabari 2/564, which he preferred, may Allah have mercy on him.]]. Qatada and Ikrima said: They are the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: They are all the believers[[Al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/369; al-Tabari 2/564.]]. ﴿They recite it as it should be recited﴾. Al-Kalbi said: They describe him in their books as he truly is, to anyone among the people who asks them. The pronoun ("it") refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). Others said: It refers to the Book. They differed about its meaning. Ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They read it as it was revealed and do not distort it, they make lawful what it makes lawful and unlawful what it makes unlawful. Al-Hasan said: They act upon its clear verses (muhkam), they believe in its ambiguous verses (mutashabih), and they leave the knowledge of what is unclear to them to its Knower. Mujahid said: They follow it as it truly should be followed.

His saying: ﴿Those are the ones who believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers. O Children of Israel, remember My blessing which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds. And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will ransom be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped﴾. 18/a

His exalted saying: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾. Ibn ʿAmir recited "Ibrahaam" with an alif in most places. It is a non-Arabic name, which is why it is not declined. He is Ibrahim ibn Tarikh ibn Nakhur. His birthplace was al-Sus in the land of al-Ahwaz, and it was said Babil, and it was said Kufa, and it was said [Lashkar][[In b: Kaskar.]], and it was said Harran. His father moved him to the land of Babil, the land of Nimrod ibn Kanaan. The meaning of ibtila' (testing) is examination, trial, and command. Allah's testing of His servants is not so that He may know their conditions through the testing, for He already knows them, but so that the servants may know their own conditions and thus some of them may come to know others.

They differed about the "words" with which Allah tested Abraham, peace be upon him. Ikrima and Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: They are thirty, which they named as the laws of Islam, and no one was tested with them and fulfilled them all except Abraham, so acquittal was written for him. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And Abraham who fulfilled﴾ (53:37). Ten are in Surat al-Tawba, "the repentant, the worshippers" to the end; ten are in al-Ahzab, "Indeed the Muslim men and Muslim women"; and ten are in Surat al-Mu'minun, in His saying: "The believers have certainly succeeded," the verses; and His saying ﴿except those who pray﴾ in "A questioner asked"[[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/375.]].

Tawus said, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): Allah tested him with ten things, which are: five pertaining to the head: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, the siwak (tooth-cleaning stick), and parting the hair; and five pertaining to the body: cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, and cleaning with water after relieving oneself[[See Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/289; al-Bahr al-Muhit 1/375.]].

It is reported in a narration: "Indeed Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to trim his moustache, the first to be circumcised, the first to cut his nails, and the first to see gray hair. When he saw it he said: 'O Lord, what is this?' He said: 'The mark of dignity.' He said: 'O Lord, increase me in dignity.'"[[Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir 2/98, and in the Muwatta' and others, from Yahya ibn Saʿid, that he heard Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab say: Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to be circumcised... etc. See also al-Durr al-Manthur 1/281.]]

Mujahid said: They are the verses that follow in His exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾ (2:124), to the end of the story. Al-Rabi' and Qatada said: They are the rites of Hajj. Al-Hasan said: Allah tested him with seven things: with the stars, the moon, and the sun, and he contemplated them well and knew that his Lord is eternal and does not cease; with the fire, and he endured it; with migration; with the sacrifice of his son; and with circumcision, and he endured it. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: They are the words of Abraham and Ishmael when they raised the House: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾ (2:127), the verse. They raised it with "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, [and Allah is the Greatest]"[[In b: Yaman.]]. Yaman ibn Rabab said: They are his argument with his people. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And his people argued with him﴾, up to His saying, exalted: ﴿And that is Our argument which We gave to Abraham﴾ (6:83). It was also said: They are His saying: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ (26:78), up to the end of the verses.

﴿And fulfilled them﴾. Qatada said: He discharged them. Al-Dahhak said: He stood by them. And [Nuʿman][[Omitted in b.]] said: He acted upon them. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾, one who is followed in good. ﴿He said﴾, meaning Abraham: ﴿And from my offspring﴾, meaning also from my children, so appoint from them leaders who are followed in good. ﴿He said﴾, Allah, exalted: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾. Hamza and Hafs recited it with the yaʾ sukun (ʿahdi), and the rest with fath. The meaning: whoever among them is a wrongdoer, it will not reach him. ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah said: "My covenant" means My mercy. Al-Suddi said: My prophethood. It was also said: The leadership. Mujahid said: No wrongdoer is to be obeyed in his wrongdoing. The meaning of the verse: What I have covenanted to you of prophethood and leadership will not reach those among your descendants who are wrongdoers. It was also said: By "covenant" He meant security from the Fire, and by "wrongdoer" the polytheist, as in His saying: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their faith with wrongdoing, those will have security﴾ (6:82).

Al-Baghawi's commentary (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 2, verse 125:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [remember] when We made the House﴾, meaning the Ka'bah, ﴿a place of return (mathabah) for the people﴾, meaning a place to which they return. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they come to it from every side and perform Hajj. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: a refuge and a place of safety. Qatadah and 'Ikrimah said: a gathering place. ﴿And a sanctuary (amnan)﴾, meaning a place of safety where they are secure from harm by the polytheists. The polytheists did not molest the people of Makkah; they would say, "They are the People of Allah," but they would attack those around it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ (29:67).

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Ali ibn Abd Allah informed us, Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "This city, Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth. It is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny plants shall not be cut, its game shall not be startled, its lost property shall not be picked up except by one who announces it, and its grass shall not be cut." Al-'Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, except for idhkhir (a fragrant grass), for it is for their smiths and for their houses." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Except for idhkhir."[[Related by al-Bukhari: in Funerals, chapter: Idhkhir and grass, 3/213. And Muslim: in Hajj, chapter: The sanctity of Makkah, its game and its grass, nos. (353, 354, 355), 2/986. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/249.]]

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And take﴾. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with a fatha on the kha' (﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا﴾), as a statement; the rest read it with a kasra on the kha' (﴿وَاتَّخِذُوا﴾), as a command. ﴿From the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾. Ibn Yaman[[In B: Yaman.]] said: the entire mosque is the Station of Ibrahim. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: the entire Haram is the Station of Ibrahim. It has also been said that by the Station of Ibrahim is meant all the places of Hajj, such as 'Arafat, Muzdalifah, and all the other sites.

The correct view is that the Station of Ibrahim is the stone in the mosque where the imams pray. It is the stone on which Ibrahim, peace be upon him, stood when building the House. It has also been said that the traces of the toes of his feet were clearly visible on it, but they were worn away by the frequent touching of hands. Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: they were commanded to pray at the Station of Ibrahim, but they were not commanded to touch or kiss it.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Musaddad informed us, from Yahya ibn Humayd, from Anas, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I agreed with Allah in three matters, or my Lord agreed with me in three matters. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, why do you not take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾. And I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you, so why do you not order the Mothers of the Believers to observe hijab?' So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed the verse of hijab. He said: 'And it reached me that the Prophet ﷺ rebuked some of his wives, so I entered upon them and said to them: "If you do not desist, Allah will surely give him better wives than you." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you﴾."[[Related by al-Bukhari: in Tafsir, chapter on His saying: And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer, 8/168. And Muslim: in Virtues of the Companions, chapter: From the virtues of 'Umar, no. (2399), 4/1865, abridged. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/93. See also: Qatf al-Thamar fi Muwafaqat 'Umar by al-Suyuti, in al-Hawi lil-Fatawa, 1/377.]] the verse (66:5).

Muhammad ibn Isma'il also related it from 'Amr ibn 'Awf, who informed us, Hushaym informed us, from Humayd, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I agreed with my Lord in three matters. I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, why do you not take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer?' Then it was revealed: ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Prayer, chapter: What has come concerning the qiblah, and whoever does not see the need to repeat prayer for one who forgot..., 1/504.]]

As for the beginning of the story of the Station: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, brought Isma'il and Hajar and placed them in Makkah, a period of time passed. The Jurhum settled there, and Isma'il married a woman from among them, and Hajar died. Ibrahim asked Sarah's permission to visit Hajar, and she gave him permission but stipulated that he should not stay. Ibrahim came to Makkah after Hajar had died. He went to Isma'il's house and said to his wife: "Where is your husband?" She said: "He has gone hunting." Isma'il, peace be upon him, used to go out of the Haram to hunt. Ibrahim said to her: "Do you have any hospitality?" She said: "I have no hospitality." He asked her about their livelihood, and she said: "We are in hardship and distress." She complained to him, and he said to her: "When your husband comes, convey my greetings to him and tell him to change the threshold of his door." Then Ibrahim left. When Isma'il came, he found his father's scent and said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "An old man came to me, with such-and-such a description, as if belittling his affairs," [he said: "What did he say to you?"] She said: "He said: 'Convey my greetings to your husband and tell him to change the threshold of his door.'" He said: "That was my father, and he has commanded me to part from you. Go back to your family." So he divorced her and married another woman from among them.[[Omitted in A.]] Ibrahim stayed as long as Allah willed, then he asked Sarah's permission to visit Isma'il, and she gave him permission but stipulated that he should not stay. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, came until he reached the door of Isma'il's house and said to his wife: "Where is your husband?" She said: "He has gone hunting, and he will come now, if Allah wills. Dismount, may Allah have mercy on you." He said: "Do you have any hospitality?" She said: "Yes," and she brought milk and meat. He asked her about their livelihood, and she said: "We are in goodness and abundance." So he prayed for blessing for them both. Had she come to him that day with bread of wheat or barley and dates, it would have been the most abundant of Allah's lands in wheat, barley, or dates. She said to him: "Dismount until I wash your head." He did not dismount, so she brought him the stone and placed it at his right side, and he placed his foot on it. She washed the right side of his head, then turned him to his left side and washed the left side of his head, and the traces of his two feet remained on it. He said to her: "When your husband comes, convey my greetings to him and tell him: 'Your doorstep has been made firm.'" When Isma'il came, he found his father's scent and said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "Yes, an old man, the most handsome of people in face and the most fragrant in scent. He said to me such-and-such, and I said to him such-and-such. I washed his head, and this is the place of his feet." He said: "That was Ibrahim, the Prophet, my father, and you are the doorstep. He commanded me to keep you."[[Related by al-Bukhari, at length, in the Prophets, chapter: Yazifun (they hasten): al-nislan (a gait) in walking, 6/396, and in other places.]]

It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr[[Folio 18b.]] from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Then he stayed away from them as long as Allah willed. Then he came after that, and Isma'il was shaping arrows under a dawmah tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he rose to him, and they did as a father does with his son and a son with his father. Then he said: 'O Isma'il, Allah the Exalted has commanded me with a matter, will you help me with it?' He said: 'I will help you.' He said: 'Allah has commanded me to build a house here.' At that, they raised the foundations of the House. Isma'il would bring the stones, and Ibrahim would build, until the structure rose high. He brought this stone and placed it for him, and Ibrahim stood on the stone, the Maqam, while building, and Isma'il handed him the stones, and they were both saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing﴾." It is said in a report: "The Corner (of the Black Stone) and the Station are two rubies from the rubies of Paradise. Had they not been touched by the hands of the polytheists, they would have illuminated what is between the east and the west."[[Related by al-Tirmidhi from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr with the wording: "The Corner and the Station are two rubies from the rubies of Paradise. Allah extinguished their light; had He not extinguished their light, they would have illuminated..." 3/618, and he said it is a gharib hadith. Al-Hakim related it in Hajj from Dawud al-Zabraqan, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Qatadah ibn Di'amah, from Anas, and said it is sahih; al-Dhahabi rejected this, saying that Dawud is in its chain, and Abu Dawud said he is matruk (abandoned) (Fayd al-Qadir: 4/59). It is also related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr; see al-Mustadrak: 1/456. Al-Wahidi related it in al-Wasit: 1/190, and see Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 1/618-619.]]

The Mighty and Majestic's saying: ﴿And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾, meaning We commanded them and revealed to them. It has been said: Isma'il was so named because Ibrahim used to pray to Allah to grant him a son and would say: "Isma' ya Il," and Il is Allah; when he was granted a son, Allah named him by it. ﴿That purify My House﴾, meaning the Ka'bah. He attributed it to Himself as a specification and honor, meaning: build it upon purity and monotheism. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ata' said: purify it from idols, impurities, and false speech. It has also been said: perfume it and make it fragrant. The people of Madinah and Hafs read ﴿بَيْتِيَ﴾ (bayti) with a fatha on the ya' here and in Surah al-Hajj. Hafs added in Surah Nuh ﴿لِلطَّائِفِينَ﴾ (for those who circumambulate), meaning those who go around it; ﴿وَالْعَاكِفِينَ﴾ (and those who stay), meaning those who reside and dwell there; ﴿وَالرُّكَّعِ﴾ (and those who bow), plural of rakiʿ; ﴿السُّجُودِ﴾ (and prostrate), plural of sajid, meaning those who pray. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: the Ṭa'ifin are the strangers, and the 'Akifin are the people of Makkah. 'Ata', Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: circumambulation is more virtuous for strangers, and prayer is more virtuous for the people of Makkah.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 126–127:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this a secure city"﴾. That is, Makkah. It was also said: the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram). ﴿Secure﴾, that is, possessing security, where its people are safe. ﴿And provide its people with fruits﴾. He supplicated for this only because it was a valley without cultivation. It is related in the stories (al-qasas) that al-Ta'if was among the cities of Syria, in Urdunn. When Abraham, peace be upon him, made this supplication, Allah the Exalted commanded Gabriel, peace be upon him, to uproot it from its base and carry it around the House seven times, then place it in the position where it is now. Thus most of the fruits of Makkah come from it. ﴿Whoever among them believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾: he supplicated for the believers specifically. ﴿He said﴾: Allah the Exalted said, ﴿And whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited fa-umti'uhu (with a light form, with a ḍamma on the hamza), while the rest recited it with a shadda (fa-umatti'uhu). Their meaning is one and the same. "A little" means: I will also provide for the disbeliever, a little, until the end of his term. That is because Allah the Exalted promised provision to all creation, both its believers and its disbelievers. He restricted it to "little" only because the enjoyment of this world is little. ﴿Then I will compel him﴾, that is, I will force him in the Hereafter ﴿to the punishment of the Fire; and wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place of return to which he comes. Mujahid said: A book was found near the Maqam containing: "Allah is the Lord of Bakkah. I fashioned it on the day I created the sun and the moon, and I made it sacred on the day I created the heavens and the earth. I encircled it with seven angels, upright in devotion (hunafa'). Its provision comes to it from three paths. Blessing is upon it in its meat and its water."

His saying, may He be mighty and majestic: ﴿And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House﴾. The narrators (al-Ruwat) said: [[The narrators mentioned these stories and reports about the building of the House, most of which are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives taken from the Jewish and Christian traditions) by which no proof is established. What suffices us is what has come in established narrations, such as what al-Bukhari mentioned in the Book of the Traditions of the Prophets, chapter: "Allah took Abraham as a friend (khalil)." See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/302 onward; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya 1/163–166; al-Isra'iliyyat wa'l-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shuhbah, pp. 235–237.]] Allah the Exalted created the place of the House two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the water. Then the earth was spread out from beneath it. When Allah sent Adam, peace be upon him, down to the earth, he felt lonely and complained to Allah the Exalted. So Allah sent down the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur) from a ruby of the rubies of Paradise, having two doors of green emerald, one eastern and one western. He placed it on the site of the House and said: "O Adam, I have sent down for you a house that you will circumambulate, just as the throne of Mine is circumambulated, and you will pray beside it, just as beside My throne." He also sent down the Black Stone, which had been white but turned black from the touch of menstruating women in the Jahiliyyah. Adam set out from the land of India toward Makkah on foot, and Allah assigned to him an angel to guide him to the House. He performed the pilgrimage to the House and established the rites. When he had finished, the angels met him and said: "May your pilgrimage be accepted, O Adam! We performed pilgrimage to this House two thousand years before you." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Adam performed forty pilgrimages from India to Makkah on foot. He continued in this way until the days of the Flood. Then Allah lifted him up to the fourth heaven, where seventy thousand angels enter it each day and never return to it. Allah sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, who concealed the Black Stone on Mount Abu Qubays to protect it from drowning. So the site of the House remained empty until the time of Abraham. Then, after Ishmael and Isaac had been born to him, Allah the Exalted commanded Abraham to build a house in which He would be remembered. He asked Allah, mighty and majestic, to show him its location. So Allah sent al-Sakinah (the divine tranquility) to guide him to the site of the House. It is a wind that blows strongly, having two heads like a serpent. Abraham was commanded to build wherever al-Sakinah settled. So Abraham followed it until they reached Makkah, and al-Sakinah circled around the site of the House like a shield (kata-ttawi al-hajfah). This is the saying of 'Ali and al-Hasan.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah the Exalted sent a cloud the size of the Ka'bah, which began to move while Abraham walked in its shade, until it reached Makkah and stopped over the site of the House. Abraham was called from it: "Build in its shade, neither exceeding it nor falling short." It was also said: Allah sent Gabriel to guide him to the site of the House, as in His saying: ﴿And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House﴾. Abraham and Ishmael built the House. Abraham was building and Ishmael was passing him the stones. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House﴾, that is, its bases (usus), whose singular is qa'idah. Al-Kisa'i said: the walls of the House. Ibn 'Abbas said: The House was built from five mountains: Tur Sinai, Tur Zaytha, Lubnan (a mountain in Syria), al-Judi (a mountain in al-Jazirah), and they built its foundations from Hira' (a mountain in Makkah). When Abraham reached the place of the Black Stone, he said to Ishmael: "Bring me a fine stone that will serve as a sign for the people." Ishmael brought him a stone, and he said: "Bring me something better than this." Ishmael went off searching for it, and Abu Qubays cried out: "O Abraham, I have a deposit for you; take it." So he took the Black Stone and placed it in its position. It was also said: Allah the Exalted built a house in the heavens, which is the Frequented House, also called al-Darah. He commanded the angels to build the Ka'bah on earth opposite it, according to its measure and likeness. It was also said: the first to build the Ka'bah was Adam, and it was obliterated during the time of the Flood. Then Allah revealed it to Abraham, until he built it. [[Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "No authentic report from an infallible source has come that the House was built before the Friend (Abraham), peace be upon him. Whoever holds to this on the basis of His saying 'the place of the House' has no sound or clear argument, because what is meant is its place decreed in Allah's knowledge, established in His power, and held in honour by the prophets from the time of Adam to the time of Abraham, peace be upon him." See: al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya 1/163, 165.]]

His saying: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾. There is an implied element in this: that is, and they both say: "Our Lord, accept from us our building." ﴿Indeed You are the All-Hearing﴾ of our supplication, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of our intentions.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 128:

﴿Our Lord, and make us both Muslims [in submission] to You﴾: monotheists, obedient, sincere, humbled before You.

﴿And from our descendants﴾: that is, our children, ﴿a community﴾: a group. The ummah (community) are the followers of the prophets. ﴿Muslim [in submission] to You﴾: humbled before You.

﴿And show us﴾: teach us and make us know. Ibn Kathir read it with the r sukun (wa-arnā, with the r silent), Abu 'Amr read it with ikhtilas (a rapid, reduced vowel), and the rest read it with a kasra on the r. Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr agreed on sukun in Ha Mim al-Sajdah. Its original form is arina, so the hamza was dropped seeking lightness and its vowel was transferred to the r. Whoever reads it with sukun says: the hamza has gone, so its vowel has gone too. ﴿Our rites﴾ (manasikana): the laws of our religion and the markers of our pilgrimage (hajj).

It is also said: the places of our pilgrimage. Mujahid said: our slaughtering places; the nusuk is the sacrificial animal. It is also said: our acts of worship. The root of nusuk is worship, and the nasik is the worshipper. So God the Exalted answered their supplication: He sent Gabriel, who showed them the rites on the day of 'Arafah. When he reached 'Arafat, he said: "Have you recognized (araft), O Ibrahim?" He said: "Yes." Hence the time was named 'Arafah and the place 'Arafat.

﴿And turn to us [in forgiveness]﴾: pardon us, ﴿indeed You are the Ever-Returning, the Most Merciful. Our Lord, and raise up among them﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 129:

That is, in the Muslim community (ummah) from the offspring of Ibrahim and Isma'il. It is also said: from the people of Makkah. ﴿A messenger from among them﴾, that is, a messenger sent from among them. By this he meant Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Sayyid Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Musa al-Musawi narrated to us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abbas al-Balkhi told me: al-Imam Abu Sulayman Hamad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Khattabi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Makki informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: the son of my brother (Ibn Wahb) informed us: my uncle informed us: Mu'awiyah informed us, from Salih, from Sa'id ibn Suwayd, from Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal al-Sulami, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed I am written with Allah as the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still lying in his clay. I will inform you of the beginning of my affair: I am the answer to the prayer of Ibrahim, the glad tidings of Isa, and the vision of my mother, who saw when she gave birth to me that a light came forth from her by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated." [[Narrated by Ahmad: 4/127-128, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah; and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/418, 600. Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zaman: p. 512. And al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah: 1/389-390. And al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani. al-Haythami said: "One of Ahmad's chains has narrators who are the narrators of the Sahih except Sa'id ibn Suwayd, whom none declared reliable except Ibn Hibban" (Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/223). The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/207. See also: al-Kafi al-Shaf by Ibn Hajar, p. (10).]]

And by the prayer of Ibrahim he meant this, for he prayed that a messenger be raised up among the children of Isma'il from among them. Ibn Abbas said: All the prophets were from the children of Isra'il except ten: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, Lut, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

﴿Recites﴾, that is, reads, ﴿to them Your verses﴾, meaning Your Book, that is, the Qur'an. An āyah of the Qur'an is a connected utterance up to its end. It is also said: it is a group of letters, as one says, "The people went out with their āyah," meaning with their group. ﴿And teaches them the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and the wisdom﴾. Mujahid said: the understanding of the Qur'an. Muqatil said: the admonitions of the Qur'an and the rulings contained in it. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is knowledge and action, and a man is not wise until he combines the two. It is also said: it is the Sunnah. It is also said: it is the rulings and judgment. It is also said: wisdom is jurisprudence (fiqh).

Abu Bakr ibn Duraid said: Every word that admonishes you, or calls you to nobility, or forbids you from something ugly, is wisdom.

﴿And purifies them﴾, that is, cleanses them from shirk and sins. It is also said: he takes zakah from their wealth. Ibn Kaysan said: he will testify for them on the Day of Resurrection to their uprightness (adalah), when they testify to the prophets that they conveyed the message, and tazkiyah is ta'dil (declaring someone upright). ﴿Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "al-Aziz" is the One for whom there is no equal. Al-Kalbi said: "al-Muntaqim" (the Avenger). Its explanation is the words of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah is Mighty, Owner of retribution﴾ (3:4). It is also said: "al-Mani'" (the Impregnable), which no hand can reach and nothing can attain. It is also said: "al-Qawi" (the Strong); and 'izzah means strength. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So We strengthened [them] with a third﴾ (36:14), that is, We strengthened. It is also said: "al-Ghalib" (the Dominant). Allah the Exalted says, reporting: ﴿And he overpowered me in speech﴾ (38:23), that is, he overcame me. And it is said in the proverb: "Whoever is mighty plunders," that is, whoever overcomes, despoils.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 130–131:**

﴿And who would turn away from the creed of Ibrahim﴾. This was because Abdullah ibn Salam invited his two nephews, Salamah and Muhajir, to Islam. He said to them: "You both know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in the Torah: 'I will raise up from the offspring of Isma'il a prophet whose name is Ahmad. Whoever believes in him has been guided, and whoever does not believe in him is cursed.'" Salamah accepted Islam, but Muhajir refused to accept it. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And who would turn away from the creed of Ibrahim﴾ [[See: Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyuti, p. 51, in the margin of al-Jalalayn.]]. That is, who would abandon his religion and his law. It is said: raghiba fi al-shay' (رَغِبَ فِي الشَّيْءِ) means he desired it, and raghiba 'anhu (رَغِبَ عَنْهُ) means he abandoned it.

His words ﴿And who﴾: the wording is an interrogative, but its meaning is rebuke and reproach, meaning: no one turns away from the creed of Ibrahim ﴿except one who makes himself foolish﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "one who ruins himself." Al-Kalbi said: "one who has gone astray through his own fault." Abu Ubaydah said: "one who destroys himself." Ibn Kaysan and al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is "one who makes himself ignorant." Al-safaha (السَّفَاهَةُ) means ignorance and weakness of judgement, and every safih (سَفِيهٌ) is ignorant. This is because whoever worships other than Allah has made himself ignorant, since he did not recognise that Allah created him. It has been reported: "Whoever knows himself knows his Lord" [[Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: this is a fabricated hadith (hadith mawdu'). See: al-Asrar al-Marfu'ah by al-Qari, p. 337, and Kashf al-Khafa' by al-Ajluni: 1/262.]]. And in the reports: "Allah, Exalted, revealed to Dawud: 'Know yourself and know Me.' He said: 'O Lord, how do I know myself, and how do I know You?' Allah revealed to him: 'Know yourself by weakness, incapacity and mortality, and know Me by power, capability and permanence.'"

Al-Akhfash said: its meaning is "he made himself foolish," and according to this view nafsahu (نَفْسَهُ) is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition of specification. Al-Farra' said: it is accusative as a tafsir (explanation). The original would have been "safihat nafsuhu" (سَفِهَتْ نَفْسُهُ), but when the verb was attributed to its owner, the nafs was brought out as an explanatory term to show the place of the foolishness, as one says: "dhiqtu bihi dhar'an" (ضِقْتُ بِهِ ذَرْعًا), meaning "my capacity was constrained by him" (ضَاقَ ذَرْعِي بِهِ).

﴿And We certainly chose him in this world﴾, meaning We selected him in this world. ﴿And indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous﴾, meaning among the prophets in Paradise. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, its meaning being: "And We certainly chose him in this world and the Hereafter, and indeed he is among the righteous."

﴿When his Lord said to him: "Submit"﴾, that is: remain steadfast upon Islam and persist in it, because he was already a Muslim.

Ibn Abbas said: He said to him when he came out of the sarab (السَّرَبِ) [[al-sarab, with the letter ra' vocalised with a fatha: a pit beneath the ground; it is also said: a house beneath the ground.]]. Al-Kalbi said: "Make your religion and your worship sincerely for Allah." Ata' said: "Submit to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and entrust your affairs to Him."

﴿He said: "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds"﴾, that is, I have entrusted myself. Ibn Abbas said: He fulfilled this when he did not seek help from any of the angels when he was cast into the fire.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 132:**

﴿And Abraham charged his sons with it, and so did Jacob﴾. The people of Madina and Syria read "wa-awsa" (أَوْصَى) with an alif, and it is written that way in their copies of the Qur'an (masahif, sing. mushaf, codices). The rest read "wa-wassa" (وَوَصَّى) with the doubled letter. The two are dialectal variants (lughatan), like "anzala" and "nazzala." The meaning is: "Abraham charged his sons with it, and Jacob charged his sons." Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: it refers to the words of sincere faith (kalimat al-ikhlas), "There is no god but Allah." Abu 'Ubaydah said: if you wish, you may refer the pronoun (al-kina'ah) to the religion (al-millah), since it mentions the religion of Abraham. If you wish, you may refer it to the charge (al-wasiyyah). That is: Abraham charged his eight sons: Isma'il and his mother Hajar the Copt, and Ishaq and his mother Sarah, and six sons whose mother was Qanturah, daughter of Yaqtan, the Canaanite. Abraham married her after the death of Sarah. Jacob is named so because he and Esau (al-'Is) were twins. Esau came out of their mother's womb first, and Jacob came out after him, holding on to his heel ('aqib). This is related from Ibn 'Abbas. It is also said that Jacob was named for the abundance of his offspring ('aqib). The meaning is that Jacob also charged his twelve sons.

﴿O my sons﴾: the meaning is "that, O my sons." ﴿Indeed, Allah has chosen﴾, meaning, has selected, ﴿for you the religion﴾, meaning the religion of Islam. ﴿So do not die except while you are Muslims﴾, meaning believers. It is also said: sincere (mukhlisun). It is also said: submitting (mufawwidun). The prohibition in the outward wording falls on death, but in reality the prohibition is against abandoning Islam. The meaning is: persist in Islam until death does not find you except while you are Muslims.

It is related from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "﴿Except while you are Muslims﴾" means: those who think well (muhsinun) of their Lord.

Akhbarana 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliyhi: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh told us: Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi told us: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd told us: Abu Ja'far al-Razi told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) three days before his death say: "None of you should die except while thinking well of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

[Recorded by Muslim: in al-Jannah (Paradise), chapter: the command to think well of Allah at the time of death, no. 2877, 4/2205. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/372.]

﴿Or were you witnesses﴾. That is, "Were you [not] witnesses?" He means: were you not present as witnesses? ﴿when death came to Ya'qub﴾, that is, when Ya'qub (Jacob) drew near to death. It was said that this was revealed concerning the Jews, when they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do you not know that when Ya'qub died he enjoined his sons to be Jews?" According to this view, the address is to the Jews. Al-Kalbi said: when Ya'qub entered Egypt, he saw them worshipping idols and fires, so he gathered his sons and feared for them because of this, and the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?"﴾. 'Ata' said: Allah does not take the soul of a prophet until He gives him the choice between life and death. When Ya'qub was given the choice, he said: "Give me respite until I ask my sons and advise them." Allah did this for him. So he gathered his sons and his grandsons and said to them: "My appointed time has come. What will you worship after me?" ﴿They said: "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq."﴾ Isma'il was their paternal uncle, and the Arabs call the paternal uncle "father," just as they call the maternal aunt "mother." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A man's paternal uncle is the twin of his father" [[Narrated by Muslim: in Zakat, chapter on hastening zakat and withholding it, no. 983, 2/676–677. See Sharh al-Sunnah 6/33.]]. He also said concerning his uncle al-'Abbas: "Return my father to me, for I fear that Quraysh will do to him what Thaqif did to 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud" [[Ibn Abi Shaybah said in the Maghazi section of his Musannaf 14/480–484: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us from Ayyub from 'Ikrimah who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a truce with the people of Makkah ..." until he said: "al-'Abbas went out, mounted the Messenger of Allah's white mule and went to Quraysh to invite them to Allah. He was delayed, so the Messenger of Allah said: 'Return my father to me, for the uncle of a man is the twin of his father; I fear that they will do to him ...'" See al-Kafi al-Shaf by Ibn Hajar, pp. 11–12.]]. That is because they killed him.

﴿One God﴾: accusative as a badal (substitution/apposition) for His words "your God." It was also said: "We acknowledge Him as one God." ﴿And to Him we are Muslims.﴾

﴿That is a community﴾, a group, ﴿which has passed away﴾, which has gone. ﴿For it is what it earned﴾ of deeds, ﴿and for you is what you earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do﴾. That is: each one will be asked about his own deeds, not about the deeds of others.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 135–136:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: Be Jews or Christians, and you will be guided.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning the leaders of the Jews of Medina, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Wahb ibn Yahuda and Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab, and concerning the Christians of Najran, al-Sayyid and al-'Aqib and their companions. That was because they disputed with the Muslims about the religion, each group claiming that it had the greater right to the religion of God. The Jews said: Our prophet Musa is the best of the prophets, our book the Torah is the best of the books, and our religion is the best of the religions, and they disbelieved in 'Isa, the Injil, Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. The Christians said: Our prophet is the best of the prophets, our book the Injil is the best of the books, and our religion is the best of the religions, and they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. Each of the two groups said to the believers: Follow our religion, for there is no religion but this. [[See: al-Wasit of al-Wahidi, p. 202, where it is given in more detail in Asbab al-Nuzul: 1/38.]] So God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿Rather, the religion of Ibrahim﴾, meaning: rather, we follow the religion of Ibrahim. Al-Kisa'i said: it is in the accusative as an incitement (al-igha', a form of urging someone to follow), as if he were saying: follow the religion of Ibrahim. It was also said that its meaning is: rather, we shall be upon the religion of Ibrahim, so "upon" (ʿala) was deleted and it became accusative. ﴿Hanifan﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) according to the grammarians of Basra. According to the grammarians of Kufa, it is in the accusative as a detached qualifier (qat'). The meaning is: rather, the religion of Ibrahim, the hanif; when the definite article was dropped, the definite noun did not follow the indefinite, so it was detached from it and put in the accusative.

Mujahid said: al-hanifiyya is following Ibrahim in what he brought of the law, by which he became an imam for the people. Ibn 'Abbas said: the hanif is one who inclines away from all religions toward the religion of Islam; its root is from al-hanaf, which is an inclination and a crookedness in the foot. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the hanif is the pilgrim who has been circumcised.

Al-Dahhak said: if the hanif is with a Muslim, then he is the pilgrim; and if he is not with a Muslim, then he is the Muslim. Qatada said: al-hanifiyya is circumcision, the prohibition of mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts and maternal aunts, and the performance of the rites.

﴿And he was not of the polytheists.﴾ Then he taught the believers the way of faith, and so He, whose remembrance is glorious, said:

﴿Say: We believe in God and in what has been sent down to us﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and what was sent down to Ibrahim﴾, ten scrolls, ﴿and Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the tribes﴾, meaning the sons of Ya'qub, who were twelve tribes, each one called a sibt (tribe). They were so named because each of them had a group of descendants born to him. The sibt of a man is his grandson, and from this it is said of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them both, that they were the two grandsons (sibtan) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The tribes among the Children of Israel were like the clans among the Arabs from the Children of Isma'il and the peoples among the non-Arabs. Among the tribes there were prophets, and therefore He said: "and what was sent down to them." It was also said that they were the sons of Ya'qub from his loins, all of whom became prophets. ﴿And what was given to Musa﴾, meaning the Torah, ﴿and 'Isa﴾, meaning the Injil, ﴿and what was given﴾, meaning bestowed, ﴿to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them﴾, that is, we believe in all of them and do not distinguish between any one of them, so that we believe in some and disbelieve in others as the Jews and Christians did. ﴿And to Him we are Muslims.﴾

Akhbarana 'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Na'imi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar informed us: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar informed us: 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it to the People of Islam in Arabic. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor disbelieve them, but say: We believe in God, and the verse..." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-I'tisam, chapter: the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): Do not ask the People of the Book about anything: 13/333. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/269.]]

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-I'tisam, chapter: the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): Do not ask the People of the Book about anything: 13/333. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/269.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 137:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So if they believe in the like of what you believe in﴾: that is, in that which you believe in. Thus Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it. The word "mithl" (like) here is an extra element (silah), as in His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾, meaning, "There is nothing like Him." It is also said that the meaning is: ﴿if they believe in everything that you believe in﴾, that is, they come with a belief like your belief and a monotheism like your monotheism. It is also said that the meaning is: ﴿if they believe the like of what you believe in,﴾ and the "ba'" (in "bihi") is extra, as in His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿and shake the trunk of the palm tree toward you﴾ (19:25). Abu Mu'adh al-Nahwi said: the meaning is, "If they believe in your Book as you believed in their Book." ﴿Then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, they are only in opposition﴾, that is, in dissension and hostility. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata'. It is said: "shaqqa, yushaqqu, mushaqqatan," when he opposes, as though each one of them is taking a side different from the side of his companion. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Let not my opposition (shiqaq) bring upon you﴾ (11:89), that is, my opposition. It is also said: it means enmity. Its proof is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is because they opposed (shaqqu) Allah﴾ (8:13), that is, they were hostile to Allah. ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them,﴾ O Muhammad, that is, He will suffice you against the evil of the Jews and the Christians. He has indeed sufficed [you] by the expulsion of the Banu al-Nadir, the killing of the Banu Qurayzah, and the imposition of the jizyah upon the Jews and the Christians. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of their statements, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their conditions.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 138–143:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿the colouring of Allah﴾. Ibn Abbas, in the transmission of al-Kalbi, Qatadah and al-Hasan, said: the religion of Allah. He called it "colouring" because the effect of religion appears on the one who adheres to it, just as the effect of dye appears on cloth. It was said that it is because the one who adheres to religion is bound to it and does not part from it, as dye clings to cloth. Mujahid said: the natural disposition (fitrah) of Allah, which is close to the first meaning. It was said: the sunnah of Allah. It was also said: He meant circumcision, because it colours its bearer with blood. Ibn Abbas [[See: al-Wasit of al-Wahidi: 1/206.]] said: It is that when a child is born to one of the Christians and seven days pass over him, they immerse him in a yellowish water belonging to them, called al-Mu'ammadiyy, and they dye him with it, to purify him by that water in place of circumcision. When they have done this to him they say: "Now he has truly become a Christian." So Allah informed that His religion is Islam, not what the Christians do. It is in the accusative as an exhortation, meaning: adhere to the religion of Allah. Al-Akhfash said: it is an apposition to His words "the religion of Ibrahim." ﴿And who is better than Allah in colouring?﴾ meaning, in religion. It was said: in purification. ﴿And we are His worshippers﴾, meaning, obedient to Him.

﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the Jews and the Christians: ﴿Do you dispute with us concerning Allah?﴾, that is, concerning the religion of Allah. Al-muhajjah means arguing about Allah in order to demonstrate proof. This is because they said: the prophets were from among us and upon our religion, and our religion is more upright, so we have more right to Allah than you. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: Say: Do you dispute with us concerning Allah? ﴿And He is our Lord and your Lord﴾, that is, we and you are equal regarding Allah, for He is our Lord and your Lord. ﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds﴾, that is, each one has the recompense of his deed. So how can you claim that you have more right to Allah? ﴿And we are sincere to Him﴾, while you associate others with Him.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Sincerity (ikhlas) is that the servant makes his religion and his deed pure, so that he does not associate anyone with Him in his religion and does not show off (riya', i.e., performing deeds to be seen) in his deed. Al-Fudayl said: Abandoning deeds for the sake of people is riya', and doing deeds for the sake of people is shirk (associating partners with Allah), and sincerity is that Allah protects you from both of them.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you say﴾, meaning: Do you say? It is a form of interrogation, and its meaning is rebuke. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it with the letter ta' (tu), because of His words: ﴿Say: Do you dispute with us concerning Allah?﴾ and because He said after it: ﴿Say: Are you more knowledgeable, or is Allah?﴾ The others read it with the letter ya' (yu), meaning the Jews and the Christians say: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the tribes were Jews or Christians.﴾ ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿Are you more knowledgeable﴾ about their religion ﴿or is Allah?﴾ Allah has informed that Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif, a Muslim. ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals﴾, that is, hides ﴿a testimony he has from Allah﴾, which is their knowledge that Ibrahim and his sons were Muslims, and that Muhammad ﷺ is true and a messenger, which Allah made them bear witness to in their books. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

﴿That is a nation that has passed away. For them is what they earned, and for you is what you earned. And you will not be questioned about what they used to do.﴾ He repeated it for emphasis.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿The foolish among the people will say﴾, meaning the ignorant. ﴿What has turned them﴾, that is, diverted and changed them ﴿away from their qiblah which they had been facing﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis. Al-qiblah is a form derived from "facing" (al-muqabalah). It was revealed concerning the Jews and the polytheists of Makkah, who criticised the change of the qiblah from Bayt al-Maqdis to Makkah. They said to the polytheists of Makkah: Muhammad's affair has wavered; he yearned for his birthplace, and he has turned toward your land, and he is returning to your religion. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs the east and the west﴾, that is, He owns them, and creation are His servants.

﴿He guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾

﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾. It was revealed concerning the leaders of the Jews. They said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: Muhammad only abandoned our qiblah out of envy, and our qiblah is the qiblah of the prophets, and Muhammad knows that we are just among the people. Mu'adh said: We are upon truth and justice. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And thus﴾, that is, likewise. It was said: the kaf is for comparison, meaning: just as We chose Ibrahim and his offspring and preferred them, ﴿and thus We have made you a median nation﴾, which is linked to His words: ﴿And We had certainly chosen him in this world﴾ (2:130), that is, a just and excellent nation. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The best of them said﴾ (68:28), that is, the best and most just of them. The best of things is the middle of them. Al-Kalbi said: it means the people of a middle religion, between excess (ghuluww) and negligence (taqsir), since both are blameworthy in religion.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Ma'shar Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Warraq informed us: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu al-Salt informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us: Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us one day after the afternoon prayer, and he did not leave anything until the Day of Resurrection without mentioning it in that gathering, until the sun was on the tops of the palm trees and the edges of the walls. He said: "Indeed, nothing of this world that has passed remains except as much as remains of this day of yours. Note: this nation will live for seventy nations, and it is the last and the best of them, and the most honoured by Allah, exalted is He." [[Narrated by Ahmad: 3/19, and it is part of a hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Majah: in Zuhd, chapter: The description of the nation of Muhammad ﷺ, 2/1433, and its wording from Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed you have completed seventy nations; you are the best of them and the most honoured by Allah."]]

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, that the messengers had indeed conveyed to them. Al-Akhfash said: it is an apposition to His words "the religion of Ibrahim." ﴿And who is better than Allah in colouring?﴾ meaning, in religion. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ishaq ibn Mansur informed us: Abu Usamah informed us, saying: al-A'mash said: Abu Salih informed us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nuh will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: Did you convey? He will say: Yes, my Lord. Then his nation will be asked: Did he convey to you? They will say: No warner came to us. It will be said: Who are your witnesses? He will say: Muhammad and his nation." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Then you will be brought and you will testify." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: "And thus We have made you a median nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and that the Messenger may be a witness over you." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-I'tisam, chapter: "And thus We have made you a median nation," 13/316, and in Tafsir and al-Anbiya'. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/141.]]

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you had been facing﴾, that is, its change, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis. So it is from the omission of the qualifier (hadhf al-mudaf). It is also possible that the second object of "made" is omitted, with the sense: "And We did not make the qiblah which you had been facing a qiblah that was abrogated." It was said that its meaning is: "the one you are upon," which is the Ka'bah, as in His words: ﴿You are the best nation﴾, that is, you are.

﴿Except that We might know who follows the Messenger﴾. If it is said: what is the meaning of His words "except that We might know," when He knows all things before they exist? It was said: He meant the knowledge upon which reward and punishment depend, for it does not relate to what He knows in the unseen; it relates only to what exists. Its meaning is: that He might know the knowledge by which the doer deserves reward or punishment. It was also said: "except that We might know" means: that We might see and distinguish who follows the Messenger regarding the qiblah ﴿from those who turn back on their heels﴾, so that he apostatises. It is mentioned in a hadith that when the qiblah was changed, some Muslims reverted to Judaism, and they said: Muhammad has returned to the religion of his fathers. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its meaning is: "except that We might make known to Us," that is, who follows the Messenger from among those who turn back on their heels. As if it had already been decreed in His knowledge that the change of the qiblah would be a cause of guidance for some people and misguidance for others. The word for the future is sometimes used with the meaning of the past, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah?﴾ (2:91), that is, why did you kill them. ﴿And indeed it was﴾, that is, it had indeed been, meaning the turning toward the Ka'bah. It was said: the pronoun refers to the qiblah, and it was said: to the Ka'bah. Al-Zajjaj said: "And indeed the change was ﴿a great [matter]﴾, burdensome and severe ﴿except for those whom Allah has guided﴾, that is, whom Allah has guided. Sibawayh said: "in" (in) is an emphasis resembling an oath, and for this reason the lam entered its answer.

﴿And Allah would never have caused your faith to be lost﴾. This is because Huyayy ibn Akhtab and his companions among the Jews said to the Muslims: Tell us about your prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis. If it was guidance, then you have changed from it; and if it was misguidance, then you have worshipped Allah with it, and whoever of you dies upon it has died upon misguidance. The Muslims said: Guidance is only what Allah has commanded, and misguidance is what Allah has forbidden.

They said: Then what about your testimony concerning those among you who died upon our qiblah? Among the Muslims who had died before the qiblah was changed were As'ad ibn Zurarah of Banu al-Najjar, and al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur of Banu Salamah, who were among the nuqaba' (leaders of the pledge), and other men. Their clans went to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has turned you toward the qiblah of Ibrahim, so what about our brothers who died while they were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis? Then Allah revealed [[See Fath al-Bari, Kitab al-Tafsir, chapter "The foolish among the people will say...": 8/171. Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/167–169.]] ﴿And Allah would never have caused your faith to be lost﴾, meaning your prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿Indeed Allah is, toward the people, Kind and Merciful.﴾ The people of the Hijaz, Ibn Amir and Hafs read the word ra'uf with a lengthened vowel in the pattern fa'ul, because most of the names of Allah, exalted is He, follow the patterns fa'ul and fa'il, such as al-Ghafur, al-Shakur, al-Rahim, al-Karim and others. Abu Ja'far softens the hamzah. The others read it with a short vowel (ikhtilas) in the pattern fa'ul. Jarir said: "You see for the Muslims a right over you, like the deed of the one, the Kind (ra'uf), the Merciful."

Al-Ra'fah is the most intense mercy.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 138–143:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿the colouring of Allah﴾. Ibn Abbas, in the transmission of al-Kalbi, Qatadah and al-Hasan, said: the religion of Allah. He called it "colouring" because the effect of religion appears on the one who adheres to it, just as the effect of dye appears on cloth. It was said that it is because the one who adheres to religion is bound to it and does not part from it, as dye clings to cloth. Mujahid said: the natural disposition (fitrah) of Allah, which is close to the first meaning. It was said: the sunnah of Allah. It was also said: He meant circumcision, because it colours its bearer with blood. Ibn Abbas [[See: al-Wasit of al-Wahidi: 1/206.]] said: It is that when a child is born to one of the Christians and seven days pass over him, they immerse him in a yellowish water belonging to them, called al-Mu'ammadiyy, and they dye him with it, to purify him by that water in place of circumcision. When they have done this to him they say: "Now he has truly become a Christian." So Allah informed that His religion is Islam, not what the Christians do. It is in the accusative as an exhortation, meaning: adhere to the religion of Allah. Al-Akhfash said: it is an apposition to His words "the religion of Ibrahim." ﴿And who is better than Allah in colouring?﴾ meaning, in religion. It was said: in purification. ﴿And we are His worshippers﴾, meaning, obedient to Him.

﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the Jews and the Christians: ﴿Do you dispute with us concerning Allah?﴾, that is, concerning the religion of Allah. Al-muhajjah means arguing about Allah in order to demonstrate proof. This is because they said: the prophets were from among us and upon our religion, and our religion is more upright, so we have more right to Allah than you. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: Say: Do you dispute with us concerning Allah? ﴿And He is our Lord and your Lord﴾, that is, we and you are equal regarding Allah, for He is our Lord and your Lord. ﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds﴾, that is, each one has the recompense of his deed. So how can you claim that you have more right to Allah? ﴿And we are sincere to Him﴾, while you associate others with Him.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Sincerity (ikhlas) is that the servant makes his religion and his deed pure, so that he does not associate anyone with Him in his religion and does not show off (riya', i.e., performing deeds to be seen) in his deed. Al-Fudayl said: Abandoning deeds for the sake of people is riya', and doing deeds for the sake of people is shirk (associating partners with Allah), and sincerity is that Allah protects you from both of them.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you say﴾, meaning: Do you say? It is a form of interrogation, and its meaning is rebuke. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it with the letter ta' (tu), because of His words: ﴿Say: Do you dispute with us concerning Allah?﴾ and because He said after it: ﴿Say: Are you more knowledgeable, or is Allah?﴾ The others read it with the letter ya' (yu), meaning the Jews and the Christians say: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the tribes were Jews or Christians.﴾ ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿Are you more knowledgeable﴾ about their religion ﴿or is Allah?﴾ Allah has informed that Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif, a Muslim. ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals﴾, that is, hides ﴿a testimony he has from Allah﴾, which is their knowledge that Ibrahim and his sons were Muslims, and that Muhammad ﷺ is true and a messenger, which Allah made them bear witness to in their books. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

﴿That is a nation that has passed away. For them is what they earned, and for you is what you earned. And you will not be questioned about what they used to do.﴾ He repeated it for emphasis.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿The foolish among the people will say﴾, meaning the ignorant. ﴿What has turned them﴾, that is, diverted and changed them ﴿away from their qiblah which they had been facing﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis. Al-qiblah is a form derived from "facing" (al-muqabalah). It was revealed concerning the Jews and the polytheists of Makkah, who criticised the change of the qiblah from Bayt al-Maqdis to Makkah. They said to the polytheists of Makkah: Muhammad's affair has wavered; he yearned for his birthplace, and he has turned toward your land, and he is returning to your religion. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs the east and the west﴾, that is, He owns them, and creation are His servants.

﴿He guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾

﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾. It was revealed concerning the leaders of the Jews. They said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: Muhammad only abandoned our qiblah out of envy, and our qiblah is the qiblah of the prophets, and Muhammad knows that we are just among the people. Mu'adh said: We are upon truth and justice. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And thus﴾, that is, likewise. It was said: the kaf is for comparison, meaning: just as We chose Ibrahim and his offspring and preferred them, ﴿and thus We have made you a median nation﴾, which is linked to His words: ﴿And We had certainly chosen him in this world﴾ (2:130), that is, a just and excellent nation. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The best of them said﴾ (68:28), that is, the best and most just of them. The best of things is the middle of them. Al-Kalbi said: it means the people of a middle religion, between excess (ghuluww) and negligence (taqsir), since both are blameworthy in religion.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Ma'shar Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Warraq informed us: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu al-Salt informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us: Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us one day after the afternoon prayer, and he did not leave anything until the Day of Resurrection without mentioning it in that gathering, until the sun was on the tops of the palm trees and the edges of the walls. He said: "Indeed, nothing of this world that has passed remains except as much as remains of this day of yours. Note: this nation will live for seventy nations, and it is the last and the best of them, and the most honoured by Allah, exalted is He." [[Narrated by Ahmad: 3/19, and it is part of a hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Majah: in Zuhd, chapter: The description of the nation of Muhammad ﷺ, 2/1433, and its wording from Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed you have completed seventy nations; you are the best of them and the most honoured by Allah."]]

Ibn Juraij said: I said to Ata: What is the meaning of His words, exalted is He, "so that you may be witnesses over the people"? He said: The nation of Muhammad ﷺ are witnesses over whoever among all people abandons the truth. ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾, Muhammad ﷺ, as one who vouches for and certifies you. This is because Allah gathers the first and the last in one plain, then He says to the disbelievers of the past nations: ﴿Did there not come to you a warner?﴾ (67:8). They deny and say: No bringer of good tidings or warner came to us. Allah then asks the prophets, peace be upon them, about that, and they say: They have lied; we had indeed conveyed to them. He asks them for evidence, although He knows them best, to establish the proof. The nation of Muhammad ﷺ is then brought, and they testify for them that they had conveyed. The past nations say: How do they know, when they came after us? So He asks this nation, and they say: You sent to us a messenger and revealed to him a book, in which You informed us of the conveyance of the messengers, and You are truthful in what You inform. Then Muhammad ﷺ is brought, and he is asked about the state of his nation, and he vouches for them and testifies to their truthfulness.
