**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 144:**

God Most High says: ﴿We have seen the turning of your face towards the sky﴾. This verse, although it comes later in the recitation, comes earlier in meaning, for it is the head of the story. The matter of the qiblah was the first matter of the Sharia to be abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a earlier ruling by a later one). The reason was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions used to pray in Makkah facing the Ka'bah. When he emigrated to Madinah, Allah commanded him to pray facing the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), so that it would be closer to the Jews accepting him when he prayed towards their qiblah, given what they found of his description in the Torah. He therefore prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months after the Hijrah. He loved to be turned towards the Ka'bah, because it was the qiblah of his father Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Mujahid said: he loved this for the sake of the Jews, because they used to say, "Muhammad opposes us in our religion and follows our qiblah." So he said to Jibril (peace be upon him): "I wish that Allah would turn me to the Ka'bah, for it is the qiblah of my father Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." Jibril said: "I am only a servant like you, and you are honoured before your Lord. Ask your Lord, for you have a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Then Jibril departed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to gaze steadily at the sky, hoping that Jibril would descend with what he loved concerning the matter of the qiblah. [Al-Suyuti said in ad-Durr al-Manthur: Abu Dawud recorded it in his Nasikh (book on abrogation) from Abu al-'Aliyah, 1/343.] Then Allah Most High revealed: ﴿We have seen the turning of your face towards the sky, so We shall surely turn you to a qiblah﴾, meaning, We shall surely change you to a qiblah, ﴿that you will be pleased with﴾, that is, that you love and desire. ﴿So turn﴾, that is, change, ﴿your face towards the Sacred Mosque﴾, that is, towards it, and by it he meant the Ka'bah; al-Haram means the forbidden (sanctuary). ﴿And wherever you are﴾, whether on land or sea, east or west, ﴿turn your faces towards it﴾ during prayer.

Al-Baghawi (his chain of narration): We were informed by Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was informed by Ishaq ibn Nasr, who was informed by Abd al-Razzaq, who was informed by Ibn Juraij, from Ata', who said: I heard Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) say: When the Prophet (ﷺ) entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners and did not pray until he came out of it. When he came out, he prayed two rak'ahs facing the qiblah of the Ka'bah, and he said: "This is the qiblah." [Al-Bukhari recorded it in the Book of the Qiblah, chapter: the saying of Allah, "And take from the station of Ibrahim a place of prayer" (2:125), 1/501. Muslim recorded it in the Book of Hajj, chapter: the recommendation for the pilgrim and others to enter the Ka'bah, no. 1330, 2/968, from Usamah ibn Zayd. The author (al-Baghawi) mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/334.]

We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was informed by Amr ibn Khalid, who was informed by Zuhayr, who was informed by Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' (that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he first came to Madinah, stayed with his grandfathers, or he said his maternal uncles, from the Ansar; and that he prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months; and he loved that his qiblah would be towards the House. And that the first prayer he prayed was the Asr prayer, and a group prayed with him. A man from among those who prayed with him went out and passed by the people of the mosque of Quba', who were bowing, and he said: "I bear witness before Allah that I prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) facing Makkah," so they turned as they were, towards the House. The Jews had been pleased when he prayed towards al-Maqdis, because it was the qiblah of the People of the Book; but when he turned his face towards the House, they denied that. Al-Bara', in this narration, said: "Men died while facing the qiblah before it was changed, and they were killed, and we did not know what to say about them." So Allah Most High revealed: ﴿And Allah would not let your faith go to waste﴾.) [Al-Bukhari recorded it in the Book of Tafsir, chapter: "The foolish among the people will say, 'What has turned them from their qiblah?'" (2:142), 8/171. Muslim recorded it in the Book of Mosques and Places of Prayer, chapter: the change of the qiblah from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah, no. 525, 1/374. The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/322-323.]

The change of the qiblah happened in Rajab, after the sun had passed its zenith, two months before the battle of Badr. Mujahid and others said: this verse was revealed while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the Mosque of Banu Salamah, and he had led his Companions in two rak'ahs of the Dhuhr prayer; so he turned during the prayer, facing the mihrab (the niche indicating the qiblah), and the men moved to the place of the women and the women to the place of the men. That mosque was therefore named the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs. It was also said: the change occurred outside the prayer, between the two prayers, and the news reached the people of Quba' during the Subh (dawn) prayer.

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi, who was informed by Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih al-Sarakhsi, who was informed by Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi al-Samarri, who was informed by Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Anas, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, that Abd Allah ibn Umar said: While the people were at Quba' in the Subh prayer, a caller came to them and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has received a Qur'an tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka'bah, so face it." Their faces had been towards Syria, so they turned around towards the Ka'bah. [Al-Bukhari recorded it in the Book of Tafsir, chapter: "And even if you were to bring to those who were given the Scripture every sign" (2:145), 8/174. Muslim recorded it in the Book of Mosques and Places of Prayer, chapter: the change of the qiblah from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah, no. 526, 1/375. The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/323-324.]

When the qiblah was changed, the Jews said: "O Muhammad, this is only something you have innovated of your own accord. Sometimes you pray towards Bayt al-Maqdis and sometimes towards the Ka'bah. If you had stayed on our qiblah, we would have hoped that you were our companion whom we are waiting for." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it﴾, meaning the matter of the Ka'bah, ﴿is the truth from their Lord﴾. Then He threatened them, saying: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the letter ta' (you do, addressed to the believers). Ibn Abbas said: it means that you, O company of believers, seek My pleasure, and I am not unaware of your reward and recompense. The rest read it with the letter ya' (they do), meaning: I am not unaware of what the Jews do, and I will requite them in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 145:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you were to bring to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah﴾. He means the Jews and the Christians. They said: "Bring us a sign for what you say." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you were to bring to those who were given the Scripture every sign﴾ [every miraculous sign] ﴿they would not follow your qiblah﴾, meaning the Ka'bah, ﴿nor are you a follower of their qiblah, nor are some of them followers of the qiblah of others﴾. This is because the Jews face Bayt al-Maqdis, which is to the west, and the Christians face the east, while the qiblah of the Muslims is the Ka'bah.

Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jirahi informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu 'Isa Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us: al-Hasan ibn Bakr al-Marwazi informed us: al-Mu'alla ibn Mansur informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Makhzumi related to us from 'Uthman al-Akhnasi, from Sa'id al-Maqbari, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The qiblah is between the east and the west." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salah: Chapter on what has come that what is between the east and the west is a qiblah: 2/317-319, and he said: a hasan sahih hadith. And Ibn Majah in Iqamat al-Salah, chapter: al-Qiblah, no. (1011), with the wording "What is between the east and the west is a qiblah." And al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/205-206, from Ibn 'Umar. And al-Bayhaqi: 2/9. See also Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/277-281.]]

He intended by this, with regard to the people of the east, and by "the east" he meant the sunrise point of winter on the shortest day of the year, and by "the west" the sunset point of summer on the longest day of the year. Whoever places the sunset of summer at this time on his right and the sunrise of winter on his left, his face is toward the qiblah.

﴿And if you were to follow their desires﴾, their intended address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), while the intended meaning is the Ummah, ﴿after the knowledge that has come to you﴾ [the truth concerning the qiblah], ﴿indeed, you would then be among the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 146–149:

Allah's words: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book﴾ mean the believers among the People of the Book, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and his companions. ﴿They recognize him﴾ means they recognize Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿as they recognize their own sons﴾ among the boys.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said to ʿAbdullah ibn Salam: "Allah has revealed to His Prophet: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons.﴾ So what is this recognition?" ʿAbdullah said: "O ʿUmar, I recognized him the moment I saw him, as I recognize my son, and my recognition of Muhammad (ﷺ) is stronger than my recognition of my son." ʿUmar said: "How so?" He said: "I testify that he is the Messenger of Allah, a truth from Allah, the Exalted, and Allah has described him in our Book. But I do not know what the women do." ʿUmar said: "May Allah grant you success, O son of Salam, for you have spoken the truth." [[Narrated by al-Tha'labi from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas. In its chain is al-Kalbi, who is a liar. (Al-Fath al-Samawi, 1/195). See: al-Wasit by al-Wahidi, 1/215; also his Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 40.]]

﴿But a party of them conceal the truth﴾ means the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the matter of the Ka'bah, ﴿while they know﴾.

Then He said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾. That is, this truth is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), i.e. هَذَا الْحَقُّ (this is the truth). It was also said that it is in the nominative by means of an omitted verb, i.e. جَاءَكَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ (the truth has come to you from your Lord). ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾, the skeptics.

Allah's words: ﴿For every community there is a direction﴾. That is, for the people of every religion there is a qibla. Al-wijhah (direction) is the name of that toward which one turns. ﴿He turns toward it﴾, that is, he faces it and moves toward it. It is said: walaytuhu and walaytu ilayhi, meaning I turned toward him/it, and walaytu ʿanhu, meaning I turned away from him. Mujahid said: ﴿He turns toward it﴾ means he turns his face toward it. Al-Akhfash said: it is a metaphor (kinayah) for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meaning that Allah turns the nations toward their qiblah. Ibn ʿAmir read مُوَلَّاهَا (mawallaha), i.e. the one who faces it is turned toward it. ﴿So race to the good works﴾, that is, to the good things; meaning, hasten to the acts of obedience. The intended meaning is hastening to accept (the command). ﴿Wherever you are﴾, you and the People of the Book, ﴿Allah will bring you all together﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, and He will repay you for your deeds. ﴿Indeed, Allah has power over all things.﴾

Allah's words: ﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and indeed it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Abu ʿAmr read it with the ya' (يَعْمَلُونَ, "they do"), and the rest read it with the ta' (تَعْمَلُونَ, "you do").

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 150:

﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.﴾ He repeated it to emphasize the abrogation (naskh, the replacement of one ruling by another). ﴿So that people will have no argument against you, except those who do wrong.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of this verse and the sense of the word ﴿except﴾ (illa). Some of them said: its meaning is that the qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah, ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾ if you face other than it, and they would say, "You have no qiblah," ﴿except those who do wrong﴾, namely the Quraysh and the Jews. As for the Quraysh, they would say, "Muhammad has returned to the Ka'bah, because he knew that it is the truth and that it is the qiblah of his forefathers, so he will likewise return to our religion." As for the Jews, they would say, "He did not turn away from Bayt al-Maqdis while knowing that it is the truth, except that he acts according to his own opinion." Others said: ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾ refers to the Jews, and their argument, by way of contention against the believers regarding their prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis, was that they would say, "Muhammad and his companions did not know where their qiblah was until we guided them."

As for His words ﴿except those who do wrong﴾, they refer to the polytheists of Makkah, and their argument was that when their qiblah was turned to the Ka'bah they said, "Muhammad has become confused in his religion, and he will return to our creed just as he returned to our qiblah." This is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid, 'Ata' and Qatadah. According to these two interpretations, the exception is sound. His words ﴿except those who do wrong⁠﴾ mean: no one has an argument against you except the polytheists of Quraysh, for they will dispute with you, contend with you and argue against you with falsehood and injustice. Argument based on falsehood is also called an argument (hujjah), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their argument is void in the sight of their Lord﴾ (42:16). The position of ﴿alladhina⁠﴾ (those who) is in the genitive case, as if He had said: "other than those who do wrong." This is the view of al-Kisa'i. Al-Farra' said it is in the accusative by virtue of the exception.

His words, Exalted is He, ﴿minhum⁠﴾ mean "from among the people." It has also been said that this is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati') from the earlier statement, meaning: "But those who do wrong argue with you with falsehood," just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption﴾ (4:157), meaning: "but they follow assumption." It is like a man saying, "You owe me nothing except that you wrong me."

Abu Rawq said: ﴿so that people will have no argument﴾ refers to the Jews, ﴿against you﴾. The reason is that they knew the Ka'bah was the qiblah of Ibrahim, and they found in the Torah that Muhammad would be turned toward it, so Allah the Exalted turned him toward it so that they would have no argument, for they would say: "The prophet whom we find in our book would be turned toward it, and you were not turned." When he was turned toward it, their argument vanished. ﴿Except those who do wrong⁠﴾ means: except those who do wrong by concealing what they knew of the truth.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: His words ﴿except those who do wrong⁠﴾ are not an exception, but "illa" stands in the place of the conjunction waw, meaning: "and those who do wrong also will have no argument," just as the poet said: "And every brother who parts from his brother... by the life of your father, except the two Farqads," meaning: "and the two Farqads also part." So the meaning of the verse is: turn toward the Ka'bah, ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿who would say: why did you abandon the Ka'bah, which is the qiblah of Ibrahim, while you are upon his religion?⁠﴾ and not those who do wrong, who are the polytheists of Makkah, who would say: why did Muhammad abandon the qiblah of his grandfather and turn away from it to the qiblah of the Jews? ﴿So do not fear them⁠﴾ regarding your turning toward the Ka'bah, or their support against you through disputation, for I am your Protector; I will make you prevail over them with proof and victory. ﴿And fear Me, and that I may complete My favor upon you⁠﴾ is coordinated with His words ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾, meaning: and so that I may complete My favor upon you by My guidance of you to the qiblah of Ibrahim, so that the upright religion (al-millah al-hanifiyyah) is complete for you. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the completion of the favor is death upon Islam.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: a favor is not completed upon a Muslim except that Allah admits him into Paradise. ﴿And that you may be guided⁠﴾ means: so that you may be guided away from misguidance. "La'alla" and "'asa" from Allah are binding.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 151:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As We have sent among you﴾. This kaf is for comparison (tashbih), and it needs something to which it refers. Some of them said: it refers to what precedes it, meaning: ﴿And that I may complete My favour upon you, and that you may be guided﴾ (2:150), just as We have sent among you a messenger. Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, made two supplications. The first was when he said: ﴿Our Lord, and make us Muslims [submitting] to You, and of our descendants a Muslim nation [submitting] to You﴾ (2:128). The second was his saying: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves﴾ (2:129). So God sent the Messenger, who is Muhammad ﷺ, and He promised to answer the second supplication by placing among his descendants a Muslim nation. That is, just as I answered his supplication by guiding you to his religion, making you Muslims, and completing My favour upon you by explaining the laws of the upright religion (al-milla al-hanifiyya).[[Al-Tabari said in his tafsir (3/208-209): "He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: 'As We have sent among you a messenger, and that I may complete My favour upon you by explaining the laws of your upright religion, and guide you to the religion of My friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him, so I grant you his supplication with which he called upon Me and his request which he asked of Me, when he said: "Our Lord, and make us Muslims [submitting] to You, and of our descendants a Muslim nation [submitting] to You, and show us our rites and turn to us in forgiveness. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful" (Surah al-Baqarah: 128), just as I have granted you his supplication with which he called upon Me, and his request which he asked of Me, when he said: "Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise" (Surah al-Baqarah: 129). So I have sent to you from among you My messenger whom my friend Ibrahim and his son Isma'il asked Me to send from their descendants."]] Mujahid, 'Ata' and al-Kalbi said: it is connected to what follows it, which is His saying: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ (2:152), meaning: as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, so remember Me. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/210.]] This verse is addressed to the people of Makkah and the Arabs, meaning: as We have sent among you, O assembly of the Arabs.

﴿A messenger from yourselves﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿Reciting to you Our verses﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿And purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom﴾. It was said: wisdom (al-hikmah) is the Sunnah; and it was said: it is the admonitions (mawa'iz) of the Qur'an. ﴿And teaching you that which you did not know﴾: the rulings (al-ahkam) and the laws of Islam.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 152:

﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Remember Me through obedience to Me, and I will remember you through My forgiveness." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Remember Me in ease and prosperity, and I will remember you in hardship and affliction." Its explanation is in ﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify (Allah), he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾ (37:143-144).

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Umar ibn Hafs informed us; my father informed us; al-A'mash informed us, saying: I heard Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs. If he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.'"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tawhid - chapter: the saying of Allah the Exalted, "And Allah warns you of Himself": 13/384. Muslim in Dhikr, Du'a and Repentance - chapter on urging the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, no. (2675) 4/61. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/273.]]

Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Qadi informed us, and Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Tawbah al-Kushmihani narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Siraj al-Tahhan informed us; Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Quraysh ibn Sulayman informed us; Abu Abd al-Malik al-Dimashqi informed us; Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us; Mundhir ibn Ziyad informed us, from Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah, from al-Hasan, from Anas, who said: "Indeed I heard this hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, counting these ten fingers of mine, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, if you remember Me in yourself, I remember you in Myself; and if you remember Me in an assembly, I remember you in an assembly better than it. If you draw near to Me a span, I draw near to you a cubit; if you draw near to Me a cubit, I draw near to you a fathom; if you walk toward Me, I hasten toward you; and if you hasten toward Me, I rush toward you; if you ask Me, I give you; and if you do not ask Me, I become angry with you.'"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tawhid - chapter: the saying of Allah the Exalted, "And Allah warns you of Himself": 13/384. Muslim in Dhikr, Du'a and Repentance - chapter: the virtue of dhikr and du'a, no. (2675) 4/2067, via Anas; it also comes via Abu Dhar, and the wording of this narration differs from that in al-Bukhari.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us; Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us; Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us; Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us; Yahya ibn Abd Allah informed us; al-Awza'i informed us; Isma'il ibn Abd Allah informed us, from Abu al-Darda', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I am with My servant so long as he remembers Me and his lips move with Me."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in suspended form in Tawhid - chapter: the saying of Allah, "Do not move your tongue with it": 13/499. Ibn Hibban in al-Adhkar p. 576 (Mawarid al-Zam'an). Ibn Hajar said this is a part of a hadith narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari in Khalq Af'al al-'Ibad, and al-Tabarani from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Isma'il ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhajir, from Karima bint al-Hassas, from Abu Hurayrah; al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, Ibn Majah, al-Hakim and Ibn Hibban also narrated it from various chains. See Fath al-Bari 13/500, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 5/13, with the commentary of Shaykh al-Arna'ut.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us; Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us; Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us; Isma'il ibn Ayyash informed us; Amr ibn Qays al-Sakuni informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Busr, who said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, which deeds are best?" He said: "That you depart this world while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of Allah the Exalted."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Du'a - chapter: the virtue of dhikr, 9/314-315, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith from this route. Ahmad 4/188, 190 from Abd Allah ibn Busr with different wording. Ibn Hibban in al-Adhkar - chapter: the virtue of dhikr and those who remember (Mawarid al-Zam'an), no. (2318) p. 576.]].

The Exalted saying: ﴿And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾. That is: be grateful to Me through obedience, and do not deny Me through disobedience, for whoever obeys Allah has indeed thanked Him, and whoever disobeys Him has indeed denied Him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 153–154:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾, "by aid and support."

﴿And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not﴾. It was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr from among the Muslims, who were fourteen men: six from the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and eight from the Ansar (Helpers). People used to say of whoever was killed in the way of Allah, "So-and-so has died, and the delights and pleasures of this world have departed from him." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not﴾. Similarly, He said concerning the martyrs of Uhud: ﴿And never think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ (3:169). Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, the martyrs are alive with Allah, exalted is He. Their provisions are presented to their souls, so joy and delight reach them, just as the Fire is presented to the souls of the family of Pharaoh morning and evening, so pain reaches them."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 153–154:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾, "by aid and support."

﴿And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not﴾. It was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr from among the Muslims, who were fourteen men: six from the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and eight from the Ansar (Helpers). People used to say of whoever was killed in the way of Allah, "So-and-so has died, and the delights and pleasures of this world have departed from him." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not﴾. Similarly, He said concerning the martyrs of Uhud: ﴿And never think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ (3:169). Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, the martyrs are alive with Allah, exalted is He. Their provisions are presented to their souls, so joy and delight reach them, just as the Fire is presented to the souls of the family of Pharaoh morning and evening, so pain reaches them."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 155–157:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you﴾, meaning: and We will surely try you, O community of Muhammad. The lam is the lam of the answer to an oath, its implied sense being "By Allah, We will surely test you." Testing (ibtila') from Allah is for the manifestation of the obedient from the disobedient, not so that He may know something He did not already know. ﴿With something of fear﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means fear of the enemy. ﴿And hunger﴾, meaning famine. ﴿And loss of wealth﴾ through losses and destruction. ﴿And lives﴾, meaning through killing and death; and it was said: through sickness and graying of hair. ﴿And fruits﴾, meaning calamities befalling crops. It is related from al-Shafi'i that he said: the fear is the fear of Allah the Exalted, the hunger is fasting in Ramadan, the loss of wealth is paying zakat and charities, the lives are illnesses, and the fruits are the death of children, because a man's child is the fruit of his heart.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliehi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjuyah informed us, al-Hasan ibn Musa informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Abu Sinan, who said: I buried my son Sinan, and Abu Talhah al-Khawlani was at the edge of the grave. When I wanted to leave, he took my hand and brought me out, and said: "Shall I not give you good news? Al-Dahhak told me, from 'Arzab, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When a servant's child dies, Allah the Exalted says to His angels: "Have you taken the child of My servant?" They say: "Yes." He says: "Have you taken the fruit of his heart?" They say: "Yes." He says: "What did My servant say?" They say: "He praised You and said *istirja'*." He says: "Build for him a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise."'"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Janaiz, chapter: The Merit of Affliction When One Seeks Reward: 4/101, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/456. The editor said: In its chain is Abu Sinan, whose name is Isa ibn Sinan al-Qasmali; al-Hafiz [Ibn Hajar] described him as weak in al-Taqrib. Ibn Ma'in said: "His hadith is weak." Abu Zur'ah said: "He was confused" (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib). Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. Ibn Hibban authenticated it in Mawarid al-Zam'an, no. 726, p. 185. Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, pp. 12–13: "Ahmad and others narrated it from a hadith, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Shu'ab both marfu' and mawquf." al-Albani mentioned it in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah, no. 1408, and said: "The hadith, by the totality of its chains, is hasan at the least."]]

﴿And give good news to the patient﴾, those who are patient in tribulations and calamities. Then He described them, saying:

﴿Those who, when a disaster strikes them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah﴾, as slaves and possessions, ﴿and indeed to Him we will return﴾ in the Hereafter.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliehi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjuyah informed us, Muhadir ibn al-Muwarri' informed us, Sa'd informed us, from Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, who informed us, from the mawla of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No calamity befalls a servant who says: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better,' except that Allah will reward him in his calamity and replace it for him with something better." Umm Salamah said: When Abu Salamah died, I said what Allah had commanded me: "O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better." And Allah replaced for me the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Janaiz, chapter: What is said at a calamity: no. 918, 2/632–633. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/293–294.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No one has been given in calamity what this community has been given, meaning *al-istirja'*. And if anyone had been given it, Ya'qub (peace be upon him) would have been given it. Do you not hear His saying, the Exalted, in the story of Yusuf (peace be upon him): ﴿Oh, my grief over Yusuf!﴾ (12:84).

﴿Those﴾, the people of this description, ﴿upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy﴾. Blessings (salawat) here means mercy, for the prayer (salah) from Allah is mercy. And "mercy" is mentioned by Allah for emphasis, and all the blessings, meaning: mercy after mercy. ﴿And those are the ones guided﴾ to the *istirja'*. It was also said: to the truth and the right, and it was said: to Paradise and reward. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What an excellent pair, and what an excellent addition."[[Narrated by al-Wahidi in al-Wasit with his chain from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): 1/226. al-Qurtubi said in al-Tafsir: 2/177: "He meant by the two pairs: the blessing and the mercy; and by the addition: the guidance."]] So the two pairs are the blessing and the mercy, and the addition is the guidance.

Reports have come concerning the reward of the afflicted and the recompense of the patient. Among them is what Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah, that he said: I heard Abu al-Hubab Sa'id ibn Yasar say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whomever Allah wills good for, He afflicts with trials."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Marda, chapter: What has come concerning the expiation of illness: 10/103. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/232.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliehi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Na'imi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, Abd al-Malik ibn Amr informed us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad informed us, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Halhalah, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No fatigue, nor sickness, nor anxiety, nor grief, nor harm, nor distress befalls a Muslim, not even a thorn that pricks him, except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Marda, chapter: What has come concerning the expiation of illness: 10/103. Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter: The reward of the believer for what befalls him: no. 2573, 4/1993. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/233.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliehi informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjuyah informed us, Muhammad ibn Ubayd informed us, Muhammad ibn Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A woman who had *lamam* (a mild affliction of the jinn) came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He cures me." He said: "If you wish, I will pray to Allah to cure you, and if you wish, be patient and there is no reckoning for you." She said: "Rather I will be patient, and there is no reckoning for me."[[Ibn Hibban in al-Janaiz, chapter: Patience with *lamam*, p. 182. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/236. Its chain is strong; it was also narrated by al-Bazzar.]]

Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, Abu Sa'id Khalaf ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nizar informed us, Abu Mansur al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Nadrawi informed us, Ahmad ibn Najdah informed us, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, from Asim, who is Ibn Abi al-Najud, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the people who are most severely tested. He said: "The prophets, then the most excellent, then the most excellent. A man is tested according to his religion. If he is firm in his religion, he is tested according to that degree, and if there is weakness in his religion, it is lightened for him. So he continues thus until he walks upon the earth with no sin upon him."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter: On patience with affliction: 7/78–79, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, chapter: Patience with affliction, no. 4023, 2/1334. al-Darimi in al-Riqaq, chapter: On the people most severely tested: 2/320. Ahmad: 1/172, 174, 180, 185, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from his father. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/244. Its chain is hasan, and al-Hakim and Ibn Hibban authenticated it.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliehi informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjuyah informed us, Abd Allah ibn Salih informed us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Sinan, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, the greatness of the reward with Allah is with the greatness of the trial. For when Allah loves a people, He tests them. Whoever is content, for him is contentment, and whoever is angry, for him is anger."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter: Patience with affliction: 7/77–78, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route." Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, chapter: Patience with affliction, no. 4031, 2/1338. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/245. See the margin of Sharh al-Sunnah.]]

Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Muhammad ibn Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Affliction will not cease for the believing man and woman in their self, their wealth, and their children, until they meet Allah with no sin upon them."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter: Patience with affliction: 7/80, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." al-Hakim: 1/346, and he authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed. Ahmad: 2/287, 450, from Abu Hurayrah. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/246.]]

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bishran informed us, Abu Ali Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi informed us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the believer is like the likeness of a field of crops: the wind keeps bending it, and the believer continues to be struck by affliction. And the likeness of the hypocrite is like the likeness of the cedar tree [al-arzah]{Al-arzah: with the letter ra' either sukun or fatha, a tree known as the cedar; some said it is the pine; some said it is "arzah" in the pattern fa'ilah, but Abu Ubaydah denied it. Al-Nihayah 1/38.}, which does not shake until it is cut down."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter: On will and intention: 13/446. Muslim in al-Munafiqin, chapter: The likeness of the believer is like the field of crops, no. 2809, 4/2163, and the wording is his. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/247.]]

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran informed us, Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi informed us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-I'zar ibn Hurayth, from Umar ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer! If good befalls him, he praises Allah and gives thanks, and if a calamity befalls him, he praises Allah and is patient. So the believer is rewarded in every matter, even for the morsel he raises to the mouth of his wife."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Zuhd, chapter: The believer's affair is entirely good, from Suhayb, no. 2999, 4/2295, with the wording: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer! His whole affair is good for him, and this is not so for anyone except the believer: if he is given ease, he is grateful, and that is good for him; and if he is afflicted with hardship, he is patient, and that is good for him." The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/448.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 155–157:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you﴾, meaning: and We will surely try you, O community of Muhammad. The lam is the lam of the answer to an oath, its implied sense being "By Allah, We will surely test you." Testing (ibtila') from Allah is for the manifestation of the obedient from the disobedient, not so that He may know something He did not already know. ﴿With something of fear﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means fear of the enemy. ﴿And hunger﴾, meaning famine. ﴿And loss of wealth﴾ through losses and destruction. ﴿And lives﴾, meaning through killing and death; and it was said: through sickness and graying of hair. ﴿And fruits﴾, meaning calamities befalling crops. It is related from al-Shafi'i that he said: the fear is the fear of Allah the Exalted, the hunger is fasting in Ramadan, the loss of wealth is paying zakat and charities, the lives are illnesses, and the fruits are the death of children, because a man's child is the fruit of his heart.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliehi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjuyah informed us, al-Hasan ibn Musa informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Abu Sinan, who said: I buried my son Sinan, and Abu Talhah al-Khawlani was at the edge of the grave. When I wanted to leave, he took my hand and brought me out, and said: "Shall I not give you good news? Al-Dahhak told me, from 'Arzab, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When a servant's child dies, Allah the Exalted says to His angels: "Have you taken the child of My servant?" They say: "Yes." He says: "Have you taken the fruit of his heart?" They say: "Yes." He says: "What did My servant say?" They say: "He praised You and said *istirja'*." He says: "Build for him a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise."'"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Janaiz, chapter: The Merit of Affliction When One Seeks Reward: 4/101, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/456. The editor said: In its chain is Abu Sinan, whose name is Isa ibn Sinan al-Qasmali; al-Hafiz [Ibn Hajar] described him as weak in al-Taqrib. Ibn Ma'in said: "His hadith is weak." Abu Zur'ah said: "He was confused" (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib). Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. Ibn Hibban authenticated it in Mawarid al-Zam'an, no. 726, p. 185. Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, pp. 12–13: "Ahmad and others narrated it from a hadith, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Shu'ab both marfu' and mawquf." al-Albani mentioned it in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah, no. 1408, and said: "The hadith, by the totality of its chains, is hasan at the least."]]

﴿And give good news to the patient﴾, those who are patient in tribulations and calamities. Then He described them, saying:

﴿Those who, when a disaster strikes them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah﴾, as slaves and possessions, ﴿and indeed to Him we will return﴾ in the Hereafter.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliehi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjuyah informed us, Muhadir ibn al-Muwarri' informed us, Sa'd informed us, from Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, who informed us, from the mawla of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No calamity befalls a servant who says: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better,' except that Allah will reward him in his calamity and replace it for him with something better." Umm Salamah said: When Abu Salamah died, I said what Allah had commanded me: "O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better." And Allah replaced for me the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Janaiz, chapter: What is said at a calamity: no. 918, 2/632–633. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/293–294.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No one has been given in calamity what this community has been given, meaning *al-istirja'*. And if anyone had been given it, Ya'qub (peace be upon him) would have been given it. Do you not hear His saying, the Exalted, in the story of Yusuf (peace be upon him): ﴿Oh, my grief over Yusuf!﴾ (12:84).

﴿Those﴾, the people of this description, ﴿upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy﴾. Blessings (salawat) here means mercy, for the prayer (salah) from Allah is mercy. And "mercy" is mentioned by Allah for emphasis, and all the blessings, meaning: mercy after mercy. ﴿And those are the ones guided﴾ to the *istirja'*. It was also said: to the truth and the right, and it was said: to Paradise and reward. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What an excellent pair, and what an excellent addition."[[Narrated by al-Wahidi in al-Wasit with his chain from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): 1/226. al-Qurtubi said in al-Tafsir: 2/177: "He meant by the two pairs: the blessing and the mercy; and by the addition: the guidance."]] So the two pairs are the blessing and the mercy, and the addition is the guidance.

Reports have come concerning the reward of the afflicted and the recompense of the patient. Among them is what Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah, that he said: I heard Abu al-Hubab Sa'id ibn Yasar say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whomever Allah wills good for, He afflicts with trials."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Marda, chapter: What has come concerning the expiation of illness: 10/103. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/232.]]

Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter: The reward of the believer for what befalls him: no. 2573, 4/1993. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/233.]]

Its chain is strong; it was also narrated by al-Bazzar.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 158:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾. Al-Safa is the plural of safah, which is a hard, smooth, solid rock. It is said: safah and safa, like hasah and hasa (pebble and pebbles), and nawah and nawa (date stone and date stones). Al-Marwah is a soft stone; its plural is marawat, and the plural of the collective is marw, like tamrah, tamarat and tamr (a date, dates, and dates collectively). By these two He means the two well-known mountains in Makkah at the two ends of al-Mas'a (the place of sa'y), and for this reason He added the definite article (al) to them. Sha'a'ir Allah (the symbols of Allah) are the markers of His religion. Its root is from al-ish'ar, which is informing (ilam), and its singular is sha'irah. Everything that is a marker for an offering by which one draws near to Allah, may He be exalted, whether prayer, supplication or sacrifice, is a sha'irah. So the place of circumambulation (al-mataf), the place of standing (al-mawqif) and the place of sacrifice (al-nahr) are all symbols of Allah, and similarly the mashа'ir (rites sites). The meaning of "symbols" here is the rites which Allah made markers of His obedience. So al-Safa and al-Marwah are among them, so that they are circumambulated together. ﴿So whoever performs the Hajj to the House or makes the 'umrah﴾. Linguistically, hajj means intention (al-qasd), and 'umrah means visitation (al-ziyarah). In the lawful hajj and 'umrah there is intention and visitation. ﴿there is no blame upon him﴾, meaning there is no sin upon him. Its origin is from janaha, meaning he deviated from the intended course. ﴿in going back and forth between them﴾, meaning circling around them. Its origin is yataṭawwaf, and the ta' was assimilated into the ta' (of the verb form), so it became yaṭṭawwaf.

The occasion of revelation of this verse was that on al-Safa and al-Marwah there were two idols, Isaf and Na'ilah. Isaf was on al-Safa and Na'ilah was on al-Marwah. The people of the Jahiliyyah used to circumambulate between al-Safa and al-Marwah, venerating the two idols and rubbing against them. When Islam came and the idols were broken, the Muslims used to feel uneasy about performing sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah on account of the two idols. So Allah permitted it and informed that it is among the symbols of Allah. [[Al-Bukhari reported from 'Urwah who said: I asked 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and I said to her: Have you considered the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs the Hajj to the House or makes 'umrah, there is no blame upon him in going back and forth between them." By Allah, is there no blame upon anyone for not going back and forth between al-Safa and al-Marwah? She said: Evil is what you said, O nephew. If this were as you interpret it, it would be "there is no blame upon him for not going back and forth between them." Rather, it was revealed concerning the Ansar, who used to assume ihram for Manat, the idol worshipped at al-Mushallal. Whoever among them assumed ihram would feel uneasy about going back and forth between al-Safa and al-Marwah. When they embraced Islam, they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, we used to feel uneasy about going back and forth between al-Safa and al-Marwah." So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah," and the verse. 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established going back and forth between them, so no one has the right to abandon going back and forth between them.]]

The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse and the obligation of sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah in hajj and 'umrah. A group held that it is obligatory, and this is the view of Ibn 'Umar, Jabir and 'A'ishah, and al-Hasan said likewise, and Malik and al-Shafi'i also held this. Another group held that it is voluntary (tatawwu'), and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Sirin and Mujahid said likewise, and Sufyan al-Thawri and the Ashab al-Ra'y (the people of opinion, i.e., the Hanafis) held this. Al-Thawri and the Ashab al-Ra'y said: whoever abandons it incurs a penalty of blood (a sacrifice) [[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/183; Ahkam al-Qur'an by Ibn al-'Arabi: 1/48; Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas: 1/118-122; Ibn Kathir: 1/347.]].

Those who held it obligatory based their argument on what 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisa'i al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'ammal al-A'idhi informed us, from 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah who said: The daughter of Abu Tijrah, whose name is Habibah, one of the women of Bani 'Abd al-Dar, informed me, saying: I entered with women of Quraysh the house of the family of Abu Husayn, looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he was performing sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. I saw him running, and his waist-wrapper was turning because of the intensity of the running, until I would say: I can see his knees. I heard him say: "Run, for Allah has prescribed for you the sa'y." [[Narrated by al-Daraqutni from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: Ma'ruf ibn Mishkan informed me, Mansur ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Umm Safiyyah who said: women of Bani 'Abd al-Dar who had met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me... The author of al-Tanqih said: its chain is sahih; Ma'ruf ibn Mishkan is saduq (truthful), and we do not know of anyone who criticized him; this Mansur is thiqah (trustworthy) and his narrations are included in the two Sahihs. Al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, in which is 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mu'ammal; Ibn Hibban regarded him as thiqah and said he errs, and others weakened him (al-Majma': 3/247). Ahmad: 6/422, from Habibah bint Abi Tajza'ah, and the correct is bint Abi Tijrah (see Usd al-Ghabah 7/59). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/141.]]

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that he said: I said to 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ: Have you considered the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs the Hajj to the House or makes 'umrah, there is no blame upon him in going back and forth between them﴾? I do not see anything upon anyone for not going back and forth between them. 'A'ishah said: No indeed. If it were as you say, it would be "there is no blame upon him for not going back and forth between them." This verse was only revealed concerning the Ansar, who used to assume ihram for Manat, and Manat was at Qudayd. They felt uneasy about going back and forth between al-Safa and al-Marwah. When Islam came, they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾, the verse. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir: 8/175, Muslim in Hajj: 2/928, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/139.]]

'Asim said: I asked Anas ibn Malik: Did you used to dislike sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah? He said: Yes, because it was among the symbols of the Jahiliyyah, until Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he went out of the mosque, intending al-Safa, saying: "We begin with what Allah, may He be exalted, began with," and he began with al-Safa. And he said: When he stood on al-Safa, he would say the takbir three times and say: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things capable. He would do this three times and supplicate, and he would do the same on al-Marwah. And he said: When he descended from al-Safa, he walked until his feet touched the bottom of the valley, then he ran until he came out of it. [[Narrated by Muslim in Hajj, chapter: The Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ, no. 1218, 2/886, at length, from the well-known hadith of Jabir. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/136.]] Mujahid said, may Allah have mercy on him: Musa, peace be upon him, performed Hajj on a red camel, wearing two qat wani cloaks [[Al-qatwaniyyah: a short white cloak; the nun is extra. Al-Nihayah: 4/85.]], and he circumambulated the House, then ascended al-Safa and supplicated, then descended to the sa'y while saying the talbiyah: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk." Allah, may He be exalted, said: "Labbayka, My servant, and I am with you," and Musa, peace be upon him, fell down in prostration.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the ya' and with the shaddah on the ta' and sukun on the 'ayn, and likewise the second occurrence, ﴿And whoever volunteers good, then indeed Allah is Grateful﴾ (2:184), in the sense of yatatawwa'u (he volunteers). Ya'qub agreed on the first, and the rest read it with the ta' and a fatha on the 'ayn in the past tense. Mujahid said: its meaning is: whoever volunteers by circumambulating between al-Safa and al-Marwah. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: whoever volunteers, meaning adds to the circumambulation beyond what is obligatory. It was also said: whoever volunteers with hajj and 'umrah after performing the obligatory hajj. Al-Hasan and others said: it refers to all deeds, i.e., performing what is not obligatory upon him, of zakah, prayer, circumambulation and other kinds of acts of obedience. ﴿Then indeed Allah is Shakir﴾, rewarding His servant for his deed. ﴿Knowing﴾ of his intention. Gratitude (shukr) from Allah, may He be exalted, is that He gives His servant more than he deserves: He rewards the little and gives abundantly.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 159–160:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance, after We have made it clear for the people in the Book﴾. It was revealed concerning the scholars of the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), the verse of stoning, and other rulings that were in the Torah. [[Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal, brother of Banu Salama, and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, brother of Banu al-Ashhal, and Kharija ibn Zayd, brother of al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, asked a number of the rabbis of the Jews about some of what was in the Torah, but they concealed it from them and refused to inform them. So Allah revealed concerning them: (Indeed, those who conceal ...). See al-Suyuti, al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi al-Ma'thur, 1/390.]] ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah curses﴾. The origin of la'n (cursing) is expulsion and distance. ﴿And those who curse curse them﴾, i.e., they ask Allah to curse them, saying: "O Allah, curse them." They differed concerning these cursers. Ibn Abbas said: all of creation except the jinn and mankind. Qatadah said: they are the angels. Ata' said: the jinn and mankind. Al-Hasan said: all the servants of Allah. Ibn Mas'ud said: No two Muslims curse each other except that the curse returns upon the Jews and Christians who concealed the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his description. Mujahid said: the cursers are the animals, who curse the sinful children of Adam when the drought is severe and the rain is withheld, saying, "This is from the evil of the sins of the children of Adam." Then He made an exception, saying:

﴿Except those who repent﴾ from disbelief, ﴿and reform﴾ — they embraced Islam and reformed their deeds between themselves and their Lord, ﴿and make clear﴾ what they had concealed. ﴿Those, I accept their repentance﴾, i.e., I overlook their sins and accept their repentance, ﴿and I am the Accepting of repentance﴾, the One who turns the hearts of My servants, which have turned away from Me, back to Me, ﴿the Merciful﴾ toward them after they have turned to Me.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 161–163:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels﴾, meaning the curse of the angels, 22/b, ﴿and of mankind, all of them﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "This is on the Day of Resurrection. The disbeliever will be made to stand, and Allah will curse him, then the angels will curse him, then the people will curse him." If it is said: "He has said ﴿and of mankind, all of them﴾, and the one cursed is part of mankind, so how can he curse himself?" It is said: he will curse himself on the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and some of you will curse others﴾ (29:25, al-'Ankabut). It is also said that they will curse the wrongdoers and the disbelievers, and whoever curses the wrongdoers and the disbelievers while being one of them has cursed himself.

﴿Abiding therein﴾: remaining in the curse, and it is said, in the Fire. ﴿The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite﴾: they will not be granted delay or postponement. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "They will not be permitted to make excuses," like His saying: ﴿nor will they be permitted, so that they may make excuses﴾ (36:36, al-Mursalat).

His saying the Exalted: ﴿And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾. The occasion of revelation of this verse is that the disbelievers of Quraysh said: "O Muhammad, describe your Lord for us and give us His lineage." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse and Surah al-Ikhlas [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. (548–549), and the references to its verification.]]. "The One" means the one who has no like and no partner.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Hamid ibn Zanjawayh informed us, Bakr ibn Ibrahim and Abu 'Asim informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, that she said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed, in these two verses is the Greatest Name of Allah': ﴿And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ and ﴿Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salat, chapter on supplication, 2/45; al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter on what has come in the Collection of Supplications from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), 9/447, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Ibn Majah in al-Du'a', chapter on the Greatest Name of Allah, no. "3855", 2/1267. Al-Darimi in Fada'il al-Qur'an, chapter on the virtue of the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah and the Verse of the Throne, 2/450. Ahmad, 6/461, from Asma' bint Yazid. The author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah, 5/39, and said: "A gharib hadith; all of them are from the hadith of Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad from Shahr ibn Hawshab, and Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad is not strong; Abu Dawud said his narrations are munkar." See Mizan al-I'tidal 3/8, Taqrib al-Tahdhib, al-Du'afa' wa'l-Matrukin of al-Nasa'i p. 156. And Shahr ibn Hawshab is not strong, and he made many errors and mursal narrations; see Mizan al-I'tidal 2/283, Taqrib al-Tahdhib, al-Du'afa' wa'l-Matrukin of al-Nasa'i p. 134.]].

Abu al-Duha [[See al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi'l-Ma'thur by al-Suyuti, 1/395, where he attributes it to Waki', al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]] said: "When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: 'Muhammad says that your God is one God. Let him bring us a sign, if he is among the truthful.' So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed..."

Abu al-Duha [[See al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi'l-Ma'thur by al-Suyuti, 1/395, where he attributes it to Waki', al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]] said: "When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: 'Muhammad says that your God is one God. Let him bring us a sign, if he is among the truthful.' So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed..."

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. He mentioned "the heavens" in the plural form and "the earth" in the singular form, because each heaven is not of one kind but of a different kind, whereas all the earths are of one kind, which is soil. So the sign in the heavens is their thickness and height without pillars or supports, and what you see in them of the sun, the moon and the stars. The sign in the earth is its extent, its spreading out and its vastness, and what you see in it of trees, rivers, mountains, seas, minerals and plants.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿and the alternation of the night and the day﴾, meaning their succession in going and coming, one of them replacing the other: when one goes, the other comes after it, that is, behind it. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day to succeed one another﴾ (62, al-Furqan). ʿAtaʾ said: He meant their difference in light and darkness, and in lengthening and shortening. "Al-layl" (the night) is the plural of "laylah" (a night), and "al-layali" (the nights) is the plural of the plural. "Al-nahar" (the day) has the plural "nuhr". He mentioned the night before the day in the recitation because it is older than it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day﴾ (37, Ya-Sin).

﴿and the ship that runs in the sea﴾, meaning the ships. Its singular and its plural are the same (fulk). When it is intended as a plural it is feminine, and when it is singular it is masculine. Allah, the Exalted, said in the singular and masculine form: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ (140, al-Saffat), and He said in the plural and feminine form: ﴿Until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a good wind﴾ (22, Yunus).

﴿and the ship that runs in the sea﴾. The sign in the ship is its subjection (to the water) and its running upon the surface of the water, while it is loaded and does not sink beneath the water. ﴿with what benefits people﴾, meaning riding on it and carrying loads on it for trade, gains and various kinds of livelihood. ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of water﴾, meaning the rain. It was said: by "the sky" he meant the clouds, and Allah creates the water in the clouds and then it descends from the clouds. And it was said: he meant the known sky, Allah creates the water in the sky, then it descends from the sky to the clouds, and then from the clouds it descends to the earth. ﴿and thereby gives life﴾, that is, by the water, ﴿to the earth after its death﴾, that is, after its dryness and barrenness. ﴿and scatters throughout it﴾, that is, spreads throughout it, ﴿every kind of creature﴾, ﴿and the turning of the winds﴾.

Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "al-rih" (the wind) without an alif, while the rest read it with an alif. Every instance of "rih" in the Qur'an that has neither an alif nor a lam, the readers differed over whether it is plural or singular, except in al-Dhariyat: ﴿the barren wind﴾ (41, al-Dhariyat), on which they agreed that it is singular. And in the first passage of Surah al-Rum: ﴿the winds as bearers of good news﴾ (46, al-Rum), on which they agreed that it is plural. Abu Jaʿfar read the rest of them in the plural, while the readers differ concerning them. "Al-rih" may be masculine or feminine. Its turning means that it shifts toward the south, the north, the east and the west, and the southwest and the northeast winds. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/275–276; al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/396–397.]]

It was also said: its turning is that at times it is gentle, at times it is violent, at times it is hot and at times it is cold. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The greatest of Allah's armies are the wind and the water." The wind was named "rih" because it refreshes (yurih) the souls. Shurayh al-Qadi said: "No wind blows except for the healing of the sick or the sickness of the healthy." Good news comes through three of the winds: the eastern (al-saba), the northern (al-shamal) and the southern (al-janub). As for the western wind (al-dabbur), it is the barren wind, and there is no good news in it. It was also said: the winds are eight, four for mercy and four for punishment. As for those for mercy: the bearers of good news, the spreaders, the scatterers and the senders. As for those for punishment: the barren, the sharp (al-sarsar) on land, and the violent and the crashing (al-qasif) at sea.

﴿and the subjected cloud﴾, that is, the cloud made subservient, called "sahab" because it moves (yansahib), meaning it travels swiftly, as if it is dragged (yasḥab), that is, pulled. ﴿between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who understand﴾, so that they know that these things have a Creator and Maker. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "There are three things of which no one knows from where the thunder, the lightning and the cloud come."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 165:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the people are those who take, besides Allah, rivals﴾, that is, idols which they worship, ﴿who love them as they love Allah﴾, that is, they love their gods as the believers love Allah. Al-Zajjaj said: they love the idols as they love Allah, because they associated them with Allah, and so they equated between Allah and their idols in love. ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah﴾, that is, more steadfast and more constant in their love for Him, because they do not choose anything over Allah. When the polytheists took an idol and then saw one better than it, they cast away the first and chose the second. Qatadah said: The disbelievers turn away from their object of worship in a time of trial and turn to Allah, may He be exalted, just as Allah, mighty and majestic, has informed us about them when He said: ﴿And when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ (29:65). The believer does not turn away from Allah in ease or hardship, in prosperity or adversity. [[See: al-Wasit of al-Wahidi: 1/236.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: On the Day of Resurrection Allah, mighty and majestic, will command whoever burned himself in this world out of devotion to the idols to enter Hell together with their idols, but they will not enter, knowing that the punishment of Hell is everlasting. Then He will say to the believers, while they are among the disbelievers: "If you are My beloved, then enter Hell," and they will plunge into it. Then a caller from beneath the Throne will call out: ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah﴾. It was also said that He said ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah﴾ because Allah, may He be exalted, loved them first, and then they loved Him, and whoever has been witnessed by the One worshipped as beloved, his love is more complete. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾ (5:54).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if only those who have wronged would see﴾. Nafi', Ibn Amir and Ya'qub recited "walaw tara" with the ta' (you), and the others recited it with the ya' (they). The response of "law" (if) here is omitted, and its like is frequent in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains would be moved or the earth cut asunder...﴾ (13:31), meaning: this Qur'an would be [the one]. Whoever recites with the ta' means: and if you, O Muhammad, could see those who wronged themselves in the severity of punishment, you would see a grave matter. It was said: its meaning is, say, O Muhammad: O you who are wronging, if you could see those who wronged or associated partners in the severity of punishment, you would see a dreadful matter. Whoever recites with the ya' means: and if those who wronged themselves could see at the sight of the punishment, that is, if they saw the severity of Allah's punishment and His retribution when they see the punishment, they would know the harm of disbelief and that what they took of idols does not benefit them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When they see the punishment﴾. Ibn Amir recited with a dammah on the ya' (idhyarawna being read as "yurawna"), and the rest with a fathah on it. ﴿That the power belongs to Allah entirely and that Allah is severe in punishment﴾, that is, that the power belongs to Allah entirely; the meaning is that they would have seen and been certain that the power belongs to Allah entirely.

Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub recited "inna al-quwwata" and "wa-inna Allah" with a kasrah on the alif, as a new sentence, and the statement is complete at His saying ﴿when they see the punishment﴾, with the response omitted.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 166–167:

﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment﴾ This refers to the Day of Resurrection, when Allah gathers the leaders and the followers, and some of them disown others. This is the statement of most of the exegetes (mufassirun). Al-Suddi said: they are the devils who disown mankind. ﴿And their bonds are cut off from them﴾, i.e. from them, ﴿the bonds (al-asbab)﴾, i.e. the relationships that existed between them in the world, of kinship and friendship, and their companionship turned into enmity. Ibn Juraij said: these are the ties of kinship, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So there will be no kinship between them that Day﴾ (23:101). Al-Suddi said: it means the deeds they used to do in the world, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (25:23).

The root meaning of sabab (cause, means, bond) is that by which one reaches a thing, whether a means, a kinship, or affection, and from this one says of a rope "sabab" and of a road "sabab".

﴿And those who followed will say﴾, meaning the followers, ﴿If only we had a return (karrah)﴾, i.e. a return to the world, ﴿so that we might disown them﴾, i.e. the ones who were followed, ﴿as they have disowned us﴾ today. ﴿Thus﴾, i.e. just as He showed them the punishment, thus ﴿Allah will show them﴾. It was also said: just as some of them disown others, Allah will show them ﴿their deeds as regrets (hasarat) upon them﴾. Hasarat is the plural of hasrah. It was said: Allah will show them the evil they committed, so they will regret why they did it; and it was said: He will show them the good they neglected, so they will feel remorse over losing it. Ibn Kaysan said: they associated idols with Allah, hoping they would bring them near to Allah the Mighty and Majestic; so when they were punished for what they had hoped for in reward, they regretted and grieved. Al-Suddi said: Paradise will be raised for them, and they will look at it and at their houses in it, which they would have had had they obeyed Allah. It will be said to them: "That is your dwelling, had you obeyed Allah." Then it will be divided among the believers, and that is when they will feel remorse and grief. [[See al-Tabari 3/296.]] ﴿And they will not come out of the Fire﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 168–169:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, eat of what is on the earth, lawful and good﴾. It was revealed concerning Thaqif, Khuza'ah, 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah and the Banu Mudlij regarding what they had forbidden to themselves of the tilth (al-harth) and the livestock: the bahirah, the sa'ibah, the wasilah and the ham. So "lawful" (halal) is what the Shari'ah has made lawful, and "good" (tayyib) is said to mean what is pleasant and agreeable. The Muslim finds the lawful pleasant and shuns the unlawful. It is also said that "good" (tayyib) means pure (tahir). ﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Ya'qub read it with a dammah on the ta' (khutuwat), and the rest read it with a sukun. "Footsteps of Satan" (khutuwat al-shaytan) means his traces and his slips. It is also said that they are vows in acts of disobedience. Abu 'Ubaydah said: they are the minor sins. al-Zajjaj said: his paths. ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾, manifestly hostile. It is also said: one who displays enmity. He displayed his enmity by his refusal to prostrate to Adam and his deception of him until he expelled him from the Garden.

"Abana" (to make clear) may be intransitive and transitive. Then he mentioned his enmity, saying: ﴿He only commands you to evil﴾, that is, to sin. The root of "su'" (evil) is that which distresses its possessor; it is a verbal noun from sa'a, yasu'u, su'an and mas'ah, meaning it grieved him; and sawwa'tuhu, fa-sa'a, meaning I grieved him, so he grieved. ﴿And immorality (al-fahsha')﴾: acts of disobedience and whatever is ugly of speech and deed; it is a verbal noun like al-sarra' and al-darra'. Badhan related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "Al-fahsha' among acts of disobedience is that for which the prescribed punishment (hadd) is due, and su' among sins is that for which there is no prescribed punishment." al-Suddi said: it is fornication (zina). It is also said it is stinginess (bukhl). ﴿And that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾: the forbidding of the tilth and the livestock.
