The appointed days (al-ayyam al-ma'dudat) are the days of tashriq (the days after Eid al-Adha), which are the days of Mina and the stoning of the pillars. They were called ma'dudat (counted) because of their small number, as in His saying: ﴿a few dirhams﴾ (12:20). The known days (al-ayyam al-ma'lumat) are the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, the last of which is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr). This is the saying of most scholars. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the known days are the day of sacrifice and the two days after it, and the counted days are the days of tashriq. It is narrated from 'Ali who said: the known days are the day of sacrifice and three days after it. 'Ata' said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: the known days are the day of 'Arafah, the day of sacrifice, and the days of tashriq. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: they are one and the same thing, and they are the days of tashriq. It is narrated from Nubayshah al-Hudhali who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The days of tashriq are days of eating, drinking and remembrance of Allah." [Reported by Muslim in the Book of Fasting, chapter on the prohibition of fasting on the days of tashriq, no. 1141, 2/800. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 6/351.]

Among the remembrance during the days of tashriq is the takbir. The scholars differed concerning it. It is narrated from 'Umar and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar that they used to say takbir in Mina on those days after the prayers, in the gathering, on the bed, in the tent, and on the road, and the people would say takbir along with their takbir, interpreting this verse. Saying takbir after the prayers during these days is prescribed for both the pilgrim and the non-pilgrim according to the majority of scholars, though they differed about its duration. One group held that the takbir begins after the dawn prayer on the day of 'Arafah and ends after the afternoon prayer on the last of the days of tashriq. This is narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and Makhul said likewise, and Abu Yusuf, may Allah be pleased with him, adopted this view. Another group held that the takbir begins after the dawn prayer on the day of 'Arafah and ends after the afternoon prayer on the day of sacrifice. This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and Abu Hanifah said likewise. Others said it begins after the noon prayer on the day of sacrifice and ends after the dawn prayer on the last day of tashriq. This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and Malik and al-Shafi'i said likewise. Al-Shafi'i said: "Because people follow the pilgrims in this, and the pilgrims' remembrance before this time is the talbiyah, and they begin the takbir on the day of sacrifice from the noon prayer." As for the wording of the takbir: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan used to say: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar" three times in succession. This is the saying of the people of Madinah, and al-Shafi'i adopted it, and he said: "Whatever additional remembrance of Allah is added is good." According to the people of Iraq, one says it twice, narrated from Ibn Mas'ud.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him﴾, meaning: whoever departs from the pilgrims on the second day of the days of tashriq, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾. This is because it is obligatory for the pilgrim to spend the first and second nights of the days of tashriq in Mina and to stone, each day after midday, twenty-one pebbles, seven at each pillar. Leaving the overnight stay was permitted for shepherds of camels and for those responsible for providing water to the pilgrims. [It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: al-'Abbas asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to spend the nights of Mina in Makkah because of his watering duty, and he granted him permission (agreed upon). And from 'Asim ibn 'Adi that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted the shepherds of camels to forgo the nights in Mina, stoning on the day of sacrifice, then stoning on the following day and the day after it for two days, and then stoning on the day of departure. Reported by Imam Ahmad, the authors of the Sunan, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim. See Nayl al-Awtar of al-Shawkani, 6/187 and 190.] Then whoever stones on the second day of the days of tashriq and wishes to depart, forgoing the overnight stay of the third night and stoning on its day, that is permissible for him, by His saying: ﴿But whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him﴾. And whoever does not depart until the sun sets must spend the night and stone on the third day, then depart. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾.

Meaning: there is no sin upon the one who hastens and departs on the second day in his hastening, and upon the one who delays until he departs on the third day, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾ in his delay. It was also said: its meaning is ﴿whoever hastens﴾ has taken the concession, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾ for taking the concession; ﴿and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾ for leaving the concession. It was also said its meaning is that he returns forgiven, with no sin upon him whether he hastens or delays, as we have related: "Whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or sin returns as on the day his mother bore him." [Previously cited, see p. 227.] This is the saying of 'Ali and Ibn Mas'ud.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿For him who fears (Allah)﴾, meaning: for him who guards against committing in his Hajj anything Allah has forbidden him, as He said: "Whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or sin." Ibn Mas'ud said: the forgiveness of sins was only made conditional upon fearing Allah, Exalted is He, in one's Hajj. In the narration of al-Kalbi from Ibn 'Abbas, the meaning of ﴿for him who fears﴾ is: hunting is not lawful for him, so that he may not kill game until the days of tashriq pass [i.e., end]. Abu al-'Aliyah said: it means if he fears Allah for what remains of his life. ﴿And fear Allah and know that you will be gathered to Him﴾, meaning: you will be assembled in the Hereafter, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 204–207 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Ata' said: It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhra. His name was Ubayy, and he was called al-Akhnas because on the Day of Badr he withdrew (khanasa) with three hundred men from Banu Zuhra from fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was a man sweet of speech and pleasant of appearance. He would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sit with him, and display Islam, saying, "I truly love you," and swearing by Allah to that. But he was a hypocrite, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would bring him closer in his gathering. Then the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. [[See: al-Tabari 4/229; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 96.]] That is, you find it good and it becomes great in your heart. It is said that for approval one says "a'jabani kadha" (this impressed me), and for dislike and disapproval one says " 'ajibtu min kadha" (I am astonished at such and such).

﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾, meaning the hypocrite's saying: "By Allah, I believe in you and I love you." ﴿Yet he is the most contentious of opponents﴾, that is, the most fierce in disputation. It is said: "Laddta, ya hadha, wa anta talidd laddan wa ladadatan." When you want to say that he overcame his opponent, you say: "laddahu yaliddahu laddan." It is said: "rajul aladd" (a man most contentious), "imra'a laddaa" (a woman most contentious), and "qawm lud" (a people most contentious). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that you may warn thereby a people most contentious﴾ (Maryam 19:97).

Al-Zajjaj said: Its derivation is from ladidayi al-'unuq, which are the two sides of the neck. Its interpretation is that whichever way he takes, right or left, in the methods of dispute, he prevails. Al-Khisam is the verbal noun of "khasamahu khisaman wa mukhasamatan," as said by Abu 'Ubayda. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the plural of khasm, as in "khasm, khisam, khusum," like "bahr, bihar, buhur." Al-Hasan said: "Alladd al-khisam" means one who speaks falsely. Qatada said: One who is most severe in disobedience, contentious in falsehood, who speaks with wisdom but acts with sin.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the most hateful of men to Allah the Exalted is the most contentious disputer (al-alladd al-khasim)." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," 13/180; and Muslim in al-'Ilm, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," no. 2668, 4/2054. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 10/97.]]

﴿And when he turns away﴾, that is, he withdraws and turns from you. ﴿He strives in the land﴾, that is, he works in it. It is also said: he travels and walks in it. ﴿To spread corruption therein﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: He cuts off the ties of kinship and sheds the blood of Muslims. ﴿And destroys crops and animals﴾. This is because al-Akhnas [[al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, with a fatha on the shin, a kasra on the ra', and a qaf at the end, a man of Thaqif.]] had a dispute between himself and Thaqif, so he raided them by night, burned their crops, and destroyed their livestock. [[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/302; also his Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 58.]]

Muqatil said: He went out to al-Ta'if to collect money owed to him by a debtor, and he burned the debtor's heap of grain and slaughtered his she-donkey. "Al-nasl" (offspring) means the offspring of every animal, and humans are included among them. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And when he turns away﴾ means when he takes charge of affairs and becomes a ruler. ﴿He strives in the land﴾. Mujahid said regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land﴾: When he becomes ruler, he acts with aggression and oppression, so Allah withholds the rain and destroys the crops and the offspring. ﴿And Allah does not love corruption﴾, that is, He does not approve of corruption. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Cutting a dirham (i.e., cheating over it) is a form of corruption in the land.

His saying: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah,"﴾, that is, be mindful of Allah, ﴿pride takes him to sin﴾, that is, the pride and zealotry of the Age of Ignorance (hamiyyat al-jahiliyya) drive him to act sinfully, that is, to act wrongfully. Al-'Izza means arrogance and self-protection. It is also said the meaning is: ﴿pride takes him﴾ on account of the sin that is in his heart, so the preposition "bi" stands in place of "li."

His saying: ﴿Then Hell is sufficient for him﴾, that is, it is enough for him. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾, that is, the bed. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Among the greatest sins before Allah is that it be said to a servant, "Fear Allah," and he replies, "Look to yourself."

It is narrated that it was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: "Fear Allah," so he placed his cheek on the ground in humility before Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, that is, seeking the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. ﴿And Allah is Compassionate to the servants﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak that this verse was revealed concerning the expedition of al-Raji' (sariyyat al-Raji'). That is because the disbelievers of Quraysh sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was in Madinah, saying: "We have embraced Islam, so send to us some men of your companions' scholars to teach us your religion." This was a deception from them. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari, Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bukayr, Abd Allah ibn Tariq ibn Shihab al-Balawi, and Zayd ibn al-Dathina, and he appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn Abi al-Aflah al-Ansari.

Abu Hurayra said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ten spies and appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit al-Ansari. They set out and halted at Batn al-Raji', between Makkah and Madinah, and with them were dates of 'ajwa. They ate, and an old woman passed by and saw the date pits. She returned to her people in Makkah and said: "The people of Yathrib, companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), have traveled this route." So seventy men mounted, carrying spears, until they surrounded them.

Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They were reported to a tribe of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan, so about a hundred archers set out for them. They followed their tracks until they found the place where they had eaten the dates at a campsite they had stayed in. They said: "Dates of Yathrib!" So they followed their tracks. When 'Asim and his companions sensed them, they took refuge on a fadfad. [[Al-fadfad: a hard, rough, elevated place. In manuscript A it reads: Qudayr.]] The people surrounded them, and they killed Marthad, Khalid and Abd Allah ibn Tariq. 'Asim ibn Thabit emptied his quiver, which contained seven arrows, and with every arrow he killed a man of the leading polytheists. Then he said: "O Allah, I have protected Your religion at the beginning of the day, so protect my flesh at the end of the day." Then the polytheists surrounded him and killed him. When they had killed him, they wanted to cut off his head to sell it to Sulafa bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd, for when her son had been struck at the Battle of Uhud, she had vowed: "If I can get hold of the head of 'Asim, I will drink wine from his skull." So Allah sent a swarm of hornets (dabr), which are wasps, and they shielded 'Asim, so they could not reach him. He was thus called "Hami al-Dabr" (the Guarded by the Hornets). They said: "Leave him until the evening, then it will pass from him and we will take him." But a black cloud came and rained a torrent like the gushing of a waterskin [[al-'Azali: plural of al-'azla', the lower mouth of a waterskin; the sudden rush of the rain is compared to what gushes from the mouth of a waterskin.]], and Allah caused the valley to become a torrent, which carried 'Asim away to Paradise, and carried fifty of the polytheists to the Fire. 'Asim had given a covenant to Allah the Exalted that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say, when it reached him that the hornets had protected him: "How wondrous is Allah's protection of the believing servant. 'Asim had vowed that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist, so Allah protected him after his death just as 'Asim had refrained in his life."

The polytheists captured Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari and Zayd ibn al-Dathina and took them to Makkah. As for Khubayb, the sons of al-Harith ibn 'Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought him in order to kill him in revenge for their father. Khubayb was the one who had killed al-Harith on the Day of Badr. Khubayb remained with them as a captive until they resolved to kill him. He borrowed a razor from the daughters of al-Harith to shave with, and they lent it to him. A small child of theirs wandered off while she was unaware, and the woman was startled to find Khubayb with the child seated on his thigh and the razor in his hand. The woman screamed. Khubayb said: "Do you fear that I will kill him? I would never do that. Treachery is not among our ways." The woman said afterwards: "By Allah, I have never seen a captive better than Khubayb. By Allah, one day I found him eating a bunch of grapes in his hand while he was bound in iron, and there was no fruit in Makkah at that time. It was nothing but a provision that Allah had granted to Khubayb."

Then they went out of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) to kill him in the open area (al-Hill) and intended to crucify him. Khubayb said to them: "Let me pray two rak'ahs." So they left him. Khubayb was the first to establish the prayer for every Muslim who is killed in captivity (sabran) [[Every living being that is bound and then killed is said to have been killed in captivity (sabran).]]. He prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "Were it not that they would think I was anxious, I would have prolonged it. O Allah, count them, kill them one by one, and leave none of them." Then he recited:

"I care not, when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall for the sake of Allah."
"And that is for the sake of God; if He wills, He will bless the scattered limbs of a torn body."

Then they crucified him alive, and he said: "O Allah, You know that there is no one near me to convey my greetings to Your Messenger, so convey my greetings to him." Then Abu Sirwa'a Uqba ibn al-Harith stood up and killed him.

It is also said that there was a polytheist man called Salaman, Abu Maysara, who had a spear, and he placed it between Khubayb's breasts. Khubayb said to him: "Fear Allah." But that only increased him in arrogance, so he thrust it in and pierced him through. This is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride takes him to sin﴾, meaning Salaman.

As for Zayd ibn al-Dathina, Safwan ibn Umayya bought him in order to kill him in revenge for his father Umayya ibn Khalaf. He sent him with a freedman of his called Nistas to al-Tan'im to kill him for his father. A group of Quraysh gathered, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. When Zayd was brought forward to be killed, Abu Sufyan said to him: "I beseech you by Allah, O Zayd, would you love that Muhammad were here now in your place, and we would strike his neck, and you were with your family?" He said: "By Allah, I would not love that Muhammad (ﷺ), at this moment, in the place where he is, should have a thorn prick him and harm him, while I sit with my family." Abu Sufyan said: "I have never seen anyone love another as the companions of Muhammad love Muhammad." Then Nistas killed him.

When this report reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said to his companions: "Which of you will take Khubayb down from his cross, and he will have Paradise?" [[In manuscript A (in the margin): "will bring down" (yunzil).]] Al-Zubayr said: "I will, O Messenger of Allah, and my companion al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad." So the two of them set out, walking by night and hiding by day, until they reached al-Tan'im at night. Around the cross were forty polytheist men, asleep and intoxicated. They took him down, and he was fresh and pliable, nothing about him had changed after forty days. His hand was over his wound, and it was dripping blood. The color was the color of blood, and the scent was the scent of musk. Al-Zubayr carried him on his horse, and they departed. The disbelievers woke up and found that Khubayb was missing, so they informed Quraysh, and seventy of them rode out. When they caught up with the two, al-Zubayr threw Khubayb, and the earth swallowed him, so he was called "Balee' al-Ard" (the one swallowed by the earth).

Al-Zubayr said: "What has emboldened you against us, O assembly of Quraysh?" Then he lifted the turban from his head and said: "I am al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, my mother is Safiyyah bint 'Abd al-Muttalib, and my companion is al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. We are two lions lying in wait, defending our two cubs. If you wish, we will contend with you in archery; if you wish, we will fight you hand to hand; and if you wish, you may depart." So they turned back to Makkah. The two of them then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Jibril was with him. He said: "O Muhammad, the angels take pride in these two of your Companions." So there was revealed concerning al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad: ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, when the two of them sold themselves to bring down Khubayb from his cross.[[See Fath al-Bari: 7/378-379, and 'Uyun al-Athar by Ibn Sayyid al-Nas: 2/56-66.]]

And most of the exegetes said: It was revealed concerning Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi when the polytheists seized him, along with a group of believers, and tortured them. Suhayb said to them: "I am an old man; it will not harm you whether I was with you or with others. Will you take my wealth and leave me and my religion?" They agreed, and he had stipulated for them a mount and provisions. He remained in Makkah for as long as Allah willed, then set out for Madinah. Abu Bakr and 'Umar met him with some men. Abu Bakr said to him: "Your sale has profited you, O Abu Yahya!" Suhayb replied: "And yours too; do not be grieved." Suhayb said: "What is that?" Abu Bakr said: "Allah has revealed concerning you," and he recited to him this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ata' said: Suhayb came migrating toward the Prophet ﷺ, and a group of Quraysh polytheists followed him. He dismounted from his mount, emptied what was in his quiver, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know well that I am among the most skilled archers of you. By Allah, I will not place an arrow from my quiver except in the heart of one of you, and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot every arrow in my quiver, then struck with my sword while anything remains in my hand. Then do whatever you wish. Or, if you wish, I will show you my wealth in Makkah and you will leave my way." They said: "Yes." He did so, and Allah revealed this verse.[[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/304; Ibn Kathir 1/437; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 58; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 3/227-228.]]

al-Hasan said: Do you know concerning whom this verse was revealed? It was revealed concerning a Muslim who meets a disbeliever, and says to him, "Say: there is no god but Allah," but he refuses to say it. The Muslim said: "By Allah, I will sell myself for Allah," so he advanced and fought alone until he was killed.

It was also said that the verse was revealed concerning enjoining good and forbidding evil. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I see the one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah stands up and commands this man to fear Allah, but he does not accept, and pride in sin seizes him. He [the first] says: 'I sell myself to Allah,' and fights him. The two men then fight over that." 'Ali, whenever he recited this verse, would say: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the two have fought!" And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, and 'Umar said: ﴿Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return﴾ — a man stood up to enjoin good and forbid evil, and was killed.

Abu Umamah reported that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said: "The best jihad is the one who speaks a word of truth before an unjust ruler."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in al-Malahim, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, 6/191. And al-Tirmidhi: in al-Fitan, chapter on the best jihad being a word of justice before an unjust ruler, 6/395, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route" (and Abu Umamah's hadith supports it). And al-Nasa'i: in al-Bay'ah, chapter on the virtue of one who speaks the truth before an unjust ruler, 7/161. And Ibn Majah: in al-Fitan, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, 2/1329. And Ahmad: 3/19 (part of a hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri); 4/324 from Tariq ibn Shihab; 5/251-256 from Abu Umamah.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 204–207 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Ata' said: It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhra. His name was Ubayy, and he was called al-Akhnas because on the Day of Badr he withdrew (khanasa) with three hundred men from Banu Zuhra from fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was a man sweet of speech and pleasant of appearance. He would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sit with him, and display Islam, saying, "I truly love you," and swearing by Allah to that. But he was a hypocrite, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would bring him closer in his gathering. Then the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. [[See: al-Tabari 4/229; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 96.]] That is, you find it good and it becomes great in your heart. It is said that for approval one says "a'jabani kadha" (this impressed me), and for dislike and disapproval one says " 'ajibtu min kadha" (I am astonished at such and such).

﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾, meaning the hypocrite's saying: "By Allah, I believe in you and I love you." ﴿Yet he is the most contentious of opponents﴾, that is, the most fierce in disputation. It is said: "Laddta, ya hadha, wa anta talidd laddan wa ladadatan." When you want to say that he overcame his opponent, you say: "laddahu yaliddahu laddan." It is said: "rajul aladd" (a man most contentious), "imra'a laddaa" (a woman most contentious), and "qawm lud" (a people most contentious). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that you may warn thereby a people most contentious﴾ (Maryam 19:97).

Al-Zajjaj said: Its derivation is from ladidayi al-'unuq, which are the two sides of the neck. Its interpretation is that whichever way he takes, right or left, in the methods of dispute, he prevails. Al-Khisam is the verbal noun of "khasamahu khisaman wa mukhasamatan," as said by Abu 'Ubayda. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the plural of khasm, as in "khasm, khisam, khusum," like "bahr, bihar, buhur." Al-Hasan said: "Alladd al-khisam" means one who speaks falsely. Qatada said: One who is most severe in disobedience, contentious in falsehood, who speaks with wisdom but acts with sin.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the most hateful of men to Allah the Exalted is the most contentious disputer (al-alladd al-khasim)." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," 13/180; and Muslim in al-'Ilm, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," no. 2668, 4/2054. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 10/97.]]

﴿And when he turns away﴾, that is, he withdraws and turns from you. ﴿He strives in the land﴾, that is, he works in it. It is also said: he travels and walks in it. ﴿To spread corruption therein﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: He cuts off the ties of kinship and sheds the blood of Muslims. ﴿And destroys crops and animals﴾. This is because al-Akhnas [[al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, with a fatha on the shin, a kasra on the ra', and a qaf at the end, a man of Thaqif.]] had a dispute between himself and Thaqif, so he raided them by night, burned their crops, and destroyed their livestock. [[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/302; also his Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 58.]]

Muqatil said: He went out to al-Ta'if to collect money owed to him by a debtor, and he burned the debtor's heap of grain and slaughtered his she-donkey. "Al-nasl" (offspring) means the offspring of every animal, and humans are included among them. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And when he turns away﴾ means when he takes charge of affairs and becomes a ruler. ﴿He strives in the land﴾. Mujahid said regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land﴾: When he becomes ruler, he acts with aggression and oppression, so Allah withholds the rain and destroys the crops and the offspring. ﴿And Allah does not love corruption﴾, that is, He does not approve of corruption. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Cutting a dirham (i.e., cheating over it) is a form of corruption in the land.

His saying: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah,"﴾, that is, be mindful of Allah, ﴿pride takes him to sin﴾, that is, the pride and zealotry of the Age of Ignorance (hamiyyat al-jahiliyya) drive him to act sinfully, that is, to act wrongfully. Al-'Izza means arrogance and self-protection. It is also said the meaning is: ﴿pride takes him﴾ on account of the sin that is in his heart, so the preposition "bi" stands in place of "li."

His saying: ﴿Then Hell is sufficient for him﴾, that is, it is enough for him. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾, that is, the bed. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Among the greatest sins before Allah is that it be said to a servant, "Fear Allah," and he replies, "Look to yourself."

It is narrated that it was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: "Fear Allah," so he placed his cheek on the ground in humility before Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, that is, seeking the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. ﴿And Allah is Compassionate to the servants﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak that this verse was revealed concerning the expedition of al-Raji' (sariyyat al-Raji'). That is because the disbelievers of Quraysh sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was in Madinah, saying: "We have embraced Islam, so send to us some men of your companions' scholars to teach us your religion." This was a deception from them. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari, Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bukayr, Abd Allah ibn Tariq ibn Shihab al-Balawi, and Zayd ibn al-Dathina, and he appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn Abi al-Aflah al-Ansari.

Abu Hurayra said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ten spies and appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit al-Ansari. They set out and halted at Batn al-Raji', between Makkah and Madinah, and with them were dates of 'ajwa. They ate, and an old woman passed by and saw the date pits. She returned to her people in Makkah and said: "The people of Yathrib, companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), have traveled this route." So seventy men mounted, carrying spears, until they surrounded them.

Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They were reported to a tribe of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan, so about a hundred archers set out for them. They followed their tracks until they found the place where they had eaten the dates at a campsite they had stayed in. They said: "Dates of Yathrib!" So they followed their tracks. When 'Asim and his companions sensed them, they took refuge on a fadfad. [[Al-fadfad: a hard, rough, elevated place. In manuscript A it reads: Qudayr.]] The people surrounded them, and they killed Marthad, Khalid and Abd Allah ibn Tariq. 'Asim ibn Thabit emptied his quiver, which contained seven arrows, and with every arrow he killed a man of the leading polytheists. Then he said: "O Allah, I have protected Your religion at the beginning of the day, so protect my flesh at the end of the day." Then the polytheists surrounded him and killed him. When they had killed him, they wanted to cut off his head to sell it to Sulafa bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd, for when her son had been struck at the Battle of Uhud, she had vowed: "If I can get hold of the head of 'Asim, I will drink wine from his skull." So Allah sent a swarm of hornets (dabr), which are wasps, and they shielded 'Asim, so they could not reach him. He was thus called "Hami al-Dabr" (the Guarded by the Hornets). They said: "Leave him until the evening, then it will pass from him and we will take him." But a black cloud came and rained a torrent like the gushing of a waterskin [[al-'Azali: plural of al-'azla', the lower mouth of a waterskin; the sudden rush of the rain is compared to what gushes from the mouth of a waterskin.]], and Allah caused the valley to become a torrent, which carried 'Asim away to Paradise, and carried fifty of the polytheists to the Fire. 'Asim had given a covenant to Allah the Exalted that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say, when it reached him that the hornets had protected him: "How wondrous is Allah's protection of the believing servant. 'Asim had vowed that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist, so Allah protected him after his death just as 'Asim had refrained in his life."

The polytheists captured Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari and Zayd ibn al-Dathina and took them to Makkah. As for Khubayb, the sons of al-Harith ibn 'Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought him in order to kill him in revenge for their father. Khubayb was the one who had killed al-Harith on the Day of Badr. Khubayb remained with them as a captive until they resolved to kill him. He borrowed a razor from the daughters of al-Harith to shave with, and they lent it to him. A small child of theirs wandered off while she was unaware, and the woman was startled to find Khubayb with the child seated on his thigh and the razor in his hand. The woman screamed. Khubayb said: "Do you fear that I will kill him? I would never do that. Treachery is not among our ways." The woman said afterwards: "By Allah, I have never seen a captive better than Khubayb. By Allah, one day I found him eating a bunch of grapes in his hand while he was bound in iron, and there was no fruit in Makkah at that time. It was nothing but a provision that Allah had granted to Khubayb."

Then they went out of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) to kill him in the open area (al-Hill) and intended to crucify him. Khubayb said to them: "Let me pray two rak'ahs." So they left him. Khubayb was the first to establish the prayer for every Muslim who is killed in captivity (sabran) [[Every living being that is bound and then killed is said to have been killed in captivity (sabran).]]. He prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "Were it not that they would think I was anxious, I would have prolonged it. O Allah, count them, kill them one by one, and leave none of them." Then he recited:

"I care not, when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall for the sake of Allah."
"And that is for the sake of God; if He wills, He will bless the scattered limbs of a torn body."

Then they crucified him alive, and he said: "O Allah, You know that there is no one near me to convey my greetings to Your Messenger, so convey my greetings to him." Then Abu Sirwa'a Uqba ibn al-Harith stood up and killed him.

It is also said that there was a polytheist man called Salaman, Abu Maysara, who had a spear, and he placed it between Khubayb's breasts. Khubayb said to him: "Fear Allah." But that only increased him in arrogance, so he thrust it in and pierced him through. This is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride takes him to sin﴾, meaning Salaman.

As for Zayd ibn al-Dathina, Safwan ibn Umayya bought him in order to kill him in revenge for his father Umayya ibn Khalaf. He sent him with a freedman of his called Nistas to al-Tan'im to kill him for his father. A group of Quraysh gathered, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. When Zayd was brought forward to be killed, Abu Sufyan said to him: "I beseech you by Allah, O Zayd, would you love that Muhammad were here now in your place, and we would strike his neck, and you were with your family?" He said: "By Allah, I would not love that Muhammad (ﷺ), at this moment, in the place where he is, should have a thorn prick him and harm him, while I sit with my family." Abu Sufyan said: "I have never seen anyone love another as the companions of Muhammad love Muhammad." Then Nistas killed him.

When this report reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said to his companions: "Which of you will take Khubayb down from his cross, and he will have Paradise?" [[In manuscript A (in the margin): "will bring down" (yunzil).]] Al-Zubayr said: "I will, O Messenger of Allah, and my companion al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad." So the two of them set out, walking by night and hiding by day, until they reached al-Tan'im at night. Around the cross were forty polytheist men, asleep and intoxicated. They took him down, and he was fresh and pliable, nothing about him had changed after forty days. His hand was over his wound, and it was dripping blood. The color was the color of blood, and the scent was the scent of musk. Al-Zubayr carried him on his horse, and they departed. The disbelievers woke up and found that Khubayb was missing, so they informed Quraysh, and seventy of them rode out. When they caught up with the two, al-Zubayr threw Khubayb, and the earth swallowed him, so he was called "Balee' al-Ard" (the one swallowed by the earth).

Al-Zubayr said: "What has emboldened you against us, O assembly of Quraysh?" Then he lifted the turban from his head and said: "I am al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, my mother is Safiyyah bint 'Abd al-Muttalib, and my companion is al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. We are two lions lying in wait, defending our two cubs. If you wish, we will contend with you in archery; if you wish, we will fight you hand to hand; and if you wish, you may depart." So they turned back to Makkah. The two of them then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Jibril was with him. He said: "O Muhammad, the angels take pride in these two of your Companions." So there was revealed concerning al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad: ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, when the two of them sold themselves to bring down Khubayb from his cross.[[See Fath al-Bari: 7/378-379, and 'Uyun al-Athar by Ibn Sayyid al-Nas: 2/56-66.]]

And most of the exegetes said: It was revealed concerning Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi when the polytheists seized him, along with a group of believers, and tortured them. Suhayb said to them: "I am an old man; it will not harm you whether I was with you or with others. Will you take my wealth and leave me and my religion?" They agreed, and he had stipulated for them a mount and provisions. He remained in Makkah for as long as Allah willed, then set out for Madinah. Abu Bakr and 'Umar met him with some men. Abu Bakr said to him: "Your sale has profited you, O Abu Yahya!" Suhayb replied: "And yours too; do not be grieved." Suhayb said: "What is that?" Abu Bakr said: "Allah has revealed concerning you," and he recited to him this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ata' said: Suhayb came migrating toward the Prophet ﷺ, and a group of Quraysh polytheists followed him. He dismounted from his mount, emptied what was in his quiver, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know well that I am among the most skilled archers of you. By Allah, I will not place an arrow from my quiver except in the heart of one of you, and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot every arrow in my quiver, then struck with my sword while anything remains in my hand. Then do whatever you wish. Or, if you wish, I will show you my wealth in Makkah and you will leave my way." They said: "Yes." He did so, and Allah revealed this verse.[[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/304; Ibn Kathir 1/437; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 58; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 3/227-228.]]

al-Hasan said: Do you know concerning whom this verse was revealed? It was revealed concerning a Muslim who meets a disbeliever, and says to him, "Say: there is no god but Allah," but he refuses to say it. The Muslim said: "By Allah, I will sell myself for Allah," so he advanced and fought alone until he was killed.

It was also said that the verse was revealed concerning enjoining good and forbidding evil. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I see the one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah stands up and commands this man to fear Allah, but he does not accept, and pride in sin seizes him. He [the first] says: 'I sell myself to Allah,' and fights him. The two men then fight over that." 'Ali, whenever he recited this verse, would say: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the two have fought!" And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, and 'Umar said: ﴿Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return﴾ — a man stood up to enjoin good and forbid evil, and was killed.

Abu Umamah reported that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said: "The best jihad is the one who speaks a word of truth before an unjust ruler."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in al-Malahim, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, 6/191. And al-Tirmidhi: in al-Fitan, chapter on the best jihad being a word of justice before an unjust ruler, 6/395, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route" (and Abu Umamah's hadith supports it). And al-Nasa'i: in al-Bay'ah, chapter on the virtue of one who speaks the truth before an unjust ruler, 7/161. And Ibn Majah: in al-Fitan, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, 2/1329. And Ahmad: 3/19 (part of a hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri); 4/324 from Tariq ibn Shihab; 5/251-256 from Abu Umamah.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 204–207 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Ata' said: It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhra. His name was Ubayy, and he was called al-Akhnas because on the Day of Badr he withdrew (khanasa) with three hundred men from Banu Zuhra from fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was a man sweet of speech and pleasant of appearance. He would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sit with him, and display Islam, saying, "I truly love you," and swearing by Allah to that. But he was a hypocrite, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would bring him closer in his gathering. Then the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. [[See: al-Tabari 4/229; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 96.]] That is, you find it good and it becomes great in your heart. It is said that for approval one says "a'jabani kadha" (this impressed me), and for dislike and disapproval one says " 'ajibtu min kadha" (I am astonished at such and such).

﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾, meaning the hypocrite's saying: "By Allah, I believe in you and I love you." ﴿Yet he is the most contentious of opponents﴾, that is, the most fierce in disputation. It is said: "Laddta, ya hadha, wa anta talidd laddan wa ladadatan." When you want to say that he overcame his opponent, you say: "laddahu yaliddahu laddan." It is said: "rajul aladd" (a man most contentious), "imra'a laddaa" (a woman most contentious), and "qawm lud" (a people most contentious). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that you may warn thereby a people most contentious﴾ (Maryam 19:97).

Al-Zajjaj said: Its derivation is from ladidayi al-'unuq, which are the two sides of the neck. Its interpretation is that whichever way he takes, right or left, in the methods of dispute, he prevails. Al-Khisam is the verbal noun of "khasamahu khisaman wa mukhasamatan," as said by Abu 'Ubayda. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the plural of khasm, as in "khasm, khisam, khusum," like "bahr, bihar, buhur." Al-Hasan said: "Alladd al-khisam" means one who speaks falsely. Qatada said: One who is most severe in disobedience, contentious in falsehood, who speaks with wisdom but acts with sin.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the most hateful of men to Allah the Exalted is the most contentious disputer (al-alladd al-khasim)." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," 13/180; and Muslim in al-'Ilm, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," no. 2668, 4/2054. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 10/97.]]

﴿And when he turns away﴾, that is, he withdraws and turns from you. ﴿He strives in the land﴾, that is, he works in it. It is also said: he travels and walks in it. ﴿To spread corruption therein﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: He cuts off the ties of kinship and sheds the blood of Muslims. ﴿And destroys crops and animals﴾. This is because al-Akhnas [[al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, with a fatha on the shin, a kasra on the ra', and a qaf at the end, a man of Thaqif.]] had a dispute between himself and Thaqif, so he raided them by night, burned their crops, and destroyed their livestock. [[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/302; also his Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 58.]]

Muqatil said: He went out to al-Ta'if to collect money owed to him by a debtor, and he burned the debtor's heap of grain and slaughtered his she-donkey. "Al-nasl" (offspring) means the offspring of every animal, and humans are included among them. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And when he turns away﴾ means when he takes charge of affairs and becomes a ruler. ﴿He strives in the land﴾. Mujahid said regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land﴾: When he becomes ruler, he acts with aggression and oppression, so Allah withholds the rain and destroys the crops and the offspring. ﴿And Allah does not love corruption﴾, that is, He does not approve of corruption. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Cutting a dirham (i.e., cheating over it) is a form of corruption in the land.

His saying: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah,"﴾, that is, be mindful of Allah, ﴿pride takes him to sin﴾, that is, the pride and zealotry of the Age of Ignorance (hamiyyat al-jahiliyya) drive him to act sinfully, that is, to act wrongfully. Al-'Izza means arrogance and self-protection. It is also said the meaning is: ﴿pride takes him﴾ on account of the sin that is in his heart, so the preposition "bi" stands in place of "li."

His saying: ﴿Then Hell is sufficient for him﴾, that is, it is enough for him. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾, that is, the bed. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Among the greatest sins before Allah is that it be said to a servant, "Fear Allah," and he replies, "Look to yourself."

It is narrated that it was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: "Fear Allah," so he placed his cheek on the ground in humility before Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, that is, seeking the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. ﴿And Allah is Compassionate to the servants﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak that this verse was revealed concerning the expedition of al-Raji' (sariyyat al-Raji'). That is because the disbelievers of Quraysh sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was in Madinah, saying: "We have embraced Islam, so send to us some men of your companions' scholars to teach us your religion." This was a deception from them. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari, Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bukayr, Abd Allah ibn Tariq ibn Shihab al-Balawi, and Zayd ibn al-Dathina, and he appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn Abi al-Aflah al-Ansari.

Abu Hurayra said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ten spies and appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit al-Ansari. They set out and halted at Batn al-Raji', between Makkah and Madinah, and with them were dates of 'ajwa. They ate, and an old woman passed by and saw the date pits. She returned to her people in Makkah and said: "The people of Yathrib, companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), have traveled this route." So seventy men mounted, carrying spears, until they surrounded them.

Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They were reported to a tribe of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan, so about a hundred archers set out for them. They followed their tracks until they found the place where they had eaten the dates at a campsite they had stayed in. They said: "Dates of Yathrib!" So they followed their tracks. When 'Asim and his companions sensed them, they took refuge on a fadfad. [[Al-fadfad: a hard, rough, elevated place. In manuscript A it reads: Qudayr.]] The people surrounded them, and they killed Marthad, Khalid and Abd Allah ibn Tariq. 'Asim ibn Thabit emptied his quiver, which contained seven arrows, and with every arrow he killed a man of the leading polytheists. Then he said: "O Allah, I have protected Your religion at the beginning of the day, so protect my flesh at the end of the day." Then the polytheists surrounded him and killed him. When they had killed him, they wanted to cut off his head to sell it to Sulafa bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd, for when her son had been struck at the Battle of Uhud, she had vowed: "If I can get hold of the head of 'Asim, I will drink wine from his skull." So Allah sent a swarm of hornets (dabr), which are wasps, and they shielded 'Asim, so they could not reach him. He was thus called "Hami al-Dabr" (the Guarded by the Hornets). They said: "Leave him until the evening, then it will pass from him and we will take him." But a black cloud came and rained a torrent like the gushing of a waterskin [[al-'Azali: plural of al-'azla', the lower mouth of a waterskin; the sudden rush of the rain is compared to what gushes from the mouth of a waterskin.]], and Allah caused the valley to become a torrent, which carried 'Asim away to Paradise, and carried fifty of the polytheists to the Fire. 'Asim had given a covenant to Allah the Exalted that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say, when it reached him that the hornets had protected him: "How wondrous is Allah's protection of the believing servant. 'Asim had vowed that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist, so Allah protected him after his death just as 'Asim had refrained in his life."

The polytheists captured Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari and Zayd ibn al-Dathina and took them to Makkah. As for Khubayb, the sons of al-Harith ibn 'Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought him in order to kill him in revenge for their father. Khubayb was the one who had killed al-Harith on the Day of Badr. Khubayb remained with them as a captive until they resolved to kill him. He borrowed a razor from the daughters of al-Harith to shave with, and they lent it to him. A small child of theirs wandered off while she was unaware, and the woman was startled to find Khubayb with the child seated on his thigh and the razor in his hand. The woman screamed. Khubayb said: "Do you fear that I will kill him? I would never do that. Treachery is not among our ways." The woman said afterwards: "By Allah, I have never seen a captive better than Khubayb. By Allah, one day I found him eating a bunch of grapes in his hand while he was bound in iron, and there was no fruit in Makkah at that time. It was nothing but a provision that Allah had granted to Khubayb."

Then they went out of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) to kill him in the open area (al-Hill) and intended to crucify him. Khubayb said to them: "Let me pray two rak'ahs." So they left him. Khubayb was the first to establish the prayer for every Muslim who is killed in captivity (sabran) [[Every living being that is bound and then killed is said to have been killed in captivity (sabran).]]. He prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "Were it not that they would think I was anxious, I would have prolonged it. O Allah, count them, kill them one by one, and leave none of them." Then he recited:

"I care not, when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall for the sake of Allah."
"And that is for the sake of God; if He wills, He will bless the scattered limbs of a torn body."

Then they crucified him alive, and he said: "O Allah, You know that there is no one near me to convey my greetings to Your Messenger, so convey my greetings to him." Then Abu Sirwa'a Uqba ibn al-Harith stood up and killed him.

It is also said that there was a polytheist man called Salaman, Abu Maysara, who had a spear, and he placed it between Khubayb's breasts. Khubayb said to him: "Fear Allah." But that only increased him in arrogance, so he thrust it in and pierced him through. This is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride takes him to sin﴾, meaning Salaman.

As for Zayd ibn al-Dathina, Safwan ibn Umayya bought him in order to kill him in revenge for his father Umayya ibn Khalaf. He sent him with a freedman of his called Nistas to al-Tan'im to kill him for his father. A group of Quraysh gathered, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. When Zayd was brought forward to be killed, Abu Sufyan said to him: "I beseech you by Allah, O Zayd, would you love that Muhammad were here now in your place, and we would strike his neck, and you were with your family?" He said: "By Allah, I would not love that Muhammad (ﷺ), at this moment, in the place where he is, should have a thorn prick him and harm him, while I sit with my family." Abu Sufyan said: "I have never seen anyone love another as the companions of Muhammad love Muhammad." Then Nistas killed him.

When this report reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said to his companions: "Which of you will take Khubayb down from his cross, and he will have Paradise?" [[In manuscript A (in the margin): "will bring down" (yunzil).]] Al-Zubayr said: "I will, O Messenger of Allah, and my companion al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad." So the two of them set out, walking by night and hiding by day, until they reached al-Tan'im at night. Around the cross were forty polytheist men, asleep and intoxicated. They took him down, and he was fresh and pliable, nothing about him had changed after forty days. His hand was over his wound, and it was dripping blood. The color was the color of blood, and the scent was the scent of musk. Al-Zubayr carried him on his horse, and they departed. The disbelievers woke up and found that Khubayb was missing, so they informed Quraysh, and seventy of them rode out. When they caught up with the two, al-Zubayr threw Khubayb, and the earth swallowed him, so he was called "Balee' al-Ard" (the one swallowed by the earth).

Al-Zubayr said: "What has emboldened you against us, O assembly of Quraysh?" Then he lifted the turban from his head and said: "I am al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, my mother is Safiyyah bint 'Abd al-Muttalib, and my companion is al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. We are two lions lying in wait, defending our two cubs. If you wish, we will contend with you in archery; if you wish, we will fight you hand to hand; and if you wish, you may depart." So they turned back to Makkah. The two of them then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Jibril was with him. He said: "O Muhammad, the angels take pride in these two of your Companions." So there was revealed concerning al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad: ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, when the two of them sold themselves to bring down Khubayb from his cross.[[See Fath al-Bari: 7/378-379, and 'Uyun al-Athar by Ibn Sayyid al-Nas: 2/56-66.]]

And most of the exegetes said: It was revealed concerning Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi when the polytheists seized him, along with a group of believers, and tortured them. Suhayb said to them: "I am an old man; it will not harm you whether I was with you or with others. Will you take my wealth and leave me and my religion?" They agreed, and he had stipulated for them a mount and provisions. He remained in Makkah for as long as Allah willed, then set out for Madinah. Abu Bakr and 'Umar met him with some men. Abu Bakr said to him: "Your sale has profited you, O Abu Yahya!" Suhayb replied: "And yours too; do not be grieved." Suhayb said: "What is that?" Abu Bakr said: "Allah has revealed concerning you," and he recited to him this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ata' said: Suhayb came migrating toward the Prophet ﷺ, and a group of Quraysh polytheists followed him. He dismounted from his mount, emptied what was in his quiver, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know well that I am among the most skilled archers of you. By Allah, I will not place an arrow from my quiver except in the heart of one of you, and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot every arrow in my quiver, then struck with my sword while anything remains in my hand. Then do whatever you wish. Or, if you wish, I will show you my wealth in Makkah and you will leave my way." They said: "Yes." He did so, and Allah revealed this verse.[[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/304; Ibn Kathir 1/437; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 58; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 3/227-228.]]

al-Hasan said: Do you know concerning whom this verse was revealed? It was revealed concerning a Muslim who meets a disbeliever, and says to him, "Say: there is no god but Allah," but he refuses to say it. The Muslim said: "By Allah, I will sell myself for Allah," so he advanced and fought alone until he was killed.

It was also said that the verse was revealed concerning enjoining good and forbidding evil. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I see the one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah stands up and commands this man to fear Allah, but he does not accept, and pride in sin seizes him. He [the first] says: 'I sell myself to Allah,' and fights him. The two men then fight over that." 'Ali, whenever he recited this verse, would say: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the two have fought!" And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, and 'Umar said: ﴿Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return﴾ — a man stood up to enjoin good and forbid evil, and was killed.

Abu Umamah reported that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said: "The best jihad is the one who speaks a word of truth before an unjust ruler."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in al-Malahim, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, 6/191. And al-Tirmidhi: in al-Fitan, chapter on the best jihad being a word of justice before an unjust ruler, 6/395, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route" (and Abu Umamah's hadith supports it). And al-Nasa'i: in al-Bay'ah, chapter on the virtue of one who speaks the truth before an unjust ruler, 7/161. And Ibn Majah: in al-Fitan, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, 2/1329. And Ahmad: 3/19 (part of a hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri); 4/324 from Tariq ibn Shihab; 5/251-256 from Abu Umamah.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 204–207 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Ata' said: It was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhra. His name was Ubayy, and he was called al-Akhnas because on the Day of Badr he withdrew (khanasa) with three hundred men from Banu Zuhra from fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was a man sweet of speech and pleasant of appearance. He would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sit with him, and display Islam, saying, "I truly love you," and swearing by Allah to that. But he was a hypocrite, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would bring him closer in his gathering. Then the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world impresses you﴾. [[See: al-Tabari 4/229; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 96.]] That is, you find it good and it becomes great in your heart. It is said that for approval one says "a'jabani kadha" (this impressed me), and for dislike and disapproval one says " 'ajibtu min kadha" (I am astonished at such and such).

﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾, meaning the hypocrite's saying: "By Allah, I believe in you and I love you." ﴿Yet he is the most contentious of opponents﴾, that is, the most fierce in disputation. It is said: "Laddta, ya hadha, wa anta talidd laddan wa ladadatan." When you want to say that he overcame his opponent, you say: "laddahu yaliddahu laddan." It is said: "rajul aladd" (a man most contentious), "imra'a laddaa" (a woman most contentious), and "qawm lud" (a people most contentious). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that you may warn thereby a people most contentious﴾ (Maryam 19:97).

Al-Zajjaj said: Its derivation is from ladidayi al-'unuq, which are the two sides of the neck. Its interpretation is that whichever way he takes, right or left, in the methods of dispute, he prevails. Al-Khisam is the verbal noun of "khasamahu khisaman wa mukhasamatan," as said by Abu 'Ubayda. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the plural of khasm, as in "khasm, khisam, khusum," like "bahr, bihar, buhur." Al-Hasan said: "Alladd al-khisam" means one who speaks falsely. Qatada said: One who is most severe in disobedience, contentious in falsehood, who speaks with wisdom but acts with sin.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu 'Asim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the most hateful of men to Allah the Exalted is the most contentious disputer (al-alladd al-khasim)." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," 13/180; and Muslim in al-'Ilm, chapter "al-Alladd al-Khasim," no. 2668, 4/2054. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 10/97.]]

﴿And when he turns away﴾, that is, he withdraws and turns from you. ﴿He strives in the land﴾, that is, he works in it. It is also said: he travels and walks in it. ﴿To spread corruption therein﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: He cuts off the ties of kinship and sheds the blood of Muslims. ﴿And destroys crops and animals﴾. This is because al-Akhnas [[al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, with a fatha on the shin, a kasra on the ra', and a qaf at the end, a man of Thaqif.]] had a dispute between himself and Thaqif, so he raided them by night, burned their crops, and destroyed their livestock. [[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/302; also his Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 58.]]

Muqatil said: He went out to al-Ta'if to collect money owed to him by a debtor, and he burned the debtor's heap of grain and slaughtered his she-donkey. "Al-nasl" (offspring) means the offspring of every animal, and humans are included among them. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿And when he turns away﴾ means when he takes charge of affairs and becomes a ruler. ﴿He strives in the land﴾. Mujahid said regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land﴾: When he becomes ruler, he acts with aggression and oppression, so Allah withholds the rain and destroys the crops and the offspring. ﴿And Allah does not love corruption﴾, that is, He does not approve of corruption. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: Cutting a dirham (i.e., cheating over it) is a form of corruption in the land.

His saying: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah,"﴾, that is, be mindful of Allah, ﴿pride takes him to sin﴾, that is, the pride and zealotry of the Age of Ignorance (hamiyyat al-jahiliyya) drive him to act sinfully, that is, to act wrongfully. Al-'Izza means arrogance and self-protection. It is also said the meaning is: ﴿pride takes him﴾ on account of the sin that is in his heart, so the preposition "bi" stands in place of "li."

His saying: ﴿Then Hell is sufficient for him﴾, that is, it is enough for him. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾, that is, the bed. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Among the greatest sins before Allah is that it be said to a servant, "Fear Allah," and he replies, "Look to yourself."

It is narrated that it was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: "Fear Allah," so he placed his cheek on the ground in humility before Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, that is, seeking the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. ﴿And Allah is Compassionate to the servants﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak that this verse was revealed concerning the expedition of al-Raji' (sariyyat al-Raji'). That is because the disbelievers of Quraysh sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was in Madinah, saying: "We have embraced Islam, so send to us some men of your companions' scholars to teach us your religion." This was a deception from them. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari, Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bukayr, Abd Allah ibn Tariq ibn Shihab al-Balawi, and Zayd ibn al-Dathina, and he appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn Abi al-Aflah al-Ansari.

Abu Hurayra said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ten spies and appointed over them 'Asim ibn Thabit al-Ansari. They set out and halted at Batn al-Raji', between Makkah and Madinah, and with them were dates of 'ajwa. They ate, and an old woman passed by and saw the date pits. She returned to her people in Makkah and said: "The people of Yathrib, companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), have traveled this route." So seventy men mounted, carrying spears, until they surrounded them.

Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They were reported to a tribe of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan, so about a hundred archers set out for them. They followed their tracks until they found the place where they had eaten the dates at a campsite they had stayed in. They said: "Dates of Yathrib!" So they followed their tracks. When 'Asim and his companions sensed them, they took refuge on a fadfad. [[Al-fadfad: a hard, rough, elevated place. In manuscript A it reads: Qudayr.]] The people surrounded them, and they killed Marthad, Khalid and Abd Allah ibn Tariq. 'Asim ibn Thabit emptied his quiver, which contained seven arrows, and with every arrow he killed a man of the leading polytheists. Then he said: "O Allah, I have protected Your religion at the beginning of the day, so protect my flesh at the end of the day." Then the polytheists surrounded him and killed him. When they had killed him, they wanted to cut off his head to sell it to Sulafa bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd, for when her son had been struck at the Battle of Uhud, she had vowed: "If I can get hold of the head of 'Asim, I will drink wine from his skull." So Allah sent a swarm of hornets (dabr), which are wasps, and they shielded 'Asim, so they could not reach him. He was thus called "Hami al-Dabr" (the Guarded by the Hornets). They said: "Leave him until the evening, then it will pass from him and we will take him." But a black cloud came and rained a torrent like the gushing of a waterskin [[al-'Azali: plural of al-'azla', the lower mouth of a waterskin; the sudden rush of the rain is compared to what gushes from the mouth of a waterskin.]], and Allah caused the valley to become a torrent, which carried 'Asim away to Paradise, and carried fifty of the polytheists to the Fire. 'Asim had given a covenant to Allah the Exalted that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist.

Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say, when it reached him that the hornets had protected him: "How wondrous is Allah's protection of the believing servant. 'Asim had vowed that no polytheist would ever touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist, so Allah protected him after his death just as 'Asim had refrained in his life."

The polytheists captured Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari and Zayd ibn al-Dathina and took them to Makkah. As for Khubayb, the sons of al-Harith ibn 'Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought him in order to kill him in revenge for their father. Khubayb was the one who had killed al-Harith on the Day of Badr. Khubayb remained with them as a captive until they resolved to kill him. He borrowed a razor from the daughters of al-Harith to shave with, and they lent it to him. A small child of theirs wandered off while she was unaware, and the woman was startled to find Khubayb with the child seated on his thigh and the razor in his hand. The woman screamed. Khubayb said: "Do you fear that I will kill him? I would never do that. Treachery is not among our ways." The woman said afterwards: "By Allah, I have never seen a captive better than Khubayb. By Allah, one day I found him eating a bunch of grapes in his hand while he was bound in iron, and there was no fruit in Makkah at that time. It was nothing but a provision that Allah had granted to Khubayb."

Then they went out of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) to kill him in the open area (al-Hill) and intended to crucify him. Khubayb said to them: "Let me pray two rak'ahs." So they left him. Khubayb was the first to establish the prayer for every Muslim who is killed in captivity (sabran) [[Every living being that is bound and then killed is said to have been killed in captivity (sabran).]]. He prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "Were it not that they would think I was anxious, I would have prolonged it. O Allah, count them, kill them one by one, and leave none of them." Then he recited:

"I care not, when I am killed as a Muslim, on which side I fall for the sake of Allah."
"And that is for the sake of God; if He wills, He will bless the scattered limbs of a torn body."

Then they crucified him alive, and he said: "O Allah, You know that there is no one near me to convey my greetings to Your Messenger, so convey my greetings to him." Then Abu Sirwa'a Uqba ibn al-Harith stood up and killed him.

It is also said that there was a polytheist man called Salaman, Abu Maysara, who had a spear, and he placed it between Khubayb's breasts. Khubayb said to him: "Fear Allah." But that only increased him in arrogance, so he thrust it in and pierced him through. This is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride takes him to sin﴾, meaning Salaman.

As for Zayd ibn al-Dathina, Safwan ibn Umayya bought him in order to kill him in revenge for his father Umayya ibn Khalaf. He sent him with a freedman of his called Nistas to al-Tan'im to kill him for his father. A group of Quraysh gathered, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. When Zayd was brought forward to be killed, Abu Sufyan said to him: "I beseech you by Allah, O Zayd, would you love that Muhammad were here now in your place, and we would strike his neck, and you were with your family?" He said: "By Allah, I would not love that Muhammad (ﷺ), at this moment, in the place where he is, should have a thorn prick him and harm him, while I sit with my family." Abu Sufyan said: "I have never seen anyone love another as the companions of Muhammad love Muhammad." Then Nistas killed him.

When this report reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said to his companions: "Which of you will take Khubayb down from his cross, and he will have Paradise?" [[In manuscript A (in the margin): "will bring down" (yunzil).]] Al-Zubayr said: "I will, O Messenger of Allah, and my companion al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad." So the two of them set out, walking by night and hiding by day, until they reached al-Tan'im at night. Around the cross were forty polytheist men, asleep and intoxicated. They took him down, and he was fresh and pliable, nothing about him had changed after forty days. His hand was over his wound, and it was dripping blood. The color was the color of blood, and the scent was the scent of musk. Al-Zubayr carried him on his horse, and they departed. The disbelievers woke up and found that Khubayb was missing, so they informed Quraysh, and seventy of them rode out. When they caught up with the two, al-Zubayr threw Khubayb, and the earth swallowed him, so he was called "Balee' al-Ard" (the one swallowed by the earth).

Al-Zubayr said: "What has emboldened you against us, O assembly of Quraysh?" Then he lifted the turban from his head and said: "I am al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, my mother is Safiyyah bint 'Abd al-Muttalib, and my companion is al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. We are two lions lying in wait, defending our two cubs. If you wish, we will contend with you in archery; if you wish, we will fight you hand to hand; and if you wish, you may depart." So they turned back to Makkah. The two of them then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Jibril was with him. He said: "O Muhammad, the angels take pride in these two of your Companions." So there was revealed concerning al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad: ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, when the two of them sold themselves to bring down Khubayb from his cross.[[See Fath al-Bari: 7/378-379, and 'Uyun al-Athar by Ibn Sayyid al-Nas: 2/56-66.]]

And most of the exegetes said: It was revealed concerning Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi when the polytheists seized him, along with a group of believers, and tortured them. Suhayb said to them: "I am an old man; it will not harm you whether I was with you or with others. Will you take my wealth and leave me and my religion?" They agreed, and he had stipulated for them a mount and provisions. He remained in Makkah for as long as Allah willed, then set out for Madinah. Abu Bakr and 'Umar met him with some men. Abu Bakr said to him: "Your sale has profited you, O Abu Yahya!" Suhayb replied: "And yours too; do not be grieved." Suhayb said: "What is that?" Abu Bakr said: "Allah has revealed concerning you," and he recited to him this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ata' said: Suhayb came migrating toward the Prophet ﷺ, and a group of Quraysh polytheists followed him. He dismounted from his mount, emptied what was in his quiver, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know well that I am among the most skilled archers of you. By Allah, I will not place an arrow from my quiver except in the heart of one of you, and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot every arrow in my quiver, then struck with my sword while anything remains in my hand. Then do whatever you wish. Or, if you wish, I will show you my wealth in Makkah and you will leave my way." They said: "Yes." He did so, and Allah revealed this verse.[[See: Tafsir al-Wahidi 1/304; Ibn Kathir 1/437; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 58; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 3/227-228.]]

al-Hasan said: Do you know concerning whom this verse was revealed? It was revealed concerning a Muslim who meets a disbeliever, and says to him, "Say: there is no god but Allah," but he refuses to say it. The Muslim said: "By Allah, I will sell myself for Allah," so he advanced and fought alone until he was killed.

It was also said that the verse was revealed concerning enjoining good and forbidding evil. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I see the one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah stands up and commands this man to fear Allah, but he does not accept, and pride in sin seizes him. He [the first] says: 'I sell myself to Allah,' and fights him. The two men then fight over that." 'Ali, whenever he recited this verse, would say: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the two have fought!" And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿And among people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, and 'Umar said: ﴿Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return﴾ — a man stood up to enjoin good and forbid evil, and was killed.

Abu Umamah reported that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said: "The best jihad is the one who speaks a word of truth before an unjust ruler."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in al-Malahim, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, 6/191. And al-Tirmidhi: in al-Fitan, chapter on the best jihad being a word of justice before an unjust ruler, 6/395, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route" (and Abu Umamah's hadith supports it). And al-Nasa'i: in al-Bay'ah, chapter on the virtue of one who speaks the truth before an unjust ruler, 7/161. And Ibn Majah: in al-Fitan, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, 2/1329. And Ahmad: 3/19 (part of a hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri); 4/324 from Tariq ibn Shihab; 5/251-256 from Abu Umamah.]]

**Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah 2, verses 208–210:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace (al-silm) completely﴾. The people of the Hijaz and al-Kisa'i read *al-silm* here with a fatha on the sin (*al-silm*). The rest read it with a kasra (*al-silm*). In Surah al-Anfal, *"wa in janahu lil-silm"* (﴿and if they incline to peace﴾) is read with a kasra by Abu Bakr and the rest with a fatha. In Surah Muhammad (ﷺ), *al-silm* is read with a kasra by Hamzah and Abu Bakr.

This verse was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Book, Abdullah ibn Salam al-Nadiri and his companions. They used to honour Saturday and disliked eating the flesh and drinking the milk of camels after they had embraced Islam. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Torah is the Book of Allah, so let us leave it to us to perform its rites in our night prayers." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace completely﴾. [[See: Al-Wahidi, *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 97.]] That is, into Islam.

Mujahid said: "In the rulings of the people of Islam and their deeds." *Kaffah* means "all together." It was also said: "Enter into Islam to the end of its laws, restraining yourselves from going beyond it to anything else." The root of *al-silm* is from *al-istislam* (submission) and *al-inqiyad* (compliance), and for this reason reconciliation is called *silm*.

Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said concerning this verse: "Islam has eight shares," and he enumerated: prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, Umrah, jihad, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong. He said: "Whoever has no share in it has failed."

﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, that is, his traces, in what he has made attractive to you, such as the prohibition of Saturday, camel flesh, and other things. ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾.
