Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 211:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Ask the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., ask, O Muhammad, the Jews of Madinah. ﴿How many clear signs We gave them﴾, i.e., how many We gave their fathers and forebears, ﴿of a clear sign﴾, a manifest proof of the prophethood of Musa (peace be upon him), such as the staff and the white hand, the splitting of the sea, and others. It was also said: its meaning is the proofs which He gave them in the Torah and the Gospel concerning the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And whoever substitutes﴾, i.e., changes, ﴿the favour of Allah﴾, meaning the Book of Allah. It was also said: the covenant of Allah. And it was said: whoever denies the proof of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿after it has come to him, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 212–213:**

﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾. Most scholars hold that the one who makes it attractive is Allah, Exalted is He. Allah's making things attractive means that He created good things and wondrous sights, so creation looked at them beyond their true worth, they were pleased with them, and they were seduced by them. Al-Zajjaj said: "Satan made it attractive to them." It is said that this verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of the Arabs, Abu Jahl and his companions, who enjoyed the wealth that Allah had spread for them in this world and denied the Return. ﴿And they mock those who believe﴾, meaning they ridicule the poor among the believers.

Ibn 'Abbas said: By "those who believe" he meant 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Suhayb, Bilal, Khabbab and those like them. Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who enjoyed luxury in this world and mocked the weak among the believers and the poor among the Emigrants, saying, "Look at these people whom Muhammad claims he will triumph through!" 'Ata' said: It was revealed concerning the leaders of the Jews of the Banu Qurayza, al-Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa', who mocked the poor Emigrants. So Allah promised them that He would give them the wealth of Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir without fighting. [[See: al-Wasit: 1/308; al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/581.]] ﴿And they mock those who believe﴾ because of their poverty. ﴿But those who feared Allah﴾, meaning these poor people, ﴿will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, because they will be in the highest 'Illiyyin, while those (mockers) will be in the lowest of the lowest.

Abu Sa'id 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Adhafiri informed us: Ishaq al-Dabari informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Usama ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I stood at the gate of Paradise and I saw that most of its people were the poor. And I stood at the gate of the Fire and I saw that most of its people were women. And the people of wealth [[al-Ghani: the rich.]] were detained, except that those among them who were of the people of the Fire had already been ordered to the Fire." [[A portion of a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari from Anas: in al-Nikah, chapter no. (87), 9/298, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/266.]]

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il said to us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim said to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim related to me, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, that he said: A man passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to a man sitting beside him, "What is your opinion of this one?" He said: "This man is among the nobles of the people; by Allah, he is worthy, if he proposes marriage, to be married to, and if he intercedes, to have his intercession accepted." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent. Then another man passed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "What is your opinion of this one?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is one of the poor Muslims. He is worthy, if he proposes marriage, not to be married to, and if he intercedes, not to have his intercession accepted, and if he speaks, not to be listened to." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This one is better than a whole earth full of the likes of that one." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-Nikah, chapter on equality (kafa'a) in religion, 9/132.]]

﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: It means abundantly, without measure, because whatever is subject to reckoning is little. The meaning is: He widens provision for whom He wills and extends it to whom He wills among His servants. Al-Dahhak said: It means without accountability; He provides for him in this world and does not call him to account in the Hereafter. It is also said: This refers to Allah, Exalted is He; its meaning is that He restricts provision for whom He wills and extends it for whom He wills, and He does not give everyone according to their need. Rather, He gives much to one who has no need of it and gives little to one who is in need. So He is not to be questioned about what He provides, and He is not to be called to account for it, nor is it said: "Why did You give this and withhold that? Why did You give this more than that?" It is also said that the meaning is: He does not fear the depletion of His treasuries, so that He would need to reckon what goes out from them, for reckoning on the part of a giver only arises from fear of the depletion of his treasuries.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Mankind was one community﴾, upon one religion. Mujahid said: He meant Adam alone; he was one community. He said: The singular was expressed in the plural form because he is the origin of descendants and the father of humankind. Then Allah created Eve and spread humanity from the two of them, and they dispersed, and they were Muslims until Qabil killed Habil, and then they differed. ﴿So Allah sent the prophets﴾. Al-Hasan and 'Ata' said: From the time of Adam's death until the sending of Nuh, people were one community upon the religion of disbelief, like cattle; so Allah sent Nuh and other prophets. [[This view is refuted by the opinion of Qatada and 'Ikrima; it is related from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf report, and its chain is sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari (see Ibn Kathir: 1/443, takhrij al-Wadi'i).]] Qatada and 'Ikrima said: People were from the time of Adam until the sending of Nuh, and between them were ten generations, all upon one law of truth and guidance. Then they differed in the time of Nuh, so Allah sent Nuh to them; he was the first prophet sent, and then He sent prophets after him.

Al-Kalbi said: They were the people of Nuh's ark, who were believers, and then they differed after the death of Nuh.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: In the time of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, people were one community, all of them disbelievers; so Allah sent Ibrahim and other prophets. It is also said: The Arabs were upon the religion of Ibrahim until 'Amr ibn Luhay changed it. It is related from Abu al-'Aliya, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When people were presented to Adam and brought out from his loins and acknowledged servitude, they were one community, all of them Muslims, and they were never one community other than on that day. Then they differed after Adam. Its parallel is in Surah Yunus: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, then they differed; and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them concerning that wherein they differed﴾ (10:19). Their total was one hundred and twenty-four thousand, and the messengers among them were three hundred and thirteen, and those mentioned in the Qur'an by name were twenty-eight prophets. ﴿Bearers of good news﴾ of reward to whoever believes and obeys, ﴿and warners﴾, cautioning of punishment, to whoever disbelieves and disobeys. ﴿And He sent down with them the Book﴾, meaning the Books, the meaning being: He sent down with each one of them the Book. ﴿In truth﴾, with justice and truthfulness, ﴿so that it might judge between the people﴾. Abu Ja'far read ﴿liyahkuma﴾ with a damma on the yā' and a fatha on the kāf here, and in the first of Al 'Imran, and in two places in al-Nur, because the Book does not in reality judge; rather, the judgment is made by it. The recitation of the general body of readers is with a fatha on the yā' and a damma on the kāf, meaning "so that the Book might judge," and it is expressed this way for breadth of speech, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This Our Book speaks against you with truth﴾ (45:29). It is also said that the meaning is: so that each prophet might judge by his Book. ﴿Concerning that wherein they differed﴾, meaning concerning the Book, ﴿and none differed concerning it except those who were given it﴾, meaning those who were given the Book, ﴿after clear proofs had come to them﴾, meaning the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel. Al-Farra' said: Their differing has two meanings. The first is that some of them disbelieved in the Book of others; Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others"﴾ (4:150). The second is their distortion of the Book of Allah; Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They distort words from their places﴾ (4:46). It is also said that the verse refers to Muhammad ﷺ and his Book, concerning which the People of the Book differed, ﴿after clear proofs had come to them﴾, the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their books, ﴿out of envy and rivalry among themselves﴾, meaning out of injustice and jealousy. ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that wherein they differed﴾, meaning concerning what they differed about ﴿of the truth, by His permission﴾, by His knowledge and His will regarding them. Ibn Zayd said concerning this verse: They differed regarding the qibla: some of them prayed toward the east, some toward the west, and some toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and Allah guided us to the Ka'ba. They differed regarding fasting, and Allah guided us to the month of Ramadan. They differed regarding the days: the Jews took Saturday and the Christians Sunday, and Allah guided us to Friday. They differed regarding Ibrahim, peace be upon him: the Jews said he was a Jew, and the Christians said he was a Christian, and Allah guided us to the truth about that. They differed regarding 'Isa: the Jews made him a slander, and the Christians made him a god, and Allah guided us to the truth concerning him. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 212–213:**

﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾. Most scholars hold that the one who makes it attractive is Allah, Exalted is He. Allah's making things attractive means that He created good things and wondrous sights, so creation looked at them beyond their true worth, they were pleased with them, and they were seduced by them. Al-Zajjaj said: "Satan made it attractive to them." It is said that this verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of the Arabs, Abu Jahl and his companions, who enjoyed the wealth that Allah had spread for them in this world and denied the Return. ﴿And they mock those who believe﴾, meaning they ridicule the poor among the believers.

Ibn 'Abbas said: By "those who believe" he meant 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Suhayb, Bilal, Khabbab and those like them. Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who enjoyed luxury in this world and mocked the weak among the believers and the poor among the Emigrants, saying, "Look at these people whom Muhammad claims he will triumph through!" 'Ata' said: It was revealed concerning the leaders of the Jews of the Banu Qurayza, al-Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa', who mocked the poor Emigrants. So Allah promised them that He would give them the wealth of Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir without fighting. [[See: al-Wasit: 1/308; al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/581.]] ﴿And they mock those who believe﴾ because of their poverty. ﴿But those who feared Allah﴾, meaning these poor people, ﴿will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, because they will be in the highest 'Illiyyin, while those (mockers) will be in the lowest of the lowest.

Abu Sa'id 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Adhafiri informed us: Ishaq al-Dabari informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Usama ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I stood at the gate of Paradise and I saw that most of its people were the poor. And I stood at the gate of the Fire and I saw that most of its people were women. And the people of wealth [[al-Ghani: the rich.]] were detained, except that those among them who were of the people of the Fire had already been ordered to the Fire." [[A portion of a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari from Anas: in al-Nikah, chapter no. (87), 9/298, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/266.]]

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il said to us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim said to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim related to me, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, that he said: A man passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to a man sitting beside him, "What is your opinion of this one?" He said: "This man is among the nobles of the people; by Allah, he is worthy, if he proposes marriage, to be married to, and if he intercedes, to have his intercession accepted." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent. Then another man passed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "What is your opinion of this one?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is one of the poor Muslims. He is worthy, if he proposes marriage, not to be married to, and if he intercedes, not to have his intercession accepted, and if he speaks, not to be listened to." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This one is better than a whole earth full of the likes of that one." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-Nikah, chapter on equality (kafa'a) in religion, 9/132.]]

﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: It means abundantly, without measure, because whatever is subject to reckoning is little. The meaning is: He widens provision for whom He wills and extends it to whom He wills among His servants. Al-Dahhak said: It means without accountability; He provides for him in this world and does not call him to account in the Hereafter. It is also said: This refers to Allah, Exalted is He; its meaning is that He restricts provision for whom He wills and extends it for whom He wills, and He does not give everyone according to their need. Rather, He gives much to one who has no need of it and gives little to one who is in need. So He is not to be questioned about what He provides, and He is not to be called to account for it, nor is it said: "Why did You give this and withhold that? Why did You give this more than that?" It is also said that the meaning is: He does not fear the depletion of His treasuries, so that He would need to reckon what goes out from them, for reckoning on the part of a giver only arises from fear of the depletion of his treasuries.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Mankind was one community﴾, upon one religion. Mujahid said: He meant Adam alone; he was one community. He said: The singular was expressed in the plural form because he is the origin of descendants and the father of humankind. Then Allah created Eve and spread humanity from the two of them, and they dispersed, and they were Muslims until Qabil killed Habil, and then they differed. ﴿So Allah sent the prophets﴾. [[This view is refuted by the opinion of Qatada and 'Ikrima; it is related from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf report, and its chain is sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari (see Ibn Kathir: 1/443, takhrij al-Wadi'i).]] Qatada and 'Ikrima said: People were from the time of Adam until the sending of Nuh, and between them were ten generations, all upon one law of truth and guidance. Then they differed in the time of Nuh, so Allah sent Nuh to them; he was the first prophet sent, and then He sent prophets after him.

Al-Kalbi said: They were the people of Nuh's ark, who were believers, and then they differed after the death of Nuh.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: In the time of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, people were one community, all of them disbelievers; so Allah sent Ibrahim and other prophets. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 214:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise﴾. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this verse was revealed concerning the Battle of the Trench (ghazwat al-Khandaq), when the Muslims suffered what they suffered of hardship, severe fear, cold, straitened living, and various kinds of harm, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾ [33:10, al-Ahzab]. It was also said that it was revealed concerning the Battle of Uhud.

ʿAṭāʾ said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions entered Medina, hardship bore heavily upon them, because they had left with no wealth, had left their homes and their property in the hands of the polytheists, and had preferred the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger. The Jews openly showed enmity toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a group concealed hypocrisy. So Allah the Exalted revealed, to comfort their hearts: ﴿Or did you think﴾, meaning: "Did you think?" The mim (am) is a connecting particle (silah), as al-Farra' said. Al-Zajjaj said: it means "Rather, did you think?" The meaning of the verse is: "Did you suppose, O believers, that you would enter Paradise ﴿while there has not yet come to you﴾ — wa-lamma here is a connecting particle (silah) — ﴿the example of those who passed away﴾, that is, those who passed on ﴿before you﴾, the prophets and the believers, ﴿touched by misfortune﴾, meaning poverty, hardship and affliction, ﴿and adversity﴾, meaning illness and infirmity, ﴿and they were shaken﴾, meaning they were moved by various kinds of trials and calamities and were frightened, ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him said: When will the help of Allah come?﴾" The affliction continued upon them until they found the help slow in coming.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾. Nafi' read ḥattā yaqūla al-rasūl with the nominative (raf'), meaning "until the Messenger said." When the verb following ḥattā (ḥattā, "until") has the sense of the past tense while its form is that of the future (al-mustaqbal), there are two readings available: raf' (nominative) and naṣb (accusative). The naṣb follows the apparent sense of the sentence, because ḥattā governs the future verb in the accusative. The raf' is used because its meaning is past, and ḥattā does not govern the past tense.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 215–216:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾. It was revealed concerning 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was an elderly man of wealth. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what should we give in charity, and upon whom should we spend?" So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾. In His words ﴿mādhā﴾ there are two grammatical possibilities (i'rab). One is that its position is in the accusative (naṣb) governed by ﴿yunfiqūn﴾ (they spend), its meaning being "what thing do they spend." The other is that it is in the nominative (raf') with ﴿mā﴾ (what), and its meaning is "what is it that they spend." ﴿Say: Whatever wealth you spend for good﴾, that is, from property, ﴿is for parents, kinsfolk, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾, meaning He will reward you for it. The people of tafsir said: this was before the obligation of zakat, and it was abrogated (naskh) by zakat.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾, that is, jihad has been made obligatory upon you. The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse. ʿAṭāʾ said: jihad is voluntary (tatawwuʿ), and the verse is directed at the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone, not others. This view was adopted by al-Thawri. Those who held this view cited the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit back by a degree. And to all Allah has promised the best﴾ (4:95). If the one who sits back were neglecting an obligation, He would not have promised him the best. Others followed the apparent meaning of the verse and said: jihad is an obligation upon all Muslims until the Hour comes.

Abu Saʿid Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi al-Kharazmi informed us: Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Thaʿlabi informed us: Abu ʿAmr Ahmad ibn Ubayy al-Furati informed us: Abu al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us: Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Gharazah informed us: Saʿid ibn ʿUthman al-Saʿidi informed us, from ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever dies without having fought in battle and without having resolved in his soul to fight, dies upon a branch of hypocrisy." [Narrated by Muslim: in the Book of Leadership, chapter "Condemnation of one who dies without fighting and without having resolved to fight," no. (1910), 3/1517.]

But a group, and the majority (jumhur) hold this view, said: jihad is obligatory as a collective duty (fard kifayah). When some of the people perform it, it is dropped from the rest, like the funeral prayer and returning a greeting. Al-Zuhri and al-Awza'i said: Allah has prescribed jihad upon the people, whether by fighting or by remaining behind. Whoever fights, then it is good and excellent; and whoever remains behind, he is a reserve: if he is sought for help, he helps; if he is called to march forth, he marches; and if he is found to be unneeded, he remains.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And it is hateful to you﴾, that is, burdensome to you. Some scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: this hatred is in terms of the soul's aversion to it because of what it entails of financial burden, hardship upon the self, and risk to life, not that they disliked the command of Allah the Exalted. ʿIkrimah said: it was abrogated by the words of the Exalted: ﴿We hear and we obey﴾, meaning that they disliked it, then they loved it, and so they said ﴿We hear and we obey﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you﴾, because in fighting there is one of the two best outcomes: either victory and spoils, or martyrdom and Paradise. ﴿And perhaps you love a thing﴾, meaning sitting back from fighting, ﴿and it is bad for you﴾, because of what it entails of losing spoils and reward. ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 217:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it.﴾ The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ʿAbdullah ibn Jahsh, who was the son of the paternal aunt of the Prophet (ﷺ), in Jumada al-Akhira, two months before the battle of Badr, at the end of seventeen months from his migration to Madinah. He sent with him eight men from the Muhajirun: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri, ʿUkkasha ibn Mihsan al-Asadi, ʿUtba ibn Ghazwan al-Sulami, Abu Hudhayfa ibn ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Suhayl ibn Bayda, ʿAmir ibn Rabiʿa, Waqid ibn ʿAbdullah, and Khalid ibn Bukayr. He wrote a letter for their commander ʿAbdullah ibn Jahsh and said to him: "Set out in the name of Allah and do not look into the letter until you have travelled for two days. Then when you descend, open the letter and read it to your companions, then proceed with what I have commanded you, and do not compel any of your companions to go with you." So ʿAbdullah travelled for two days, then he descended, opened the letter, and in it was: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. To proceed: Set out in the blessing of Allah with those of your companions who are with you, until you alight at Batn Nakhla, and watch there for the caravan of Quraysh, perhaps you may bring us some news from them." When he looked into the letter he said: "I hear and I obey." Then he said to his companions what he had been told, and said: "He has forbidden me to compel any of you. Whoever desires martyrdom, let him go forward, and whoever dislikes it, let him return." Then he went on, and his companions went with him; none of them lagged behind him, until he reached Maʿdin above al-Fur‘, at a place in the Hijaz called Bahran. Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and ʿUtba ibn Ghazwan lost a camel they were riding in turns, so they lagged behind in search of it, while he proceeded with the rest of his companions until they alighted at Batn Nakhla between Makkah and al-Ta'if.

While they were in that state, a caravan of Quraysh passed by, carrying raisins, leather, and goods from the trade of al-Ta'if, among them ʿAmr ibn al-Hadrami, al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, the client of Hisham ibn al-Mughira, and ʿUthman ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mughira and his brother Nawfal ibn ʿAbdullah, both of Makhzum. When they saw the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they feared them. ʿAbdullah ibn Jahsh said: "The people have been frightened of you. Shave the head of one man among you and let him approach them." So they shaved the head of ʿUkkasha, then they looked down upon them and said: "The people of ʿAmmar, there is no harm upon you," and they gave them safety. This was on the last day of Jumada al-Akhira, though they thought it was from Jumada, while it was from Rajab. The people consulted and said: "If you leave them tonight, they will enter the Haram and be protected from you." So they resolved to engage the people in battle, and Waqid ibn ʿAbdullah al-Sahmi shot ʿAmr ibn al-Hadrami with an arrow and killed him, so he was the first slain of the polytheists [and he was the first slain in the Hijra, and the Prophet (ﷺ) paid the blood-money of Ibn al-Hadrami to his heirs from Quraysh. Mujahid and others said: because there was a covenant between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Quraysh, a truce with the people of Makkah for two years, that he would not fight them and they would not fight him] [[Omitted from (B).]]

Al-Hakam and ʿUthman were taken captive, so they were the first two captives in Islam. Nawfal escaped and eluded them. The believers drove off the caravan and the two captives until they arrived before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah. Quraysh said: "Muhammad has made lawful the sacred month, shedding blood in it, seizing property," and the people of Makkah reproached those Muslims who were among them, saying: "O company of the apostates, you have made the sacred month lawful and fought in it!"

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard this, he said to Ibn Jahsh and his companions: "I did not command you to fight in the sacred month." He halted the caravan and the two captives and refused to take anything from it. This weighed heavily on the companions of the expedition, and they thought they were ruined and were distressed, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have killed Ibn al-Hadrami, then we entered the evening and looked at the crescent of Rajab, and we do not know whether we struck him in Rajab or in Jumada?" The people spoke much about this, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then took the caravan and set aside from it the one-fifth, which was the first fifth in Islam, and divided the rest among the companions of the expedition, and it was the first booty in Islam. The people of Makkah sent to ransom their two captives. He said: "Rather, we will hold them until Saʿd and ʿUtba arrive, and if they do not arrive, we will kill them in exchange for them." When the two arrived, he ransomed them. As for al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, he embraced Islam and remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah, and he was killed as a martyr on the day of Bir Maʿuna. As for ʿUthman ibn ʿAbdullah, he returned to Makkah and died there as a disbeliever. As for Nawfal, he struck the belly of his horse on the day of the Confederates in order to enter the trench, and he fell into the trench with his horse, and both were smashed together, and Allah killed him. The polytheists then sought his corpse for a price, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take it, for its corpse is evil and its blood-money is evil." This is the occasion of the revelation of this verse. [[Narrated by Ibn Hisham in his Sirah from Ibn Ishaq, 2/251 and following. Al-Bayhaqi related it in his al-Sunan al-Kubra, 9/12, with a sound chain from al-Zuhri from ʿUrwa as a mursal report; and both he and Ibn Abi Hatim linked it through Sulayman al-Tamimi from al-Hadrami from Abu al-Sawwar from Jundub Abu ʿAbdullah. Its chain is sound if this al-Hadrami is Ibn Lahiq (see: al-Albani's takhrij of the hadiths of Fiqh al-Sirah of al-Ghazali, pp. 230-231; Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 99-102).]]

His saying: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month﴾ meaning Rajab, so named because fighting is forbidden in it.

﴿About fighting in it﴾, i.e., concerning fighting in it. ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿Fighting in it is a great [sin]﴾, grave. The speech ends here, then he begins: ﴿But barring from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., your barring the Muslims from Islam, ﴿and disbelief in Him﴾, i.e., your disbelief in Allah, ﴿and [barring from] the Sacred Mosque﴾, i.e., the Sacred Mosque; it is also said: and your barring [them] from the Sacred Mosque, ﴿and expelling its people from it﴾, i.e., expelling the people of the Mosque from it, ﴿is greater﴾ and more grievous in burden ﴿in the sight of Allah. And persecution﴾, i.e., the shirk in which you are, ﴿is worse than killing﴾, i.e., worse than the killing of Ibn al-Hadrami in the sacred month. When this verse was revealed, ʿAbdullah ibn Unays wrote to the believers in Makkah: "If the polytheists reproach you for fighting in the sacred month, then reproach them with disbelief, with expelling the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Makkah, and with preventing the Muslims from the Sacred House." Then He said: ﴿And they will not cease﴾, meaning the polytheists of Makkah, and this is a verb with no infinitive, like ʿasa, ﴿fighting you﴾, O company of believers, ﴿until they turn you﴾ back, ﴿away from your religion, if they are able to. And whoever of you turns back from his religion and dies﴾ — a jussive by coordination — ﴿while he is a disbeliever, these are the ones whose deeds are rendered void﴾, nullified, ﴿their good deeds, in this world and the Hereafter. And these are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever.﴾

The companions of the expedition said, "O Messenger of Allah, will we be rewarded for this campaign of ours? And do we hope that this journey of ours will count as a ghazw (military raid)?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated﴾, that is, they left their tribes, their dwellings and their wealth, ﴿and have striven﴾ against the polytheists ﴿in the cause of Allah﴾, in obedience to Allah. So He made it jihad. ﴿Those expect the mercy of Allah﴾; He informed that they are in hope of mercy. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 219–220 (part 1 of 2):

The Exalted One's saying: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ to the end of the verse. It was revealed concerning 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with them both, and a group of the Ansar, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, give us a ruling on wine and gambling, for they take away the intellect and strip away wealth." So Allah revealed this verse. [[See: al-Wasit by al-Wahidi: 1/316; Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 102–103; al-Mustadrak by al-Hakim: 2/278.]]

The sum of what the exegetes (mufassirun) say on the prohibition of wine is that Allah revealed four verses about wine. They were revealed in Makkah, and they are: ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes you take intoxicant and good provision﴾ (16:67). So the Muslims drank it, and it was lawful for them at that time. Then the verse was revealed concerning the question of 'Umar and Mu'adh ibn Jabal: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin﴾. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah has already laid down [the groundwork for] the prohibition of wine." So some people abstained from it because of His words ﴿great sin﴾, and some people continued to drink it because of His words ﴿and benefits for mankind﴾. This continued until 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf prepared a meal and invited some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and he brought them wine, so they drank and became intoxicated. When the time of the Maghrib prayer came, they put one of them forward to lead them in prayer, and he recited: "Say: O you disbelievers, I worship what you worship," [reciting] in this manner to the end of the surah, omitting the "not" (la). So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾ (4:43). So He prohibited intoxication during the times of prayer. When this verse was revealed, some people gave it up and said: "There is no good in anything that comes between us and the prayer." Others gave it up during the times of prayer but drank it at other times, until a man would drink after the 'Isha' prayer and rise in the morning with the intoxication gone, and would drink after the Fajr prayer and be sober by the time of Dhuhr.

'Utban ibn Malik prepared a feast and invited men from among the Muslims, among them Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and he had roasted for them the head of a camel. They ate from it and drank wine until it overpowered them. Then they boasted to one another, (and traced their lineages,) [[From (b).]] and recited poetry to one another. Sa'd recited a qasidah in which there was satire against the Ansar and boasting of his own people. A man from the Ansar took the jawbone of the camel and struck Sa'd's head with it, wounding him with a mudihah [[A head wound that exposes the bone.]]. Sa'd went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him about the Ansari. 'Umar said: "O Allah, make Your opinion on wine clear to us with a healing clarity." So Allah the Exalted revealed the prohibition of wine in Surah al-Ma'idah, up to His words ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ (5:91).

This was a few days after the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "We have desisted, O Lord." Anas said: "Wine was prohibited, and there was no pleasure for the Arabs more appealing than it, and He did not prohibit anything upon them more severe than wine." [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/605–606.]]

[And from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When the verse in Surah al-Ma'idah (34/a) was revealed, wine was prohibited. So we went out with the jars [[Al-Khabiyah is a Persian word that has been Arabicized.]] to the road and poured out what was in them. Some of us broke their jars, and some of us washed them with water and clay. The alleys of Madinah were left [[Left behind.]] in that state for a while, and when it rained, the color of wine became visible in them and its smell wafted from them.] [[Omitted from (b).]]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Taysafuni informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani informed us: 'Ali ibn Hujr informed us: Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, from Da'ud ibn Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whatever in large quantity intoxicates, its small quantity is also forbidden." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in the Book of Drinks, chapter on the prohibition of intoxicants, 5/266. And al-Tirmidhi: in the Book of Drinks, chapter: "Whatever in large quantity intoxicates, its small quantity is forbidden," 5/606, and he said: a hasan gharib hadith. And Ibn Hibban: in the Book of Drinks, chapter: on a small amount of what a large amount intoxicates, no. 1385, p. 336 (Mawarid al-Zam'an). And Ibn Majah: in the Book of Drinks, chapter: "Whatever in large quantity intoxicates, its small quantity is forbidden," nos. 3393–3394, 2/1125. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/351. See also al-Talkhis al-Habir: 4/73.]]

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us: 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks wine in this world and dies while addicted to it and without repenting, will not drink it in the Hereafter." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in the Book of Drinks, chapter on the saying of the Exalted: "Indeed, wine and gambling..." 10/30. 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ahmad ibn Abi Raja' informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Hayyan al-Taymi informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar preached on the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "The prohibition of wine has been revealed, and it is from five things: from grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and honey. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/351.]] And al-Sha'bi narrated from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, from grapes there is wine, and from dates there is wine, and from honey there is wine, and from wheat there is wine, and from barley there is wine." Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a gharib hadith, and the hadith has corroborations, such as what al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from 'Umar, as previously mentioned. Ahmad also narrated it: 4/267, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]] Thus it is established that wine is not restricted to what is made from grapes or dates.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, that he informed him that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came out to them and said: "I have smelled the scent of a drink from so-and-so, and he claims that he drank al-Tila' (boiled grape syrup). I will question him about what he drank. If it intoxicates, I will flog him." So 'Umar gave him the full prescribed flogging. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in suspended form (mu'allaq) in the Book of Drinks, chapter on al-Baadhiq and on one who forbids every intoxicant, 10/62. Malik in al-Muwatta', chapter on the penalty for wine, connected from al-Zuhri from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid. It was also narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur from Ibn 'Uyaynah from al-Zuhri, who heard al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid say: 'Umar stood on the pulpit and said: "It was mentioned to me that 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar and his companions drank a drink..." and he related it. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/353, and its chain is sahih.]] As for what was narrated from 'Umar, Abu 'Ubaydah and Mu'adh concerning al-Tila', it refers to what was boiled until it ceased to be intoxicating. Ibn 'Abbas was asked about al-Baadhiq [[What is boiled from grape juice a little, so that it becomes strong, and is intoxicating.]] and said: "Muhammad ﷺ has already preceded us regarding al-Baadhiq: whatever intoxicates is forbidden."

The Exalted One's saying: ﴿and gambling﴾ means maysir, which is games of chance. Ibn 'Abbas said: In the pre-Islamic period a man would stake his family and wealth against another man, and whichever of them won over his companion would take away his family and wealth. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. Al-maysir is a noun of place (maf'il) from their saying: "yasara li al-shay'" when it became due, yaysiru, yasran and maysiran. Then gambling itself was called maysir, and the gambler was called yasir and yasir. The origin of maysir was in the camel. The wealthy among the Arabs would buy a she-camel, slaughter it, and divide it into ten portions. Then they would draw lots over it with ten arrows called al-azlam and al-aqlam, of which seven had shares: al-Fadh, who has one share; al-Tawam, who has two shares; al-Raqib, who has three shares; al-Hils, who has four; al-Nafis, who has five; al-Musbil, who has six; and al-Mu'alla, who has seven. Three of them had no shares: al-Manih, al-Safih, and al-Wagh. Then they placed the arrows in a bag called al-Rababah and put it in the hands of a man among them who was trusted, called al-Mujil and al-Mufid. He would shuffle them and take out an arrow bearing the name of one of them. Whoever's arrow came out would take his share according to what came out. If one of the three that had no shares came out for someone, he would take nothing and would have to pay the full price of the camel.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 219–220 (part 2 of 2):

Some of them said: he (the one who took part) would not take any share and would not pay any fine, and that arrow would be void. Then they would give that slaughtered camel to the poor, and would not eat any of it. They took pride in this and would blame whoever did not do it, calling him "al-baram" (the stingy one). This was the origin of the gambling (qimar) that the Arabs practised. The intended meaning of the verse includes all types of gambling. Tawus, 'Ata' and Mujahid said: "Anything in which there is gambling is part of al-maysir (gambling), even children's games with walnuts and knucklebones." It is reported from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that backgammon (nard) and chess (shatranj) are both part of al-maysir.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: In both there is a great sin﴾ means a great burden of wrongdoing, from quarrelling, abusing and foul speech. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *ithmun kathir* with the letter *tha'* (ث), while the rest read it with the letter *ba'* (ب). The sin in wine and gambling is what Allah mentioned in Surah al-Ma'idah:

﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred between you through wine and gambling, and to prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. Will you then not desist?﴾ (91, al-Ma'idah)

﴿And benefits for people﴾: the benefit of wine is the pleasure when drinking it, the joy, the enjoyment of food, and the profit they gain from trading in it. The benefit of gambling is acquiring wealth without toil or effort, and the poor being supported by it. The sin in it is that when a man loses his wealth without any return, it grieves him, so he becomes hostile to his companion and intends evil toward him.

﴿But their sin is greater than their benefit﴾: al-Dahhak and others said: "Their sin after the prohibition is greater than their benefit before the prohibition." It was also said: "Their sin is greater than their benefit before the prohibition, which is the enmity and hatred that arise from them."

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend﴾. The reason is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged them to give charity, so they said: "What should we spend?" He said: ﴿Say: al-'afw (the surplus)﴾. Abu 'Amr read *al-'afwa* with a *damma* (raf'), meaning: "What they spend is the surplus." The others read it with a *fatha* (nasb), with the sense of: "Say: Spend the surplus."

They differed about the meaning of al-'afw. Qatadah, 'Ata' and al-Suddi said: it is what exceeds one's need. The Companions used to earn wealth, keep enough for their expenses, and give the surplus in charity according to the ruling of this verse. Then it was abrogated (nusikha) by the verse of zakat (obligatory alms). Mujahid said: its meaning is giving charity out of richness, so that one does not become a burden upon people.

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir informed us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Kufi informed us: Waki' related to us from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best charity is that given out of richness, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and begin with those you are responsible for."[[Related by al-Bukhari: in Zakat, chapter: "There is no charity except out of richness," 3/294, and in Nafaqat (Expenditures). Muslim: in Zakat, chapter: "The upper hand is better than the lower hand," no. (1034), 2/717. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/187.]]

'Amr ibn Dinar said: it is the middle course, without extravagance or stinginess. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ (67, al-Furqan). Tawus said: it is what is easy. Al-'afw means ease in everything. From this is His saying: ﴿Take what is easy (al-'afw)﴾ (199, al-A'raf), meaning what is easy of people's characters.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan related to us from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a dinar." He (ﷺ) said: "Spend it on yourself." He said: "I have another." He said: "Spend it on your child." He said: "I have another." He said: "Spend it on your wife." He said: "I have another." He said: "Spend it on your servant." He said: "I have another." He said: "You know best."[[Related by Abu Dawud in Zakat, chapter on maintaining ties of kinship: 2/260, and al-Mundhiri said: its chain includes Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan. Also al-Nasa'i in Zakat, chapter "The upper hand": 5/62. Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/251, 471 from Abu Hurayrah, and al-Hakim authenticated it on the condition of Muslim: 1/415. Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an no. (828), al-Shafi'i 2/418-419, and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/193; see the editor's note. Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan is truthful, but his narrations from Abu Hurayrah became confused, of the fifth tabaqah (Taqrib 2/190 and Mizan al-I'tidal 3/644).]]

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: He said "thus" addressing a single person while He is addressing a group, because the group means the tribe, as if He said: "Thus, O tribe." It was also said: this is address to the Prophet (ﷺ), since his address includes address to the community, as in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ (1, al-Talaq).

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So that you may reflect upon this world and the Hereafter﴾. It was said: its meaning is: Allah makes clear to you the verses concerning spending, so that you may reflect upon this world and the Hereafter, and so that you retain from your wealth what will sustain you in the livelihood of this world and spend the rest on what will benefit you in the next life. Most of the exegetes said its meaning is thus: Allah makes clear to you the verses concerning the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, ﴿so that you may reflect﴾ upon the passing away and perishing of this world, so that you may be detached from it, and upon the coming and enduring of the Hereafter, so that you may desire it.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they ask you about orphans﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: When the verse ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner﴾ (152, al-An'am) was revealed, and His saying ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ (10, al-Nisa') and so on, the Muslims became exceedingly scrupulous about the property of orphans. They separated the orphans' property from their own, to the point that food would be prepared for an orphan and some would be left over, and they would leave it and not eat it until it spoiled. This was difficult for them, so they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Setting things right for them is good﴾, meaning that the improvement of their property [[Addition from (B).]] without a wage or taking any compensation is better for you and greater in reward, because of the reward you gain by it, and better for them, because of the increase of their wealth preserved for them. Mujahid said: one should provide for them from one's own food and not extend from the orphan's food. ﴿And if you mix with them﴾: this is the permission for mixing, that is, if you share with them in their property and mix it with your property in your expenses, your dwellings, your servants and your animals, so that you take from their property as compensation for your managing their affairs, and you repay them for what you take from their property. ﴿Then they are your brothers﴾, that is, they are your brothers, and brothers help one another and take from one another's property in a way that is good and agreeable. ﴿And Allah knows the one who corrupts﴾ their property ﴿from the one who sets right﴾ it, meaning the one who intends by mixing to betray and corrupt the orphan's property and to consume it unjustly, from the one who intends to set things right. ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have put you in difficulty﴾, that is, He would have constrained you and not permitted you to mix with them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Had Allah willed, He would have made what you took from the orphans' property a ruin for you. The root of 'anat is hardship and difficulty; its meaning is that He would have imposed upon you in every matter what is burdensome for you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Almighty﴾, and the Almighty is the one who commands with might, who made things easy for the servants or made them difficult for them. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He does of His arrangement and in leaving off causing difficulty.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ahmad ibn Abi Raja' informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Hayyan al-Taymi informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar preached on the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "The prohibition of wine has been revealed, and it is from five things: from grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and honey. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, that he informed him that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came out to them and said: "I have smelled the scent of a drink from so-and-so, and he claims that he drank al-Tila' (boiled grape syrup). I will question him about what he drank. If it intoxicates, I will flog him." So 'Umar gave him the full prescribed flogging. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in suspended form (mu'allaq) in the Book of Drinks, chapter on al-Baadhiq and on one who forbids every intoxicant, 10/62. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/353, and its chain is sahih.]] As for what was narrated from 'Umar, Abu 'Ubaydah and Mu'adh concerning al-Tila', it refers to what was boiled until it ceased to be intoxicating. Ibn 'Abbas was asked about al-Baadhiq [[What is boiled from grape juice a little, so that it becomes strong, and is intoxicating.]] and said: "Muhammad ﷺ has already preceded us regarding al-Baadhiq: whatever intoxicates is forbidden."

The Exalted One's saying: ﴿and gambling﴾ means maysir, which is games of chance. Ibn 'Abbas said: In the pre-Islamic period a man would stake his family and wealth against another man, and whichever of them won over his companion would take away his family and wealth. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. Al-maysir is a noun of place (maf'il) from their saying: "yasara li al-shay'" when it became due, yaysiru, yasran and maysiran. Then gambling itself was called maysir, and the gambler was called yasir and yasir. The origin of maysir was in the camel. The wealthy among the Arabs would buy a she-camel, slaughter it, and divide it into ten portions. Then they would draw lots over it with ten arrows called al-azlam and al-aqlam, of which seven had shares: al-Fadh, who has one share; al-Tawam, who has two shares; al-Raqib, who has three shares; al-Hils, who has four; al-Nafis, who has five; al-Musbil, who has six; and al-Mu'alla, who has seven. Three of them had no shares: al-Manih, al-Safih, and al-Wagh. Then they placed the arrows in a bag called al-Rababah and put it in the hands of a man among them who was trusted, called al-Mujil and al-Mufid. He would shuffle them and take out an arrow bearing the name of one of them. Whoever's arrow came out would take his share according to what came out. If one of the three that had no shares came out for someone, he would take nothing and would have to pay the full price of the camel.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 219–220 (part 2 of 2):

Some of them said: he (the one who took part) would not take any share and would not pay any fine, and that arrow would be void. Then they would give that slaughtered camel to the poor, and would not eat any of it. They took pride in this and would blame whoever did not do it, calling him "al-baram" (the stingy one). This was the origin of the gambling (qimar) that the Arabs practised. The intended meaning of the verse includes all types of gambling. Tawus, 'Ata' and Mujahid said: "Anything in which there is gambling is part of al-maysir (gambling), even children's games with walnuts and knucklebones." It is reported from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that backgammon (nard) and chess (shatranj) are both part of al-maysir.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: In both there is a great sin﴾ means a great burden of wrongdoing, from quarrelling, abusing and foul speech. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *ithmun kathir* with the letter *tha'* (ث), while the rest read it with the letter *ba'* (ب). The sin in wine and gambling is what Allah mentioned in Surah al-Ma'idah:

﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred between you through wine and gambling, and to prevent you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. Will you then not desist?﴾ (91, al-Ma'idah)

﴿And benefits for people﴾: the benefit of wine is the pleasure when drinking it, the joy, the enjoyment of food, and the profit they gain from trading in it. The benefit of gambling is acquiring wealth without toil or effort, and the poor being supported by it. The sin in it is that when a man loses his wealth without any return, it grieves him, so he becomes hostile to his companion and intends evil toward him.

﴿But their sin is greater than their benefit﴾: al-Dahhak and others said: "Their sin after the prohibition is greater than their benefit before the prohibition." It was also said: "Their sin is greater than their benefit before the prohibition, which is the enmity and hatred that arise from them."

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend﴾. The reason is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged them to give charity, so they said: "What should we spend?" He said: ﴿Say: al-'afw (the surplus)﴾. Abu 'Amr read *al-'afwa* with a *damma* (raf'), meaning: "What they spend is the surplus." The others read it with a *fatha* (nasb), with the sense of: "Say: Spend the surplus."

They differed about the meaning of al-'afw. Qatadah, 'Ata' and al-Suddi said: it is what exceeds one's need. The Companions used to earn wealth, keep enough for their expenses, and give the surplus in charity according to the ruling of this verse. Then it was abrogated (nusikha) by the verse of zakat (obligatory alms). Mujahid said: its meaning is giving charity out of richness, so that one does not become a burden upon people.

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir informed us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Kufi informed us: Waki' related to us from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best charity is that given out of richness, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and begin with those you are responsible for."[[Related by al-Bukhari: in Zakat, chapter: "There is no charity except out of richness," 3/294, and in Nafaqat (Expenditures). Muslim: in Zakat, chapter: "The upper hand is better than the lower hand," no. (1034), 2/717. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/187.]]

'Amr ibn Dinar said: it is the middle course, without extravagance or stinginess. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ (67, al-Furqan). Tawus said: it is what is easy. Al-'afw means ease in everything. From this is His saying: ﴿Take what is easy (al-'afw)﴾ (199, al-A'raf), meaning what is easy of people's characters.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan related to us from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a dinar." He (ﷺ) said: "Spend it on yourself." He said: "I have another." He said: "Spend it on your child." He said: "I have another." He said: "Spend it on your wife." He said: "I have another." He said: "Spend it on your servant." He said: "I have another." He said: "You know best."[[Related by Abu Dawud in Zakat, chapter on maintaining ties of kinship: 2/260, and al-Mundhiri said: its chain includes Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan. Also al-Nasa'i in Zakat, chapter "The upper hand": 5/62. Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/251, 471 from Abu Hurayrah, and al-Hakim authenticated it on the condition of Muslim: 1/415. Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an no. (828), al-Shafi'i 2/418-419, and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/193; see the editor's note. Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan is truthful, but his narrations from Abu Hurayrah became confused, of the fifth tabaqah (Taqrib 2/190 and Mizan al-I'tidal 3/644).]]

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: He said "thus" addressing a single person while He is addressing a group, because the group means the tribe, as if He said: "Thus, O tribe." It was also said: this is address to the Prophet (ﷺ), since his address includes address to the community, as in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ (1, al-Talaq).

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So that you may reflect upon this world and the Hereafter﴾. It was said: its meaning is: Allah makes clear to you the verses concerning spending, so that you may reflect upon this world and the Hereafter, and so that you retain from your wealth what will sustain you in the livelihood of this world and spend the rest on what will benefit you in the next life. Most of the exegetes said its meaning is thus: Allah makes clear to you the verses concerning the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, ﴿so that you may reflect﴾ upon the passing away and perishing of this world, so that you may be detached from it, and upon the coming and enduring of the Hereafter, so that you may desire it.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they ask you about orphans﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: When the verse ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner﴾ (152, al-An'am) was revealed, and His saying ﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ (10, al-Nisa') and so on, the Muslims became exceedingly scrupulous about the property of orphans. They separated the orphans' property from their own, to the point that food would be prepared for an orphan and some would be left over, and they would leave it and not eat it until it spoiled. This was difficult for them, so they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Setting things right for them is good﴾, meaning that the improvement of their property [[Addition from (B).]] without a wage or taking any compensation is better for you and greater in reward, because of the reward you gain by it, and better for them, because of the increase of their wealth preserved for them. Mujahid said: one should provide for them from one's own food and not extend from the orphan's food. ﴿And if you mix with them﴾: this is the permission for mixing, that is, if you share with them in their property and mix it with your property in your expenses, your dwellings, your servants and your animals, so that you take from their property as compensation for your managing their affairs, and you repay them for what you take from their property. ﴿Then they are your brothers﴾, that is, they are your brothers, and brothers help one another and take from one another's property in a way that is good and agreeable. ﴿And Allah knows the one who corrupts﴾ their property ﴿from the one who sets right﴾ it, meaning the one who intends by mixing to betray and corrupt the orphan's property and to consume it unjustly, from the one who intends to set things right. ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have put you in difficulty﴾, that is, He would have constrained you and not permitted you to mix with them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Had Allah willed, He would have made what you took from the orphans' property a ruin for you. The root of 'anat is hardship and difficulty; its meaning is that He would have imposed upon you in every matter what is burdensome for you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Almighty﴾, and the Almighty is the one who commands with might, who made things easy for the servants or made them difficult for them. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He does of His arrangement and in leaving off causing difficulty.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verse 221:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾. The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi to Makkah to secretly bring out some Muslims from it. When he arrived there, a female idolater named Inaq, who had been his mistress in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), heard of him. She came to him and said: "O Abu Marthad, will you not come to me?" He said to her: "Woe to you, O Inaq! Islam has come between us and that." She said: "Would you then like to marry me?" He said: "Yes, but I will return to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and seek his permission." She said: "Are you then becoming impatient?" Then she called for help against him, and they beat him severely, then let him go. When he had finished his business in Makkah and returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he informed him of what had happened concerning himself and Inaq, and of what he had suffered because of her, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it lawful for me to marry her?" So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿And do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾. [[See: al-Tabari: 4/368; al-Wasit: 1/320-321.]]

It was said: the verse is abrogated (mansukh) with respect to the women of the People of the Book, by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ (5: al-Ma'idah). If it is asked: how did you apply the name of "shirk" (association of partners with Allah) to those who deny only the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ)? Abu al-Hasan ibn Faris said: because whoever says that the Qur'an is the speech of other than Allah has associated another with Allah. Qatadah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: by "al-mushrikat" is meant the women who worship idols. For Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) married Na'ilah bint Furafisah, who was a Christian, and she embraced Islam while under him. Talhah ibn Abd Allah married a Christian woman, and Hudhayfah married a Jewish woman. [Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to him: "Divorce her." He wrote back: "Do you consider her unlawful?" He said: "I do not consider her unlawful, but I fear that you may take up with the prostitutes among them."] [[Omitted from (B).]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a believing slave-woman is better than an idolatress, even though she pleases you﴾ — by her beauty and her wealth. It was revealed concerning Khansa', a black slave-girl who belonged to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. Hudhayfah said: "O Khansa', you have been mentioned in the highest assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la), despite your blackness and your ugliness." He freed her and married her. Al-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning Abd Allah ibn Rawahah, who had a black slave-woman. He became angry with her and slapped her, then regretted it and went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of this. He (ﷺ) said to him: "And what is she, O Abd Allah?" He said: "She testifies that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, she fasts Ramadan, she performs wudu' well, and she prays." He (ﷺ) said: "This is a believer." Abd Allah said: "By the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, I will indeed free her and indeed marry her." He did so. Some Muslims criticized him and said: "Will you marry a slave-woman?" and they offered him a free idolatress. So Allah revealed this verse. [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari from al-Suddi as a mursal report, 4/368, edited by Ahmad Shakir.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not marry [your women to] idolaters until they believe﴾. This is a consensus (ijma'): it is not permissible for a Muslim woman to marry an idolater. ﴿And a believing slave is better than an idolater, even though he pleases you. Those invite to the Fire﴾ — meaning the idolaters — ﴿to the Fire﴾, that is, to the deeds that necessitate the Fire. ﴿But Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness, by His permission﴾, that is, by His decree and His will. ﴿And He makes clear His verses to the people﴾, that is, His commands and His prohibitions, ﴿that they may remember﴾, that is, that they may take heed.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 222–223 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾. Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani informed us: Abu Umar al-Qasim ibn Ja'far ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani informed us: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us: Hammad ibn Salama informed us: Thabit al-Bunani related to us from Anas ibn Malik that the Jews, when a woman among them menstruated, would expel her from the house, would not eat with her, would not drink with her, and would not have intercourse with her in the house. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about that, and Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an harm, so keep away from women during menstruation﴾, the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said: "Have intercourse with them in the houses, and do everything except marriage [the act of intercourse]." The Jews said: "This man does not want to leave any matter of ours without opposing us in it." Then Usayd ibn Hudayr and Abbad ibn Bishr came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews say such and such. Shall we not have intercourse with them during menstruation?" The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed until we thought he was angry with them, so they went out. A gift of milk was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he sent after them and gave them to drink, and we understood that he was not angry with them.[[Related by Muslim: Kitab al-Hayd, bab: jawaz ghasl al-ha'id ras zawjiha ... no. 302, 1/246. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/125.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾: that is, about the ḥayḍ (menstruation). It is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from "ḥāḍat al-mar'atu taḥīḍu ḥayḍan wa maḥīḍan," like al-sayr and al-masir (the going). The root meaning of ḥayḍ is flowing and streaming. His saying ﴿It is an harm﴾: that is, filth (qadhar). Al-adha is everything disliked in anything. ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾: by "keeping away" he meant abstaining from intercourse. ﴿And do not approach them﴾: that is, do not have intercourse with them. As for touching and lying beside them, that is permissible.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Qabisa informed us: Sufyan related to us from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I used to bathe, I and the Prophet (ﷺ), from one vessel, both of us in a state of major impurity (janabah). He would order me to wear a wrapper, and he would embrace me while I was menstruating. He would put his head out to me while he was in seclusion (i'tikaf), and I would wash it while I was menstruating."[[Related by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Hayd, bab mubashara al-ha'id, 1/403. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/131.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Abu Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Sa'd ibn Hafs informed us: Shayban informed us, from Yahya, from Abu Salama, from Zaynab bint Abi Salama, who related to him from Umm Salama, who said: "I menstruated while I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the woolen blanket. I slipped away and went out of it, and I took the clothes of my menstruation and put them on. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'Have you menstruated (nafistī)?' I said: 'Yes.' So he called me and let me in with him under the blanket."[[Related by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Hayd, bab al-nawm ma'a al-ha'id wa hiya fi thiyabiha, 1/422. Muslim, Kitab al-Hayd, bab al-idtijaʻ ma'a al-ha'id fi lihaf wahid, no. 296, 1/243. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/129.]]

Abu al-Qasim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hanifi informed us: Abu al-Harith Tahir ibn Muhammad al-Tahiri informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Hakim [in Sharh al-Sunnah: Muhammad ibn Halim, with a lam][[In Sharh al-Sunnah: Muhammad ibn Halim, with a lam.]] informed us: Abu al-Muwajjih Muhammad ibn Amr informed us: Sadaqa informed us: Waki' informed us: Mis'ar and Sufyan related to us from al-Miqdam [in Sharh al-Sunnah: al-Miqdad ibn Shurayh, and this is an error][[In Sharh al-Sunnah: al-Miqdad ibn Shurayh, and this is an error.]] ibn Shurayh, from his father, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I used to drink while I was menstruating, and I would hand it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he would place his mouth on the place where my mouth had been. I would gnaw at a bone (ataʻarraq al-ʻaraq), and he would take it and place his mouth on the place where my mouth had been."[[Related by Muslim, Kitab al-Hayd, bab jawaz ghasl al-ha'id ras zawjiha, no. 300, 1/245–246. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/134.]]

So intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden (haram), and whoever does it disobeys Allah, may He be exalted, and the ruler (imam) disciplines him with a discretionary punishment (ta'zir), if he is known to have done so. The scholars differed concerning whether expiation (kaffarah) is obligatory upon him. Most of them held that there is no expiation upon him, so he should seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.[[See al-Jami' li-ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Qurtubi, 3/87.]]

Others held that expiation is obligatory upon him, among them Qatada, al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq, based on what Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us: Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukharik, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning a man who had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating: "If the blood is thick red, let him give a dinar in charity; and if it is yellowish, half a dinar."[[Related by al-Darimi, Kitab al-Wudu', bab man qala 'alayhi al-kaffarah, 1/255. See Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi, 1/421–422. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/127 with a comment. Its chain is weak because of the weakness of Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukharik (al-Taqrib; Mizan al-I'tidal). al-Nasa'i mentioned him in al-Du'afa' wa al-matrukin.]]

This is also transmitted as a statement of Ibn Abbas (mawquf). Menstruation prevents the permissibility and the obligation of prayer [in the sense that it makes prayer neither permissible nor obligatory], and it prevents the permissibility of fasting but does not prevent its obligation, so that once she becomes pure, she must make up the fast but does not have to make up the prayer. The same applies to the woman in postpartum bleeding (nufasa').

Abu Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Ali ibn Hujr informed us: Ali ibn Musahhir informed us, from Ubayda ibn Mu'attib al-Dabbi, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from al-Aswad, from Aisha, who said: "We used to menstruate in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then we would become pure, and he would order us to make up the fast, and he would not order us to make up the prayer."[[Related by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Hayd, bab: la taqdi al-ha'id al-salat, 1/421, though it contains no reference to making up the fast. Muslim, Kitab al-Hayd, bab wujub qada' al-sawm 'ala al-ha'id dun al-salat, no. 335, 1/265.]]

It is not permissible for a menstruating woman to perform circumambulation (tawaf) of the House, to remain in seclusion (i'tikaf) in the mosque, to touch the mushaf, or to recite the Qur'an, and it is not permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Ja'far informed us: Abu Ali al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud informed us: Musaddad informed us: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad informed us: Aflat ibn Khalifa informed us, saying: Jasra bint Dajaja related to me, saying: I heard Aisha say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came while the doors of his Companions' houses opened onto the mosque, and he said: "Turn these houses away from the mosque, for I do not make the mosque lawful for a menstruating woman or a person in major impurity (junub)."[[Related by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Taharah, bab fi al-junub yadkhul al-masjid, 1/157. al-Mundhiri said: al-Bukhari also related it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir with an addition, and after it a hadith of Aisha: "Close these doors except the door of Abu Bakr"; he said this is more authentic. al-Khattabi said: they regarded this hadith as weak, saying its narrator Aflat is unknown and his hadith cannot be used as proof (see Mukhtasar al-Mundhiri, 1/158). Also al-Bayhaqi, 2/442–443. al-Albani weakened it and said: it contains Jasra bint Dajaja; al-Bukhari said: "Jasra has strange reports." al-Bayhaqi said: if it is authentic, then in the case of the junub it refers to remaining in the mosque, not passing through it, based on the Qur'an (Irwa' al-Ghalil, 1/210–212).]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿until they are purified﴾. Asim, through the transmission of Abu Bakr, Hamza and al-Kisa'i, read it with a shadda on the ta' and the ha' (yaththahharna), meaning: until they have washed (yaghtasilna). The others read it with a sukun on the ta' and a damma on the ha' (yatharna), with lightening (takhfif). Its meaning is: until they become pure from menstruation and their bleeding stops. ﴿Then when they have purified themselves﴾: that is, have bathed (ightasalna). ﴿Then approach them﴾: that is, have intercourse with them. ﴿From where Allah has commanded you﴾: that is, from the place where He commanded you to keep away from them, which is the vagina (al-farj). This was said by Mujahid, Qatada and Ikrima. Ibn Abbas said: "Have intercourse with them in the vagina and do not go beyond it to anything else," meaning: beware of the rear passage (al-adbar). It has also been said that "min" here means "fi" (in), so that the meaning is: "in the place where Allah has commanded you, which is the vagina," as in His saying: ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾ (62:9), meaning "on the day of Friday." It has also been said that ﴿approach them﴾ means "in the manner in which Allah has commanded you to approach them," which is in a state of purity. Ibn al-Hanafiyya said: "From the lawful direction, not from the forbidden one." It has been said: "Do not approach them while fasting, nor while in seclusion, nor while in the state of ihram. But approach them, for their intercourse is lawful for you."

Know that the prohibition of anything that menstruation prevents does not lift merely by the cessation of the blood, until she washes or performs tayammum when water is unavailable, except for the prohibition of fasting. If the menstruating woman's blood stops at night and she intends the fast, and her washing occurs during the day, her fast is valid. Divorcing a woman during menstruation is an innovated divorce (talaq bid'i), but if he divorces her after the blood has stopped and before she washes, it is not an innovated divorce. Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, held that if her blood stops after the majority of the menstrual period, which is ten days, it is permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her before she washes. Mujahid and Tawus said: if she has washed her vagina, it is permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her before the full bath.

Most scholars hold the prohibition until she washes or performs tayammum when water is unavailable, because Allah, may He be exalted, made the permissibility of intercourse conditional upon two things: the cessation of the blood and washing. He said: ﴿until they are purified﴾, meaning from menstruation, ﴿then when they have purified themselves﴾, meaning have bathed, ﴿then approach them﴾. Whoever reads yattahharna with a shadda, the intended meaning is washing, as in His saying: ﴿And if you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves﴾ (5:6), meaning "bathe." This indicates that intercourse is not lawful before washing.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed Allah loves those who turn in repentance and loves those who purify themselves﴾. Ata', Muqatil ibn Sulayman and al-Kalbi said: "He loves those who turn in repentance from sins, and loves those who purify themselves with water from minor and major impurities (ahdath wa najasat)." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "He loves those who turn in repentance from sins, and those who purify themselves from polytheism." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Those who turn in repentance from polytheism, and those who purify themselves from sins." Mujahid said: "Those who turn in repentance from sins and do not return to them, and those who purify themselves from them, not having committed them." Al-tawwab is the one who repents every time he sins. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, He was ever forgiving to those who turn often (lil-awwabin)﴾ (17:25).
