His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your wives are a tillage for you, so go to your tillage however you wish﴾. Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us: Ibn al-Munadi informed us: Yunus informed us: Ya'qub al-Qummi informed us, from Ja'far ibn al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Umar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined." He said: "What has ruined you?" He said: "I turned my mount last night," and he gave him no answer. Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿Your wives are a tillage for you, so go to your tillage however you wish﴾, meaning: "Come from the front or from behind, but beware of the rear passage and of menstruation."[[Related by al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Tafsir, who said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith," 8/324; and Imam Ahmad from Ibn Abbas, 1/297. al-Mubarakfuri attributed it to Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah (see Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi, 8/324), and Ibn Kathir, 1/463. al-Suyuti also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya'. See al-Durr al-Manthur, 1/629.]]

Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 222–223 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi related to us: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri related to us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi related to us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib related to us: Ibn Uyaynah related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: "The Jews used to say about the man who comes to his wife from behind, into her vagina, that the child will be born squint-eyed (ahwal). So this was revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-Baqarah, chapter "Your wives are a tilth for you" (8/189). Muslim in Nikah, chapter on the permissibility of intercourse with one's wife in the vagina from the front (no. 1435, 2/1058). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (6/105).]]

Mujahid related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It was among the practices of the People of the Book not to approach women except in one manner, for that is the most concealing for the woman. This clan of the Ansar adopted that practice from them. This clan of Quraysh, however, would enjoy their women from the front, from behind, and lying on their backs. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, a man of them married a woman of the Ansar and went to do that with her, but she objected to him and said: 'We used to be approached in only one manner. If you wish, do it that way; otherwise, keep away from me.' The matter spread until it reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, meaning the place of the child, ﴿so go to your tilth however you wish﴾: from the front, from behind, and lying on the back." The word "anna" here is an interrogative particle that asks about the manner and place, and its meaning is: "how you wish and where you wish," provided it is in one and the same vagina (simam wahid). Ikrimah said: "﴿However you wish﴾ refers only to the vagina (al-farj)," and al-Hasan said the same. It has also been said: "﴿A tilth for you﴾ means a field for you and a place of growth for the child, like the land that is sown." This contains evidence for the prohibition of anal intercourse, because the place of tilling and sowing is the front (al-qubul), not the rear (al-dubur).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "This applies to 'azl (coitus interruptus, withdrawal before ejaculation). That is, if you wish, practise 'azl, and if you wish, do not practise 'azl." Ibn Abbas was asked about 'azl and said: "Your tilth: if you wish, make it thirsty, and if you wish, water it." It is also reported from him that he said: "A free woman is to be consulted about 'azl, but a slave-girl is not to be consulted." Ahmad (ibn Hanbal) also held this view. A group of scholars disliked 'azl and said: "It is the hidden burying (al-wa'd al-khafi) of the child."

It is related from Malik, from Nafi', who said: "I was holding the mushaf for Ibn Umar, and he recited this verse, ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, and said: 'Do you know concerning what this verse was revealed?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It was revealed concerning a man who came to his wife from behind, and that troubled him, so this verse was revealed.'"[[Al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Daraqutni in Gharib Malik. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/636.]]

It is related from Malik the permissibility of that, but his companions denied it. It is also reported from Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan that he met Salim ibn Abd Allah and said to him: "O Abu Umar, what is this report that Nafi' narrates from Abd Allah (ibn Umar), that he did not see any harm in approaching women in their rear passages?" He said: "The slave lied and erred. Abd Allah (ibn Umar) only said: 'They are approached in their vaginas, from their rear (i.e., from behind).'" The evidence for the prohibition of the rear passages is what was related to us by Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad ibn al-Khatib: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal related to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm related to us: al-Rabi' related to us: al-Shafi'i related to us: Umar Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Shafi' related to us: Abd Allah ibn Ali ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from Amr ibn Uhayhah ibn al-Julah, from Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about approaching women in their rear passages. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "In which of the two openings, or in which of the two holes, or in which of the two pieces of cloth? Is it from behind into the vagina? Then yes. Or from behind into the rear? Then no. Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their rear passages."[[Musnad al-Shafi'i: 2/360. Ibn Hibban (1299) and he declared it authentic. Ahmad: 5/213, from Khuzaymah, with the wording "Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth..." al-Tahawi: 2/25, and its chain is authentic (see Fath al-Bari: 8/143).]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi related to us: Zahir ibn Ahmad related to us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi related to us: Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, [36/b] from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever approaches his wife in her rear passage is cursed."[[Related by Abu Dawud in Nikah, chapter on general matters of marriage (3/77). Ibn Majah in Nikah, chapter on the prohibition of approaching women in their rear passages (no. 1923, 2/619), with the wording: "Allah does not look at a man who has intercourse with his wife in her rear passage," and he said in al-Zawa'id: its chain is authentic. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (9/106).]]

Abu Hurayrah related: "Whoever approaches his wife in her rear passage..."

[Note: the preceding line above is a duplicate of the hadith and is not part of the source text; please disregard it.]

The statement of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾. Ata' said: "It is saying the basmalah at intercourse." Mujahid said: "﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means: when one approaches his wife, let him supplicate."

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Salim, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If any one of you, when he wishes to approach his wife, says: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide us,' then if a child is decreed between them from that union, Satan will never harm it."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Nikah, chapter on what a man says when he approaches his wife (9/28). Muslim in Nikah, chapter on what is recommended to say during intercourse (no. 1434, 2/1058).]] It has also been said: "﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means: seeking offspring."

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi related to us: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Tayisfuni related to us: Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Jawhari related to us: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani related to us: Ali ibn Hujr related to us, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three: ongoing charity (sadaqah jariyah), or knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him."[[Related by Muslim in Wasiyyah, chapter on the reward that reaches a person after his death (no. 1631, 3/1255). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/300).]] It has also been said: this refers to marrying for chastity, so that the child may be righteous.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Musaddad related to us: Yahya related to us, from Ubayd Allah: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id related to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman is married for four things: for her wealth, for her lineage, for her beauty, and for her religion. So win the one with religion; may your hands be dust."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Nikah, chapter on compatibility in religion (9/131). Muslim in Nikah, chapter on the recommendation of marrying a religious woman (no. 1466, 2/1086). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (9/8).]] It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: seeking the afrat (children who die before their parents, who will intercede for them).

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi related to us: Zahir ibn Ahmad related to us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi related to us: Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim loses three children and then the Fire touches him, except as a fulfilment of an oath (tahillat al-qasam)."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Oaths and Vows, chapter on the saying of Allah: "And they swear by Allah with their most emphatic oaths" (11/541). Muslim in Birr, Silah and Adab, chapter on the virtue of one who loses a child and seeks reward for it (no. 2632, 4/2028). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (5/450).]]

Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: "﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means good and righteous deeds, as the context of the verse indicates: ﴿And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him﴾, that is, that you will return to Him, and He will recompense you for your deeds. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾."

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 222–223 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾. Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani informed us: Abu Umar al-Qasim ibn Ja'far ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani informed us: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us: Hammad ibn Salama informed us: Thabit al-Bunani related to us from Anas ibn Malik that the Jews, when a woman among them menstruated, would expel her from the house, would not eat with her, would not drink with her, and would not have intercourse with her in the house. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about that, and Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an harm, so keep away from women during menstruation﴾, the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said: "Have intercourse with them in the houses, and do everything except marriage [the act of intercourse]." The Jews said: "This man does not want to leave any matter of ours without opposing us in it." Then Usayd ibn Hudayr and Abbad ibn Bishr came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews say such and such. Shall we not have intercourse with them during menstruation?" The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed until we thought he was angry with them, so they went out. A gift of milk was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he sent after them and gave them to drink, and we understood that he was not angry with them.[[Related by Muslim: Kitab al-Hayd, bab: jawaz ghasl al-ha'id ras zawjiha ... no. 302, 1/246. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/125.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾: that is, about the ḥayḍ (menstruation). It is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from "ḥāḍat al-mar'atu taḥīḍu ḥayḍan wa maḥīḍan," like al-sayr and al-masir (the going). The root meaning of ḥayḍ is flowing and streaming. His saying ﴿It is an harm﴾: that is, filth (qadhar). Al-adha is everything disliked in anything. ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾: by "keeping away" he meant abstaining from intercourse. ﴿And do not approach them﴾: that is, do not have intercourse with them. As for touching and lying beside them, that is permissible.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Qabisa informed us: Sufyan related to us from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I used to bathe, I and the Prophet (ﷺ), from one vessel, both of us in a state of major impurity (janabah). He would order me to wear a wrapper, and he would embrace me while I was menstruating. He would put his head out to me while he was in seclusion (i'tikaf), and I would wash it while I was menstruating."[[Related by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Hayd, bab mubashara al-ha'id, 1/403. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/131.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Abu Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Sa'd ibn Hafs informed us: Shayban informed us, from Yahya, from Abu Salama, from Zaynab bint Abi Salama, who related to him from Umm Salama, who said: "I menstruated while I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the woolen blanket. I slipped away and went out of it, and I took the clothes of my menstruation and put them on. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'Have you menstruated (nafistī)?' I said: 'Yes.' So he called me and let me in with him under the blanket."[[Related by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Hayd, bab al-nawm ma'a al-ha'id wa hiya fi thiyabiha, 1/422. Muslim, Kitab al-Hayd, bab al-idtijaʻ ma'a al-ha'id fi lihaf wahid, no. 296, 1/243. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/129.]]

Abu al-Qasim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hanifi informed us: Abu al-Harith Tahir ibn Muhammad al-Tahiri informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Hakim [in Sharh al-Sunnah: Muhammad ibn Halim, with a lam][[In Sharh al-Sunnah: Muhammad ibn Halim, with a lam.]] informed us: Abu al-Muwajjih Muhammad ibn Amr informed us: Sadaqa informed us: Waki' informed us: Mis'ar and Sufyan related to us from al-Miqdam [in Sharh al-Sunnah: al-Miqdad ibn Shurayh, and this is an error][[In Sharh al-Sunnah: al-Miqdad ibn Shurayh, and this is an error.]] ibn Shurayh, from his father, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I used to drink while I was menstruating, and I would hand it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he would place his mouth on the place where my mouth had been. I would gnaw at a bone (ataʻarraq al-ʻaraq), and he would take it and place his mouth on the place where my mouth had been."[[Related by Muslim, Kitab al-Hayd, bab jawaz ghasl al-ha'id ras zawjiha, no. 300, 1/245–246. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/134.]]

So intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden (haram), and whoever does it disobeys Allah, may He be exalted, and the ruler (imam) disciplines him with a discretionary punishment (ta'zir), if he is known to have done so. The scholars differed concerning whether expiation (kaffarah) is obligatory upon him. Most of them held that there is no expiation upon him, so he should seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.[[See al-Jami' li-ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Qurtubi, 3/87.]]

Others held that expiation is obligatory upon him, among them Qatada, al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq, based on what Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us: Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukharik, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning a man who had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating: "If the blood is thick red, let him give a dinar in charity; and if it is yellowish, half a dinar."[[Related by al-Darimi, Kitab al-Wudu', bab man qala 'alayhi al-kaffarah, 1/255. See Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi, 1/421–422. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/127 with a comment. Its chain is weak because of the weakness of Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukharik (al-Taqrib; Mizan al-I'tidal). al-Nasa'i mentioned him in al-Du'afa' wa al-matrukin.]]

This is also transmitted as a statement of Ibn Abbas (mawquf). Menstruation prevents the permissibility and the obligation of prayer [in the sense that it makes prayer neither permissible nor obligatory], and it prevents the permissibility of fasting but does not prevent its obligation, so that once she becomes pure, she must make up the fast but does not have to make up the prayer. The same applies to the woman in postpartum bleeding (nufasa').

Abu Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Ali ibn Hujr informed us: Ali ibn Musahhir informed us, from Ubayda ibn Mu'attib al-Dabbi, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from al-Aswad, from Aisha, who said: "We used to menstruate in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then we would become pure, and he would order us to make up the fast, and he would not order us to make up the prayer."[[Related by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Hayd, bab: la taqdi al-ha'id al-salat, 1/421, though it contains no reference to making up the fast. Muslim, Kitab al-Hayd, bab wujub qada' al-sawm 'ala al-ha'id dun al-salat, no. 335, 1/265.]]

It is not permissible for a menstruating woman to perform circumambulation (tawaf) of the House, to remain in seclusion (i'tikaf) in the mosque, to touch the mushaf, or to recite the Qur'an, and it is not permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Ja'far informed us: Abu Ali al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud informed us: Musaddad informed us: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad informed us: Aflat ibn Khalifa informed us, saying: Jasra bint Dajaja related to me, saying: I heard Aisha say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came while the doors of his Companions' houses opened onto the mosque, and he said: "Turn these houses away from the mosque, for I do not make the mosque lawful for a menstruating woman or a person in major impurity (junub)."[[Related by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Taharah, bab fi al-junub yadkhul al-masjid, 1/157. al-Mundhiri said: al-Bukhari also related it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir with an addition, and after it a hadith of Aisha: "Close these doors except the door of Abu Bakr"; he said this is more authentic. al-Khattabi said: they regarded this hadith as weak, saying its narrator Aflat is unknown and his hadith cannot be used as proof (see Mukhtasar al-Mundhiri, 1/158). Also al-Bayhaqi, 2/442–443. al-Albani weakened it and said: it contains Jasra bint Dajaja; al-Bukhari said: "Jasra has strange reports." al-Bayhaqi said: if it is authentic, then in the case of the junub it refers to remaining in the mosque, not passing through it, based on the Qur'an (Irwa' al-Ghalil, 1/210–212).]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿until they are purified﴾. Asim, through the transmission of Abu Bakr, Hamza and al-Kisa'i, read it with a shadda on the ta' and the ha' (yaththahharna), meaning: until they have washed (yaghtasilna). The others read it with a sukun on the ta' and a damma on the ha' (yatharna), with lightening (takhfif). Its meaning is: until they become pure from menstruation and their bleeding stops. ﴿Then when they have purified themselves﴾: that is, have bathed (ightasalna). ﴿Then approach them﴾: that is, have intercourse with them. ﴿From where Allah has commanded you﴾: that is, from the place where He commanded you to keep away from them, which is the vagina (al-farj). This was said by Mujahid, Qatada and Ikrima. Ibn Abbas said: "Have intercourse with them in the vagina and do not go beyond it to anything else," meaning: beware of the rear passage (al-adbar). It has also been said that "min" here means "fi" (in), so that the meaning is: "in the place where Allah has commanded you, which is the vagina," as in His saying: ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾ (62:9), meaning "on the day of Friday." It has also been said that ﴿approach them﴾ means "in the manner in which Allah has commanded you to approach them," which is in a state of purity. Ibn al-Hanafiyya said: "From the lawful direction, not from the forbidden one." It has been said: "Do not approach them while fasting, nor while in seclusion, nor while in the state of ihram. But approach them, for their intercourse is lawful for you."

Know that the prohibition of anything that menstruation prevents does not lift merely by the cessation of the blood, until she washes or performs tayammum when water is unavailable, except for the prohibition of fasting. If the menstruating woman's blood stops at night and she intends the fast, and her washing occurs during the day, her fast is valid. Divorcing a woman during menstruation is an innovated divorce (talaq bid'i), but if he divorces her after the blood has stopped and before she washes, it is not an innovated divorce. Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, held that if her blood stops after the majority of the menstrual period, which is ten days, it is permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her before she washes. Mujahid and Tawus said: if she has washed her vagina, it is permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her before the full bath.

Most scholars hold the prohibition until she washes or performs tayammum when water is unavailable, because Allah, may He be exalted, made the permissibility of intercourse conditional upon two things: the cessation of the blood and washing. He said: ﴿until they are purified﴾, meaning from menstruation, ﴿then when they have purified themselves﴾, meaning have bathed, ﴿then approach them﴾. Whoever reads yattahharna with a shadda, the intended meaning is washing, as in His saying: ﴿And if you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves﴾ (5:6), meaning "bathe." This indicates that intercourse is not lawful before washing.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed Allah loves those who turn in repentance and loves those who purify themselves﴾. Ata', Muqatil ibn Sulayman and al-Kalbi said: "He loves those who turn in repentance from sins, and loves those who purify themselves with water from minor and major impurities (ahdath wa najasat)." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "He loves those who turn in repentance from sins, and those who purify themselves from polytheism." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Those who turn in repentance from polytheism, and those who purify themselves from sins." Mujahid said: "Those who turn in repentance from sins and do not return to them, and those who purify themselves from them, not having committed them." Al-tawwab is the one who repents every time he sins. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Indeed, He was ever forgiving to those who turn often (lil-awwabin)﴾ (17:25).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your wives are a tillage for you, so go to your tillage however you wish﴾. Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us: Ibn al-Munadi informed us: Yunus informed us: Ya'qub al-Qummi informed us, from Ja'far ibn al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Umar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined." He said: "What has ruined you?" He said: "I turned my mount last night," and he gave him no answer. Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿Your wives are a tillage for you, so go to your tillage however you wish﴾, meaning: "Come from the front or from behind, but beware of the rear passage and of menstruation."[[Related by al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Tafsir, who said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith," 8/324; and Imam Ahmad from Ibn Abbas, 1/297. al-Mubarakfuri attributed it to Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah (see Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi, 8/324), and Ibn Kathir, 1/463. al-Suyuti also attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya'. See al-Durr al-Manthur, 1/629.]]

Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 222–223 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi related to us: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri related to us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi related to us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib related to us: Ibn Uyaynah related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: "The Jews used to say about the man who comes to his wife from behind, into her vagina, that the child will be born squint-eyed (ahwal). So this was revealed: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-Baqarah, chapter "Your wives are a tilth for you" (8/189). Muslim in Nikah, chapter on the permissibility of intercourse with one's wife in the vagina from the front (no. 1435, 2/1058). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (6/105).]]

Mujahid related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It was among the practices of the People of the Book not to approach women except in one manner, for that is the most concealing for the woman. This clan of the Ansar adopted that practice from them. This clan of Quraysh, however, would enjoy their women from the front, from behind, and lying on their backs. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, a man of them married a woman of the Ansar and went to do that with her, but she objected to him and said: 'We used to be approached in only one manner. If you wish, do it that way; otherwise, keep away from me.' The matter spread until it reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, meaning the place of the child, ﴿so go to your tilth however you wish﴾: from the front, from behind, and lying on the back." The word "anna" here is an interrogative particle that asks about the manner and place, and its meaning is: "how you wish and where you wish," provided it is in one and the same vagina (simam wahid). Ikrimah said: "﴿However you wish﴾ refers only to the vagina (al-farj)," and al-Hasan said the same. It has also been said: "﴿A tilth for you﴾ means a field for you and a place of growth for the child, like the land that is sown." This contains evidence for the prohibition of anal intercourse, because the place of tilling and sowing is the front (al-qubul), not the rear (al-dubur).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "This applies to 'azl (coitus interruptus, withdrawal before ejaculation). That is, if you wish, practise 'azl, and if you wish, do not practise 'azl." Ibn Abbas was asked about 'azl and said: "Your tilth: if you wish, make it thirsty, and if you wish, water it." It is also reported from him that he said: "A free woman is to be consulted about 'azl, but a slave-girl is not to be consulted." Ahmad (ibn Hanbal) also held this view. A group of scholars disliked 'azl and said: "It is the hidden burying (al-wa'd al-khafi) of the child."

It is related from Malik, from Nafi', who said: "I was holding the mushaf for Ibn Umar, and he recited this verse, ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾, and said: 'Do you know concerning what this verse was revealed?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'It was revealed concerning a man who came to his wife from behind, and that troubled him, so this verse was revealed.'"[[Al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Daraqutni in Gharib Malik. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/636.]]

It is related from Malik the permissibility of that, but his companions denied it. It is also reported from Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan that he met Salim ibn Abd Allah and said to him: "O Abu Umar, what is this report that Nafi' narrates from Abd Allah (ibn Umar), that he did not see any harm in approaching women in their rear passages?" He said: "The slave lied and erred. Abd Allah (ibn Umar) only said: 'They are approached in their vaginas, from their rear (i.e., from behind).'" The evidence for the prohibition of the rear passages is what was related to us by Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad ibn al-Khatib: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal related to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm related to us: al-Rabi' related to us: al-Shafi'i related to us: Umar Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Shafi' related to us: Abd Allah ibn Ali ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from Amr ibn Uhayhah ibn al-Julah, from Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about approaching women in their rear passages. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "In which of the two openings, or in which of the two holes, or in which of the two pieces of cloth? Is it from behind into the vagina? Then yes. Or from behind into the rear? Then no. Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their rear passages."[[Musnad al-Shafi'i: 2/360. Ibn Hibban (1299) and he declared it authentic. Ahmad: 5/213, from Khuzaymah, with the wording "Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth..." al-Tahawi: 2/25, and its chain is authentic (see Fath al-Bari: 8/143).]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi related to us: Zahir ibn Ahmad related to us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi related to us: Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, [36/b] from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever approaches his wife in her rear passage is cursed."[[Related by Abu Dawud in Nikah, chapter on general matters of marriage (3/77). Ibn Majah in Nikah, chapter on the prohibition of approaching women in their rear passages (no. 1923, 2/619), with the wording: "Allah does not look at a man who has intercourse with his wife in her rear passage," and he said in al-Zawa'id: its chain is authentic. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (9/106).]]

Abu Hurayrah related: "Whoever approaches his wife in her rear passage..."

[Note: the preceding line above is a duplicate of the hadith and is not part of the source text; please disregard it.]

The statement of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾. Ata' said: "It is saying the basmalah at intercourse." Mujahid said: "﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means: when one approaches his wife, let him supplicate."

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Salim, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If any one of you, when he wishes to approach his wife, says: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide us,' then if a child is decreed between them from that union, Satan will never harm it."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Nikah, chapter on what a man says when he approaches his wife (9/28). Muslim in Nikah, chapter on what is recommended to say during intercourse (no. 1434, 2/1058).]] It has also been said: "﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means: seeking offspring."

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi related to us: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Tayisfuni related to us: Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Jawhari related to us: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani related to us: Ali ibn Hujr related to us, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except from three: ongoing charity (sadaqah jariyah), or knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him."[[Related by Muslim in Wasiyyah, chapter on the reward that reaches a person after his death (no. 1631, 3/1255). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/300).]] It has also been said: this refers to marrying for chastity, so that the child may be righteous.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Musaddad related to us: Yahya related to us, from Ubayd Allah: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id related to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A woman is married for four things: for her wealth, for her lineage, for her beauty, and for her religion. So win the one with religion; may your hands be dust."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Nikah, chapter on compatibility in religion (9/131). Muslim in Nikah, chapter on the recommendation of marrying a religious woman (no. 1466, 2/1086). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (9/8).]] It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: seeking the afrat (children who die before their parents, who will intercede for them).

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi related to us: Zahir ibn Ahmad related to us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi related to us: Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim loses three children and then the Fire touches him, except as a fulfilment of an oath (tahillat al-qasam)."[[Related by al-Bukhari in Oaths and Vows, chapter on the saying of Allah: "And they swear by Allah with their most emphatic oaths" (11/541). Muslim in Birr, Silah and Adab, chapter on the virtue of one who loses a child and seeks reward for it (no. 2632, 4/2028). The author in Sharh al-Sunnah (5/450).]]

Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: "﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾ means good and righteous deeds, as the context of the verse indicates: ﴿And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him﴾, that is, that you will return to Him, and He will recompense you for your deeds. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 224–225:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾. It was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah, who had a dispute with his brother-in-law (khatan), Bashir ibn al-Nu'man al-Ansari, over his sister. ʿAbdullah swore that he would not enter upon him, nor speak to him, nor reconcile between him and his opponent. When he was asked about it, he would say: "I have sworn by Allah that I will not do it, so it is not lawful for me unless you make me break my oath." So Allah revealed this verse. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 110; al-Wasit, 1/324.]]

Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he swore that he would not spend on Mistah when Mistah became involved in the talk of the slander (hadith al-ifk). [[Narrated by al-Tabari, 4/423.]]

Al-ʿUrdah (the obstacle): its original meaning is strength and power. From this comes the saying that a mount prepared for travel is called ʿurdah, because of its strength for the journey. Then the term was applied to anything suitable for something, to the extent that they said of a woman, "she is ʿurdat al-nikah" (suitable for marriage) when she is fit for it. Al-ʿUrdah is anything that stands in the way and prevents one from something. The meaning of the verse: ﴿Do not make﴾ the swearing by Allah a cause that prevents you from righteousness and piety, such that one of you is called to maintain family ties or to do good, and he says, "I have sworn by Allah that I will not do it," and so uses his oath as an excuse for abandoning righteousness. ﴿That you should be righteous﴾ means: that you should not be righteous, like His saying, ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ (4:176), meaning: lest you go astray. ﴿And be God-fearing, and make peace among people. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees that something other than it is better, let him make expiation for his oath and do what is better." [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Iman, chapter: recommending that one who has sworn an oath and then sees something better than it do so, no. 1649, 3/2272.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will not hold you to account for the idle oaths in your oaths﴾. Al-laghw is every discarded speech that is not taken into account. The people of knowledge differed concerning the idle oath mentioned in the verse. One group said it is what comes to the tongue hastily as a filler of speech, without binding intention or purpose, such as the saying of the speaker: "No, by Allah," "Yes, by Allah," and "Nay, by Allah."

Abdul-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisai informed us: Abdul-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, that she said: "The idle oath is a person's saying, 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'" Some of them raised it (to the Prophet). [[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in al-Iman, chapter: al-laghw of oaths, 4/359; al-Mundhiri said that more than one narrated it from ʿAta' from ʿAʾishah as a mawquf report. See al-Zayla'i, Nasb al-Rayah, 3/293.]] This is the view of al-Sha'bi, ʿIkrimah, and it is what al-Shafi'i said.

It is narrated from ʿAʾishah: the oaths of idle speech are those made in jest, in disputation, in quarrel, and in speech about which the heart does not form a resolve. Others said: it is swearing about something one believes to be true, then it becomes clear to him that it is otherwise. This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah and Makhul, and Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, also said so. They said there is no expiation for it and no sin upon him. ʿAli said: it is the oath made in anger, and Tawus said likewise. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the oath in disobedience, for which Allah does not hold him accountable for breaking it; rather he breaks it and makes expiation. Masruq said: there is no expiation for it; "Would he expiate the steps of Satan?" Al-Sha'bi said regarding a man who swears to do an act of disobedience: his expiation is that he repent from it. And every oath that it is not lawful for you to fulfil, there is no expiation for it; and if I ordered him to make expiation, I would order him to persist in his statement. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is a man's invoking curses upon himself, such as saying to someone: "May Allah blind my sight if I do not do such-and-such," or "May Allah take me out of my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow," or saying, "He is a disbeliever if he does such-and-such." All of this is idle speech, for which Allah does not hold him to account. Had He held them to account for it, He would have hastened the punishment upon them: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them﴾ (10:11), and He said, ﴿And man invokes evil as he invokes good﴾ (17:11).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But He will hold you to account for what your hearts have earned﴾. That is: you resolved and intended the oath. The heart's "earning" (kasb) is the binding of intention and purpose. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.﴾ Know that an oath is not valid except by Allah, or by one of His names, or by one of His attributes. An oath by Allah is that one says: "By Him whom I worship," "By Him for whom I pray," "By Him in whose hand is my soul," and the like. An oath by His names is like saying "By Allah," "By the Most Merciful," and the like. An oath by His attributes is like saying: "By the might of Allah," "By the greatness of Allah," "By the majesty of Allah," "By the power of Allah," and the like. If one swears by any of these to do something in the future and then breaks it, expiation becomes obligatory upon him. If one swears about a past matter that it occurred when it did not, or that it did not occur when it did, and he knew the truth at the time he swore, this is the oath of ghamus (perjury), which is one of the major sins. According to some scholars, expiation is obligatory for it, whether one knew or was ignorant; this is the view of al-Shafi'i. According to others, it is not obligatory, and this is the view of the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y). They said: if he knew, it is a major sin with no expiation for it, as with all major sins; and if he was ignorant, it is the idle oath according to them. As for one who swears by other than Allah, such as saying, "By the Ka'bah," "By the House of Allah," "By the Prophet of Allah," or swearing by his father and the like, it does not count as an oath, and no expiation is obligatory upon him if he swears this way; it is a disliked oath. Al-Shafi'i said: "I fear it may be a sin."

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab while he was traveling in a company and he was swearing by his father. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers. Whoever is to swear, let him swear by Allah or remain silent." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-Ayman, chapter: Do not swear by your fathers, 11/530; and Muslim: in al-Ayman wa'l-nudhur, chapter: the prohibition of swearing by other than Allah, no. 1646, 3/1266. Ibn ʿUmar added: "By Allah, I have not sworn by them since I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbid it, neither mentioning nor reporting." See the author's Sharh al-Sunnah on oaths, 10/3–8.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 224–225:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾. It was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah ibn Rawahah, who had a dispute with his brother-in-law (khatan), Bashir ibn al-Nu'man al-Ansari, over his sister. ʿAbdullah swore that he would not enter upon him, nor speak to him, nor reconcile between him and his opponent. When he was asked about it, he would say: "I have sworn by Allah that I will not do it, so it is not lawful for me unless you make me break my oath." So Allah revealed this verse. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 110; al-Wasit, 1/324.]]

Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he swore that he would not spend on Mistah when Mistah became involved in the talk of the slander (hadith al-ifk). [[Narrated by al-Tabari, 4/423.]]

Al-ʿUrdah (the obstacle): its original meaning is strength and power. From this comes the saying that a mount prepared for travel is called ʿurdah, because of its strength for the journey. Then the term was applied to anything suitable for something, to the extent that they said of a woman, "she is ʿurdat al-nikah" (suitable for marriage) when she is fit for it. Al-ʿUrdah is anything that stands in the way and prevents one from something. The meaning of the verse: ﴿Do not make﴾ the swearing by Allah a cause that prevents you from righteousness and piety, such that one of you is called to maintain family ties or to do good, and he says, "I have sworn by Allah that I will not do it," and so uses his oath as an excuse for abandoning righteousness. ﴿That you should be righteous﴾ means: that you should not be righteous, like His saying, ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ (4:176), meaning: lest you go astray. ﴿And be God-fearing, and make peace among people. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath and then sees that something other than it is better, let him make expiation for his oath and do what is better." [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Iman, chapter: recommending that one who has sworn an oath and then sees something better than it do so, no. 1649, 3/2272.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will not hold you to account for the idle oaths in your oaths﴾. Al-laghw is every discarded speech that is not taken into account. The people of knowledge differed concerning the idle oath mentioned in the verse. One group said it is what comes to the tongue hastily as a filler of speech, without binding intention or purpose, such as the saying of the speaker: "No, by Allah," "Yes, by Allah," and "Nay, by Allah."

Abdul-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisai informed us: Abdul-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, that she said: "The idle oath is a person's saying, 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'" Some of them raised it (to the Prophet). [[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in al-Iman, chapter: al-laghw of oaths, 4/359; al-Mundhiri said that more than one narrated it from ʿAta' from ʿAʾishah as a mawquf report. See al-Zayla'i, Nasb al-Rayah, 3/293.]] This is the view of al-Sha'bi, ʿIkrimah, and it is what al-Shafi'i said.

It is narrated from ʿAʾishah: the oaths of idle speech are those made in jest, in disputation, in quarrel, and in speech about which the heart does not form a resolve. Others said: it is swearing about something one believes to be true, then it becomes clear to him that it is otherwise. This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah and Makhul, and Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, also said so. They said there is no expiation for it and no sin upon him. ʿAli said: it is the oath made in anger, and Tawus said likewise. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the oath in disobedience, for which Allah does not hold him accountable for breaking it; rather he breaks it and makes expiation. Masruq said: there is no expiation for it; "Would he expiate the steps of Satan?" Al-Sha'bi said regarding a man who swears to do an act of disobedience: his expiation is that he repent from it. And every oath that it is not lawful for you to fulfil, there is no expiation for it; and if I ordered him to make expiation, I would order him to persist in his statement. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is a man's invoking curses upon himself, such as saying to someone: "May Allah blind my sight if I do not do such-and-such," or "May Allah take me out of my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow," or saying, "He is a disbeliever if he does such-and-such." All of this is idle speech, for which Allah does not hold him to account. Had He held them to account for it, He would have hastened the punishment upon them: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them﴾ (10:11), and He said, ﴿And man invokes evil as he invokes good﴾ (17:11).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But He will hold you to account for what your hearts have earned﴾. That is: you resolved and intended the oath. The heart's "earning" (kasb) is the binding of intention and purpose. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing.﴾ Know that an oath is not valid except by Allah, or by one of His names, or by one of His attributes. An oath by Allah is that one says: "By Him whom I worship," "By Him for whom I pray," "By Him in whose hand is my soul," and the like. An oath by His names is like saying "By Allah," "By the Most Merciful," and the like. An oath by His attributes is like saying: "By the might of Allah," "By the greatness of Allah," "By the majesty of Allah," "By the power of Allah," and the like. If one swears by any of these to do something in the future and then breaks it, expiation becomes obligatory upon him. If one swears about a past matter that it occurred when it did not, or that it did not occur when it did, and he knew the truth at the time he swore, this is the oath of ghamus (perjury), which is one of the major sins. According to some scholars, expiation is obligatory for it, whether one knew or was ignorant; this is the view of al-Shafi'i. According to others, it is not obligatory, and this is the view of the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y). They said: if he knew, it is a major sin with no expiation for it, as with all major sins; and if he was ignorant, it is the idle oath according to them. As for one who swears by other than Allah, such as saying, "By the Ka'bah," "By the House of Allah," "By the Prophet of Allah," or swearing by his father and the like, it does not count as an oath, and no expiation is obligatory upon him if he swears this way; it is a disliked oath. Al-Shafi'i said: "I fear it may be a sin."

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab while he was traveling in a company and he was swearing by his father. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers. Whoever is to swear, let him swear by Allah or remain silent." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-Ayman, chapter: Do not swear by your fathers, 11/530; and Muslim: in al-Ayman wa'l-nudhur, chapter: the prohibition of swearing by other than Allah, no. 1646, 3/1266. Ibn ʿUmar added: "By Allah, I have not sworn by them since I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbid it, neither mentioning nor reporting." See the author's Sharh al-Sunnah on oaths, 10/3–8.]]

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 226–228 (Part 1 of 2)**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For those who swear off their wives, there is a waiting period of four months﴾. *Yu'lun* means they swear. *Al-ilya* (the oath of abstinence) is an oath, and the intended meaning of the verse is an oath to abstain from having intercourse with the wife. Qatadah said: *Al-ila'* was a form of divorce in the Jahiliyyah. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: It was one of the harms of the people of the Jahiliyyah. A man did not love his wife and did not want anyone else to marry her, so he swore that he would never approach her. He would leave her neither unmarried nor married. They practised this at the beginning of Islam, so God set a term for it in Islam.

The scholars differed concerning it. Most of them held that if he swears never to approach his wife, or specifies a period longer than four months, he becomes a *mu'li* (one who has sworn an oath of abstinence). He is not to be pressed before four months have passed. After they have passed, he is held to account and commanded either to *fay'* (return) or to divorce, after the wife's demand. *Al-fay'* is returning from what he said by means of intercourse, if he is able to do so; if he is not able, then by words. If he neither returns nor divorces, the ruler pronounces one divorce upon him.

Umar, Uthman, Ali, Abu al-Darda' and Ibn Umar held the view of holding him to account after the period has passed. Sulayman ibn Yasar said: I met some ten or more of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and all of them said that the *mu'li* is held to account. This was also the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar and Mujahid. Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also said this.

Some scholars said: When four months have passed, one irrevocable divorce (*talaqah ba'inah*) falls upon her. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud, and Sufyan al-Thawri and the adherents of opinion (*ashab al-ra'y*) also said this.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhri said: One revocable divorce (*talaqah raj'iyyah*) falls. If he swears not to have intercourse with her for less than four months, he is not a *mu'li*; rather, he is one who has sworn an ordinary oath (*halif*). If he has intercourse with her before that period has passed, he must pay the expiation of an oath (*kaffarat al-yamin*). If he swears not to have intercourse with her for four months, he is not a *mu'li* according to those who hold the view of holding him to account after the period has passed, because the continuation of the period is a condition for the holding to account and for the establishment of the demand for return or divorce, and the period has already passed. According to those who do not hold the view of holding him to account, he is a *mu'li*, and divorce falls when the period has passed.

The period of *ila'* is four months for both the free man and the slave, according to al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, because it was set for a meaning that relates to natural disposition, namely the woman's lack of patience with the husband's absence. Thus the free man and the slave are equal in it, like the period of *'unnah* (impotence).

According to Malik and Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on them, the period of *'unnah* is halved for the slave. However, according to Abu Hanifah it is halved by the slave status of the woman, while according to Malik it is halved by the slave status of the husband, just as they both said regarding divorce.

His saying: ﴿a waiting period of four months﴾, that is, the waiting of four months. *Al-tarabbus* means to wait patiently and to hold back. ﴿And if they return﴾ means they retract the oath by intercourse. ﴿Then indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. When he has had intercourse, he is free from the *ila'*, and the expiation of an oath becomes obligatory upon him according to most of the scholars. Al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Qatadah said: There is no expiation upon him, because God promised forgiveness when He said: ﴿Then indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. According to most scholars, this refers to the removal of punishment, not to the expiation.

If he says to his wife: "If I approach you, then my slave is free," or "you will be divorced," or "it is incumbent upon me before God to free a slave, or to fast, or to pray," then he is a *mu'li*, because the *mu'li* is one upon whom a matter becomes binding concerning intercourse. He is held to account after the period has passed. If he returns, the divorce or the emancipation attached to it takes effect. If he binds himself by an obligation upon his person, then according to one opinion the expiation of an oath is binding upon him, and according to another opinion he is bound by what he obligated upon himself: emancipation, prayer or fasting.

﴿And if they resolve upon divorce﴾, that is, they carry it out by pronouncing it. ﴿Then indeed God is Hearing﴾, ﴿Knowing﴾ of their intentions. In this there is evidence that she is not divorced after the period has passed unless her husband divorces her, because He made the condition *'azm* (resolve). He said: ﴿Then indeed God is Hearing, Knowing﴾, which indicates that it requires something to be heard, and speech is what is heard.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And divorced women﴾, that is, those who have been released from the bonds of their husbands. ﴿Shall wait﴾, they shall wait ﴿by themselves for three *quru'*﴾, so they do not remarry. *Al-quru'* is the plural of *qar'*, like *far'*. Its paucal plural is *aqru'* and its plural of multitude is *aqra'*. The scholars differed concerning *al-quru'*. A group held that it means menstruation (*al-hayd*). This was the view of Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan and Mujahid also said this. Al-Awza'i, al-Thawri and the adherents of opinion also held this view. They argued that the Prophet ﷺ said to a woman suffering from *istihadah* (irregular bleeding): "Leave off prayer during the days of your *aqra'* (menstrual periods)." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud: in Purification, chapter: Whoever says she bathes from one purity to another, 1/191. And al-Tirmidhi: in Purification, chapter: What has come that the woman with *istihadah* performs ablution for every prayer, 1/393. And Ibn Majah: in Purification, chapter: What has come concerning the woman with *istihadah*, 1/204. And al-Daraqutni: in Menstruation, 1/212. See also Nasb al-Raya: 1/202–204.]] Women only leave off prayer during the days of their menstruation.

Another group held that they are the periods of purity (*al-athhar*). This was the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Umar and Aisha. It was also the view of the Seven Jurists, al-Zuhri, and Rabi'ah, Malik and al-Shafi'i also said this. They argued that when Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, divorced his wife while she was menstruating, the Prophet ﷺ said to Umar: "Command him that he take her back until she becomes pure, then if he wishes he may keep her, and if he wishes he may divorce her before he touches her. That is the waiting period (*'iddah*) in which God commanded that women be divorced." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Divorce, chapter: The prohibition of divorcing a menstruating woman without her consent, no. 1471, 3/1093. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/202–203.]]

So he informed that the time of the waiting period is purity. From the standpoint of language, there is the saying of the poet:

*"So in every year you are one who undertakes a raid,*
*Tightening for its far end the firm resolve of your endurance,*

*Leaving behind wealth and honour among the tribe,*
*Because of the *quru'* of your women that were lost during it."*

He meant that he used to go out to raiding and did not approach his women, so their *aqra'* were lost. Their *aqra'* are only lost by travel during the time of purity, not during the time of menstruation.

The benefit of the difference appears in this: when a woman in her waiting period begins the third menstruation, her waiting period ends according to the view of those who regard *quru'* as periods of purity, and the remainder of the purity in which the divorce occurred is counted as a *qar'*. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "When a divorced woman stabs into the blood of the third menstruation, she has become free of him and he is free of her." Those who held that *quru'* are menstruation say that her waiting period does not end until she becomes pure from the third menstruation.

This difference arises from the fact that the term *qar'* applies to both purity and menstruation together. It is said: *aqra'at al-mar'ah* when she menstruates, and *aqra'at* when she becomes pure, so she is *muqri'*. They differed concerning its root. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' and Abu Ubaydah said: It is the time of the coming and going of a thing. It is said: "So-and-so returned to his *qar'* and to his *qari'*," meaning to his time at which he returns. "This is the *qari'* of the winds," meaning the time of their blowing. Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said:

*"I disliked the slaughter of the Banu Shalil*
*When the winds blew at their *qari'*."*

That is, at their time. *Al-qar'* is suitable for both meanings, because menstruation comes at a time, and purity is likewise. It was also said: It is from *al-qar'*, which means restraint and gathering. The Arabs say: "The she-camel never *qara'at* a foal," meaning her womb never closed upon a young one. From this is *qaraytu al-ma'* *fi al-miqra'ah*, which is the basin, meaning I gathered the water, without the hamza. Thus *al-qar'* here is the retention and gathering of the blood. According to this, the preference is for purity, because it retains and gathers the blood, while menstruation releases and sends it forth.

The summary of the ruling concerning the waiting periods is this. If the woman is pregnant, her waiting period is by the delivery of the child, whether the separation between her and the husband occurs by divorce or by death, because of His saying: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ (Surah al-Talaq, 4). If she is not pregnant, one considers: if the separation between them occurs by the death of the husband, then she must observe a waiting period of four months and ten days, whether the husband died before or after consummation, and whether the woman is one who menstruates or not, because of God's saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 234).

If the separation between them occurs during their lifetime, one considers: if the divorce was before consummation, then there is no waiting period for her, because of God's saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period for them to count﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab, 49).

If it was after consummation, one considers: if the woman is one who has never menstruated, or who has reached the age of the postmenopausal women in old age, then her waiting period is three months, because of God's saying: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated﴾ (Surah al-Talaq, 4).

If she is one who menstruates, her waiting period is three *quru'*, because of His saying: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three *quru'*﴾. His saying ﴿shall wait by themselves﴾ is grammatically a statement, but its meaning is a command. The waiting period of a slave woman, if she is pregnant, is by the delivery of the child, like a free woman. If she is not pregnant, then in the case of death her waiting period is two months and five nights. In the case of divorce, if she is one who menstruates, her waiting period is two *qur'*; if she is one who does not menstruate, it is a month and a half. It was also said: two months, like the two *qur'* for one who menstruates.

Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: A slave may marry two wives and divorce two times, and a slave woman observes a waiting period of two menstruations. If she does not menstruate, then two months or a month and a half.

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾. Ikrimah said: This means menstruation, namely that a man wants to take her back and she says: "I have had my third menstruation." Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It means pregnancy. The meaning of the verse is: It is not lawful for a woman to conceal what God has created in her womb, of menstruation and pregnancy, in order to nullify the husband's right of return and the child. ﴿If they believe in God and the Last Day﴾ means: this is an action of believing women, and even if the believing woman and the disbelieving woman are equal in this ruling, as one says: "Give me my right if you are a believer," meaning that fulfilling rights is an action of believers.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 2, verses 226–228 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And their husbands (bu'ulatuhunna)﴾ means their spouses (azwajahunna). It is the plural of *ba'l* (husband, lord), as *fuhulah* is the plural of *fahl* (stallion). The husband is called *ba'l* because he takes care of his wife's affairs. The root meaning of *ba'l* is master and owner. ﴿Have more right to take them back (ahaqqu bi-raddihinna)﴾ means have more right to revoke them (*raj'atihinna*) and return them to themselves. ﴿In that matter (fi dhalika)﴾ means if they intend by the taking back (*raj'ah*) reform and good companionship, not harm, as they used to do in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance). A man would divorce his wife, and when her *'iddah* (waiting period) was nearly over, he would take her back, then leave her for a period, then divorce her again. When her *'iddah* was nearly over again, he would take her back, and after another period he would divorce her again, intending by this to prolong her waiting period.

﴿And they (wa-lahunna)﴾ means women have over men ﴿the same as what is due from them, according to what is reasonable (mithlu alladhi 'alayhinna bi-al-ma'ruf)﴾, as the husbands have over them. Ibn 'Abbas said regarding its meaning: "I love to adorn myself for my wife, just as my wife loves to adorn herself for me, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they have rights similar to their obligations, according to what is reasonable﴾."

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us; Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Tarafah al-Sijzi informed us; Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi informed us; Abu Bakr ibn Dasah informed us; Abu Dawud al-Sijistani informed us; Musa ibn Isma'il informed us; Hammad informed us; Abu Qaza'ah Suwayd ibn Hujayr al-Bahili narrated from Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah al-Qushayri, from his father, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the wife of one of us over him?" He said: "That you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike the face, do not revile her, and do not forsake her except within the house."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in *al-Nikah*, *bab: haqq al-mar'ah 'ala zawjiha*, 3/67–68. Ibn Majah in *al-Nikah*, *bab: fi haqq al-mar'ah 'ala al-zawj*, no. (1850), 1/593. Ahmad, 4/446–447 and 5/3–5, part of a hadith narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah. The author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 9/160.]]

Abu Isma'il Ibrahim al-Jurjani? [sic] ... *(see below)*

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us; 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us; Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us; Hatim ibn Isma'il al-Madani informed us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, that he said: "We entered upon Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and I said: 'Tell me about the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'" He then recounted the story of the Farewell Pilgrimage until he mentioned his sermon on the Day of 'Arafah. He said: "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are *'awan* (captives) with you. You have taken them with the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful through the word of Allah. You have a right over them that they not let anyone you dislike tread upon your bedding. If they do that, then strike them with a non-severe strike. Their provision and clothing are due from you according to what is reasonable. I have left among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after it: the Book of Allah. And you will be asked about me, so what will you say?" They said: "We testify that you have conveyed, fulfilled and advised." He then pointed with his index finger, raising it toward the sky and lowering it toward the people, saying: "O Allah, bear witness! O Allah, bear witness!" [[Previously cited, p. (219), footnote (2). It is part of the hadith of the Prophet's Hajj. Narrated by Muslim in *al-Hajj*, *bab: hajjat al-Nabi ﷺ*, no. (1218), 2/886.]] three times.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi [37b] informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us; Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most complete of believers in faith are the best of them in character, and the best of you are the best to your women." [[Abu Dawud in *al-Sunnah*, with the wording "Akmal al-mu'minina iman an ahsanuhum khuluqan," 7/44. It is also narrated with this wording by al-Darimi in *al-Riqaq*, *bab: fi husn al-khuluq*, 2/323. al-Tirmidhi in *al-Radla'*, *bab: ma ja'a fi haqq al-mar'ah 'ala zawjiha*, 4/325, and said: "Hasan sahih." Ibn Hibban, no. (1926), and he authenticated it. Ahmad, 2/250 and 472, from Abu Hurayrah. The author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 9/180.]].

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And men have a degree over them (wa-li-al-rijali 'alayhinna darajah)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "By what he gives her of the dower (*mahr*) and spends on her from his wealth." Qatadah said: "By jihad." It was said: "By intellect (*'aql*)," and it was said: "By testimony," and it was said: "By inheritance," and it was said: "By blood money (*diyah*)," and it was said: "By divorce, because divorce is in the hands of men," and it was said: "By the right of revocation (*raj'ah*)." Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: "By leadership (*imarah*)." Al-Qutabi said: "﴿And men have a degree over them﴾ means a superiority in right." ﴿And Allah is Mighty, Wise﴾.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Birti informed us; Hudhayfah informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, that Mu'adh ibn Jabal went out on a military campaign to which the Prophet ﷺ had sent him. Then he returned and saw men prostrating to one another. He mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "If I were to order anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would order the woman to prostrate to her husband." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in *al-Nikah*, *bab: haqq al-zawj 'ala al-mar'ah*, no. (1853), 1/595. Abu Dawud in *al-Nikah*, *bab: fi haqq al-zawj 'ala al-mar'ah*, 3/67. Ibn Hibban in his *Sahih*, no. (1290), p. 314. Ahmad, 4/381, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa; 5/228 from Mu'adh ibn Jabal; 6/76 from 'A'ishah with a different wording. The author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 9/158. Al-Haythami mentioned it in *al-Majma'*, 4/309, and said: "Narrated in full by al-Bazzar and Ahmad in abridged form, and its narrators are the narrators of the sahih."]].

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verses 226–228 (Part 1 of 2)**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For those who swear off their wives, there is a waiting period of four months﴾. *Yu'lun* means they swear. *Al-ilya* (the oath of abstinence) is an oath, and the intended meaning of the verse is an oath to abstain from having intercourse with the wife. Qatadah said: *Al-ila'* was a form of divorce in the Jahiliyyah. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: It was one of the harms of the people of the Jahiliyyah. A man did not love his wife and did not want anyone else to marry her, so he swore that he would never approach her. He would leave her neither unmarried nor married. They practised this at the beginning of Islam, so God set a term for it in Islam.

The scholars differed concerning it. Most of them held that if he swears never to approach his wife, or specifies a period longer than four months, he becomes a *mu'li* (one who has sworn an oath of abstinence). He is not to be pressed before four months have passed. After they have passed, he is held to account and commanded either to *fay'* (return) or to divorce, after the wife's demand. *Al-fay'* is returning from what he said by means of intercourse, if he is able to do so; if he is not able, then by words. If he neither returns nor divorces, the ruler pronounces one divorce upon him.

Umar, Uthman, Ali, Abu al-Darda' and Ibn Umar held the view of holding him to account after the period has passed. Sulayman ibn Yasar said: I met some ten or more of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and all of them said that the *mu'li* is held to account. This was also the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar and Mujahid. Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also said this.

Some scholars said: When four months have passed, one irrevocable divorce (*talaqah ba'inah*) falls upon her. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud, and Sufyan al-Thawri and the adherents of opinion (*ashab al-ra'y*) also said this.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhri said: One revocable divorce (*talaqah raj'iyyah*) falls. If he swears not to have intercourse with her for less than four months, he is not a *mu'li*; rather, he is one who has sworn an ordinary oath (*halif*). If he has intercourse with her before that period has passed, he must pay the expiation of an oath (*kaffarat al-yamin*). If he swears not to have intercourse with her for four months, he is not a *mu'li* according to those who hold the view of holding him to account after the period has passed, because the continuation of the period is a condition for the holding to account and for the establishment of the demand for return or divorce, and the period has already passed. According to those who do not hold the view of holding him to account, he is a *mu'li*, and divorce falls when the period has passed.

The period of *ila'* is four months for both the free man and the slave, according to al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, because it was set for a meaning that relates to natural disposition, namely the woman's lack of patience with the husband's absence. Thus the free man and the slave are equal in it, like the period of *'unnah* (impotence).

According to Malik and Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on them, the period of *'unnah* is halved for the slave. However, according to Abu Hanifah it is halved by the slave status of the woman, while according to Malik it is halved by the slave status of the husband, just as they both said regarding divorce.

When he has had intercourse, he is free from the *ila'*, and the expiation of an oath becomes obligatory upon him according to most of the scholars. Al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Qatadah said: There is no expiation upon him, because God promised forgiveness when He said: ﴿Then indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. According to most scholars, this refers to the removal of punishment, not to the expiation.

If he says to his wife: "If I approach you, then my slave is free," or "you will be divorced," or "it is incumbent upon me before God to free a slave, or to fast, or to pray," then he is a *mu'li*, because the *mu'li* is one upon whom a matter becomes binding concerning intercourse. He is held to account after the period has passed. If he returns, the divorce or the emancipation attached to it takes effect. If he binds himself by an obligation upon his person, then according to one opinion the expiation of an oath is binding upon him, and according to another opinion he is bound by what he obligated upon himself: emancipation, prayer or fasting.

﴿And if they resolve upon divorce﴾, that is, they carry it out by pronouncing it. ﴿Then indeed God is Hearing﴾, ﴿Knowing﴾ of their intentions. In this there is evidence that she is not divorced after the period has passed unless her husband divorces her, because He made the condition *'azm* (resolve). He said: ﴿Then indeed God is Hearing, Knowing﴾, which indicates that it requires something to be heard, and speech is what is heard.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And divorced women﴾, that is, those who have been released from the bonds of their husbands. ﴿Shall wait﴾, they shall wait ﴿by themselves for three *quru'*﴾, so they do not remarry. *Al-quru'* is the plural of *qar'*, like *far'*. Its paucal plural is *aqru'* and its plural of multitude is *aqra'*. The scholars differed concerning *al-quru'*. A group held that it means menstruation (*al-hayd*). This was the view of Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan and Mujahid also said this. Al-Awza'i, al-Thawri and the adherents of opinion also held this view. They argued that the Prophet ﷺ said to a woman suffering from *istihadah* (irregular bleeding): "Leave off prayer during the days of your *aqra'* (menstrual periods)." Another group held that they are the periods of purity (*al-athhar*). This was the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Umar and Aisha. It was also the view of the Seven Jurists, al-Zuhri, and Rabi'ah, Malik and al-Shafi'i also said this. So he informed that the time of the waiting period is purity. From the standpoint of language, there is the saying of the poet:

*"So in every year you are one who undertakes a raid,*
*Tightening for its far end the firm resolve of your endurance,*

*Leaving behind wealth and honour among the tribe,*
*Because of the *quru'* of your women that were lost during it."*

He meant that he used to go out to raiding and did not approach his women, so their *aqra'* were lost. Their *aqra'* are only lost by travel during the time of purity, not during the time of menstruation.

Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: "When a divorced woman stabs into the blood of the third menstruation, she has become free of him and he is free of her." Those who held that *quru'* are menstruation say that her waiting period does not end until she becomes pure from the third menstruation.

This difference arises from the fact that the term *qar'* applies to both purity and menstruation together. It is said: *aqra'at al-mar'ah* when she menstruates, and *aqra'at* when she becomes pure, so she is *muqri'*. They differed concerning its root. It is said: "So-and-so returned to his *qar'* and to his *qari'*," meaning to his time at which he returns. "This is the *qari'* of the winds," meaning the time of their blowing. Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said:

*"I disliked the slaughter of the Banu Shalil*
*When the winds blew at their *qari'*."*

From this is *qaraytu al-ma'* *fi al-miqra'ah*, which is the basin, meaning I gathered the water, without the hamza. Thus *al-qar'* here is the retention and gathering of the blood. According to this, the preference is for purity, because it retains and gathers the blood, while menstruation releases and sends it forth.

The summary of the ruling concerning the waiting periods is this. If she is not pregnant, one considers: if the separation between them occurs by the death of the husband, then she must observe a waiting period of four months and ten days, whether the husband died before or after consummation, and whether the woman is one who menstruates or not, because of God's saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 234).

If she is not pregnant, then in the case of death her waiting period is two months and five nights. In the case of divorce, if she is one who menstruates, her waiting period is two *qur'*; if she is one who does not menstruate, it is a month and a half. It was also said: two months, like the two *qur'* for one who menstruates.

Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: A slave may marry two wives and divorce two times, and a slave woman observes a waiting period of two menstruations. If she does not menstruate, then two months or a month and a half.

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾. Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 2, verses 226–228 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And their husbands (bu'ulatuhunna)﴾ means their spouses (azwajahunna). It is the plural of *ba'l* (husband, lord), as *fuhulah* is the plural of *fahl* (stallion). The husband is called *ba'l* because he takes care of his wife's affairs. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' and Abu Ubaydah said: It is the time of the coming and going of a thing. It is said: "So-and-so returned to his *qar'* and to his *qari'*," meaning to his time at which he returns. "This is the *qari'* of the winds," meaning the time of their blowing. Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said:

*"I disliked the slaughter of the Banu Shalil*
*When the winds blew at their *qari'*."*

That is, at their time. *Al-qar'* is suitable for both meanings, because menstruation comes at a time, and purity is likewise. It was also said: It is from *al-qar'*, which means restraint and gathering. The Arabs say: "The she-camel never *qara'at* a foal," meaning her womb never closed upon a young one.
