From this is *qaraytu al-ma'* *fi al-miqra'ah*, which is the basin, meaning I gathered the water, without the hamza. Thus *al-qar'* here is the retention and gathering of the blood. According to this, the preference is for purity, because it retains and gathers the blood, while menstruation releases and sends it forth.

The summary of the ruling concerning the waiting periods is this. If the woman is pregnant, her waiting period is by the delivery of the child, whether the separation between her and the husband occurs by divorce or by death, because of His saying: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ (Surah al-Talaq, 4). If she is not pregnant, one considers: if the separation between them occurs by the death of the husband, then she must observe a waiting period of four months and ten days, whether the husband died before or after consummation, and whether the woman is one who menstruates or not, because of God's saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 234).

If the separation between them occurs during their lifetime, one considers: if the divorce was before consummation, then there is no waiting period for her, because of God's saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period for them to count﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab, 49).

If it was after consummation, one considers: if the woman is one who has never menstruated, or who has reached the age of the postmenopausal women in old age, then her waiting period is three months, because of God's saying: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated﴾ (Surah al-Talaq, 4).

If she is one who menstruates, her waiting period is three *quru'*, because of His saying: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three *quru'*﴾. His saying ﴿shall wait by themselves﴾ is grammatically a statement, but its meaning is a command. The waiting period of a slave woman, if she is pregnant, is by the delivery of the child, like a free woman. If she is not pregnant, then in the case of death her waiting period is two months and five nights. In the case of divorce, if she is one who menstruates, her waiting period is two *qur'*; if she is one who does not menstruate, it is a month and a half. It was also said: two months, like the two *qur'* for one who menstruates.

Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: A slave may marry two wives and divorce two times, and a slave woman observes a waiting period of two menstruations. If she does not menstruate, then two months or a month and a half.

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾. Ikrimah said: This means menstruation, namely that a man wants to take her back and she says: "I have had my third menstruation." Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It means pregnancy. The meaning of the verse is: It is not lawful for a woman to conceal what God has created in her womb, of menstruation and pregnancy, in order to nullify the husband's right of return and the child. ﴿If they believe in God and the Last Day﴾ means: this is an action of believing women, and even if the believing woman and the disbelieving woman are equal in this ruling, as one says: "Give me my right if you are a believer," meaning that fulfilling rights is an action of believers.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 2, verses 226–228 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And their husbands (bu'ulatuhunna)﴾ means their spouses (azwajahunna). It is the plural of *ba'l* (husband, lord), as *fuhulah* is the plural of *fahl* (stallion). The husband is called *ba'l* because he takes care of his wife's affairs. The root meaning of *ba'l* is master and owner. ﴿Have more right to take them back (ahaqqu bi-raddihinna)﴾ means have more right to revoke them (*raj'atihinna*) and return them to themselves. ﴿In that matter (fi dhalika)﴾ means if they intend by the taking back (*raj'ah*) reform and good companionship, not harm, as they used to do in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance). A man would divorce his wife, and when her *'iddah* (waiting period) was nearly over, he would take her back, then leave her for a period, then divorce her again. When her *'iddah* was nearly over again, he would take her back, and after another period he would divorce her again, intending by this to prolong her waiting period.

﴿And they (wa-lahunna)﴾ means women have over men ﴿the same as what is due from them, according to what is reasonable (mithlu alladhi 'alayhinna bi-al-ma'ruf)﴾, as the husbands have over them. Ibn 'Abbas said regarding its meaning: "I love to adorn myself for my wife, just as my wife loves to adorn herself for me, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they have rights similar to their obligations, according to what is reasonable﴾."

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us; Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Tarafah al-Sijzi informed us; Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi informed us; Abu Bakr ibn Dasah informed us; Abu Dawud al-Sijistani informed us; Musa ibn Isma'il informed us; Hammad informed us; Abu Qaza'ah Suwayd ibn Hujayr al-Bahili narrated from Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah al-Qushayri, from his father, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the wife of one of us over him?" He said: "That you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike the face, do not revile her, and do not forsake her except within the house."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in *al-Nikah*, *bab: haqq al-mar'ah 'ala zawjiha*, 3/67–68. Ibn Majah in *al-Nikah*, *bab: fi haqq al-mar'ah 'ala al-zawj*, no. (1850), 1/593. Ahmad, 4/446–447 and 5/3–5, part of a hadith narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah. The author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 9/160.]]

Abu Isma'il Ibrahim al-Jurjani? [sic] ... *(see below)*

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us; 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us; Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us; Hatim ibn Isma'il al-Madani informed us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, that he said: "We entered upon Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and I said: 'Tell me about the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'" He then recounted the story of the Farewell Pilgrimage until he mentioned his sermon on the Day of 'Arafah. He said: "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are *'awan* (captives) with you. You have taken them with the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful through the word of Allah. You have a right over them that they not let anyone you dislike tread upon your bedding. If they do that, then strike them with a non-severe strike. Their provision and clothing are due from you according to what is reasonable. I have left among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after it: the Book of Allah. And you will be asked about me, so what will you say?" They said: "We testify that you have conveyed, fulfilled and advised." He then pointed with his index finger, raising it toward the sky and lowering it toward the people, saying: "O Allah, bear witness! O Allah, bear witness!" [[Previously cited, p. (219), footnote (2). It is part of the hadith of the Prophet's Hajj. Narrated by Muslim in *al-Hajj*, *bab: hajjat al-Nabi ﷺ*, no. (1218), 2/886.]] three times.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi [37b] informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us; Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most complete of believers in faith are the best of them in character, and the best of you are the best to your women." [[Abu Dawud in *al-Sunnah*, with the wording "Akmal al-mu'minina iman an ahsanuhum khuluqan," 7/44. It is also narrated with this wording by al-Darimi in *al-Riqaq*, *bab: fi husn al-khuluq*, 2/323. al-Tirmidhi in *al-Radla'*, *bab: ma ja'a fi haqq al-mar'ah 'ala zawjiha*, 4/325, and said: "Hasan sahih." Ibn Hibban, no. (1926), and he authenticated it. Ahmad, 2/250 and 472, from Abu Hurayrah. The author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 9/180.]].

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And men have a degree over them (wa-li-al-rijali 'alayhinna darajah)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "By what he gives her of the dower (*mahr*) and spends on her from his wealth." Qatadah said: "By jihad." It was said: "By intellect (*'aql*)," and it was said: "By testimony," and it was said: "By inheritance," and it was said: "By blood money (*diyah*)," and it was said: "By divorce, because divorce is in the hands of men," and it was said: "By the right of revocation (*raj'ah*)." Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: "By leadership (*imarah*)." Al-Qutabi said: "﴿And men have a degree over them﴾ means a superiority in right." ﴿And Allah is Mighty, Wise﴾.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Birti informed us; Hudhayfah informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, that Mu'adh ibn Jabal went out on a military campaign to which the Prophet ﷺ had sent him. Then he returned and saw men prostrating to one another. He mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "If I were to order anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would order the woman to prostrate to her husband." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in *al-Nikah*, *bab: haqq al-zawj 'ala al-mar'ah*, no. (1853), 1/595. Abu Dawud in *al-Nikah*, *bab: fi haqq al-zawj 'ala al-mar'ah*, 3/67. Ibn Hibban in his *Sahih*, no. (1290), p. 314. Ahmad, 4/381, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa; 5/228 from Mu'adh ibn Jabal; 6/76 from 'A'ishah with a different wording. The author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 9/158. Al-Haythami mentioned it in *al-Majma'*, 4/309, and said: "Narrated in full by al-Bazzar and Ahmad in abridged form, and its narrators are the narrators of the sahih."]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 229–230 (part 1 of 2):

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾. It is narrated from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "In the beginning, people would divorce without limit or count. A man would divorce his wife, and when she neared the end of her waiting period ('idda), he would take her back, then divorce her again, and then take her back again, intending to harm her. So this verse was revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, meaning that the divorce after which one may take the wife back (raj'a) is twice. If he divorces three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿then either retain her in kindness﴾. It has been said that by "retaining" is meant taking her back after the second divorce. The sounder view is that what is meant is retention after the return: that is, if he has taken her back after the second return, he must retain her in kindness. "Kindness" (al-ma'ruf) is whatever is recognized in the Sharia, including fulfilling the rights of marriage and good companionship. ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾: that he leave her after the divorce until her waiting period ends. It has also been said that this refers to the third divorce.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾. The explicit words by which divorce takes effect without intention are three: "talaq" (divorce), "firaq" (separation), and "sarah" (release). According to Abu Hanifa, the explicit word is only the term "talaq" itself. The general ruling on this is that if a free man divorces his wife one or two times after consummation, he may take her back without her consent as long as she is within the waiting period. If he does not take her back until her waiting period ends, or if he divorces her before consummation, or if she obtains a khul' (divorce through compensation paid by the wife) from him, then she is not lawful to him except by a new marriage with her permission and the permission of her guardian. If he divorces her three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband. As for a slave whose wife is under him, if he divorces her twice, she is not lawful to him except after she marries another husband.

The scholars differed concerning the case where one of the spouses is a slave. Most of them held that the number of divorces is reckoned by the husband's status: a free man has three divorces over his slave wife, while a slave has only two divorces over his free wife. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Divorce is by men and the waiting period is by women," meaning that the husband's status determines the number of divorces, and the wife's status determines the length of the waiting period. This is the view of Uthman, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them all, and Ata, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and it is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. Others held that the reckoning in the number of divorces is by the wife's status, so a slave has three divorces over his free wife, and a free man has only two divorces over his slave wife. This is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri and the Companions of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y).

The words of the Exalted: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾, i.e., what you have given them, ﴿anything﴾, meaning the dowries and other things. Then He made an exception for khul', saying: ﴿unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. It was revealed concerning Jamila, daughter of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa; it is also said: Habiba, daughter of Sahl. She was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and she disliked him while he loved her. There was a quarrel between them, so she went to her father and complained to him about her husband, saying: "He mistreats me and beats me." He said: "Go back to your husband, for I dislike that a woman should keep raising her hands complaining about her husband." She returned to him a second time with marks of the beating on her. He said to her: "Go back to your husband." When she saw that her father would not help her, she went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him about her husband, showing him the marks of his beating on her, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, neither I nor he [can continue]." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Thabit and said: "What is your matter with your wife?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, there is nobody on the face of the earth more beloved to me than her, except you." He said to her: "What do you say?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he asked her, so she said: "He has spoken the truth, O Messenger of Allah, but I have feared that he will destroy me, so remove me from him." She also said: "O Messenger of Allah, I would not tell you a matter which Allah would reveal to you the opposite of. He is among the most generous of people in his love for his wife, but I dislike him, so neither I nor he [can continue]." Thabit said: "I have given her a garden; let her return it to me, and I will release her." He said to her: "Will you return his garden to him and be free of your matter?" She said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Thabit, take back from her what you gave her and release her." So he did.

Abu Abdullah... [The chain continues:] We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Zahir ibn Jamil informed us, who said: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi informed us, who said: Khalid informed us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the wife of Thabit ibn Qays came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Thabit—I do not blame him for his character or his religion, but I dislike disbelief after Islam." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you return his garden to him?" She said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Accept the garden and divorce her with one divorce."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿unless both fear﴾, i.e., know, ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. Abu Ja'far, Hamza, and Ya'qub read ﴿yakhafa﴾ [in the form ﴿yukhafa﴾] with a dammah on the yā', meaning: this is known about them, i.e., the judge and the guardian know this about the spouses. The evidence for this is the words of the Exalted: ﴿if you fear﴾, which assigns the fear to someone other than the spouses, and He did not say "if they both fear." The others read ﴿yakhafa﴾ with a fatha on the yā', meaning: the spouses know from themselves ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. The wife fears that she will disobey Allah regarding her husband's rights, and the husband fears, if his wife does not obey him, that he will transgress against her. So Allah forbade the man to take anything from his wife of what he had given her, except when the disobedience (nushuz) comes from her side. She then says: "I will not obey you in any command, and I will not let you lie beside me," and similar things.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up therewith﴾, i.e., for what the woman ransoms herself with from him. Al-Farra' said: By His words ﴿upon them﴾ He means the husband only, not the woman, and He mentioned both of them together because they are paired, as in His words ﴿they forgot their fish﴾ (61 - al-Kahf), though it was only the youth of Musa who forgot, not Musa himself. It has also been said that He meant there is no blame on either of them together: there is no blame on the woman for disobedience if she fears destruction and sin, nor for what she ransoms herself with and gives as wealth, because she is forbidden to waste wealth without right; and no blame on the husband for what he takes from her of wealth if she gives it willingly. Most scholars hold that khul' is permissible for more than what he gave her. Al-Zuhri said: It is not permissible for more than what he gave her of the dowry. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: He should not take from her all that he gave her, but should leave some of it. Khul' is permissible in circumstances other than nushuz, but it is disliked, because it entails severing the bond without cause.

We were informed by Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, who said: Abu Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed me, who said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Mustamli informed us, who said: Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Ishaq ibn Shakir ibn Ahmad ibn Khabbab informed us, who said: Isa ibn Yunus informed us, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the most hated of lawful things to Allah is divorce."

We were informed by Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, who said: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Ubayy informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shayba informed us, who said: Ubayy informed us, who said: Usama informed us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma al-Rahabi, from Thawban, who traced it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any need, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her."

Tawus said: Khul' is specific to the situation of fear of nushuz, based on the apparent meaning of the verse. The verse came in accordance with the custom, that khul' generally occurs only in a state of fear of nushuz. And if a man divorces his wife with the word of divorce in exchange for property, and she accepts, then the separation (bayna) takes effect and the count of divorces is reduced by it.

The scholars differed concerning khul'. Most of them held that it is an irrevocable single divorce (talaqa ba'ina), by which the count of divorces is reduced. This is the view of Umar, Uthman, Ali, and Ibn Mas'ud, and it is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Ata, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and al-Nakha'i. It is also the position of Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, and the Companions of opinion, and it is the more apparent of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i. Others held that it is a annulment (faskh) by which the count of divorces is not reduced. This is the view of Abdullah ibn Umar and Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and it is the view of Ikrima and Tawus, and it is the position of Ahmad and Ishaq. They argued that Allah the Exalted mentioned divorce twice, then mentioned khul' after it, then mentioned the third divorce after it, saying: ﴿And if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries a husband other than him﴾. If khul' were a divorce, the divorces would be four. Whoever holds the first view takes the third divorce to be ﴿or release her with good treatment﴾.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., these are the commands and prohibitions of Allah. The limits of Allah are what the Sharia prohibits from exceeding. ﴿So do not transgress them﴾, i.e., do not go beyond them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah—it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if he divorces her﴾, meaning the third divorce, ﴿then she is not lawful to him after that﴾, i.e., after the third divorce, ﴿until she marries a husband other than him﴾, i.e., other than the one who divorced her, so that he has intercourse with her. Marriage (nikah) covers both the sexual intercourse and the contract together. It was revealed concerning Tamima. It has also been said concerning Aisha, daughter of Abd al-Rahman ibn Atik al-Qurazi, who was married to her cousin Rifa'a ibn Wahb ibn Atik al-Qurazi, and he divorced her three times.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 229–230 (part 2 of 2):

Abdul-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abdul-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, the Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her), that he heard her say: The wife of Rifa'ah al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I was married to Rifa'ah al-Qurazi, and he divorced me, making my divorce final. Then I married after him 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr, but with him is only like the fringe of a garment." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "Do you wish to return to Rifa'ah? No, not until he tastes your honey and you taste his honey."

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in Divorce, chapter: Whoever says to his wife, "You are unlawful to me," 9/371. And Muslim: in Marriage, chapter: A woman divorced three times is not lawful to her former husband until she marries another husband, no. (1433), 2/1055. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/232.]]

It is also narrated that she stayed for as long as Allah willed, then returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My husband has indeed touched me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "You have lied with your first statement, so we will not believe you in the second." So she stayed until the Prophet (ﷺ) passed away. Then she came to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O Successor of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I want to return to my first husband, for my second husband has touched me and divorced me." Abu Bakr said to her: "You saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when you came to him, and he said to you what he said, so do not return to him." When Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) passed away, she came to Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) and said to him the same. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to her: "If you return to him, I will surely stone you."

[[See al-Kafi al-Shaf by Ibn Hajar, p. 20, where he attributes it to Abd al-Razzaq, and in his version it is abridged. / The author, 6/347.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them both for them to return to each other﴾, meaning: if the second husband divorces her after he has had intercourse with her, ﴿there is no blame upon them both﴾, meaning upon the woman and the first husband, ﴿for them to return to each other﴾, meaning by a new marriage contract. ﴿If they think﴾, i.e., they know, and it is said they hope, because no one knows what will occur except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., there will be righteousness and good companionship between them. Mujahid said: its meaning is, if they both know that their marriage is not based on deception, and by deception he meant intended halala (legal tahlil, marrying to make her lawful for the first husband). This is the position of Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq. They said: if a woman divorced three times marries another husband in order to make her lawful for the first husband, the marriage is invalid. A group of scholars held that if the condition is not stipulated in the marriage with the second husband that he will divorce her, then the marriage is valid, and by it the tahlil is achieved, and she is entitled to the bridal payment of her equivalent (mahr al-mithl), except that it is disliked if she intends that.

Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Isma'il al-Tamimi informed us: Abu al-Qasim Hamzah ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi informed us: Abu Ahmad Abdullah ibn Adi al-Hafiz informed us: al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj informed us: Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani informed us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Karim, namely al-Jazari, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Allah has cursed the one who makes lawful (muhallil) and the one for whom it is made lawful (muhallal lahu)."

[[The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud has two chains. The first, from Abu Qays, from Hudhayl ibn Abd al-Rahman, from him, with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Marriage, chapter on what has been related about the muhallil and the muhallal lahu, 4/264, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. Also by al-Nasa'i in Divorce, at length, chapter on making lawful a woman divorced three times and what it contains of severity, 6/149. Also al-Darimi in Marriage, chapter on the prohibition of tahlil, 5/158. Also al-Bayhaqi 7/208, and Ahmad 1/448, 462. The Hafiz said in al-Talkhis 3/170: (Ibn al-Qattan and Ibn Daqiq al-Id authenticated it on the condition of al-Bukhari). The other chain is from Abu al-Wasil, narrated by Ahmad 1/450, 451; Abu al-Wasil is unknown (majhul), as al-Husayni said. The Hafiz mentioned a third chain narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud; this al-Harith is al-A'war al-Kufi, who is weak, and some said he was a liar. It has other chains from Abu Hurayrah, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Jabir ibn Abdullah, Ibn Abbas, and Uqbah ibn Amir, narrated by Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad and others. So the hadith is sahih. See Irwa al-Ghalil 6/307-311.]]

Nafi' said: A man came to Ibn Umar and said to him: "A man divorced his wife three times, and then his brother went without consultation and married her in order to make her lawful for the first husband." He said: "No, unless it is a marriage of desire. We used to count this as fornication (sifah) during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu."

[[Authenticated by al-Hakim on the condition of the two Shaykhs: 2/199.]]

﴿And these are the limits of Allah; He makes them clear to a people who know﴾, meaning: who know what Allah, exalted is He, has commanded them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 229–230 (part 1 of 2):

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾. It is narrated from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "In the beginning, people would divorce without limit or count. A man would divorce his wife, and when she neared the end of her waiting period ('idda), he would take her back, then divorce her again, and then take her back again, intending to harm her. So this verse was revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, meaning that the divorce after which one may take the wife back (raj'a) is twice. If he divorces three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿then either retain her in kindness﴾. It has been said that by "retaining" is meant taking her back after the second divorce. The sounder view is that what is meant is retention after the return: that is, if he has taken her back after the second return, he must retain her in kindness. "Kindness" (al-ma'ruf) is whatever is recognized in the Sharia, including fulfilling the rights of marriage and good companionship. ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾: that he leave her after the divorce until her waiting period ends. It has also been said that this refers to the third divorce.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾. The explicit words by which divorce takes effect without intention are three: "talaq" (divorce), "firaq" (separation), and "sarah" (release). According to Abu Hanifa, the explicit word is only the term "talaq" itself. The general ruling on this is that if a free man divorces his wife one or two times after consummation, he may take her back without her consent as long as she is within the waiting period. If he does not take her back until her waiting period ends, or if he divorces her before consummation, or if she obtains a khul' (divorce through compensation paid by the wife) from him, then she is not lawful to him except by a new marriage with her permission and the permission of her guardian. If he divorces her three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband. As for a slave whose wife is under him, if he divorces her twice, she is not lawful to him except after she marries another husband.

The scholars differed concerning the case where one of the spouses is a slave. Most of them held that the number of divorces is reckoned by the husband's status: a free man has three divorces over his slave wife, while a slave has only two divorces over his free wife. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Divorce is by men and the waiting period is by women," meaning that the husband's status determines the number of divorces, and the wife's status determines the length of the waiting period. This is the view of Uthman, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them all, and Ata, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and it is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. Others held that the reckoning in the number of divorces is by the wife's status, so a slave has three divorces over his free wife, and a free man has only two divorces over his slave wife. This is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri and the Companions of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y).

The words of the Exalted: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾, i.e., what you have given them, ﴿anything﴾, meaning the dowries and other things. Then He made an exception for khul', saying: ﴿unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. It was revealed concerning Jamila, daughter of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa; it is also said: Habiba, daughter of Sahl. She was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and she disliked him while he loved her. There was a quarrel between them, so she went to her father and complained to him about her husband, saying: "He mistreats me and beats me." He said: "Go back to your husband, for I dislike that a woman should keep raising her hands complaining about her husband." She returned to him a second time with marks of the beating on her. He said to her: "Go back to your husband." When she saw that her father would not help her, she went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him about her husband, showing him the marks of his beating on her, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, neither I nor he [can continue]." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for Thabit and said: "What is your matter with your wife?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, there is nobody on the face of the earth more beloved to me than her, except you." He said to her: "What do you say?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he asked her, so she said: "He has spoken the truth, O Messenger of Allah, but I have feared that he will destroy me, so remove me from him." She also said: "O Messenger of Allah, I would not tell you a matter which Allah would reveal to you the opposite of. He is among the most generous of people in his love for his wife, but I dislike him, so neither I nor he [can continue]." Thabit said: "I have given her a garden; let her return it to me, and I will release her." He said to her: "Will you return his garden to him and be free of your matter?" She said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Thabit, take back from her what you gave her and release her." So he did.

Abu Abdullah... [The chain continues:] We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Zahir ibn Jamil informed us, who said: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi informed us, who said: Khalid informed us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the wife of Thabit ibn Qays came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Thabit—I do not blame him for his character or his religion, but I dislike disbelief after Islam." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you return his garden to him?" She said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Accept the garden and divorce her with one divorce."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿unless both fear﴾, i.e., know, ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. Abu Ja'far, Hamza, and Ya'qub read ﴿yakhafa﴾ [in the form ﴿yukhafa﴾] with a dammah on the yā', meaning: this is known about them, i.e., the judge and the guardian know this about the spouses. The evidence for this is the words of the Exalted: ﴿if you fear﴾, which assigns the fear to someone other than the spouses, and He did not say "if they both fear." The others read ﴿yakhafa﴾ with a fatha on the yā', meaning: the spouses know from themselves ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. The wife fears that she will disobey Allah regarding her husband's rights, and the husband fears, if his wife does not obey him, that he will transgress against her. So Allah forbade the man to take anything from his wife of what he had given her, except when the disobedience (nushuz) comes from her side. She then says: "I will not obey you in any command, and I will not let you lie beside me," and similar things.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up therewith﴾, i.e., for what the woman ransoms herself with from him. Al-Farra' said: By His words ﴿upon them﴾ He means the husband only, not the woman, and He mentioned both of them together because they are paired, as in His words ﴿they forgot their fish﴾ (61 - al-Kahf), though it was only the youth of Musa who forgot, not Musa himself. It has also been said that He meant there is no blame on either of them together: there is no blame on the woman for disobedience if she fears destruction and sin, nor for what she ransoms herself with and gives as wealth, because she is forbidden to waste wealth without right; and no blame on the husband for what he takes from her of wealth if she gives it willingly. Most scholars hold that khul' is permissible for more than what he gave her. Al-Zuhri said: It is not permissible for more than what he gave her of the dowry. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: He should not take from her all that he gave her, but should leave some of it. Khul' is permissible in circumstances other than nushuz, but it is disliked, because it entails severing the bond without cause.

We were informed by Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, who said: Abu Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed me, who said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Mustamli informed us, who said: Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Ishaq ibn Shakir ibn Ahmad ibn Khabbab informed us, who said: Isa ibn Yunus informed us, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among the most hated of lawful things to Allah is divorce."

We were informed by Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, who said: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Ubayy informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shayba informed us, who said: Ubayy informed us, who said: Usama informed us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, from Abu Asma al-Rahabi, from Thawban, who traced it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any need, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her."

Tawus said: Khul' is specific to the situation of fear of nushuz, based on the apparent meaning of the verse. The verse came in accordance with the custom, that khul' generally occurs only in a state of fear of nushuz. And if a man divorces his wife with the word of divorce in exchange for property, and she accepts, then the separation (bayna) takes effect and the count of divorces is reduced by it.

The scholars differed concerning khul'. Most of them held that it is an irrevocable single divorce (talaqa ba'ina), by which the count of divorces is reduced. This is the view of Umar, Uthman, Ali, and Ibn Mas'ud, and it is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Ata, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and al-Nakha'i. It is also the position of Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, and the Companions of opinion, and it is the more apparent of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i. Others held that it is a annulment (faskh) by which the count of divorces is not reduced. This is the view of Abdullah ibn Umar and Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and it is the view of Ikrima and Tawus, and it is the position of Ahmad and Ishaq. They argued that Allah the Exalted mentioned divorce twice, then mentioned khul' after it, then mentioned the third divorce after it, saying: ﴿And if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries a husband other than him﴾. If khul' were a divorce, the divorces would be four. Whoever holds the first view takes the third divorce to be ﴿or release her with good treatment﴾.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., these are the commands and prohibitions of Allah. The limits of Allah are what the Sharia prohibits from exceeding. ﴿So do not transgress them﴾, i.e., do not go beyond them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah—it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if he divorces her﴾, meaning the third divorce, ﴿then she is not lawful to him after that﴾, i.e., after the third divorce, ﴿until she marries a husband other than him﴾, i.e., other than the one who divorced her, so that he has intercourse with her. Marriage (nikah) covers both the sexual intercourse and the contract together. It was revealed concerning Tamima. It has also been said concerning Aisha, daughter of Abd al-Rahman ibn Atik al-Qurazi, who was married to her cousin Rifa'a ibn Wahb ibn Atik al-Qurazi, and he divorced her three times.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 229–230 (part 2 of 2):

Abdul-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abdul-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, the Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her), that he heard her say: The wife of Rifa'ah al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I was married to Rifa'ah al-Qurazi, and he divorced me, making my divorce final. Then I married after him 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr, but with him is only like the fringe of a garment." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "Do you wish to return to Rifa'ah? No, not until he tastes your honey and you taste his honey."

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in Divorce, chapter: Whoever says to his wife, "You are unlawful to me," 9/371. And Muslim: in Marriage, chapter: A woman divorced three times is not lawful to her former husband until she marries another husband, no. (1433), 2/1055. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/232.]]

It is also narrated that she stayed for as long as Allah willed, then returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My husband has indeed touched me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "You have lied with your first statement, so we will not believe you in the second." So she stayed until the Prophet (ﷺ) passed away. Then she came to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O Successor of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I want to return to my first husband, for my second husband has touched me and divorced me." Abu Bakr said to her: "You saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when you came to him, and he said to you what he said, so do not return to him." When Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) passed away, she came to Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) and said to him the same. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to her: "If you return to him, I will surely stone you."

[[See al-Kafi al-Shaf by Ibn Hajar, p. 20, where he attributes it to Abd al-Razzaq, and in his version it is abridged. / The author, 6/347.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them both for them to return to each other﴾, meaning: if the second husband divorces her after he has had intercourse with her, ﴿there is no blame upon them both﴾, meaning upon the woman and the first husband, ﴿for them to return to each other﴾, meaning by a new marriage contract. ﴿If they think﴾, i.e., they know, and it is said they hope, because no one knows what will occur except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾, i.e., there will be righteousness and good companionship between them. Mujahid said: its meaning is, if they both know that their marriage is not based on deception, and by deception he meant intended halala (legal tahlil, marrying to make her lawful for the first husband). This is the position of Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq. They said: if a woman divorced three times marries another husband in order to make her lawful for the first husband, the marriage is invalid. A group of scholars held that if the condition is not stipulated in the marriage with the second husband that he will divorce her, then the marriage is valid, and by it the tahlil is achieved, and she is entitled to the bridal payment of her equivalent (mahr al-mithl), except that it is disliked if she intends that.

Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Isma'il al-Tamimi informed us: Abu al-Qasim Hamzah ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi informed us: Abu Ahmad Abdullah ibn Adi al-Hafiz informed us: al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj informed us: Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani informed us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Karim, namely al-Jazari, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Allah has cursed the one who makes lawful (muhallil) and the one for whom it is made lawful (muhallal lahu)."

[[The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud has two chains. The first, from Abu Qays, from Hudhayl ibn Abd al-Rahman, from him, with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Marriage, chapter on what has been related about the muhallil and the muhallal lahu, 4/264, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. Also by al-Nasa'i in Divorce, at length, chapter on making lawful a woman divorced three times and what it contains of severity, 6/149. Also al-Darimi in Marriage, chapter on the prohibition of tahlil, 5/158. Also al-Bayhaqi 7/208, and Ahmad 1/448, 462. The Hafiz said in al-Talkhis 3/170: (Ibn al-Qattan and Ibn Daqiq al-Id authenticated it on the condition of al-Bukhari). The other chain is from Abu al-Wasil, narrated by Ahmad 1/450, 451; Abu al-Wasil is unknown (majhul), as al-Husayni said. The Hafiz mentioned a third chain narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud; this al-Harith is al-A'war al-Kufi, who is weak, and some said he was a liar. It has other chains from Abu Hurayrah, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Jabir ibn Abdullah, Ibn Abbas, and Uqbah ibn Amir, narrated by Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad and others. So the hadith is sahih. See Irwa al-Ghalil 6/307-311.]]

Nafi' said: A man came to Ibn Umar and said to him: "A man divorced his wife three times, and then his brother went without consultation and married her in order to make her lawful for the first husband." He said: "No, unless it is a marriage of desire. We used to count this as fornication (sifah) during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu."

[[Authenticated by al-Hakim on the condition of the two Shaykhs: 2/199.]]

﴿And these are the limits of Allah; He makes them clear to a people who know﴾, meaning: who know what Allah, exalted is He, has commanded them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 231:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When you divorce women and they reach their term﴾ to the end of the verse. It was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar called Thabit ibn Yasar, who divorced his wife, and when her waiting period (iddah) was nearly over he took her back, then divorced her again, intending by that to harm her.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 5/10.]]

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿they reach their term﴾ mean that they were about to finish their waiting period and become free of him. He did not mean the actual completion of the waiting period, because once the waiting period has ended the husband no longer has the right to retain her. So "reaching" here means reaching in the sense of approaching. In His words after this, ﴿when they have reached their term, do not prevent them﴾, it means the actual completion of the waiting period. The word "reach" (balagha) covers both meanings, as one says: "He reached the city" when he drew near to it, and when he entered it.

﴿Then retain them in kindness﴾ means take them back. It has been said that taking them back in kindness is to call witnesses to the return and to take her back by word, not by intercourse.

﴿Or release them in kindness﴾, that is, leave them until their waiting period ends, so that they are more entitled to themselves. ﴿And do not retain them to harm them, so that you transgress﴾, that is, do not intend by the return to harm them by prolonging their confinement. ﴿Whoever does that has certainly wronged himself﴾, that is, he harms himself by opposing the command of Allah the Exalted. ﴿And do not take the signs of Allah in mockery﴾. Al-Kalbi said: this means His words ﴿either retention in kindness or release with good treatment﴾. Everyone who opposes the command of the Sharia takes the signs of Allah in mockery. Abu al-Darda' said: it is that a man would divorce his wife and then say, "I was only joking," and he would free a slave and say the same, and marry and say the same.

Akhbarana Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi: Anaa Abu al-Hasan al-Tays­funi: Akhbarana 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr al-Jawhari: Akhbarana Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani: Akhbarana 'Ali ibn Hujr: Akhbarana Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Abu Habib ibn Ardak, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Mahak, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things are serious whether said in earnest or in jest: divorce, marriage, and taking back (a wife)."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud: Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on divorce in jest, 3/118-119. And al-Tirmidhi: Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on what has come about seriousness and jest in divorce, 4/362, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith. And Ibn Majah: Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on one who divorces, marries, or takes back in jest, no. 2039, 1/658. And al-Hakim: 2/197, and he declared it sahih, and al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan 3/256-257. Its isnad includes 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib ibn Ardak, who is disputed: al-Nasa'i said: munkar al-hadith, while others declared him reliable. The Hafiz said that on this basis it is hasan (Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 4/362). The author cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah 9/219. See al-Talkhis al-Habir 3/207 and Irwa' al-Ghalil 6/224-228.]]

﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾, by faith, ﴿and what He has sent down to you of the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and the wisdom﴾, meaning the Sunnah. It has also been said that the wisdom means the admonitions of the Qur'an. ﴿He admonishes you thereby. And fear Allah, and know that Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 232:

﴿When you divorce women and they reach their term﴾ It was revealed concerning Jumayla bint Yasar, sister of Ma'qil ibn Yasar al-Muzani. She was married to Abu al-Baddah, Asim ibn Adi ibn Ajlan, and he divorced her.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ahmad ibn Abi Amr informed us: my father related to me: Ibrahim related to me, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: Ma'qil ibn Yasar related to me, who said: I gave my sister in marriage to a man, and he divorced her. When her waiting period (iddah) had ended, he came proposing to her. I said to him: "I married you to her, I furnished her for you, and I honoured you, and you divorced her, then you came proposing to her? No, by Allah, she will never return to you." He was a man with no fault, and the woman wished to return to him. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾. I said: "Now I will do it, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "So I married her to him."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Nikah, chapter "Whoever says: there is no marriage except with a guardian": 9/183, and in al-Tafsir: 8/192.]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then they reach their term﴾, meaning their waiting period has ended. ﴿So do not prevent them﴾, meaning do not hinder them from marrying ﴿their husbands﴾. Al-'adl (prevention) is holding back; its root meaning is constriction and hardship. It is said: "the woman was 'adulat" when her child became stuck in her womb and its exit was constricted for it; and "al-da' al-'udal" (the incurable disease) is one that cannot be borne. In the verse there is evidence that a woman does not conduct the contract of marriage herself, for if she possessed that right there would be no prevention, and the prohibition addressed to the guardian against preventing would have no meaning. It is also said the verse is addressed to the husbands, to prevent them from harming (the wives), because the beginning of the verse is addressed to them. The first view is more sound.

﴿when they agree among themselves in a proper manner﴾, with a lawful contract and a permissible dowry. ﴿That﴾, meaning that which was mentioned of the prohibition, ﴿is admonished by it whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. He said "that" in the singular, while the address is to the guardians, because the original form for addressing a group is "dhalikum"; then it became common until people imagined the kaf was part of the word itself and not a kaf of address, so they said "dhalika." When they say this, the kaf is fixed in one form for the dual, plural, feminine and masculine. It is said it is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and therefore he used the singular; then he returned to addressing the believers and said ﴿That is more purifying for you﴾, meaning better for you ﴿and purer﴾ for your hearts from doubt. That is because, if there is in the soul of each of them a bond of love, one is not safe from it extending to what Allah has not made lawful for them both, and the guardians cannot be sure that suspicion about them might not arise in their hearts, though they may be innocent of that, so that they would sin. ﴿And Allah knows while you do not know﴾, meaning He knows the love of each of them for the other, which you do not know.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And the mothers shall suckle their children﴾. That is, the divorced women who have children by their husbands shall suckle them. It is a statement with the meaning of a command, and it is a command of recommendation (istihbab, "recommended") rather than a command of obligation (ijab, "obligatory"), because it is not obligatory upon them to nurse the child if there is someone else who can nurse it. This is based on His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Talaq: ﴿And if they suckle for you, then give them their wages﴾ (65:6). If the mother desires to nurse, she has more right to it than others. ﴿For two full years﴾, that is, two years. Mention of "full" is for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿That is ten complete﴾ (2:196). It has also been said that He said "full two years" because the Arabs sometimes call part of a year a year and part of a month a month, as Allah the Almighty said: ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾ (2:197), when it is really two months and part of a third. And He said: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him﴾ (2:203), when one only hastens within a day and part of a day. It is also said that so-and-so resided in such-and-such a place for two years, when he only resided there for a year and part of another. So Allah the Almighty clarified that they are two complete years, twenty-four months.

The scholars differed regarding this limit. Some said it is a limit for some infants. Ikrimah related from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that if the mother gave birth after six months, she suckles him for two full years; if she gave birth after seven months, she suckles him for twenty-three months; if she gave birth after nine months, she suckles him for twenty-one months; and if she gave birth after ten months, she suckles him for twenty months. All of this completes thirty months, based on His saying: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning are thirty months﴾ (46:15).

Others said it is a limit for every infant, whenever he is born, that his nursing must not be less than two years, except by agreement of both parents. Whichever of them wishes to wean him before the completion of the two years does not have that right unless they both agree to it, based on His saying: ﴿But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation﴾. This is the view of Ibn Jurayj, al-Thawri, and a narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).

It has also been said: the purpose of the verse is to clarify that the nursing by which the prohibition of marriage (hurmah) is established is that which occurs within the two years, so what occurs after the two years does not create prohibition. Qatadah said: Allah obligated upon mothers nursing for two full years, then He revealed a concession, saying: ﴿For whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾. That is, this is the end of the nursing period, and there is no fixed limit below that; rather it depends on what is suitable for the child and what sustains him.

﴿And upon the one to whom the child belongs﴾, meaning the father, ﴿is their provision﴾, their food, ﴿and their clothing﴾, their clothes, ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, that is, according to one's means. ﴿No soul is burdened except according to its capacity﴾, that is, its ability. ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read it with a raised (damma) rā', coordinating it with His saying ﴿is not burdened﴾. Its original form is tudārir, and the first rā' was assimilated into the second rā'. The others read tudārra with a fatha on the rā', and said: when the rā' was assimilated into the rā', it was given the lightest vowel, which is the fatha. The meaning of the verse, ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾, is that the child is taken from her and given to another after she has agreed to nurse him. ﴿Nor a father through his child﴾, that is, the mother should not abandon him to his father after he has become attached to her, harming him by that. It has also been said that its meaning is: ﴿No mother shall be harmed﴾ by being forced to nurse him when she dislikes nursing him, and the child accepts another woman's milk, because that is not obligatory upon her. ﴿Nor a father through his child﴾, so it is possible that the mother is given more than what is due to her if the child will not take milk from anyone else.

According to these two views, the original form of the word is lā tuḍārir, with a fatha on the first rā', as a passive verb, and "the mother" and "the one to whom the child belongs" are the two objects. It is also possible that the verb belongs to them both, and tuḍārra means tuḍārir with a kasra on the first rā', as an active verb. The meaning would then be: ﴿No mother shall be harmed﴾ by refusing to nurse her child in order to trouble his father, ﴿nor a father﴾, that is, the father should not harm the child's mother by taking him from her and preventing her from nursing him. According to these views, the harm returns to the two parents, each harming the other because of the child. It is also possible that the harm returns to the child, meaning that neither of them should harm the child: so the mother does not nurse him until he dies, or the father does not provide for him, or he takes him from the mother to the point of harming the child. In this case the bā' is extra (ziyadah), and the meaning is: ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾, and no father through his child. All of these opinions have been transmitted from the exegetes.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾. The scholars differed concerning this "heir". Some said: it is the heir of the child, meaning: upon the heir of the child, if the child dies and has property, the one who inherits it bears the like of what was upon his father during his lifetime. Then they differed as to which of the heirs is meant. Some said: it is the child's agnatic relatives (asabah) among the men, such as the grandfather, the brother, the nephew, the paternal uncle, and the paternal uncle's son. This is the view of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and Ibrahim, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Ata' said likewise, and it is the position of Sufyan. They said: if the child has no means to be provided for, his agnatic heirs are compelled to have him nursed. It was also said: it is the child's heir, whether a man or a woman. This is the view of Qatadah and Ibn Abi Layla, and the position of Ahmad and Ishaq. They said: every heir is compelled to provide for him in proportion to his inheritance, whether agnatic or otherwise.

Some said: it is whoever is a mahram relative among the child's heirs. As for a non-mahram, such as the paternal uncle's son or a client (mawla), he is not meant by the verse. This is the view of Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him). A group held that the heir meant is the child himself, who is the heir of his deceased father; the cost of his nursing and his maintenance is from his own property, and if he has no property, then it falls upon the mother. Only the two parents are compelled to maintain a child. This is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on them both). It has also been said: it is the surviving one of the child's two parents after the death of the other, who bears the like of what was upon the father: the wage for nursing, maintenance, and clothing.

It has also been said: the meaning is not maintenance; rather, the meaning is: upon the heir is abstaining from harm. This was said by al-Sha'bi and al-Zuhri. ﴿But if they both desire﴾, meaning the two parents, ﴿weaning﴾, that is, weaning before the two years, ﴿by mutual consent﴾, that is, agreement of the two parents, ﴿and consultation﴾, that is, they consult the people of knowledge about it until they are informed that weaning at that time does not harm the child. Consultation is the drawing out of an opinion. ﴿Then there is no blame upon them﴾, that is, there is no sin upon them for weaning before the two years. ﴿And if you wish to have your children nursed﴾, that is, to find wet nurses for your children other than their mothers, if their mothers refuse to nurse them, or are unable due to some impediment in them, such as the cessation of milk, or they wish to marry. ﴿Then there is no blame upon you if you pay﴾ to their mothers ﴿what you have given﴾, what you have named for them as the wage for nursing in proportion to what they nursed. It has also been said: if you pay the nurses' wages to them in a reasonable manner. Ibn Kathir read ﴿mā ātaytum﴾ and in Surat al-Rum ﴿And what you give in usury﴾ (30:39) with a shortened alif, and its meaning is "what you do." One says "ataytu jamīlan" when one has done a good deed. According to this reading, the word "payment" (taslīm) means obedience and submission, not the payment of the wage; that is, if you submit to His command and comply with His judgment. It has also been said: if you hand over for nursing by mutual consent and agreement, without harm. ﴿And fear Allah, and know that Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ [39a]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 2, verse 234:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾ means those who die, and whose terms (ājāl) are fulfilled. Tawaffā (to be taken in full) and istawfā (to receive in full) have one meaning, and the meaning of tawaffī is taking a thing in full. ﴿And leave wives behind﴾ means they leave wives. ﴿Let them wait﴾ means let them refrain, ﴿with themselves for four months and ten days﴾ means they must observe the 'idda (waiting period) for this duration by abstaining from adornment, perfume, and moving out upon separation from their husbands. Except if they are pregnant, in which case their 'idda ends with the delivery of the child. The 'idda for death was initially a full year, based on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, let them bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without expulsion﴾ (240 al-Baqarah). Then it was abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later one) by four months and ten days.

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: This 'idda, that is four months and ten days, was obligatory in the household of her husband. Then God revealed ﴿a provision for a year﴾, so He granted her the full year, seven months and twenty nights, as a bequest. If she wished, she could remain in the household as part of the bequest, and if she wished, she could leave. This is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿without expulsion. But if they leave, there is no blame upon you for what they do﴾ (240 al-Baqarah). So the 'idda remains as it is, obligatory upon her.

And ʿAṭāʾ said: Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: This verse abrogated her 'idda in the household of her husband, and she was to remain in her bequest, and if she wished, she could leave. ʿAṭāʾ said: Then the inheritance came and abrogated the residence (suknā), so she observes her 'idda wherever she wishes, and she has no right to residence. It is obligatory upon her to observe ihdād (mourning) during the 'idda for death, which means she must refrain from adornment and perfume. It is not permissible for her to oil her head with any oil, whether or not it contains perfume. She may oil her body with oil that contains no perfume, but if it contains perfume it is not permissible. She may not apply kohl that contains perfume or that is decorative, such as black kohl. There is no harm in Persian kohl that has no adornment. If she is compelled to use kohl containing adornment, many scholars permitted it, among them Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, Sulayman ibn Yasar, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Nakhaʿi. Malik and the proponents of personal opinion (ashāb al-ra'y) also held this view. Al-Shafiʿi, may God have mercy on him, said: She may apply it at night and wipe it off during the day.

Umm Salamah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon me when Abu Salamah had died, and I had applied aloe (ṣabr) to myself. He said: "It beautifies the face, so do not apply it except at night, and remove it during the day." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Talaq, chapter: What the woman observing 'idda should avoid during her 'idda, 3/201-202. And al-Nasa'i in al-Talaq, chapter: The concession for the mourning woman to comb her hair with lote-tree leaves, 6/204.]]

It is not permissible for her to dye (her hair or hands) with henna, or to wear embroidered silk, brocade, or jewelry. She may wear white garments, wool, and fur. She must not wear garments dyed for adornment, such as bright red, bright green, or yellow. Garments dyed for other than adornment, such as black and dark blue, are permitted. Sufyan said: She must not wear dyed garments under any circumstances.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr Muhammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Hazm, from Humayd ibn Nafi', from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, that she informed him of these three hadiths. Zaynab said: I entered upon Umm Habibah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when her father Abu Sufyan ibn Harb had died. Umm Habibah called for perfume containing yellowness, either khaluq or something else, and she applied it to a young slave girl, then touched her own belly with it. Then she said: By God, I have no need of perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say on the pulpit: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn over a dead person for more than three nights, except for a husband, for four months and ten days." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Talaq, chapter: The mourning of a widow for her husband for four months and ten days, 9/484, and in al-Janaiz. And Muslim in al-Talaq, chapter: The obligation of ihdad, no. (1486), 2/1124. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/306-307.]]

Zaynab also said: Then I entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh when her brother ʿAbd Allah had died, and she called for perfume and touched herself with it. Then she said: By God, I have no need of perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say on the pulpit: "It is not lawful for a woman to mourn over a dead person for more than three nights, except for a husband, for four months and ten days." Zaynab said: And my mother, Umm Salamah, heard this, saying:

A woman came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: O Messenger of God, my daughter's husband has died, and her eye has become sore. May I apply kohl to it? The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No." Then he said: "It is only four months and ten days. In the Jahiliyyah, one of you would throw a dung-pellet at the end of the year." [[A portion of the previous hadith.]] Humayd said: I asked Zaynab: What is this throwing of a dung-pellet at the end of the year? Zaynab said: When a woman's husband died, she would enter a hafsh (a small, humble room; the word means a small, cramped, low-roofed dwelling, named for its narrowness), that is, a small house, and she wore her worst clothes and touched no perfume or anything else until a year had passed over her. Then an animal would be brought to her, a donkey, a sheep, or a bird, and she would rub herself against it. She rarely rubbed herself against anything without it dying. Then she would come out and be given a dung-pellet, which she would throw, and afterward she could use whatever perfume or other things she wished. Malik said: Yaftaḍḍu means she wipes her skin.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: The wisdom behind this period is that during it the soul is breathed into the child. It is said that the child moves (yartakiḍu) in the womb at about half the period of pregnancy. Four months and ten days is about half the period of pregnancy. He said "ʿashran" (ten) in the feminine form because he meant nights, since when the Arabs leave the number unspecified between nights and days, they give precedence to the nights, saying "ṣumnā ʿashran" (we fasted ten), though fasting only occurs during the day.

Al-Mubarrad said: He made the word "ʿashr" feminine because he meant periods (mudad), that is ten periods, each period being a day and a night.

If the widow is pregnant, her 'idda ends with the delivery of the child, according to the majority of scholars from among the Companions and those after them. It is also reported from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them, that she waits for the later of the two terms: delivery of the child or four months and ten days.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, said: Surat al-Nisa' al-Qusra (the short one) was revealed after al-Tula (the long one). By al-Qusra he meant Surat al-Talaq: ﴿And for those with children, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ (4 al-Talaq). It was revealed after His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿let them wait with themselves for four months and ten days﴾ in Surat al-Baqarah, so he interpreted it as abrogation (naskh). Most jurists restricted the verse by the hadith of Subay'ah. This is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, that Subay'ah gave birth a few nights after her husband's death. She came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and asked his permission to marry, and he permitted her, and she married. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Talaq, chapter: "And for those with children, their term is until they deliver their burden," 9/469. And Muslim in al-Talaq, chapter: The end of the 'idda of a widow and others is by delivery of the child, no. (1485), 2/1123.]]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾, that is, when their 'idda has ended, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾ is addressed to the guardians (awliyā'), ﴿for what they do with themselves﴾, that is, of choosing husbands without a marriage contract, since the contract belongs to the guardian. It is also said it means what they do of adorning themselves for men, an adornment that the Shari'ah does not disapprove, ﴿in a reasonable manner. And God is Acquainted with what you do﴾.

Ihdad is obligatory upon the woman during the 'idda for death. As for a woman in 'idda after divorce, one must consider: if it is a revocable divorce (raj'iyyah), there is no ihdad upon her during the 'idda, because she may adorn herself to attract her husband's heart so that he will take her back. As for a woman divorced irrevocably (bā'innah) by khul' (divorce by the wife's request) or by three divorces, there are two opinions. The first is that ihdad is obligatory upon her as it is upon a widow; this is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and Abu Hanifah also held it. The second is that there is no ihdad upon her; this is the view of ʿAṭāʾ, and Malik also held it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 235:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon you for what you imply in your proposal to women﴾, meaning women in their waiting period (iddah). The root of ta'rid (allusion, indirect speech) is hinting at something (talwih bi'l-shay'). Ta'rid in speech is that by which the listener understands the speaker's intent without explicit statement. Allusive proposal (ta'rid bi'l-khitbah) is permissible during the waiting period, and it is that one says: "Many a man desires you; who would find one like you? Indeed you are beautiful; indeed you are righteous; indeed you are dear to me; indeed I am desirous of you; indeed among my aims is to marry, and if Allah brings us together in what is lawful, it would please me; and if I marry you, I will surely treat you well," and similar speech, without saying "Marry me." The woman may answer him in kind if she is inclined to him. Ibrahim said: There is no harm in his sending her a gift and attending to her affairs during the waiting period, if that is his custom.

It is narrated that Sukayna bint Handhalah was divorced from her husband, and Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir entered upon her during her waiting period and said: "O daughter of Handhalah, you know my kinship to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the right of my grandfather over me, and my precedence in Islam." Sukayna said: "Are you proposing to me while I am in my waiting period, and you are one from whom knowledge is taken?" He said: "I only informed you of my kinship to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon Umm Salamah while she was in the waiting period of her husband Abu Salamah, and he mentioned to her his station with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, while he was leaning heavily on his hand, so much that the mat left its mark on his hand from the intensity of his leaning on it." [Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in the Book of Marriage; al-Daraqutni reported it from the narration of Muhammad ibn al-Salt from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, who is Ibn al-Ghasil. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf by Ibn Hajar, p. 21.]

Allusive proposal is permissible in the waiting period of death. As for the woman in the waiting period following separation while alive, it is examined: if she is one whom the man who separated from her may not marry again, such as a woman divorced three times, or one separated by li'an or by fosterage, then it is permissible to propose to her allusively. If she is one whom the husband may marry, such as a woman divorced by khul' or a woman whose marriage was annulled, it is permissible for her husband to propose to her both allusively and explicitly.

Is it permissible for another man to propose allusively? There are two opinions: the first is that it is permissible, like the woman divorced three times; the second is that it is not permissible, because the resumption of relations with the woman in her waiting period is like one who has a revocable divorce, and it is not permissible for another to propose to her allusively.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿of proposal to women﴾. Khitbah is seeking marriage, and it is the verbal noun of "khataba al-rajulu al-mara'ah, yakhtubu khitbah" (the man proposed to the woman). Al-Akhfash said: khitbah means mention (dhikr), and khutbah means the tashahhud (the recitation of testimony), so its meaning would be: concerning what you allude to of mentioning women in their presence. ﴿Or you conceal﴾, that is, you hold secretly ﴿in yourselves﴾ their marriage. It is said: akantu al-shay' and kantuhu are two dialects (for "I concealed the thing"). Tha'lab said: akantu al-shay' means I hid it within myself, and kantuhu means I covered it. Al-Suddi said: it is that he enters, greets, and gives a gift if he wishes, and says nothing. ﴿Allah knows that you will remember them﴾ in your hearts, ﴿but do not make promises to them in secret﴾. They differed concerning the secret that is forbidden. A group said it is adultery: a man would enter upon a woman for the sake of fornication while alluding to marriage, saying to her: "Wait for me; when you complete your waiting period, I will make my marriage to you public." This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibrahim, Ata', and a report of Atiyyah from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it means that he should not marry her secretly and keep her, and when she is free, he publicizes it.

Mujahid said: it is the man's saying, "Do not escape me by yourself, for I will marry you." Al-Sha'bi and al-Suddi said: it is taking her pledge that she will not marry anyone else. Ikrimah said: he should not marry her or propose to her during the waiting period.

Al-Shafi'i said: the secret is intercourse. Al-Kalbi said: that is, do not describe yourselves to them with frequent intercourse, so that one says: "I will come to you four or five times," and similar things. "Secret" is used to mean intercourse; Imru' al-Qays said:

"Did not Basbasa's people claim that I have grown old, and that men like me do not do well at the secret (intercourse)?"

Adultery and intercourse are called "secret" because they occur in concealment between a man and a woman.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except that you say a fitting word﴾, meaning what we have mentioned of allusive proposal.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not resolve upon the tie of marriage until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾, meaning: do not firmly resolve upon the contract of marriage during the waiting period until the prescribed period (kitab) reaches its term, that is, until the waiting period is completed. Allah called it "kitab" because it is an obligation from Allah, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Fasting is prescribed for you﴾, meaning obligated upon you. ﴿And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him﴾, meaning fear Allah. ﴿And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾, who does not hasten punishment.

Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on surah 2, verse 236:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or specified for them a bridal gift﴾. That is, *and you have not touched them and have not specified*. It was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who married a woman from Banu Hanifa and did not specify a dower (*mahr*) for her, then divorced her before he had consummated the marriage. So this verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Give her a provision, even if it is with your cap."¹

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ma lam tamassuhunna﴾ with an alif here, and in (surah al-Ahzab) in the form of *mufa'alah* (mutual action), because the body of each of the two meets the body of the other, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿before they touch one another﴾ (58:3). The rest read ﴿tamassuhunna﴾ without an alif, because the act of intercourse (*ghishyan*) is done by the man. Its proof is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿No human has touched me﴾ (3:47).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿or you specify for them a bridal gift﴾, that is, you make a dower (*sadaq*) obligatory for them. If it is asked: what is the reason for removing blame from the one who divorces? It is said: divorce cuts off the cause of the bond. A hadith says: "The most hated of lawful things to Allah the Exalted is divorce."² So He removed blame from him when separation is better than keeping the wife. It is also said that the meaning is: there is no claim (*sabil*) for the women against you if you divorce them before touching and before specifying a dower or maintenance.
