It is also said: there is no blame upon you for divorcing them before touching at whatever time you wish, whether the woman is menstruating or in a state of purity, because there is neither *sunnah* (the prescribed way) nor *bid'ah* (innovation) in divorcing them before consummation, unlike one with whom intercourse has taken place, for it is not permissible to divorce her while she is menstruating. ﴿And provide for them﴾, that is, give them from your wealth what they may enjoy. *Mut'ah* and *mata'* are what one takes as provision for the journey. ﴿According to the wealthy﴾, that is, the rich man, ﴿his means﴾, and ﴿according to the straitened﴾, that is, the poor man, ﴿his means﴾, that is, according to his ability and capacity. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read *qadarahu* with a fatha on the *dal* in both places, while the others read it with a sukun on both. Both are dialectal forms. It is also said that *qadr* with a sukun is the verbal noun (*masdar*), and with a fatha it is the noun (*ism*). *Mata'an* is in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning: provide for them. ﴿A provision in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, that is, in accordance with what Allah has commanded you, without oppression. ﴿A duty upon the good-doers﴾.

The ruling of the verse is that whoever marries a woman without specifying a dower for her and then divorces her before consummation, she is owed *mut'ah* by unanimous agreement. If he divorces her after a dower has been specified but before consummation, then according to the majority she has no *mut'ah*, and she has half of the specified dower.

Scholars differ concerning a divorced woman after consummation. One group held that she has no *mut'ah*, because she is entitled to the dower; this is the view of the people of opinion (*ashab al-ra'y*). Another group held that she is entitled to *mut'ah*, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And for divorced women is provision according to what is reasonable﴾ (2:241). This is the view of Abdullah ibn Umar, and it was also said by 'Ata', Mujahid and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and al-Shafi'i adopted it, because her entitlement to the dower is in return for what was lost to her of the benefit of intimacy; so she has *mut'ah* as compensation for the distress of separation. According to the first view, there is *mut'ah* only for one woman, the one divorced before the specifying of a dower and before consummation. According to the second view, every divorced woman has *mut'ah* except one, the one for whom a dower was specified before consummation. Abdullah ibn Umar said: every divorced woman has *mut'ah* except the one for whom a dower was specified and whom her husband did not touch; for her, half the dower suffices.

Al-Zuhri said: there are two kinds of *mut'ah*: the authority (*sultan*) enforces one of them, and does not enforce the other, but it is binding upon him between himself and Allah the Exalted.

As for the one that the authority enforces, it is the woman divorced before specifying and before consummation, and this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿a duty upon the good-doers﴾. The one that is binding upon him between himself and Allah the Exalted, but which the authority does not enforce, is the woman divorced after consummation, and this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿a duty upon the God-fearing﴾ (2:241).

Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr held that every divorced woman has *mut'ah*, whether it was before specifying and consummation or after specifying and before consummation, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And for divorced women is provision according to what is reasonable﴾ (2:241), and on His saying in surah al-Ahzab: ﴿So provide for them and release them with a fair release﴾ (33:49). The two said that the meaning of the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or specified for them a bridal gift﴾ is: *or you have not specified for them a bridal gift*. Some said: *mut'ah* is not obligatory; the command to give it is a command of recommendation and desirability.

It is narrated that a man divorced his wife after he had consummated the marriage, and she brought her case to Shurayh concerning *mut'ah*. Shurayh said: "Do not refuse to be among the good-doers, and do not refuse to be among the God-fearing." He did not compel him to do so.

They differed concerning the amount of *mut'ah*. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: the highest of it is a servant, the middle of it is three garments (a shirt, a head-covering and a wrapper), and less than that is a protective garment or some silver. This was also said by al-Sha'bi and al-Zuhri, and it is the school of al-Shafi'i, who said: the highest of it, for the wealthy, is a servant; the middle of it is a garment; and the least of it is the least that has a value, and the good amount is thirty dirhams. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf divorced his wife and gave her a black slave-girl as *mut'ah* (*hammaha*, that is, he provided for her). Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, gave a wife of his ten thousand dirhams as *mut'ah*, and she said: "A little provision from a beloved who is parting."

Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: its limit, when the spouses disagree, is half the dower of her equivalent (*mahr mithl*), which must not be exceeded. The verse indicates that the husband's circumstances, whether in hardship or ease, are taken into account.

Among the rulings of the verse: whoever marries an adult woman with her consent without a dower, the marriage is valid, and the woman has the right to demand that he specify a dower for her. If he consummates the marriage before a dower is specified, she is owed the dower of her equivalent. If he divorces her before a dower is specified and before consummation, she is owed *mut'ah*. If one of the two dies before a dower is specified and before consummation, the scholars differ as to whether she is entitled to the dower. One group held that she has no dower, and this is the view of 'Ali, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Umar and Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, just as if he had divorced her before specifying and consummation. Another group held that she is owed the dower, because death is like consummation in confirming the named dower, and likewise in requiring the dower of her equivalent when there was no named dower in the contract. This is the view of al-Thawri and the people of opinion. They argued with what is reported from 'Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he was asked about a man who married a woman, did not specify a dower for her, did not consummate the marriage, and then died. Ibn Mas'ud said: "She has the dower of women like her, without deficiency and without excess, she must observe the waiting period, and she has inheritance." Ma'qil ibn Sinan al-Ashja'i stood up and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled concerning Bar'a bint Washiq, a woman from among us, in the same way as you have ruled," and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, rejoiced at this.³

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: if the hadith of Bar'a bint Washiq is established, then no one's opinion is a proof against the word of the Prophet ﷺ. If it is not established, then she has no dower, and she has inheritance. 'Ali used to say, concerning the hadith of Bar'a: the word of a Bedouin from Ashja' is not accepted against the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 237:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, but you have already specified for them a dower, then half of what you have specified⁠﴾. This refers to a divorced woman after the dower has been fixed and before consummation (al-masis). For her is half of the dower specified. And if one of them dies before consummation, then she is entitled to the full specified dower. The meaning of "touching" (al-mass) mentioned in the verse is intercourse (al-jima'). The scholars differed regarding the case where a man is alone with his wife and then divorces her before he has consummated the marriage. One group held that she is owed only half the dowry (al-sadaq), and no waiting period ('idda) is incumbent upon her, because Allah Exalted required, upon divorce before consummation, half the dower, and did not require a waiting period. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn Mas'ud, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

Another group said: she is owed the full dower, and a waiting period is incumbent upon her, based on what has been reported from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "When the curtains are drawn, the dowry becomes due." Similar was reported from Zayd ibn Thabit. Some of them interpreted the statement of 'Umar as referring to the obligation to hand over the dowry to her when she has surrendered herself, not to the determination of the dowry's amount. It was also said that this verse abrogates the verse in Surat al-Ahzab: ﴿So for you there is no waiting period on them that you should count; so provide for them⁠﴾ (33:49). Thus a woman divorced before consummation had a provision (mata'), and it was abrogated by this verse, which required for the divorced woman whose dower had been specified before consummation half of the specified dower, and there is no provision for her.

And His saying: ﴿and you have already specified for them a dower⁠﴾, that is, you have named for them a dower. ﴿then half of what you have specified⁠﴾, that is, for her is half of the named dower. ﴿unless they forgo⁠﴾, meaning the women, that is, unless the woman gives up her share, whereupon the entire dowry returns to the husband.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should forgo⁠﴾. The scholars differed concerning this. Some held that the one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the guardian (wali), and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him. The meaning: unless the woman forgoes by giving up her share to the husband, if she is a thayyib (previously married) woman who is of those entitled to forgo; or her guardian forgoes and gives up her share, if the woman is a virgin (bikr) or not permitted to manage her own affairs, so that her guardian's forgoing is valid. This is the view of 'Alqama, 'Ata', al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and Rabi'a. Others held that the guardian's forgoing is valid only when the woman is a virgin; if she is a thayyib, her guardian's forgoing is not valid. And some said: the one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the husband, and this is the view of 'Ali, and it was also the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Shurayh, Mujahid and Qatada. They said: it is not permissible for her guardian to give up any part of the dowry, whether she is a virgin or a thayyib, just as it is not permissible for him to do so before divorce by agreement, and just as it is not permissible for him to give away any of her property. They said: the meaning of the verse is: unless the woman forgoes her share, whereupon the entire dowry returns to the husband, or the husband forgoes his share, whereupon she receives the entire dowry. According to this interpretation, the verse means: the one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the one who holds the marriage of himself in every case, before or after divorce. ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to righteousness⁠﴾: its position is nominative as the subject (mubtada'), meaning: so forgoing is nearer to righteousness, that is, to piety. The address is to men and women together, because when the masculine and feminine are combined, the masculine takes precedence; the meaning is: the forgiveness of some of you toward others is nearer to righteousness. ﴿And do not forget graciousness among yourselves⁠﴾, that is, the bounty of some of you toward others, by the man giving the full dowry or the woman giving up her share. He urged both of them toward doing good. ﴿Indeed Allah is Seer of what you do⁠﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 238–239:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, meaning: be constant and persistent in the obligatory prayers, at their appointed times, within their limits, and in completing their pillars. Then He singled out the middle prayer from among them for special guarding, as an indication of its excellence. "Al-wusta" is the feminine of "al-awsat," and the middle (wasat) of a thing is its best and most balanced part. The scholars among the Companions and those after them differed concerning the middle prayer. Some said it is the Fajr prayer, and this is the view of ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, Muʿadh and Jabir. ʿAta', ʿIkrimah and Mujahid also said so, and Malik and al-Shafiʿi inclined to it, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And stand before Allah in devout obedience﴾, and qunut means prolonged standing, and the Subh prayer is specifically characterized by prolonged standing and qunut. Moreover, Allah, exalted is He, singled it out from among the prayers in another verse, saying: ﴿And the recitation of the dawn; indeed, the recitation of the dawn is ever witnessed﴾ (17:78), meaning it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, so it is recorded in the register of the night and the register of the day. And because it lies between two prayers that are combined, and it is neither shortened nor combined with another.

Others held that it is the Zuhr prayer, and this is the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri and Usamah ibn Zayd, because it falls in the middle of the day, and it is the longest of the daytime prayers in length.

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz informed us: Abu al-Qasim ibn Jaʿfar al-Hashimi informed us: Abu ʿAli al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna informed us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us: Shuʿbah informed me: ʿAmr ibn Abi Hakim said: I heard al-Zibriqan narrate from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Zuhr at the time of the intense heat, and he did not pray any prayer that was more difficult for the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ than it. So this verse was revealed: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾. [Narrated by Imam Ahmad from Zayd ibn Thabit (5/183); Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Salat, Bab Waqt al-ʿAsr (1/240); al-Tahawi in Sharh Maʿani al-Athar (1/167); al-Tabari in his Tafsir (5/206); al-Bayhaqi (1/458). al-Suyuti also attributed it to al-Bukhari in his al-Tarikh al-Kabir, Abu Yaʿla and al-Tabarani; see al-Durr al-Manthur (1/720) and Tafsir al-Tabari, edited by Mahmud Shakir (5/207).]

Most scholars held that it is the ʿAsr prayer. This was narrated by a group from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it is the view of ʿAli, ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, Abu Ayyub, Abu Hurayrah and ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them all. Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Qatadah and al-Hasan also said so.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Musʿab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from al-Qaʿqaʿ ibn Hakim, from Abu Yunus, the freedman of ʿA'ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: ʿA'ishah ordered me to write a mushaf for her, and said: "When you reach this verse, inform me: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾." When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer "ṣalat al-ʿaṣr"﴾ ﴿and stand before Allah in devout obedience﴾. [Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Masajid, Bab: The proof for the one who says the middle prayer is the ʿAsr prayer, no. 629 (1/437); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (2/232).] ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," and from Hafsah similar to that.

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Abu Nuʿaym informed us: Sufyan informed us, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: We said to ʿUbaydah, "Ask ʿAli about the middle prayer." So he asked him, and he said: "We used to think it was the Fajr prayer, until I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the day of the Trench: 'They have kept us busy from the middle prayer, the ʿAsr prayer. May Allah fill their bellies and their graves with fire.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir Surat al-Baqarah, Bab: "Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer," (8/195); Muslim in Kitab al-Masajid, Bab: The proof for the one who says the middle prayer is the ʿAsr prayer, no. 627 (1/436); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (2/233–234).] Also, it is a prayer of the daytime and a prayer that is part of the night's two sides, and the Prophet ﷺ singled it out with emphasis.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us: Hisham informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Malih, who said: We were with Buraydah on a campaign on a cloudy day, and he said: "Hasten the ʿAsr prayer, for the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever abandons the ʿAsr prayer, his deeds are nullified.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Mawaqit, Bab: Whoever abandons the ʿAsr (2/31), and Bab: Hastening the prayer on a cloudy day; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (2/213–237).]

Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb said: It is the Maghrib prayer, because it is a middle prayer, being neither the fewest nor the most in rak'ahs. No one from the earlier generation (al-salaf) is reported to have said that it is the ʿIsha prayer; rather, some later scholars mentioned it, because it lies between two prayers that are not shortened. Some of them said: it is one of the five prayers, unspecified, which Allah, exalted is He, left unnamed to urge the servants to guard the performance of all of them, just as He concealed the Night of Decree in Ramadan, the hour of answered supplication on Friday, and the Greatest Name among the names, so that they would guard all of them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And stand before Allah in devout obedience﴾, meaning: obedient. Al-Sha'bi, ʿAta', Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Tawus said: qunut is obedience. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿A nation devoutly obedient﴾ (16:120), meaning obedient.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: every religious community has a prayer in which they stand in disobedience; so stand, you, before Allah in your prayer, in obedience. It was also said: qunut is silence regarding what it is not permissible to speak during the prayer.

Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Mani' informed us: Hushaym informed us: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from al-Harith ibn Shubayl, from Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "We used to speak behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the prayer; a man among us would speak to his companion beside him, until this verse was revealed: ﴿And stand before Allah in devout obedience﴾. So we were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-ʿAmal fi al-Salah, Bab: What is forbidden of speech in prayer (3/73), and in Tafsir; and Muslim in Kitab al-Masajid, Bab: The prohibition of speech in prayer and the abrogation of what was permitted, no. 539 (1/383).]

Mujahid said: "devoutly humble." He said: qunut includes prolonged bowing, lowering the gaze, stillness, and lowering the wing. The scholars, when one of them stood to pray, would be in awe of the Most Merciful, so that he would not turn, nor move pebbles, nor play with anything, nor let his mind dwell on any worldly matter, except forgetfully. It was also said: the intended meaning of qunut is prolonged standing.

Abu ʿUthman al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Ibn Abi ʿUmar informed us: Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Which prayer is the best?" He said: "Prolonged qunut." [Narrated by Muslim in Kitab Salat al-Musafirin, Bab: The best prayer is prolonged qunut, no. 756 (1/520); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (3/152–153).] It was also said that ﴿qanitin﴾ means supplicating.

Evidence for this is what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed qunut for a month consecutively, supplicating against some tribes of Sulaym: Ri'l, Dhakwan and ʿUsayyah. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Witr, Bab: Qunut before and after the bowing (2/490); al-Bukhari's narration from Anas says: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed qunut for a month, supplicating against Ri'l and Dhakwan." It is also narrated by Ahmad and by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Salat, Bab: Qunut in the prayers; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (3/122).] It was also said its meaning is "praying," in accordance with His saying: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night﴾ (39:9), meaning one who prays.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾. ﴿Fa-rijalan﴾ means on foot. It is said: rajil and rijal, like sahib and sihab, qa'im and qiyam, na'im and niyam. ﴿Or riding﴾ on their mounts, and it is the plural of rakib. The meaning is: if it is not possible for you to pray devoutly obedient, giving the prayer its due, because of fear, then pray on foot on your feet or riding on the backs of your mounts. This applies in a state of fighting and battle: one prays wherever one is, on foot or riding, facing the qibla or not facing it, and signals with bowing and prostration, making the prostration lower than the bowing. Likewise, if a predator approaches him or a flood overtakes him, fearing for his life, and he flees ahead while praying by gesture, that is permissible.

The prayer in a state of fear has several forms. This is the prayer of extreme fear; the remaining forms will be explained in Surat al-Nisa', God willing. According to most scholars, the number of rak'ahs is not reduced because of fear. It is narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Allah made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ: four rak'ahs at home, two rak'ahs when traveling, and one rak'ah in fear. [Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Musafirin, Bab: The prayer of travellers and its shortening, no. 687 (1/479).] This is also the view of ʿAta', Tawus, al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah: that one prays one rak'ah in a state of extreme fear. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: If you are in combat, and people are striking one another, then say: "Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar, and remember Allah; that is your prayer." ﴿Then when you are safe, remember Allah﴾, meaning: perform the five prayers in full, with their due rights, ﴿as He has taught you what you did not know﴾.

[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Masajid, Bab: The proof for the one who says the middle prayer is the ʿAsr prayer, no. 629 (1/437); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (2/232).] ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," and from Hafsah similar to that.

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Jaʿfar al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Abu Nuʿaym informed us: Sufyan informed us, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: We said to ʿUbaydah, "Ask ʿAli about the middle prayer." So he asked him, and he said: "We used to think it was the Fajr prayer, until I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the day of the Trench: 'They have kept us busy from the middle prayer, the ʿAsr prayer. May Allah fill their bellies and their graves with fire.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir Surat al-Baqarah, Bab: "Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer," (8/195); Muslim in Kitab al-Masajid, Bab: The proof for the one who says the middle prayer is the ʿAsr prayer, no. 627 (1/436); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (2/233–234).] Also, it is a prayer of the daytime and a prayer that is part of the night's two sides, and the Prophet ﷺ singled it out with emphasis.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us: Hisham informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Malih, who said: We were with Buraydah on a campaign on a cloudy day, and he said: "Hasten the ʿAsr prayer, for the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever abandons the ʿAsr prayer, his deeds are nullified.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Mawaqit, Bab: Whoever abandons the ʿAsr (2/31), and Bab: Hastening the prayer on a cloudy day; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (2/213–237).]

Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb said: It is the Maghrib prayer, because it is a middle prayer, being neither the fewest nor the most in rak'ahs. No one from the earlier generation (al-salaf) is reported to have said that it is the ʿIsha prayer; rather, some later scholars mentioned it, because it lies between two prayers that are not shortened. Some of them said: it is one of the five prayers, unspecified, which Allah, exalted is He, left unnamed to urge the servants to guard the performance of all of them, just as He concealed the Night of Decree in Ramadan, the hour of answered supplication on Friday, and the Greatest Name among the names, so that they would guard all of them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And stand before Allah in devout obedience﴾, meaning: obedient. Al-Sha'bi, ʿAta', Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Tawus said: qunut is obedience. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿A nation devoutly obedient﴾ (16:120), meaning obedient.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: every religious community has a prayer in which they stand in disobedience; so stand, you, before Allah in your prayer, in obedience. It was also said: qunut is silence regarding what it is not permissible to speak during the prayer.

Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Mani' informed us: Hushaym informed us: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from al-Harith ibn Shubayl, from Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "We used to speak behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the prayer; a man among us would speak to his companion beside him, until this verse was revealed: ﴿And stand before Allah in devout obedience﴾. So we were commanded to be silent and forbidden to speak." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-ʿAmal fi al-Salah, Bab: What is forbidden of speech in prayer (3/73), and in Tafsir; and Muslim in Kitab al-Masajid, Bab: The prohibition of speech in prayer and the abrogation of what was permitted, no. 539 (1/383).]

Mujahid said: "devoutly humble." He said: qunut includes prolonged bowing, lowering the gaze, stillness, and lowering the wing. The scholars, when one of them stood to pray, would be in awe of the Most Merciful, so that he would not turn, nor move pebbles, nor play with anything, nor let his mind dwell on any worldly matter, except forgetfully. It was also said: the intended meaning of qunut is prolonged standing.

Abu ʿUthman al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Ibn Abi ʿUmar informed us: Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Which prayer is the best?" He said: "Prolonged qunut." [Narrated by Muslim in Kitab Salat al-Musafirin, Bab: The best prayer is prolonged qunut, no. 756 (1/520); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (3/152–153).] It was also said that ﴿qanitin﴾ means supplicating.

Evidence for this is what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed qunut for a month consecutively, supplicating against some tribes of Sulaym: Ri'l, Dhakwan and ʿUsayyah. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Witr, Bab: Qunut before and after the bowing (2/490); al-Bukhari's narration from Anas says: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed qunut for a month, supplicating against Ri'l and Dhakwan." It is also narrated by Ahmad and by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Salat, Bab: Qunut in the prayers; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (3/122).] It was also said its meaning is "praying," in accordance with His saying: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night﴾ (39:9), meaning one who prays.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾. ﴿Fa-rijalan﴾ means on foot. It is said: rajil and rijal, like sahib and sihab, qa'im and qiyam, na'im and niyam. ﴿Or riding﴾ on their mounts, and it is the plural of rakib. The meaning is: if it is not possible for you to pray devoutly obedient, giving the prayer its due, because of fear, then pray on foot on your feet or riding on the backs of your mounts. This applies in a state of fighting and battle: one prays wherever one is, on foot or riding, facing the qibla or not facing it, and signals with bowing and prostration, making the prostration lower than the bowing. Likewise, if a predator approaches him or a flood overtakes him, fearing for his life, and he flees ahead while praying by gesture, that is permissible.

The prayer in a state of fear has several forms. This is the prayer of extreme fear; the remaining forms will be explained in Surat al-Nisa', God willing. According to most scholars, the number of rak'ahs is not reduced because of fear. It is narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Allah made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ: four rak'ahs at home, two rak'ahs when traveling, and one rak'ah in fear. [Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Musafirin, Bab: The prayer of travellers and its shortening, no. 687 (1/479).] This is also the view of ʿAta', Tawus, al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah: that one prays one rak'ah in a state of extreme fear. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: If you are in combat, and people are striking one another, then say: "Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar, and remember Allah; that is your prayer." ﴿Then when you are safe, remember Allah﴾, meaning: perform the five prayers in full, with their due rights, ﴿as He has taught you what you did not know﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 240:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those of you who are taken in death﴾, O assembly of men, ﴿and leave behind wives﴾, i.e., they leave behind, ﴿a bequest for their wives﴾. The people of Basra, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and Hafs read wasiyyatan (a bequest) in the accusative, meaning "let them bequeath a bequest" (fal-yuwsu wasiyyatan). The rest read it in the nominative, meaning "a bequest has been prescribed for you" (kutiba 'alaykumu al-wasiyyah). ﴿Provision for a year﴾: matā'an is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning "provide for them as provision." It was also said: God made that provision for them. Al-matā'  is the year's maintenance for their food, clothing, lodging, and whatever else they need. ﴿Without being driven out﴾: ghayra ikhrāj is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). It was also said it is in the accusative by removal of a preposition, as a qualifier, meaning "without expulsion."

This verse was revealed concerning a man from the people of Ta'if called Hakim ibn al-Harith. He emigrated to Madinah, leaving children, and with him were his parents and his wife. He died, so God revealed this verse. The Prophet (ﷺ) gave his parents and children from his inheritance, and did not give his wife anything. He instructed them to spend on her from her husband's estate for a full year. In the beginning of Islam the waiting period (iddat al-wafat) for a widow was a full year, and it was forbidden for the heirs to expel her from the house before the year was complete. Her maintenance and lodging were obligatory from her husband's wealth for that year, as long as she did not leave. She had no share of inheritance. If she left her husband's house, her maintenance lapsed. It was incumbent upon the man to make a bequest for her, and this remained so until the verse of inheritance was revealed. God abrogated the year's maintenance by the quarter and the eighth, and abrogated the year's waiting period by four months and ten days.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But if they leave﴾, meaning of their own accord, before the year is over, without the heirs expelling them, ﴿then there is no blame upon you﴾, O guardians of the deceased, ﴿for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾, meaning adorning themselves for marriage. There are two interpretations of lifting blame from the men:

First: there is no blame upon you in stopping their maintenance if they leave before the year ends.

Second: there is no blame upon you in not preventing them from going out, because staying in her husband's house for a year is not obligatory upon her. God gave her the choice between remaining a year with maintenance and lodging, or leaving with no maintenance and no lodging, until He abrogated it by four months and ten days.

﴿And Allah is Mighty, Wise﴾.

﴿For divorced women there is a provision according to what is customary, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾. He repeated the mention of the provision (mut'ah) here to add a meaning. In the earlier verse, the ruling concerned the one who had not been touched (ghayr al-mamsusah, a woman not yet consummated with), while in this verse the ruling on the provision applies to all divorced women. It is also said: when the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed, ﴿And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means﴾ up to His words ﴿a duty upon the good-doers﴾ (2:236), a man among the Muslims said: "If I do good, I will do it, and if I do not intend that, I will not do it." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For divorced women there is a provision﴾, making the provision theirs by the lam of ownership (lam al-tamlik), then He said: ﴿a duty upon the God-fearing﴾, meaning the believing God-fearing who avoid shirk.

﴿For divorced women there is a provision according to what is customary, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾. He repeated the mention of the provision (mut'ah) here to add a meaning. In the earlier verse, the ruling concerned the one who had not been touched (ghayr al-mamsusah, a woman not yet consummated with), while in this verse the ruling on the provision applies to all divorced women. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 243–245:

God's words: ﴿Have you not considered those who left their homes⦅...⦆﴾ Most of the people of exegesis (tafsir, the science of interpreting the Qur'an) said: There was a town called Dawardan, near Wasit, in which the plague (ṭāʿūn) struck. A group of its people left and another group stayed. More of those who stayed in the town died, and those who left were spared. When the plague lifted, they returned safe. Those who had stayed said: "Our companions were more prudent than us. If we had done as they did, we would have survived. If the plague strikes again, we will certainly leave for a land where there is no pestilence." The plague struck again the following year, and most of the town's people fled. They went out until they settled in a wide valley [[Spacious.]]. When they reached the place where they sought safety, a king from the bottom of the valley and another from its top called out to them: "Die!" And they all died.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab related to us from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'ah, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) set out for Syria. When he reached Sargh [[With an unvocalised initial letter... the word is a dialectal variant: the first border of the Hijaz and the last of Syria. It was also said to be a village in the valley of Tabuk. See Marasid al-Ittila' 2/707–708.]], he was informed that the plague had struck Syria. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you hear of it in a land, do not enter upon it; and if it strikes a land while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it" [[Related by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Jami', nos. 22, 23, 24. Related by al-Bukhari in al-Tibb, chapter: What is mentioned about the plague, 10/179. Related by Muslim in al-Salam, chapter: The plague, omens, soothsaying and the like, no. (2219), 4/1742.]]. So Umar turned back from Sargh.

Al-Kalbi, Muqatil and al-Dahhak said: They only fled from jihad. That is because a king of the kings of the Children of Israel commanded them to go out to fight their enemy. They encamped, then grew cowardly and disliked death, so they made excuses and said to their king: "In the land to which you are taking us there is plague. We will not go there until the plague has ended from it." So Allah sent death upon them, and they left their homes fleeing from death. When the king saw this, he said: "O Allah, Lord of Ya'qub and God of Musa, You see the disobedience of Your servants. Show them a sign in themselves so that they know they cannot escape from You." When they went out, Allah the Exalted said to them: "Die," as a punishment for them, and they all died, and their animals died like the death of one man. Eight days passed over them until they swelled and their bodies became bloated. The people came out to them but were unable to bury them, so they built an enclosure around them to keep off the predators and left them inside it [[Ibn Atiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned some reports about this and then said: "All of this narrative has weak chains of transmission. What is necessarily derived from the verse is that Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), in the form of an admonition and a warning, about a people of mankind who left their homes fleeing from death. Allah caused them to die and then brought them back to life, so that they and everyone who came after them would see that causing death is in the hand of Allah alone and not in the hand of anyone else. So there is no sense in fear for the fearful, nor in complacency for the complacent. Allah the Exalted made this verse a preface to His command to the believers of the Muhammad's community to fight in jihad. This is the view of al-Tabari, and it is the apparent meaning of the verse. The storytellers who related this tale added embellishments, which I have omitted because they are weak." Al-Muharrar al-Wajiz of Ibn Atiyyah: 2/345.]].

They differed about the total number of them. ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani said: They were three thousand. Wahb said: four thousand. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: eight thousand. Abu Rawq said: ten thousand. Al-Suddi said: some thirty-odd thousand. Ibn Jurayj said: forty thousand. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah said: seventy thousand. The most sound of these opinions is the view of the one who said they were more than ten thousand, because Allah the Exalted said ﴿and they were thousands⦅ulūf⦆﴾, and ulūf is the plural of many (kathīr), while its plural of few is ālāf. It is not said of fewer than ten thousand that they are ulūf.

They said: A long period passed, and their bodies had decayed and their bones were bare. Then a prophet named Ḥizqil ibn Būdā passed by them. He was the third of the successors of the Children of Israel after Musa (peace be upon him). The one in charge of the affairs of the Children of Israel after Musa was Yusha' ibn Nun, then Kalib ibn Yuqanna, then Ḥizqil [[Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned this view from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, and said: Ibn Jarir said: that is Ephraim ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub. This view is far-fetched, because this was a long time after Musa, and it occurred in the time of Dawud (peace be upon him), as is clearly stated in the story. Between Dawud and Musa there were more than a thousand years. And Allah knows best. Ibn Kathir 1/533, edited by al-Wad'i.]]. He was called Ibn al-ʿAjuz (the son of the old woman) because his mother was an old woman; she asked Allah for a child after she had grown old and become barren, and Allah granted him to her. Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: He is Dhu al-Kifl, and Ḥizqil was called Dhu al-Kifl because he took responsibility for seventy prophets and saved them from being killed. When Ḥizqil passed by those dead people, he stopped over them and began reflecting on them in wonder. Allah revealed to him: "Do you want Me to show you a sign?" He said: "Yes." So Allah brought them back to life. It was also said: Ḥizqil supplicated his Lord that He would bring them to life, and He brought them to life.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: They were the people of Ḥizqil, whom Allah revived after eight days. When that happened to them, Ḥizqil went out searching for them and found them dead. He wept and said: "O Lord, I was among a people who praised You, glorified You, sanctified You, magnified You, and declared Your oneness, and now I remain alone with no people." Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "I have placed their life in your hands." Ḥizqil said: "Live by the permission of Allah," and they lived.

Mujahid said: When they were brought back to life, they said: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You; there is no god but You." Then they returned to their people and lived a long time, with the mark of death upon their faces. Whenever they wore a garment, it became greasy like a shroud, until they died at the appointed times that had been written for them.

Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: That same smell is still found today among that tribe of the Jews.

Qatadah said: Allah hated them for their fleeing from death, so He caused them to die as a punishment. Then they were raised so that they might complete the term of their appointed lives, for had their appointed times come, they would not have been raised. This is the meaning of His words ﴿Have you not considered⦅...⦆﴾, that is: Have you not known through My informing you? It is from seeing with the heart (ru'yat al-qalb).

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: It is an expression of wonder, as if saying: "Have you ever seen the like of them?" Just as you say: "Have you not considered what so-and-so is doing?" Every instance in the Qur'an of "Have you not considered" concerning something the Prophet (ﷺ) did not witness is to be understood in this way. ﴿to those who left their homes, while they were thousands⦅ulūf⦆﴾: ulūf is the plural of alf (thousand). It was also said: their hearts were united, as the plural of ālif, like qā'id and qu'ūd. The correct view is that the intended meaning is their number. ﴿in fear of death⦅ḥadhar al-mawt⦆﴾, that is, for fear of death. ﴿Then Allah said to them: "Die"⦅mūtū⦆﴾: this is an imperative of transformation (amr taḥwīl), like His words ﴿Be apes, despised⦅kūnū qiradatan khasi'īn⦆﴾ (2:65). ﴿Then He brought them back to life⦅thumma aḥyāhum⦆﴾ after their death. ﴿Indeed Allah is full of bounty toward mankind⦅inna Allāha la-dhū faḍl ʿalā al-nās⦆﴾: it was said that this is general, concerning all people in this world; and it was said it is specific, concerning the believers. ﴿But most people do not give thanks⦅wa-lākinna akthar al-nās lā yashkurūn⦆﴾: as for the disbelievers, they did not give thanks; and as for the believers, they did not reach the utmost degree of thanks.

﴿And fight in the way of Allah⦅wa-qātilū fī sabīl Allāh⦆﴾, that is, in obedience to Allah, against the enemies of Allah. ﴿And know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing⦅wa-iʿlamū anna Allāh samīʿ ʿalīm⦆﴾. Most of the people of exegesis said: This is an address to those who were brought back to life, who had been commanded to fight in the way of Allah, but who went out of their homes fleeing from jihad; then Allah caused them to die, then brought them back to life, and commanded them to strive. It was also said: The address is to this community, commanding them to jihad.

God's words: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan⦅man dhā alladhī yuqriḍu Allāha qarḍan ḥasanan⦆﴾. Qarḍ (loan) is a name for everything that a person gives in order to be compensated for it. Allah the Exalted called the deeds of the believers for Him, in hope of the reward He promised them, a loan, because they perform them seeking His reward. Al-Kisa'i said: Qarḍ is what you send ahead of good or evil deeds. The root meaning of qarḍ in the language is "cutting," because it cuts off some of one's wealth which one gives so that its equivalent returns to him. It was also said that there is an elision in the verse, meaning: "Who is it that would lend to the servants of Allah and to those of His creatures who are in need?" like His words ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger⦅...⦆﴾ (33:57), meaning: those who harm the servants of Allah. This is as in the sound hadith from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'O son of Adam, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me.' He will say: 'My Lord, how could I feed You when You are the Lord of the worlds?' He will say: 'My servant so-and-so asked you for food and you did not feed him. Did you not know that if you had fed him, you would have found that with Me?'" [[Related by Muslim, in al-Birr, chapter: The virtue of visiting the sick, no. (2569), 4/1990.]].

God's words: ﴿Allah multiplies it for him⦅yuqriḍu Allāha⦆⦅fa-yuḍāʿifahu lahu⦆﴾, that is, spends in obedience to Allah, ﴿a goodly loan⦅qarḍan ḥasanan⦆﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read ﴿fa-yuḍaʿʿifahu⦆﴾ with the doubled ʿayn, and its family (of forms) is likewise doubled. Abu Amr agreed with them in surah al-Ahzab. The others read ﴿fa-yuḍāʿifahu⦆﴾ with an alif and without doubling. Both are dialectal forms. The evidence for the doubled form is His words ﴿manifold increases⦅aḍʿāfan kathīrah⦆﴾, because doubling indicates multiplicity. Ibn Amir, ʿĀṣim and Ya'qub read ﴿fa-yuḍāʿifahu⦆﴾ with the fa in the accusative (fa-yuḍāʿifahu), and likewise in surah al-Hadid, as an answer to the interrogative. It was also said that it is governed by an implied "an" (anna). The others read the fa in the nominative, as a conjunction coordinated with His words ﴿yuqriḍu﴾ (lends). ﴿Manifold increases⦅aḍʿāfan kathīrah⦆﴾. Al-Suddi said: This multiplication, no one knows it except Allah the Mighty and Majestic. It was also said: seven hundredfold.

﴿And Allah withholds and extends⦅wa-Allāh yaqbiḍu wa-yabsuṭu⦆﴾. The people of Basra and Hamzah read ﴿yabsuṭu⦆﴾ here and in al-A'raf with the letter sin (yabsuṭu, bastah), like their counterparts. The others read them with ṣād. It was said: yaqbiḍu means withholding provision and life and restricting, and yabsuṭu means widening. It was also said: yaqbiḍu means accepting repentance and charity, and yabsuṭu means giving succession and reward. It was said: it is giving life and causing death: whoever He causes to die has been withheld from, and whoever He extends in his lifespan has been extended to. It was also said: this concerns the hearts. When Allah the Exalted commanded them to give charity, He informed them that they could not do so except by His grace. He said: He withholds some hearts so that they do not become eager for good, and He extends others so that they send forward good for themselves, as in the hadith: "The hearts are between two of the fingers of the Merciful; Allah turns them however He wills," the hadith [[Related by Muslim, in al-Qadar, chapter: Allah the Exalted turns hearts however He wills, no. (2654), 4/2045. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 1/165.]].

﴿And to Him you will be returned⦅wa-ilayhi turja'ūn⦆﴾, that is: you will return to Allah, and He will recompense you for your deeds. Qatadah said: The pronoun refers to the dust, as an allusion to something not mentioned, meaning: He created them from dust, and to Him they return.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 243–245:

God's words: ﴿Have you not considered those who left their homes⦅...⦆﴾ Most of the people of exegesis (tafsir, the science of interpreting the Qur'an) said: There was a town called Dawardan, near Wasit, in which the plague (ṭāʿūn) struck. A group of its people left and another group stayed. More of those who stayed in the town died, and those who left were spared. When the plague lifted, they returned safe. Those who had stayed said: "Our companions were more prudent than us. If we had done as they did, we would have survived. If the plague strikes again, we will certainly leave for a land where there is no pestilence." The plague struck again the following year, and most of the town's people fled. They went out until they settled in a wide valley [[Spacious.]]. He wept and said: "O Lord, I was among a people who praised You, glorified You, sanctified You, magnified You, and declared Your oneness, and now I remain alone with no people." Mujahid said: When they were brought back to life, they said: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You; there is no god but You." Whenever they wore a garment, it became greasy like a shroud, until they died at the appointed times that had been written for them.

Then they were raised so that they might complete the term of their appointed lives, for had their appointed times come, they would not have been raised. This is the meaning of His words ﴿Have you not considered⦅...⦆﴾, that is: Have you not known through My informing you? It is from seeing with the heart (ru'yat al-qalb).

﴿And fight in the way of Allah⦅wa-qātilū fī sabīl Allāh⦆﴾, that is, in obedience to Allah, against the enemies of Allah. ﴿And know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing⦅wa-iʿlamū anna Allāh samīʿ ʿalīm⦆﴾. God's words: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan⦅man dhā alladhī yuqriḍu Allāha qarḍan ḥasanan⦆﴾. Al-Suddi said: This multiplication, no one knows it except Allah the Mighty and Majestic. It was also said: seven hundredfold.
