Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 246:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Have you not considered the eminent men (al-mala') of the Children of Israel﴾. Al-mala' among a people are their notables and their nobles. The root meaning of al-mala' is a group of people, and it has no singular from its own form, like al-qawm (people), al-rahṭ (company), al-ibil (camels), al-khayl (horses) and al-jaysh (army). Its plural is amla'. ﴿after Moses﴾, that is, after the death of Moses; ﴿when they said to a prophet of theirs﴾. The scholars differed about who that prophet was. Qatadah said he was Yusha' ibn Nun ibn Afra'im ibn Yusuf, peace be upon him. al-Suddi said: his name was Shim'un. He was named Shim'un because his mother asked God to grant her a boy, and God answered her prayer, and she bore a boy and named him Sam'un, saying: "God, exalted is He, has heard my supplication." The sin is changed to shin in Hebrew. He was Shim'un ibn Safiyyah ibn 'Alqamah, from the descendants of Lawi ibn Ya'qub. The rest of the commentators said: he was Ishmawil, and in Hebrew it is Isma'il ibn Yal ibn 'Alqamah. Muqatil said: he was of the lineage of Harun. Mujahid said: he was Ishmawil, and in Hebrew it is Isma'il ibn Yal ibn 'Alqamah.

Wahb, Ibn Ishaq, al-Kalbi and others said: the reason for their request of him was that when Moses, peace be upon him, died, Yusha' ibn Nun succeeded him among the Children of Israel, maintaining among them the Torah and the command of God, until God took him. Then Kalib succeeded them in the same way until God took him. Then Hizqil succeeded until God took him. Then the innovations among the Children of Israel grew great, and they forgot the covenant of God, until they worshipped idols. So God sent Ilyas (Elijah) to them as a prophet, and he called them to God, may He be exalted. The prophets among the Children of Israel after Moses were sent to them to renew what they had forgotten of the Torah. Then after Ilyas, al-Yasa' succeeded him, and he was among them as God willed, until God took him. Successors came after them, and sins grew great. There appeared against them an enemy called al-Bilshatha, who are the people of Goliath (Jalut). They used to dwell on the coast of the Roman Sea between Egypt and Palestine, and they were the Amalekites. They prevailed over the Children of Israel, overcame much of their land, took many of their offspring captive, and seized four hundred and forty young men from the sons of their kings. They imposed the jizyah (poll tax) upon them and took their Torah. The Children of Israel suffered from them affliction and hardship, and they had no prophet to manage their affairs. The tribe of prophethood had been destroyed, so that none remained of them except a pregnant woman. They confined her in a house, fearing that she would bear a girl, which she would then exchange for a boy, given the eagerness of the Children of Israel for her child. The woman began to pray to God to grant her a boy, and she bore a boy, and she named him Ishmawil, saying: "God, exalted is He, has heard my supplication." The boy grew up, and she handed him over to learn the Torah in the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis). A shaykh from among their scholars took charge of him and adopted him. When the boy reached maturity, Gabriel came to him while he was sleeping beside the shaykh, for the shaykh did not entrust him to anyone. Gabriel called him in the voice of the shaykh: "O Ishmawil!" The boy got up frightened and went to the shaykh and said: "O father, did you call me?" The shaykh disliked saying "no," lest the boy be alarmed, so he said: "O my son, go back and sleep." The boy went back and slept. Then he called him a second time, and the boy said: "O father, did you call me?" He said: "Go back and sleep, and if I call you a third time, do not answer me." (The boy went back and slept.) [[Omitted in B and in the printed edition.]] When it was the third time, Gabriel appeared to him and said: "Go to your people and convey to them the message of your Lord, for God, mighty and majestic, has sent you among them as a prophet." When he came to them, they denied him and said: "You have hastened to prophethood and had not attained it." They said to him: "If you are truthful, then raise up for us a king, and we will fight in the way of God, as a sign of your prophethood." The affairs of the Children of Israel were sustained only by gathering around kings and obeying kings, while their prophets managed their affairs for them. The king was the one who led the armies, and the prophet arranged his affairs for him, advised him with right guidance, and brought him news from his Lord. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: God sent Ishmawil as a prophet, and they remained for forty years in the best condition. Then came the matter of Jalut and the Amalekites, which came to pass, and they said to Ishmawil: ﴿Raise up for us a king, and we will fight in the way of God﴾. The verb is jussive in response to the imperative. When they said that to him, ﴿he said: "Is it likely that, if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?"﴾ It is an interrogative of doubt.

Nafi' read ʿasaytum with a kasrah on the sin throughout the Qur'an, while the rest read it with a fatḥah, and this is the eloquent dialect, as evidenced by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perhaps your Lord...﴾ (ʿasā rabbukum). ﴿If fighting is prescribed for you﴾, that is, obligated, ﴿with that king﴾; ﴿that you will not fight﴾, that is, that you will not fulfil what you say with him. ﴿They said: "And why should we not fight in the way of God?"﴾ If it is asked, what is the grammatical basis for the presence of "an" (that) in this place, when the Arabs do not say "mā laka an lā taf'al" but only say "mā laka lā taf'al"? It is said: the presence and the omission of "an" are both sound dialects. The inclusion is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿What is it with you that you are not among those who prostrate?﴾ (15:32), and the omission is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not believe in God?﴾ (57:8). Al-Kisa'i said: its meaning is "wa-mā lanā fī an lā nuqātila," with "fī" omitted. al-Farra' said: that is, "wa-mā yamna'unā an lā nuqātila fī sabīl Allāh," like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ (7:12). al-Akhfash said: "an" here is superfluous, and the meaning is: "wa-mā lanā lā nuqātilu fī sabīl Allāh." ﴿And we have been expelled from our homes and our children﴾, that is, those who were overcome were expelled from their homes. The apparent sense of the speech is general, and its inner sense is particular, because those who said to their prophet, "Raise up for us a king that we may fight in the way of God," were in their homes and dwellings; only those among them who were taken captive were expelled. The meaning of the verse is that they said, in reply to their prophet: "We were only reluctant to fight when we were restrained in our lands, and our enemy did not prevail over us. But when that has reached us, we will obey our Lord in fighting and protect our women and children."

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away﴾, that is, they turned away from jihad and neglected the command of God, ﴿except for a few of them﴾, those who crossed the river with Talut and were content with a single handful, as will come, God willing. ﴿And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, God has sent Talut to you as king." This was because Ishmawil had asked God, exalted is He, to send them a king. He brought a staff and a horn [[He meant the flask in which oil and perfume are kept. It seems they used to make such flasks from cow horns and similar things.]] containing the oil of holiness (duhn al-quds). It was said to him: "Your companion who will be king is as tall as this staff. Look at this horn with the oil in it. When a man enters upon you and the oil in the horn sizzles [[Nasha al-ma' yanushshu nashan wa nashishan: the water makes a sound when it boils.]], he is the king of the Children of Israel. Anoint his head with it and make him king over them."

Talut's name in Hebrew was Shawul ibn Qays, from the descendants of Binyamin ibn Ya'qub. He was called Talut because of his height. He was taller than anyone else by his head and shoulders. He was a tanner who worked hides, [[The hide when it is first tanned. When it is returned to the tanning again, it is called al-ladim.]] as related by Wahb. Al-Suddi said he was a water-carrier who drew water with a donkey of his from the Nile. His donkey strayed and he went out to search for it. It was also said that he was a kharbandaj (a maker of ... ). Wahb also said: Rather, the donkeys of Talut's father had strayed, so he sent him, along with a young servant of his, to search for them. He passed by the house of Ishmawil. The servant said to Talut: "If only we went in to this prophet and asked him about the matter of the donkeys, so that he might guide us and pray for us." So they entered upon him. While they were with him, mentioning to him the matter of the donkeys, the oil in the horn sizzled. Ishmawil, peace be upon him, stood up and measured Talut with the staff, and he matched its length. He said to Talut, "Bring your head close." He brought it close, and he anointed it with the oil of holiness. Then he said to him, "You are the king of the Children of Israel whom God, exalted is He, commanded me to make king over them." Talut said, "Do you not know that my tribe is the lowest of the tribes of the Children of Israel, and my house the lowest of their houses?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then what is the sign?" He said, "The sign is that you will return and your father will have found his donkeys." And so it was.

Then he said to the Children of Israel: "Indeed, God has sent Talut to you as king." ﴿They said, "How can he have kingship over us?"﴾ That is, from where would he have kingship over us? ﴿When we have more right﴾ that is, more deserving ﴿to kingship than he does?﴾ They only said this because among the Children of Israel there were two tribes: the tribe of prophethood and the tribe of kingship. The tribe of prophethood was the tribe of Lawi ibn Ya'qub, from which Musa and Harun came. The tribe of kingship was the tribe of Yahudha ibn Ya'qub, from which Dawud and Sulayman came. Talut was not from either of them; he was from the tribe of Binyamin ibn Ya'qub. They had committed a great sin: they would have intercourse with women in the middle of the road in broad daylight. So God, exalted is He, became angry with them, and took away kingship and prophethood from them. They called him "the tribe of sin." When their prophet told them this, they denied it, because he was not from the tribe of kingship. Despite this, they said, "He is poor." ﴿And he has not been given abundance of wealth.﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, God has chosen him﴾ selected him ﴿over you, and has increased him in knowledge and physique﴾ in virtue and abundance ﴿in knowledge and physique﴾. That was because he was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel in his time. It was also said that revelation came to him when he was given kingship. Al-Kalbi said: ﴿and increased him in knowledge﴾ regarding war, and ﴿in physique﴾ regarding height. It was also said that "physique" refers to beauty, and Talut was the most handsome man among the Children of Israel and the most knowledgeable of them. ﴿And God gives His kingship to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ It was said that "All-Encompassing" means the one possessing abundance, who gives out of richness, and "All-Knowing" means the one who knows. It was also said: the one who knows what has been, and the one who knows what will be. Then they said to him, "What is the sign of his kingship?" Their prophet said to them, "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you." That is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you."﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 248:

﴿And their Prophet said to them: "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that there will come to you the Ark.﴾ The story of the Ark is that Allah, exalted is He, sent down an ark (tabut) to Adam, in which was the likeness of the prophets, peace be upon them. It was made of shimshad wood, about three cubits by two cubits. It remained with Adam until he died, and after that it was with Shith. Then the children of Adam inherited it until it reached Ibrahim. Then it was with Isma'il, because he was the eldest of his sons, then with Ya'qub. Then it was among the Children of Israel until it reached Musa, and Musa would place in it the Torah and some of his belongings. It remained with him until Musa, peace be upon him, died. Then the prophets of the Children of Israel passed it on until the time of Shmuwil (Samuel). In it was the mention of Allah, exalted is He. [[This account about the ark, its form, its inheritance, etc., has nothing authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ. Even if what is reported in the tafsir from some of the Companions or the Successors were established, it would remain open to being true or false, because the establishing of a saying and its attribution to a Companion in such matters does not mean its correctness in reality. In any case, the understanding of the noble verses does not depend on anything of what has been mentioned. And Allah knows best.]] ﴿In it is tranquility (sakinah) from your Lord.﴾ Scholars differed about what the sakinah is. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is a wind that is fine and blowing, having two heads and a face like the face of a human. It is reported from Mujahid: something resembling a cat, with a head like a cat's head and a tail like a cat's tail, and it has two wings. It was also said: it has two eyes that have rays, and two wings of emerald and chrysolite. When they heard its voice, they were certain of victory. When they went out, they placed the ark before them; when it moved, they moved, and when it stopped, they stopped.

It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he said: it is a basin of gold from Paradise in which the hearts of the prophets were washed. It is reported from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: it is a spirit from Allah that speaks when they differ about something, informing them with an explanation of what they seek. [[There is nothing in the authentically established Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ that indicates any of this explanation of the sakinah, and it is transmitted from the People of the Book. We have no need of any of it to explain the noble verse. See: al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Abu Shahba, p. (240).]] Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: it is the signs they recognize, and so they find tranquility in them. Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: sakinah is on the pattern fa'ilah from al-sukun, meaning tranquility (tuma'ninah) from your Lord, so wherever the ark was, they felt at peace with it and settled. [[Ibn ʿAtiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, favoring this meaning, said: "The correct view is that the ark contained noble things from the remains and relics of the prophets, so souls would find rest in it, become familiar with it, and be strengthened. The customary way is that Allah grants victory to truth and to noble matters with Him. The sakinah according to this is fa'ilah derived from sukun, as one says ʿazama ʿazimah and qata'a qati'ah." Al-Muharrar al-Wajiz of Ibn ʿAtiyyah: 2/361. See also: Tafsir al-Tabari: 5/329-230.]] ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind﴾, meaning Musa and Harun themselves. In it were two tablets of the Torah and fragments of the tablets that had broken, and in it was the staff of Musa, his sandals, the turban of Harun, his staff, and a qafiz of the manna that used to descend upon the Children of Israel. The ark was with the Children of Israel, and whenever they differed about something, it spoke and judged between them. When they attended battle, they placed it before them, and they sought victory over their enemy through it. When they disobeyed and corrupted, Allah gave the Amalekites power over them, and they overcame them and seized the ark.

The cause of this was that ʿAyli, the scholar who raised Shmuwil, peace be upon him, had two young sons, and ʿAyli was their rabbi and the overseer of their offerings. His two sons introduced into the offering something that had not been there before. That is because ʿAyli had a hook (manut) for the offering, which they would hang with two hooks; whatever came out of it was for the priest who hung it. His sons made hooks, and women would pray in Bayt al-Maqdis, and they would seize them. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed to Shmuwil, peace be upon him: "Go to ʿAyli and say: love of the child has prevented you from restraining your two sons from introducing into My offering and My sanctuary, and from disobeying Me. I will surely strip the priesthood from you and from your offspring, and I will destroy you and them." Shmuwil informed ʿAyli of this, and he was greatly alarmed. An enemy from among those around them marched against them, and he commanded his two sons to go out with the people and fight that enemy. They went out and brought the ark with them. When they prepared for battle, ʿAyli kept awaiting news of what they had done. A man came to him while he was sitting on his chair and informed him that the people had been routed and that his two sons had been killed. He said: "And what became of the ark?" He said: "The enemy took it away." So he gasped, fell backward from his chair onto his nape, and died. The affair of the Children of Israel became confused, and they scattered until Allah sent Talut as king. They asked him for a proof, and their Prophet said to them: "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the ark will come to you."

As for the story of the ark: those who captured the ark brought it to a town of the towns of Palestine called Azdud, and they placed it in the house of an idol of theirs, and put it beneath the greatest idol. In the morning they found the idol beneath it, so they took it and placed it on top of it, and nailed the idol's feet to the ark. In the morning they found the idol's hands and feet had been cut off and it lay prostrate beneath the ark, and their idols were all overturned. So they removed it from the idol's house and placed it in a district of their city. The people of that district were seized by a pain in their necks until most of them perished. Some of them said to others: "Do you not know that the God of the Children of Israel cannot be withstood by anything? So send it to the town of such-and-such." Allah sent a mouse upon the people of that town. The mouse would spend the night with a man, and in the morning he would be dead, having been eaten from within. They took it out to the open country and buried it in a latrine of theirs, and everyone who relieved himself there was afflicted with hemorrhoids and colic. They were bewildered. A woman who was among them, a captive of the Children of Israel from the descendants of the prophets, said to them: "You will not cease to see what you dislike as long as this ark is among you, so remove it from yourselves." They brought a cart at the woman's direction, loaded the ark onto it, then tied it to two bulls and struck their flanks. The two bulls set off walking, and Allah, exalted is He, appointed four angels to drive them. They came until they stopped at the land of the Children of Israel, broke their yokes, cut their ropes, and placed the ark in a field where the harvest of the Children of Israel was, and then returned to their land. The Children of Israel were startled by nothing but the ark, so they cried "Allahu akbar" and praised Allah. [[All of this is from the reports of the Children of Israel, who altered and changed; Allah knows best their authenticity.]] This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿carried by the angels﴾, meaning driving it. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: the angels came with the ark carrying it between heaven and earth while they looked at it, until they set it down before Talut. Al-Hasan said: the ark was with the angels in the heaven, and when Talut assumed the kingship, the angels carried it and placed it among them. Qatadah said: rather, the ark was in the wilderness, which Musa had left with Yusha ibn Nun, and it remained there, so the angels carried it until they placed it in the house of Talut, and they acknowledged his kingship. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, meaning a lesson, ﴿for you, if you are believers.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: the ark and the staff of Musa are in the Lake of Tiberias, and they will come out before the Day of Resurrection. [[Shaykh Abu Shahba, may Allah have mercy on him, says: "What we are certain of, and what must be believed, is that among the Children of Israel there was an ark, that is a chest, without investigating its reality, its form, or where it came from, since there is no authentic report from the Infallible about that. And that this ark contained remnants left by Musa and Harun, peace be upon them, with the possibility that the specifying of that is in some of what we mentioned earlier from the narrations in al-Baghawi and others. And that this ark was a source of sakinah and tranquility for the Children of Israel, especially when fighting their enemy, and that it returned to the Children of Israel, carried by the angels, without investigating the way the angels carried it. By this, the ark was a sign confirming the truth of Talut's kingship over them. As for what lies beyond that of the reports I have heard, no evidence has been established for it." See: al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at fi Kutub al-Tafsir, p. 243. As for Ustadh Sayyid Qutb, may Allah have mercy on him, he turned away from all these Israelite narrations in order to present to us what the noble verses suggest of lessons drawn from the experiences of those earlier nations, which the Noble Qur'an came to establish in believing souls and to educate them upon. See: Fi Zilal al-Qur'an: 2/260 onwards, Dar al-Shuruq edition.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 249:

﴿When Talut set out with the troops﴾, meaning he went out with them. The root of *fasl* is "cutting": he cut off his place of residence, departing toward another place. So Talut went out from Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) with the troops, who on that day numbered seventy thousand fighters. It is also said they were eighty thousand. None stayed behind except the elderly because of their old age, the sick because of their illness, or those with a valid excuse. This was because, when they saw the Ark (*al-tabut*), they had no doubt about victory, so they hastened to fight. Talut said: "I have no need for anyone who has what I see. No man should go out with me who has built a building he has not finished, or a merchant who is occupied with his trade, or a man who is in debt, or a man who has married a woman and has not yet consummated the marriage. I only want energetic, unoccupied youths." So there gathered around him eighty thousand who met his condition. It was during intense heat, and they complained among themselves about the scarcity of water between them and their enemy. They said: "The water is scarce and will not suffice us, so pray to God that He make a river flow for us."

﴿He said﴾, Talut: ﴿Indeed, God is going to test you﴾, to examine you, to see your obedience, and He is the most knowing, ﴿with a river﴾. Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: it is the river of Filastin (Palestine). Qatadah said: it is a sweet river between al-Urdunn (the Jordan) and Filastin. ﴿Whoever drinks from it is not of me﴾, meaning he is not of the people of my religion and obedience. ﴿And whoever does not taste it﴾, that is, does not drink it, ﴿then he is of me, except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Abu Amr recited *ghurfatan* with a fatha on the ghayn, while the others recited it with a damma on the ghayn. Both are dialectal forms. Al-Kisa'i said: *al-ghurfah* with a damma is what is held in the palm of water when it is scooped, and *al-ghurfah* with a fatha is the act of scooping. So the damma form is a noun and the fatha form is a verbal noun (masdar). ﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them﴾. The word *qalilan* is in the accusative as an exception. They differed about the number of the few who did not drink. Al-Suddi said they were four thousand. Others said they were three hundred and some ten, and this is the sound view.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abd Allah ibn Raja' informed us: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "We, the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), used to say that the number of the companions of Badr was equal to the number of the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a believer: ten and three hundred." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi: Chapter: The number of the companions of Badr. 7/290.]]

It is also narrated as "three hundred and thirteen." When they reached the river, thirst had overcome them, and all drank from it except this small number. Whoever scooped a handful as God commanded, his heart was strengthened, his faith was sound, he crossed the river safely, and that single handful sufficed him for drinking, for carrying, and for his animals. Those who drank and disobeyed God's command had their lips blackened, thirst overcame them, they were not quenched, and they remained on the bank of the river. They were cowardly in facing the enemy, so they did not cross over and did not witness the victory.

It is also said that all of them crossed, but only those who had not drunk attended the fighting. ﴿So when he crossed it﴾, meaning the river, ﴿he﴾, meaning Talut, ﴿and those who believed with him﴾, meaning the few, ﴿they said﴾, meaning those who had drunk and disobeyed God's command, and who were people of doubt and hypocrisy: ﴿We have no power today against Jalut and his troops﴾. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and al-Suddi said: they turned back and did not cross over. ﴿Those who were certain﴾, that is, those who were convinced, ﴿that they would meet God﴾, those who remained steadfast with Talut, said: ﴿How many a small group has overcome a large group by the permission of God﴾. A *fi'ah* is a company, a group, and it is a plural with no singular from its own form. Its plural is *fi'at* and *fi'un* in the nominative, and *fi'in* in the genitive and accusative. ﴿By the permission of God﴾, by His decree and His will. ﴿And God is with the patient﴾, with victory and assistance.

And when they came out to face Jalut (Goliath) and his forces, they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and make firm our feet and help us against the disbelieving people.﴾ (Talut and his army, meaning the believers, went out to face Jalut and his army, meaning the polytheists.) The meaning of *baraza* is that they came out into the open (*al-biraz*) of the earth, which is the level, elevated ground. "Pour upon us" means "send down upon us" and "pour out upon us." "Firm our feet" means "firm our hearts."

﴿So they routed them by the permission of Allah, and David killed Jalut, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom, and taught him of what He willed. And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted; but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.﴾ (251) ﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers.﴾ (252)

﴿So they routed them by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, by the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿And David killed Jalut﴾. As for the manner of his killing, the people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis)[[These reports, taken as a whole, are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives transmitted from Jewish and Christian sources). We have no need of them, since we have in our hands the Book and the Sunnah. Nothing in the Book of Allah or in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicates what they mention, and we have no need of any of this in understanding and reflecting upon the Qur'an, so do not pay them any heed... Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that this is among the Isra'iliyyat. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/537, Dar al-Arqam edition. Al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Abu Shahba, pp. 248–249.]] said: He crossed the river with Talut, among those who crossed. Iysha (Jesse), the father of David, had thirteen sons, and David was the youngest of them. He used to shoot with a sling (*al-qadhdhafa*). One day he said to his father: "O father, I never throw my sling at anything without knocking it down." His father said: "Rejoice, my son, for Allah has made your provision in your sling." Then he came to him another time and said: "O father, I entered between the mountains and found a lion lying down, so I mounted it and took hold of its ears, and it did not harm me." He said: "Rejoice, my son, for this is a good thing that Allah intends for you." Then he came to him on another day and said: "O father, I walk between the mountains and glorify Allah, and no mountain remains but that it glorifies Allah along with me." He said: "Rejoice, my son, for this is a good thing that Allah, the Exalted, has given you."

Then Jalut sent to Talut: "Come out to me, or send out to me a man who will fight me. If he kills me, then you will have my kingdom, and if I kill him, then I will have your kingdom." This was difficult for Talut, so he called out in his army: "Whoever kills Jalut, I will marry him to my daughter and share my kingdom with him." The people were afraid of Jalut, and none of them answered him. So Talut asked their prophet to supplicate to Allah, the Exalted, about this, and he supplicated to Allah concerning it. Then a horn containing holy oil (*duhn al-qudus*) and a furnace of iron were brought. It was said: "Your companion who will kill Jalut is the one upon whose head this horn will be placed. The oil will boil until it anoints his head, without flowing onto his face, and it will sit on his head like a crown (*al-iklil*). He will enter this furnace and fill it, and he will not shift about in it." Then Talut summoned the Children of Israel and tested them, but none of them agreed with it. So Allah revealed to their prophet that among the sons of Iysha there is one by whom Allah will kill Jalut. Talut summoned Iysha and said: "Present your sons to me." He brought out to him twelve men, like pillars (*al-sawari*)[[Plural of *sariya*, a column of stone or baked brick. It is reported in a hadith that he forbade praying between the pillars (*al-sawari*) during congregational prayer, because it breaks the row.]]. He began presenting them to the horn, but it showed nothing. He said to Iysha: "Do you have any other son besides these?" He said: "No." So the prophet said: "O Lord, he claims he has no son other than these." He said: "He lied." The prophet said: "Indeed, my Lord has called you a liar." Iysha said: "Allah has spoken truly, O Prophet of Allah. I have a young son called Dawud. I was ashamed to let people see him because of his short stature and lowliness, so I left him (*fakhallaftuhu*)[[In one copy: *fa-ja'altuhu* (I made him).]] tending the sheep in such-and-such a valley." David was a short man, sickly (*misqam*), yellowish (*misfar*), blue-eyed (*azraq*)[[He means blue-eyed, and the Arabs used to consider blue eyes a bad omen.]], and thin-haired (*am'ar*)[[Having little hair.]]. Talut summoned him. It is also said: Talut himself went out to him and found that the valley had flooded between him and the pen to which he used to bring the flock. He found David carrying two sheep, carrying them across the flood without wading through the water with them. When Talut saw him, he said: "This is him, without doubt. This one has mercy on the animals, so he is even more merciful towards people." He called him, placed the horn on his head, and the oil overflowed. Talut said: "Would you like to kill Jalut, and I will marry you to my daughter and place your seal over my kingdom?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you sensed in yourself anything by which you could strengthen yourself to kill him?" He said: "Yes. I am a shepherd, and when a lion or a leopard or a wolf comes and takes a sheep, I rise up against it, open its jaws to free the sheep, and break its neck." So Talut sent him back to his army.

David, peace be upon him, passed on his way by a stone, which called out to him: "O David, take me up, for I am the stone of Harun (Aaron), with which he killed such-and-such a king." So he took it up in his satchel (*mikhlah*). Then he passed by another stone, which said: "Take me up, for I am the stone of Musa (Moses), with which he killed such-and-such a king," so he took it up in his satchel. Then he passed by another stone, which said: "Take me up, for I am your stone with which you will kill Jalut." So he placed it in his satchel.

When the two sides lined up for battle, Jalut came forward and asked for single combat. David was chosen for him. Talut gave him a horse, armour, and weapons. David put on the weapons and mounted the horse, went a short distance, then turned back to the king. Those around him thought the boy had become frightened. He came and stood before the king, and the king said: "What is your matter?" He said: "If Allah does not help me, these weapons will avail me nothing. So let me fight as I wish." He said: "Do as you please." David took his satchel, slung it over his shoulder, took up the sling, and set off towards Jalut. Jalut was among the strongest and most powerful of men, and he used to defeat armies single-handedly. He had a helmet (*bayda*)[[Headgear worn in war.]] containing three hundred ratls of iron. When he looked at David, terror was cast into his heart, and he said to him: "Are you coming out to me?" He said: "Yes."

Jalut was on a piebald horse (*abqa*)[[Black and white, with the white markings (*tahjil*) reaching up to the thighs.]], wearing full armour. He said: "Have you come to me with a sling and a stone, as one comes to a dog?" He said: "Yes, you are worse than a dog." He said: "Without doubt, I will cut your flesh and divide it among the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky." David said: "Or rather, Allah will divide your flesh." Then David said: "In the name of the God of Ibrahim (Abraham)," and took out a stone. Then he took out another and said: "In the name of the God of Ishaq (Isaac)," and placed it in his sling. Then he took out a third and said: "In the name of the God of Ya'qub (Jacob)," and placed it in his sling. Then they all became one stone. David whirled the sling and hurled it, and Allah subjected the wind to him until the stone struck the nose of the helmet, penetrated his brain, and came out from the back of his neck, and it killed thirty men behind him. Allah, the Exalted, routed the army, and Jalut fell dead. David dragged him until he threw him before Talut. The Muslims rejoiced greatly, and they returned to the city safe and laden with booty. The people were mentioning David, so David came to Talut and said: "Fulfil for me what you promised me." He said: "Do you want the king's daughter without a dowry?" David said: "You did not stipulate a dowry for me, and I have nothing." He said: "I will not burden you with anything you cannot bear. You are a bold man, and in our vicinity are enemies of ours who are uncircumcised (*ghulf*)[[Plural of *aghlaf*, one who has not been circumcised.]]. If you kill two hundred of them and bring me their foreskins, I will marry you to my daughter." So he went out to them, and every time he killed one of them he strung its foreskin on a thread, until he had strung together all their foreskins. He brought them to Talut and threw them before him, and said: "Hand over my wife to me." So he married him to his daughter and placed his seal over his kingdom. The people inclined towards David, loved him, and mentioned him often. Talut envied him and wanted to kill him. A man called Dhu al-'Aynayn informed Talut's daughter about this, so she said to David: "You are going to be killed this night." He said: "And who will kill me?" She said: "My father." He said: "Have I committed any crime?" She said: "Someone who does not lie told me. And there is no harm to you in staying away tonight until you see the truth of that." He said: "If Allah has willed that, I cannot go out. But bring me a skin of wine (*ziqq*)[[The *ziqq* (with a kasra on the zay) is the skin of a goat, stripped from one hind leg, from the head and neck, then treated until it becomes a water-skin. They used it most for wine.]]." She brought it to him, and he placed it in his bed on the couch and covered it with a cloth, then he hid under the couch. Talut came in at midnight and said to her: "Where is your husband?" She said: "He is sleeping on the couch." So he struck it with the sword, and the wine spilled. When he smelled the scent of the drink, he said: "May Allah have mercy on David! How much he drinks wine!" and he left.

When morning came, David knew that he had not done anything. Talut said: "A man whom I have sought to harm is certainly not going to leave me alone until he takes his revenge upon me." So he strengthened his guards and chamberlains and bolted his doors. Then David came to him one night when the eyes were at rest. Allah, glorified is He, blinded the guards and opened the doors for him, so he entered upon him while he was sleeping on his bed. He placed an arrow by his head, an arrow by his feet, an arrow on his right, and an arrow on his left, then he left. When Talut awoke, he saw the arrows and recognised them. He said: "May Allah, the Exalted, have mercy on David. He is better than me. I had the upper hand over him and intended to kill him, but he had the upper hand over me and held back from me. Had he wished, he could have placed this arrow in my throat, and I am not one to be trusted." When the next night came, he came to him again, and Allah blinded the chamberlains. He entered upon him while he was sleeping, took the ewer of Talut from which he used to perform ablution and his cup from which he used to drink, cut some hairs from his beard and some threads from the hem of his garments, then he left and fled and hid himself. When Talut awoke and saw that, he set spies upon David and searched for him most intensely, but he could not find him. Then Talut rode out one day and found David walking in the wilderness. He said: "Today I will kill him." He galloped after him. David ran, and whenever he was frightened he could not be caught. He entered a cave, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed to a spider, and it spun a web over him. When Talut reached the cave and saw the spider's web, he said: "If he had entered here, he would have torn the spider's web," so he left it and went on. David set off and came to the mountain with the worshippers and worshipped there. The scholars and the devout spoke ill of Talut regarding David's affair. Talut then did not allow anyone who forbade him from killing David to live; he killed them, and he incited the killing of the scholars. He could not overcome any scholar among the Children of Israel whom he was able to kill without killing him. Until a woman who knew the Greatest Name of Allah was brought to him, and he ordered his baker to kill her. The baker had mercy on her and said: "Perhaps we will need a scholar," so he left her. Then repentance entered Talut's heart, and he regretted what he had done. He began to weep until the people had mercy on him.

Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 250–252 (part 2 of 2)

He would go out to the graves every night, weeping, and call out: "I implore Allah, any servant who knows that there is repentance for me, to inform me of it!" When he pressed them, a caller called out to him from the graves: "O Talut! Are you not content that you killed us, so that you now harm us even in death?" He wept and grieved all the more. The baker took pity on him and said: "What is wrong with you, O king?" He said: "Do you know of any scholar on earth whom I could ask whether there is repentance for me?" The baker said: "Your case is like that of a king who came to a village at nightfall. A rooster crowed, and he took it as an omen and said: 'Do not leave a single rooster in the village without slaughtering it.' When he wanted to sleep, he said to his companions: 'When the rooster crows, wake us so that we may set out before dawn.' They said to him: 'Have you left a single rooster whose voice we could hear? Rather, have you left a scholar on earth?'" So he grieved and wept all the more. When the baker saw this, he said to him: "What do you think? If I point you to a scholar, will you kill him?" He said: "No." So the baker bound him by a firm pledge, and informed him that a learned woman was with him. He said: "Take me to her, so that I may ask her whether there is repentance for me." She was from a household that knew the Greatest Name (al-Ism al-A'zam), and whenever their men died out, their women would hold this knowledge. When Talut reached the door, the baker said: "If she sees you, she will be terrified." So he left him behind him and entered alone to her, and said to her: "Am I not the one who has done you the greatest favour, having saved you from being killed and given you shelter?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Then I have a request of you: this is Talut, who asks whether there is repentance for him." She fainted from fear. He said to her: "He does not intend to kill you, but he asks you whether there is repentance for him." She said: "No, by Allah, I do not know of any repentance for Talut. But do you know the location of the grave of a prophet?" So he took them both to the grave of Ishmawil (Samuel). She prayed and supplicated, then called out: "O occupant of the grave!" Ishmawil came out of the grave, shaking the dust from his head. When he looked at the three of them, he said: "What is the matter with you? Has the Resurrection come?" She said: "No, but Talut asks you whether there is repentance for him." Ishmawil said: "O Talut, what have you done since I left?" He said: "I have left no evil undone, and I have come seeking repentance." He said: "How many sons do you have?" He said: "Ten men." He said: "I know of no repentance for you except that you renounce your kingdom, and go forth with your sons in the way of Allah, then send your sons forward so that they are killed before your eyes, and then you fight until you are killed as the last of them?" Then Ishmawil returned to the grave and fell dead. Talut returned, more grieved than ever, fearing that his son would not follow him. He wept until the lids of his eyes fell away, and his body wasted away. His sons came in to him, and he said to them: "What do you think? If I were thrown into the Fire, would you ransom me?" They said: "Yes, we would ransom you with whatever we are able." He said: "Then it is the Fire, if you do not do what I tell you." They said: "Then set it before us." He related the story to them. They said: "And you are going to be killed?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Then there is no good for us in life after you. Our souls are content with what you have asked." So he prepared himself with his wealth and his sons. His sons went forward first, and they were ten. They fought before him until they were killed. Then he himself charged after them until he was killed. The one who killed him came to Dawud to give him good news, saying: "I have killed your enemy." Dawud said: "You are not the one who will live after him." So he struck off his neck. The kingdom of Talut lasted forty years until he was killed. The Children of Israel came to Dawud, gave him the treasures of Talut, and made him king over themselves.

Al-Kalbi and al-Dahhak said: Dawud reigned for seven years after the killing of Talut, and the Children of Israel did not unite under one king except Dawud. This is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿And Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom﴾. "Wisdom" here means prophethood. Allah combined for Dawud both kingship and prophethood, which had not been combined before; rather, kingship was in one tribe and prophethood in another. It was also said: "kingdom and wisdom" means knowledge together with action. His words, may He be exalted: ﴿and taught him of what He willed﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: this means the craft of making coats of mail. He would make them and sell them, and he would eat only from the work of his hands. It was also said: it means the speech of birds, the speech of the hukl (that which has no audible sound) and of ants, and fine speech. It was also said: it refers to the Psalms (al-Zabur). It was also said: it refers to a beautiful voice and melodies. Allah did not give any of His creatures a voice like his. When he recited the Psalms, wild animals would draw near until he could take them by their necks, birds would shade him, listening attentively, the flowing water would become still, and the wind would be calm.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that Allah, exalted is He, gave him a chain attached to the Milky Way, its top at his hermitage (mihrab). Its strength was the strength of iron, its colour the colour of fire, its links circular and adorned with jewels, set with moist pearls. Whenever any event occurred in the air, the chain would ring, and Dawud would know of that event. Whoever was afflicted with a disease and touched it would be cured. After Dawud, peace be upon him, they would bring their disputes to it until it was taken up. Whoever wronged another and denied him a right would come to the chain. If he was truthful, he would stretch out his hand and grasp it; if he was lying, he could not reach it. This continued until deceit and trickery appeared among them. It is reported to us that one of their kings had entrusted a man with a precious jewel. When he asked for it back, the man denied it, and they took their dispute to the chain. The one who had the jewel went to a staff, hollowed it out, placed the jewel in it, and leaned on it until he came to the chain. The owner of the jewel said: "Return my deposit to me." The other said: "I do not know of any deposit of yours with me. If you are truthful, then take hold of the chain." He reached for it with his hand. It was said to the denier: "Stand up and you take hold of it." He said to the owner of the jewel: "Take my staff here and keep it safe until I take hold of the chain." So he took it from him. Then the denier stood up towards the chain and grasped it. The man said: "O Allah, if You know that this deposit which he claims from me has reached him, then bring the chain near to me." He stretched out his hand and grasped it. The people were astonished and doubted it. In the morning they found that Allah had taken up the chain.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling some people by means of others﴾. The people of Medina and Ya'qub read "difa'" (with an alif) here and in surah al-Hajj. The others read it without the alif, because no one can overpower Allah, and He alone is the Repeller. Whoever reads it with the alif says: repelling may come from one party, as in the Arabic saying: "May Allah repel from you the harm (ahsana Allahu 'anka al-difa')." Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "Were it not for Allah's repelling by means of the armies of the Muslims, the polytheists would have prevailed over the earth, killing the believers, and destroying the mosques and the lands." The rest of the exegetes said: "Were it not for Allah's repelling of the disbelievers and the wicked by means of believers and the righteous, the earth would have been destroyed with its inhabitants. But Allah repels the disbeliever by means of the believer, and the wicked by means of the righteous."

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Kharja informed us: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal informed us: Abu Humayd al-Himsi informed us: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Attar informed us: Hafs ibn Sulayman informed us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Wabara, from Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, repels calamity from a hundred households among the neighbours of a righteous Muslim on his account." Then he recited: "And were it not for Allah's repelling some people by means of others..." [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 5/374. In its chain is Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Attar, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared weak. Abu Dawud said: "acceptable in narration" (ja'iz al-hadith). Muhammad ibn Musaffa al-Himsi the hafiz said: "trustworthy." Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir and mentioned no criticism of him. Ibn Kathir, after attributing the hadith to al-Tabari, said: "This chain is weak, for Yahya ibn Sa'id is very weak" (Tafsir 1/537, Dar al-Arqam). Al-Haythami attributed it to al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat and said: "In it is Yahya ibn Sa'id, who is weak." See Majma' al-Zawa'id 8/163–164; Fayd al-Qadir 2/261.]] ﴿the earth would have been corrupted; but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.﴾

And when they came out to face Jalut (Goliath) and his forces, they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience and make firm our feet and help us against the disbelieving people.﴾ (Talut and his army, meaning the believers, went out to face Jalut and his army, meaning the polytheists.) The meaning of *baraza* is that they came out into the open (*al-biraz*) of the earth, which is the level, elevated ground. "Pour upon us" means "send down upon us" and "pour out upon us." "Firm our feet" means "firm our hearts."

﴿So they routed them by the permission of Allah, and David killed Jalut, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom, and taught him of what He willed. And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted; but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.﴾ (251) ﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers.﴾ (252)

﴿So they routed them by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, by the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted. ﴿And David killed Jalut﴾. As for the manner of his killing, the people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis)[[These reports, taken as a whole, are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives transmitted from Jewish and Christian sources). We have no need of them, since we have in our hands the Book and the Sunnah. Nothing in the Book of Allah or in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicates what they mention, and we have no need of any of this in understanding and reflecting upon the Qur'an, so do not pay them any heed... Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that this is among the Isra'iliyyat. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/537, Dar al-Arqam edition. Al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Abu Shahba, pp. 248–249.]] said: He crossed the river with Talut, among those who crossed.
