Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 265:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah﴾, meaning seeking the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿and for the firming of their souls﴾.

Qatadah said: "for the sake of reckoning (with Allah)" (ihtisab). Al-Sha'bi and al-Kalbi said: "for the affirmation (tasdiq) from their own souls," meaning they give out zakat cheerfully, with their souls, in certainty of the reward and in belief in Allah's promise, and they know that what they give out is better for them than what they leave behind. It was also said: "in certainty of Allah's replacement for them."

Ata' and Mujahid said: "yuthbitun," meaning they place their wealth (in the right place). Al-Hasan said: "When a man intended to give charity, he would verify it: if it was for Allah, he would carry it out, and if doubt mingled with it, he would withhold." According to this view, "tathbit" carries the meaning of "tathabbut" (verification), as in His saying: ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ (73:8), meaning tabattul (devotion).

﴿Like a garden﴾, meaning an orchard. Al-Mubarrad and al-Farra' said: if the orchard contains palm trees, it is a jannah; if it contains vines, it is a firdaws.

﴿On a height﴾. Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read "bi-rabwah," and "ila rabwah" in Surat al-Mu'minun, with a fatha on the ra'. The others read it with a damma. It means an elevated, level place through which rivers flow, so water does not overwhelm it and it is not cut off from water. He made it on a height because vegetation there is finer and more pure.

﴿Heavy rain strikes it﴾, meaning intense, abundant rain. ﴿So it yields its produce﴾, meaning its fruit. Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "ukulaha" with lightening (takhfif); the rest read it with emphasis (tathqil). Nafi' and Ibn Kathir additionally read "akulih" and "al-ukul" with lightening, and Abu 'Amr lightened "rusulana," "rusulakum," "rusulahum," and "subulana."

﴿Double﴾, meaning it doubled in its bearing. Ata' said: it bore in one year what others bear in two years. Ikrimah said: it bore twice in a year.

﴿But if heavy rain does not strike it, then light rain (tall)﴾, meaning a gentle, light drizzle, which is constant.

Al-Suddi said: it is dew. This is a parable that Allah struck for the work of the sincere believer. He says: just as this garden flourishes in every condition and does not fail, whether the rain is little or much, so Allah multiplies the charity of the sincere believer who neither reminds of it nor harms, whether his spending is little or much. This is because a drizzle that persists produces the effect of a heavy downpour.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 266–267 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Would any one of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it?﴾ This verse is connected to His statement, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reminders [of favor] and injury﴾. [His statement "Would any one of you wish (ayawaddu)" means: would any one of you love (ayuhibbu) that there be for him a garden, that is, an orchard of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it.] [[Omitted in B.]]

﴿For him therein is every [kind of] fruit, and he has been afflicted with old age while he has weak offspring﴾, meaning young children who are weak and incapable. ﴿Then it is struck by a fiery whirlwind (i'sar) and is burned﴾. The i'sar is the violent wind that rises toward the sky like a pillar; its plural is a'asir. ﴿In it is fire, and it is burned.﴾ This is a parable that Allah has struck for the deeds of the hypocrite and the one who shows off. It says: his deed, in its goodness, is like the goodness of the garden; he benefits from it as the owner of the garden benefits from the garden. Then, when he grows old or weak, and has weak children, and a fiery whirlwind strikes his garden and burns it, he becomes most in need of it and is too weak to restore it, because of his old age, and his children are too weak to restore it because of their youth. He finds nothing with which to support his children, and his children have nothing with which to support him. So they all remain bewildered and incapable, with no means in their hands. Likewise, Allah nullifies the deed of this hypocrite and this one who shows off, when there is no one to placate them [[In B: "mustatib" instead of "mughith".]] and there is no repentance and no reprieve.

Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, once said to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "About whom do you think this verse was revealed: ﴿Would any one of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾?" They said: "Allah knows best." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, became angry and said: "Say 'we know' or 'we do not know'." Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Within myself there is something about it, O Commander of the Faithful." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "My nephew, speak, and do not belittle yourself." Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "It is a parable struck for a deed." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "What deed?" Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "For the deed of the one who shows off." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "For a wealthy man who worships in obedience to Allah, Allah sends him Satan, and he commits sins until he drowns his deeds." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, the chapter of Surat al-Baqarah, on His statement (Would any one of you wish), 8/201–202.]] ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses that you may give thought﴾.

﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things﴾, meaning the best (khiyar). Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and Mujahid said: "from the lawful (halalat)." ﴿Of what you have earned﴾, through trade and craft. In this is an indication of the permissibility of earning, and that it is divided into good and bad.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Ya'la ibn Ubayd informed us: al-A'mash informed us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the best of what a man eats is from his earnings, and indeed his child is from his earnings." [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in Al-Buyu', chapter on urging earning, 7/240; Ibn Majah in Al-Tijarat, chapter on urging earning, 2/723; al-Darimi in Al-Buyu', chapter on earning and a man's work with his hands, 2/247; Ahmad, 6/31, 42, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her; Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (Mawarid al-Zam'an, no. 1091), p. 268; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 9/329. Its chain is sound.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Salih informed us: Abu Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, that he related to him from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "No one has ever eaten food better than what he eats from the work of his hand. Indeed, Dawud (David) used to eat only from the work of his hands." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Al-Buyu', chapter on a man's earning and work by his hand, 4/303. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 8/6.]]

Abu al-Qasim Yahya ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Kushmihani informed us: Najah ibn Yazid al-Muharibi informed us in Kufa: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaym al-Shaybani informed us: Ahmad ibn Hazim informed us: Yahya ibn Ubayd informed us: Aban ibn Ishaq informed us, from al-Sabbah ibn Muhammad ibn Murrah al-Hamdani, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A servant does not earn unlawful wealth and then give charity from it, and Allah accepts it from him; nor does he spend from it and then it is blessed for him; nor does he leave it behind him except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. Indeed, Allah does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed, the wicked does not erase the wicked." [[Narrated by Ahmad, 1/387, part of a hadith of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud; al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah, 8/10; part of it was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, 1/24, 2/447; al-Haythami mentioned it in al-Majma', 10/90, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it as a statement (mawquf), and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." Al-Albani weakened it in al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah, no. 2822, and in al-Mishkat, nos. 2771, 2994. In its chain is al-Sabbah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Hazim al-Bajali al-Ahmasi al-Kufi, who is weak; Ibn Hibban went to excess in weakening him (al-Taqrib).]]

Zakat is obligatory on trade goods according to most of the people of knowledge. After a year, one evaluates the merchandise and gives from its value a quarter of the tenth (2.5%), if its value reaches twenty dinars or two hundred dirhams. Samurah ibn Jundub said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to give charity from that which we prepare for sale." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, in Al-Zakat, chapter on merchandise when it is for trade, 2/175; al-Mundhiri and al-Bayhaqi remained silent about it, in al-Sunan, 4/146. Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis al-Habir: al-Daraqutni and al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Samurah from his father, and in its chain there is an unknown narrator.]]

And from Abu Amr ibn Himas that his father said: "I passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, while on my neck was a hide [[A skin.]] that I was carrying. Umar said: 'Will you not pay your zakat, O Himas?' I said: 'I have nothing but this, and a raw hide [[Plural of ihab, which is a hide before it is tanned.]] soaked in qarz [[Qarz: a well-known seed that comes from the acacia tree, with which hides are tanned.]].' He said: 'That is wealth, so put it down.' I put it down, and he estimated its value and took from it the zakat." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad, 1/229–230; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 4/147; and al-Daraqutni, 2/125. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar attributed it to Imam Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd al-Razzaq, and Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Sufyan, from Yahya ibn Sa'id; see al-Talkhis al-Habir, 2/180. Al-Albani weakened it in Irwa' al-Ghalil, 3/311, because Abu Amr ibn Himas is "unknown," as al-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan.]]

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And from what We have produced for you from the earth﴾. It has been said that this refers to paying the tithe ('ushr) on fruits and grains. The people of knowledge have agreed on the obligation of the tithe on palm trees and vineyards, and on what is eaten as staple grain, if it is irrigated by rain water or by a river whose water reaches it without cost. If it is irrigated by a water-wheel (saqiyah) or by a waterwheel with buckets (nadh), then half the tithe is due on it.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ: "For what the sky and springs water, or what is watered by a natural stream ('athari) [[The crop that is watered only by rainwater.]], the tithe is due; and for what is watered by irrigation (nadh), half the tithe is due." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Al-Zakat, chapter: the tithe on what is watered by rain water and by flowing water, 3/437. Muslim in Al-Zakat, chapter: what carries a tithe or half a tithe, no. 981, 2/675, from Jabir with different wording. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 6/42.]]

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Abd Allah ibn Nafi' informed us, from Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tammar, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Attab ibn Usayd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the zakat of grapes: "It is estimated (yukhras) just as palm trees are estimated, and then its zakat is paid in raisins, just as the zakat of palm trees is paid in dates." [[Al-Shafi'i, 1/243. Narrated by al-Nasa'i, Zakat, chapter on purchasing charity, 5/109; Ibn Majah, Zakat, chapter on estimating palm trees and grapes, 2/210–211; Abu Dawud, Zakat, chapter on estimating grapes, 2/210–211; al-Tirmidhi, Zakat, chapter on what has come regarding estimation, 3/306, and he said: "a hasan gharib hadith." Also al-Bayhaqi, 4/122; al-Daraqutni, 2/132; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 6/37. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis al-Habir, 2/171: "Its central narrator is Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Attab; Abu Dawud said he did not hear from him; Ibn al-Qani' said he did not meet him; al-Mundhiri said its disconnection is evident, for Sa'id was born in the caliphate of Umar, and Attab died the day Abu Bakr died, and Ibn Abd al-Barr preceded him in this. Abu Hatim said the sound report from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab is that the Prophet ﷺ commanded Attab: it is mursal (broken). This is the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq from al-Zuhri." Al-Nawawi said: "This hadith, although mursal, is strengthened by the statements of the Imams."]]

The people of knowledge differed regarding what is other than palm trees and vineyards, and other than the staple grains. A group held that there is no tithe on any of these; this is the view of Ibn Abi Layla and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him.

Al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i, and Malik, may Allah be pleased with them, said: it is obligatory on olives. Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the tithe is obligatory on all vegetables and herbs, like fruits, except hay (hashish) and firewood. Every fruit on which we have made zakat obligatory, it becomes due upon the appearance of ripeness (bud al-salah), and the time of payment is after picking and drying. Every grain on which we have made the tithe obligatory, its time of becoming due is when the grain hardens, and the time of payment is after threshing and cleaning. The tithe is not obligatory on any of these until it reaches five awsuq [[Plural of wasq, which is sixty sa' by the sa' of the Prophet ﷺ.]], according to most of the people of knowledge. According to Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, it is obligatory on every amount, small or large, of these.

Those who required the minimum threshold (nisab) argued with what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah al-Mazini, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no charity on less than five awsuq of dates; there is no charity on less than five uqiyah of silver; and there is no charity on less than five camels." [[Narrated by Muslim in Al-Zakat, no. 979, 2/673. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 5/499.]]

Yahya ibn Ubadah narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no charity on grain or dates until it reaches five awsuq." [[Narrated by Muslim in Al-Zakat, no. 979, 2/674. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 5/500.]] Others said: the verse refers to voluntary charity (tatawwu').

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Awanah informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No believer plants a plant or sows a crop, and then a person or a bird or an animal eats from it, except that it is a charity for him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Al-Harth wa al-Muzara'ah, chapter on the virtue of sowing and planting, 5/3, with the wording "No Muslim..." and also in Al-Adab. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 6/149.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 266–267 (part 2 of 2):

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not aim at﴾. Ibn Kathir, according to the transmission of al-Bazzi, read it with a doubled *ta'* (tashdid) when joined in recitation, in this word and in its counterparts, which number thirty-one places in the Qur'an. This is because in origin there are two *ta'*s, one of which was dropped. He restored the dropped one and assimilated (idgham) the two. The others read it with a single *ta'* (takhfif). Its meaning is: do not intend ﴿the bad, from which you spend﴾.

It is narrated from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: The Ansar used to bring, when the date harvest was gathered, clusters (aqna', plural of qinw, meaning a bunch of dates on its stalk) of dates and unripe dates (busr), and they would hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the poor emigrants (fuqara' al-Muhajirin) would eat from it. A man among them would deliberately bring a cluster of worthless dates (hashaf), thinking that it would be acceptable in the abundance of the clusters that were placed there. So this was revealed concerning those who did that: ﴿And do not aim at the bad﴾, that is, the worthless dates (hashaf) and the inferior.

Al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: They used to give in charity the worst of their fruits and the dregs of their wealth, and they would set aside the good for themselves. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad﴾, the inferior, ﴿from which you spend﴾. ﴿And you would not take it﴾, meaning the bad, ﴿except that you overlook in it﴾. Al-Ighmad is lowering the gaze (ghaḍḍ al-baṣar), and here it is intended as leniency and overlooking (al-tajawwuz wa al-musahala). Its meaning: if one of you had a right against a man, and he came to him with this, you would not accept it except while seeing that you had overlooked your right and left it.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: If you found it being sold in the market, you would not take it at the price of the good.

And it is narrated from al-Bara', who said: If that were presented to you as a gift, you would not accept it except with shame before its giver and with resentment. So how do you accept for others what you do not accept for yourselves? This applies when all of a person's wealth is good, so it is not permissible for him to give the inferior, because the recipients of the shares (ahl al-suhman) are partners in what he has. But if all of his wealth is inferior, then there is no harm in giving the inferior. ﴿And know that Allah is Free of need﴾ from your charities, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, praised in His actions.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 266–267 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Would any one of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it?﴾ This verse is connected to His statement, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reminders [of favor] and injury﴾. [His statement "Would any one of you wish (ayawaddu)" means: would any one of you love (ayuhibbu) that there be for him a garden, that is, an orchard of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it.] [[Omitted in B.]]

﴿For him therein is every [kind of] fruit, and he has been afflicted with old age while he has weak offspring﴾, meaning young children who are weak and incapable. ﴿Then it is struck by a fiery whirlwind (i'sar) and is burned﴾. The i'sar is the violent wind that rises toward the sky like a pillar; its plural is a'asir. ﴿In it is fire, and it is burned.﴾ This is a parable that Allah has struck for the deeds of the hypocrite and the one who shows off. It says: his deed, in its goodness, is like the goodness of the garden; he benefits from it as the owner of the garden benefits from the garden. Then, when he grows old or weak, and has weak children, and a fiery whirlwind strikes his garden and burns it, he becomes most in need of it and is too weak to restore it, because of his old age, and his children are too weak to restore it because of their youth. He finds nothing with which to support his children, and his children have nothing with which to support him. So they all remain bewildered and incapable, with no means in their hands. Likewise, Allah nullifies the deed of this hypocrite and this one who shows off, when there is no one to placate them [[In B: "mustatib" instead of "mughith".]] and there is no repentance and no reprieve.

Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, once said to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "About whom do you think this verse was revealed: ﴿Would any one of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾?" They said: "Allah knows best." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, became angry and said: "Say 'we know' or 'we do not know'." Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Within myself there is something about it, O Commander of the Faithful." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "My nephew, speak, and do not belittle yourself." Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "It is a parable struck for a deed." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "What deed?" Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "For the deed of the one who shows off." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "For a wealthy man who worships in obedience to Allah, Allah sends him Satan, and he commits sins until he drowns his deeds." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, the chapter of Surat al-Baqarah, on His statement (Would any one of you wish), 8/201–202.]] ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses that you may give thought﴾.

﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things﴾, meaning the best (khiyar). Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and Mujahid said: "from the lawful (halalat)." ﴿Of what you have earned﴾, through trade and craft. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Ya'la ibn Ubayd informed us: al-A'mash informed us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the best of what a man eats is from his earnings, and indeed his child is from his earnings." [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in Al-Buyu', chapter on urging earning, 7/240; Ibn Majah in Al-Tijarat, chapter on urging earning, 2/723; al-Darimi in Al-Buyu', chapter on earning and a man's work with his hands, 2/247; Ahmad, 6/31, 42, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her; Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (Mawarid al-Zam'an, no. 1091), p. 268; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 9/329. Its chain is sound.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Salih informed us: Abu Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, that he related to him from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "No one has ever eaten food better than what he eats from the work of his hand. Indeed, Dawud (David) used to eat only from the work of his hands." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Al-Buyu', chapter on a man's earning and work by his hand, 4/303. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 8/6.]]

Abu al-Qasim Yahya ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Kushmihani informed us: Najah ibn Yazid al-Muharibi informed us in Kufa: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaym al-Shaybani informed us: Ahmad ibn Hazim informed us: Yahya ibn Ubayd informed us: Aban ibn Ishaq informed us, from al-Sabbah ibn Muhammad ibn Murrah al-Hamdani, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A servant does not earn unlawful wealth and then give charity from it, and Allah accepts it from him; nor does he spend from it and then it is blessed for him; nor does he leave it behind him except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. Indeed, Allah does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed, the wicked does not erase the wicked." [[Narrated by Ahmad, 1/387, part of a hadith of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud; al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah, 8/10; part of it was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, 1/24, 2/447; al-Haythami mentioned it in al-Majma', 10/90, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it as a statement (mawquf), and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." Al-Albani weakened it in al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah, no. 2822, and in al-Mishkat, nos. 2771, 2994. In its chain is al-Sabbah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Hazim al-Bajali al-Ahmasi al-Kufi, who is weak; Ibn Hibban went to excess in weakening him (al-Taqrib).]]

Zakat is obligatory on trade goods according to most of the people of knowledge. After a year, one evaluates the merchandise and gives from its value a quarter of the tenth (2.5%), if its value reaches twenty dinars or two hundred dirhams. Samurah ibn Jundub said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to give charity from that which we prepare for sale." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, in Al-Zakat, chapter on merchandise when it is for trade, 2/175; al-Mundhiri and al-Bayhaqi remained silent about it, in al-Sunan, 4/146. Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis al-Habir: al-Daraqutni and al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Samurah from his father, and in its chain there is an unknown narrator.]]

And from Abu Amr ibn Himas that his father said: "I passed by Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, while on my neck was a hide [[A skin.]] that I was carrying. Umar said: 'Will you not pay your zakat, O Himas?' I said: 'I have nothing but this, and a raw hide [[Plural of ihab, which is a hide before it is tanned.]] soaked in qarz [[Qarz: a well-known seed that comes from the acacia tree, with which hides are tanned.]].' He said: 'That is wealth, so put it down.' I put it down, and he estimated its value and took from it the zakat." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in his Musnad, 1/229–230; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 4/147; and al-Daraqutni, 2/125. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar attributed it to Imam Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd al-Razzaq, and Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Sufyan, from Yahya ibn Sa'id; see al-Talkhis al-Habir, 2/180. Al-Albani weakened it in Irwa' al-Ghalil, 3/311, because Abu Amr ibn Himas is "unknown," as al-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan.]]

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And from what We have produced for you from the earth﴾. It has been said that this refers to paying the tithe ('ushr) on fruits and grains. The people of knowledge have agreed on the obligation of the tithe on palm trees and vineyards, and on what is eaten as staple grain, if it is irrigated by rain water or by a river whose water reaches it without cost. If it is irrigated by a water-wheel (saqiyah) or by a waterwheel with buckets (nadh), then half the tithe is due on it.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ: "For what the sky and springs water, or what is watered by a natural stream ('athari) [[The crop that is watered only by rainwater.]], the tithe is due; and for what is watered by irrigation (nadh), half the tithe is due." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Al-Zakat, chapter: the tithe on what is watered by rain water and by flowing water, 3/437. Muslim in Al-Zakat, chapter: what carries a tithe or half a tithe, no. 981, 2/675, from Jabir with different wording. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 6/42.]]

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Abd Allah ibn Nafi' informed us, from Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tammar, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Attab ibn Usayd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the zakat of grapes: "It is estimated (yukhras) just as palm trees are estimated, and then its zakat is paid in raisins, just as the zakat of palm trees is paid in dates." [[Al-Shafi'i, 1/243. Narrated by al-Nasa'i, Zakat, chapter on purchasing charity, 5/109; Ibn Majah, Zakat, chapter on estimating palm trees and grapes, 2/210–211; Abu Dawud, Zakat, chapter on estimating grapes, 2/210–211; al-Tirmidhi, Zakat, chapter on what has come regarding estimation, 3/306, and he said: "a hasan gharib hadith." Also al-Bayhaqi, 4/122; al-Daraqutni, 2/132; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 6/37. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis al-Habir, 2/171: "Its central narrator is Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Attab; Abu Dawud said he did not hear from him; Ibn al-Qani' said he did not meet him; al-Mundhiri said its disconnection is evident, for Sa'id was born in the caliphate of Umar, and Attab died the day Abu Bakr died, and Ibn Abd al-Barr preceded him in this. Abu Hatim said the sound report from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab is that the Prophet ﷺ commanded Attab: it is mursal (broken). This is the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq from al-Zuhri." Al-Nawawi said: "This hadith, although mursal, is strengthened by the statements of the Imams."]]

The people of knowledge differed regarding what is other than palm trees and vineyards, and other than the staple grains. A group held that there is no tithe on any of these; this is the view of Ibn Abi Layla and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him.

Al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i, and Malik, may Allah be pleased with them, said: it is obligatory on olives. Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the tithe is obligatory on all vegetables and herbs, like fruits, except hay (hashish) and firewood. Every fruit on which we have made zakat obligatory, it becomes due upon the appearance of ripeness (bud al-salah), and the time of payment is after picking and drying. Every grain on which we have made the tithe obligatory, its time of becoming due is when the grain hardens, and the time of payment is after threshing and cleaning. The tithe is not obligatory on any of these until it reaches five awsuq [[Plural of wasq, which is sixty sa' by the sa' of the Prophet ﷺ.]], according to most of the people of knowledge. According to Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, it is obligatory on every amount, small or large, of these.

Those who required the minimum threshold (nisab) argued with what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'ah al-Mazini, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no charity on less than five awsuq of dates; there is no charity on less than five uqiyah of silver; and there is no charity on less than five camels." [[Narrated by Muslim in Al-Zakat, no. 979, 2/673. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 5/499.]]

Yahya ibn Ubadah narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no charity on grain or dates until it reaches five awsuq." [[Narrated by Muslim in Al-Zakat, no. 979, 2/674. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 5/500.]] Others said: the verse refers to voluntary charity (tatawwu').

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Awanah informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No believer plants a plant or sows a crop, and then a person or a bird or an animal eats from it, except that it is a charity for him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Al-Harth wa al-Muzara'ah, chapter on the virtue of sowing and planting, 5/3, with the wording "No Muslim..." and also in Al-Adab. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 6/149.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 266–267 (part 2 of 2):

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not aim at﴾. Ibn Kathir, according to the transmission of al-Bazzi, read it with a doubled *ta'* (tashdid) when joined in recitation, in this word and in its counterparts, which number thirty-one places in the Qur'an. This is because in origin there are two *ta'*s, one of which was dropped. He restored the dropped one and assimilated (idgham) the two. The others read it with a single *ta'* (takhfif). Its meaning is: do not intend ﴿the bad, from which you spend﴾.

It is narrated from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: The Ansar used to bring, when the date harvest was gathered, clusters (aqna', plural of qinw, meaning a bunch of dates on its stalk) of dates and unripe dates (busr), and they would hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the poor emigrants (fuqara' al-Muhajirin) would eat from it. A man among them would deliberately bring a cluster of worthless dates (hashaf), thinking that it would be acceptable in the abundance of the clusters that were placed there. So this was revealed concerning those who did that: ﴿And do not aim at the bad﴾, that is, the worthless dates (hashaf) and the inferior.

Al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: They used to give in charity the worst of their fruits and the dregs of their wealth, and they would set aside the good for themselves. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not aim at the bad﴾, the inferior, ﴿from which you spend﴾. ﴿And you would not take it﴾, meaning the bad, ﴿except that you overlook in it﴾. Al-Ighmad is lowering the gaze (ghaḍḍ al-baṣar), and here it is intended as leniency and overlooking (al-tajawwuz wa al-musahala). Its meaning: if one of you had a right against a man, and he came to him with this, you would not accept it except while seeing that you had overlooked your right and left it.

Al-Hasan and Qatada said: If you found it being sold in the market, you would not take it at the price of the good.

And it is narrated from al-Bara', who said: If that were presented to you as a gift, you would not accept it except with shame before its giver and with resentment. So how do you accept for others what you do not accept for yourselves? This applies when all of a person's wealth is good, so it is not permissible for him to give the inferior, because the recipients of the shares (ahl al-suhman) are partners in what he has. But if all of his wealth is inferior, then there is no harm in giving the inferior. ﴿And know that Allah is Free of need﴾ from your charities, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, praised in His actions.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 268–269:

﴿The Satan threatens you with poverty﴾. That is, he frightens you with poverty. It is said: "I promised him good (wa'adtuhu khayran) and I threatened him with evil (wa'adtuhu sharran)." God Most High said regarding good: ﴿God has promised you many spoils﴾ (20 - al-Fath), and regarding evil: ﴿The Fire God has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ (72 - al-Hajj). When neither good nor evil is mentioned, you say, for good, "wa'adtuhu," and for evil, "awadtuhu." Poverty is bad condition and scarcity of means. Its root is from the breaking of the spine (kasr al-fiqar). The meaning of the verse is: the Satan frightens you with poverty and says to a man, "Hold on to your wealth, for if you give it in charity you will become poor." ﴿And he commands you to indecency﴾, that is, to stinginess and withholding zakat. Al-Kalbi said: every instance of "al-fahsha'" (indecency) in the Qur'an means fornication, except this one. ﴿But God promises you forgiveness from Him﴾, that is, for your sins, ﴿and bounty﴾, that is, provision in replacement. ﴿God is All-Embracing﴾, Rich, ﴿All-Knowing﴾.

Ḥassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us; Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us; Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us; Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us; 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us; Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Most High, says: 'Son of Adam, spend, and I will spend upon you.'" And he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The right hand of Allah is full; its contents are not diminished by spending. It is constantly flowing (saḥḥa')[[With two unpointed letters, doubled and with a long vowel; meaning constantly flowing.]] by night and day. Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? Yet what is in His right hand has not decreased." He said: "His Throne is upon the water, and in His other hand is the scale (al-qist), He raises and lowers." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in the Tafsir of Surah Hud, chapter "And His Throne was upon the water," 8/352, and in Tawhid. Muslim: in Zakat, chapter on urging spending and giving the spender glad tidings of replacement, no. (993), 2/690. The author: in Sharh al-Sunna: 6/154–155.]]

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us; Hisham ibn 'Urwa informed us, from Fatima bint al-Mundhir, from Asma', that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Spend, and do not count, lest Allah count against you; and do not hoard, lest Allah withhold from you."[[Al-Ii'a' means putting something into a container; its root meaning is preservation.]] [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in Hibah, chapter on a woman's gift to someone other than her husband and her manumission when she is married, 5/217. Muslim: in Zakat, chapter on urging spending and disliking counting, no. (1029), 2/713. The author: in Sharh al-Sunna: 6/154.]]

God Most High says: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾. Al-Suddi said: it is prophethood. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and Qatada said: it is knowledge of the Qur'an: its abrogating and abrogated verses (naskh, abrogation), its clear and ambiguous verses, its earlier and later verses, its lawful and unlawful matters, and its parables. Al-Dahhak said: it is the Qur'an and understanding of it. He said: "In the Qur'an there are one hundred and nine abrogating and abrogated verses, and a thousand verses on lawful and unlawful matters. The believers may not leave them until they learn them. Do not be like the people of Nahrawan, who interpreted verses of the Qur'an against the People of the Qibla, when they were revealed about the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab). They ignored their knowledge, so they shed blood with them, plundered wealth, and testified against us to misguidance. So hold fast to knowledge of the Qur'an, for whoever knows what God revealed it for will not differ regarding any part of it."

Mujahid said: it is the Qur'an, knowledge and jurisprudence. Ibn Abi Najih narrated from him: correctness in speech and action. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: knowing the meanings of things and understanding them.

﴿And whoever is given wisdom﴾: in the place of nominative case as an impersonal passive (ma lam yusamma fa'iluhu), and "al-hikma" (wisdom) is its predicate.[[See: al-Tibyan fi I'rab al-Qur'an by al-'Ukbari: 1/220.]] Ya'qub read "yu'ti al-hikma" with a kasra on the ta' (yu'ti), meaning: whoever God gives wisdom to; this is the reading of al-A'mash. And it is reported from al-Hasan: "whoever is given wisdom": he said: scrupulousness (al-wara') in the religion of God. ﴿Then he has been given much good. And none will be reminded﴾, that is, be admonished, ﴿except those of understanding﴾, those possessing intellects.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 268–269:

﴿The Satan threatens you with poverty﴾. That is, he frightens you with poverty. It is said: "I promised him good (wa'adtuhu khayran) and I threatened him with evil (wa'adtuhu sharran)." God Most High said regarding good: ﴿God has promised you many spoils﴾ (20 - al-Fath), and regarding evil: ﴿The Fire God has promised to those who disbelieve﴾ (72 - al-Hajj). 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us; Hisham ibn 'Urwa informed us, from Fatima bint al-Mundhir, from Asma', that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Spend, and do not count, lest Allah count against you; and do not hoard, lest Allah withhold from you."[[Al-Ii'a' means putting something into a container; its root meaning is preservation.]] [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in Hibah, chapter on a woman's gift to someone other than her husband and her manumission when she is married, 5/217. Muslim: in Zakat, chapter on urging spending and disliking counting, no. (1029), 2/713. The author: in Sharh al-Sunna: 6/154.]]

God Most High says: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾. Al-Suddi said: it is prophethood. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and Qatada said: it is knowledge of the Qur'an: its abrogating and abrogated verses (naskh, abrogation), its clear and ambiguous verses, its earlier and later verses, its lawful and unlawful matters, and its parables. Al-Dahhak said: it is the Qur'an and understanding of it. He said: "In the Qur'an there are one hundred and nine abrogating and abrogated verses, and a thousand verses on lawful and unlawful matters. The believers may not leave them until they learn them. Do not be like the people of Nahrawan, who interpreted verses of the Qur'an against the People of the Qibla, when they were revealed about the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab). They ignored their knowledge, so they shed blood with them, plundered wealth, and testified against us to misguidance. So hold fast to knowledge of the Qur'an, for whoever knows what God revealed it for will not differ regarding any part of it."

Mujahid said: it is the Qur'an, knowledge and jurisprudence. Ibn Abi Najih narrated from him: correctness in speech and action. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: knowing the meanings of things and understanding them.

﴿And whoever is given wisdom﴾: in the place of nominative case as an impersonal passive (ma lam yusamma fa'iluhu), and "al-hikma" (wisdom) is its predicate.[[See: al-Tibyan fi I'rab al-Qur'an by al-'Ukbari: 1/220.]] Ya'qub read "yu'ti al-hikma" with a kasra on the ta' (yu'ti), meaning: whoever God gives wisdom to; this is the reading of al-A'mash. And it is reported from al-Hasan: "whoever is given wisdom": he said: scrupulousness (al-wara') in the religion of God. ﴿Then he has been given much good. And none will be reminded﴾, that is, be admonished, ﴿except those of understanding﴾, those possessing intellects.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 270–272:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whatever you spend of expenditure﴾ in what Allah has enjoined upon you, ﴿or whatever vow you vow﴾, that is, what you have made obligatory upon yourselves in obedience to Allah and then fulfilled, ﴿indeed Allah knows it﴾, He preserves it until He rewards you for it. He said "yaʻlamuhu" (He knows it), and did not say "yaʻlamuhā" (He knows them), because He referred it to the latter of the two (expenditure and vow), as in His saying: ﴿And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it onto an innocent person﴾ (4:112). If you wish, you may take it as referring to "mā" (whatever), as in His saying: ﴿And what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom, He admonishes you by it﴾ (2:231), and He did not say "bihimā" (by both). ﴿And for the wrongdoers﴾, those who place charity in other than its proper place, out of showing off, or who give charity from unlawful wealth, ﴿there are no helpers﴾, aides who would repel the punishment of Allah from them. The word "anṣār" is the plural of "naṣīr," like "sharīf" and "ashrāf."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you disclose your charities﴾, that is, display them, ﴿then how excellent it is﴾, that is: how excellent a practice it is. "Mā" is in the nominative position, and "hiya" (it) is in the accusative position, just as you say "niʻma al-rajul rajulan" (how excellent the man is, a man). When it is definite, it becomes nominative, so you say "niʻma al-rajul Zayd" (how excellent the man is: Zayd). Its origin is "niʻma mā," and it was joined. The people of Medina other than Warsh, Abu ʻAmr and Abu Bakr recited "fa-niʻmā" with a kasra on the nun and a sukun on the ʻayn. Ibn ʻĀmir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited with a fatha on the nun and a kasra on the ʻayn. Ibn Kathir and Nafi' (in the transmission of Warsh), Ya'qub and Hafs recited with a kasra on both. All of these are valid dialects, and likewise in Surat al-Nisa'.

﴿And if you conceal them﴾, keep them secret, ﴿and give them to the poor﴾, that is, give them to the poor in secret, ﴿it is better for you﴾ and more virtuous. Each is accepted when the intention is sincere, but the secret charity is more excellent. And in a hadith: "Secret charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Anas ibn Malik in the Book of Zakat, chapter on the virtue of charity ("Indeed charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord and averts a bad death"), and he said: this is a strange hadith from this route, and in its chain is ʻAbd Allah ibn ʻIsa al-Khazzaz, who is munkar al-hadith. Al-Nasa'i said: he is not trustworthy. See Mizan al-I'tidal. It is also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat, more extended, from Mu'awiya ibn Haydah, in which is Sadaqa ibn ʻAbd Allah, deemed trustworthy by Duhaym but weakened by a group. Also in al-Saghir and al-Awsat from Ja'far, in which is Asram ibn Hawshab, who is weak. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah.]]

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi, who said: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, who said: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Habib ibn ʻAbd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn ʻAsim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri or from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seven whom Allah shades in His shadow on the day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler; a young man who grew up in the worship of Allah, the Exalted; a man whose heart is attached to the mosque when he leaves it until he returns to it; two men who love each other for the sake of Allah, meeting and parting on that basis; a man who remembers Allah in solitude and his eyes overflow; a man who is invited by a woman of rank and beauty and says: 'Indeed I fear Allah'; and a man who gives charity and conceals it, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Adhan, chapter on one who sits in the mosque awaiting prayer and the virtue of mosques, 2/143. And Muslim in the Book of Zakat, chapter on the virtue of concealing charity, no. (1031), 2/715. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/354.]]

It is said: the verse refers to voluntary charity; as for obligatory zakat, displaying it is better so that people may follow suit, just as the prescribed prayer in congregation is better, while the voluntary prayer at home is [better]. It is also said: the verse refers to obligatory zakat, where concealment was better in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but in our time displaying it is better, so that suspicion is not cast upon it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds﴾. Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra and Abu Bakr recited with a nun and a raised ra, meaning "and We remove." Ibn ʻĀmir and Hafs recited with a ya' and a raised ra, meaning "and Allah removes." The people of Medina, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited with a nun and a jazm, in conjunction with the fa' in His saying "fa-huwa khayrun lakum," because its position is jussive as a conditional response. As for His saying "wa-min sayyi'atikum," it is said that "min" is extra, its implication being "We remove your misdeeds"; and it is said it is for specification and partitioning, meaning: We remove the minor sins. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾.

﴿It is not upon you, [O Muhammad], to guide them﴾. Al-Kalbi said: the cause of revelation of this verse was that some Muslims had relatives and in-laws among the Jews, and they used to spend on them before they embraced Islam. When they became Muslims, they disliked spending on them and wanted them to become Muslims. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 83, with its chain from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.]]: they used to give charity to poor people of the dhimmis; when the poor among the Muslims increased, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade giving charity to the polytheists so that need would drive them to enter Islam. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾, so that you withhold charity from them to make them enter Islam out of their need for it. ﴿But Allah guides whom He wills﴾, and by this He meant the guidance of success (tawfiq). As for the guidance of clarification and invitation, it was upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So they were given after the revelation of the verse.

﴿And whatever you spend of good﴾, that is, of wealth, ﴿it is for yourselves﴾, that is, you do it for your own benefit. ﴿And you do not spend except seeking the Face of Allah﴾. "Wa-mā" here is a negation (jaḥd); its wording is a negation and its meaning a prohibition, that is: do not spend except seeking the Face of Allah. ﴿And whatever you spend of good﴾ is a conditional like the first, and for this reason the nun is dropped from both. ﴿It will be repaid to you﴾, that is, its reward will be fully given to you; its meaning is: it will be rendered to you, and for this reason "ilā" (to) entered upon it. ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾, you will not be deprived of any of the reward of your deeds. This applies to voluntary charity; Allah permitted that it be placed among the people of Islam and the dhimmis. As for obligatory charity, it is not permitted to be placed except among Muslims, namely the categories of recipients mentioned in Surat al-Tawbah.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 270–272:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whatever you spend of expenditure﴾ in what Allah has enjoined upon you, ﴿or whatever vow you vow﴾, that is, what you have made obligatory upon yourselves in obedience to Allah and then fulfilled, ﴿indeed Allah knows it﴾, He preserves it until He rewards you for it. He said "yaʻlamuhu" (He knows it), and did not say "yaʻlamuhā" (He knows them), because He referred it to the latter of the two (expenditure and vow), as in His saying: ﴿And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it onto an innocent person﴾ (4:112). If you wish, you may take it as referring to "mā" (whatever), as in His saying: ﴿And what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom, He admonishes you by it﴾ (2:231), and He did not say "bihimā" (by both). ﴿And for the wrongdoers﴾, those who place charity in other than its proper place, out of showing off, or who give charity from unlawful wealth, ﴿there are no helpers﴾, aides who would repel the punishment of Allah from them. The word "anṣār" is the plural of "naṣīr," like "sharīf" and "ashrāf."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you disclose your charities﴾, that is, display them, ﴿then how excellent it is﴾, that is: how excellent a practice it is. "Mā" is in the nominative position, and "hiya" (it) is in the accusative position, just as you say "niʻma al-rajul rajulan" (how excellent the man is, a man). When it is definite, it becomes nominative, so you say "niʻma al-rajul Zayd" (how excellent the man is: Zayd). Its origin is "niʻma mā," and it was joined. The people of Medina other than Warsh, Abu ʻAmr and Abu Bakr recited "fa-niʻmā" with a kasra on the nun and a sukun on the ʻayn. Ibn ʻĀmir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited with a fatha on the nun and a kasra on the ʻayn. Ibn Kathir and Nafi' (in the transmission of Warsh), Ya'qub and Hafs recited with a kasra on both. All of these are valid dialects, and likewise in Surat al-Nisa'.

﴿And if you conceal them﴾, keep them secret, ﴿and give them to the poor﴾, that is, give them to the poor in secret, ﴿it is better for you﴾ and more virtuous. Each is accepted when the intention is sincere, but the secret charity is more excellent. And in a hadith: "Secret charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Anas ibn Malik in the Book of Zakat, chapter on the virtue of charity ("Indeed charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord and averts a bad death"), and he said: this is a strange hadith from this route, and in its chain is ʻAbd Allah ibn ʻIsa al-Khazzaz, who is munkar al-hadith. Al-Nasa'i said: he is not trustworthy. See Mizan al-I'tidal. It is also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat, more extended, from Mu'awiya ibn Haydah, in which is Sadaqa ibn ʻAbd Allah, deemed trustworthy by Duhaym but weakened by a group. Also in al-Saghir and al-Awsat from Ja'far, in which is Asram ibn Hawshab, who is weak. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah.]]

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi, who said: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, who said: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Habib ibn ʻAbd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn ʻAsim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri or from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seven whom Allah shades in His shadow on the day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler; a young man who grew up in the worship of Allah, the Exalted; a man whose heart is attached to the mosque when he leaves it until he returns to it; two men who love each other for the sake of Allah, meeting and parting on that basis; a man who remembers Allah in solitude and his eyes overflow; a man who is invited by a woman of rank and beauty and says: 'Indeed I fear Allah'; and a man who gives charity and conceals it, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Adhan, chapter on one who sits in the mosque awaiting prayer and the virtue of mosques, 2/143. And Muslim in the Book of Zakat, chapter on the virtue of concealing charity, no. (1031), 2/715. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 2/354.]]

It is said: the verse refers to voluntary charity; as for obligatory zakat, displaying it is better so that people may follow suit, just as the prescribed prayer in congregation is better, while the voluntary prayer at home is [better]. It is also said: the verse refers to obligatory zakat, where concealment was better in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but in our time displaying it is better, so that suspicion is not cast upon it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds﴾. Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra and Abu Bakr recited with a nun and a raised ra, meaning "and We remove." Ibn ʻĀmir and Hafs recited with a ya' and a raised ra, meaning "and Allah removes." The people of Medina, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited with a nun and a jazm, in conjunction with the fa' in His saying "fa-huwa khayrun lakum," because its position is jussive as a conditional response. As for His saying "wa-min sayyi'atikum," it is said that "min" is extra, its implication being "We remove your misdeeds"; and it is said it is for specification and partitioning, meaning: We remove the minor sins. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾.

﴿It is not upon you, [O Muhammad], to guide them﴾. Al-Kalbi said: the cause of revelation of this verse was that some Muslims had relatives and in-laws among the Jews, and they used to spend on them before they embraced Islam. When they became Muslims, they disliked spending on them and wanted them to become Muslims. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 83, with its chain from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.]]: they used to give charity to poor people of the dhimmis; when the poor among the Muslims increased, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade giving charity to the polytheists so that need would drive them to enter Islam. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾, so that you withhold charity from them to make them enter Islam out of their need for it. ﴿But Allah guides whom He wills﴾, and by this He meant the guidance of success (tawfiq). As for the guidance of clarification and invitation, it was upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So they were given after the revelation of the verse.

﴿And whatever you spend of good﴾, that is, of wealth, ﴿it is for yourselves﴾, that is, you do it for your own benefit. ﴿And you do not spend except seeking the Face of Allah﴾. "Wa-mā" here is a negation (jaḥd); its wording is a negation and its meaning a prohibition, that is: do not spend except seeking the Face of Allah. ﴿And whatever you spend of good﴾ is a conditional like the first, and for this reason the nun is dropped from both. ﴿It will be repaid to you﴾, that is, its reward will be fully given to you; its meaning is: it will be rendered to you, and for this reason "ilā" (to) entered upon it. ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾, you will not be deprived of any of the reward of your deeds. This applies to voluntary charity; Allah permitted that it be placed among the people of Islam and the dhimmis. As for obligatory charity, it is not permitted to be placed except among Muslims, namely the categories of recipients mentioned in Surat al-Tawbah.
