Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 273–274:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For the poor who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾. The scholars differed concerning the position of this lam (the particle "li-," "for"). It was said that it is connected to the position of the lam in His saying "then it is for yourselves," as if He said: "And whatever good you spend, it is for the poor, and you only spend for yourselves." It was also said that its meaning is the charities mentioned earlier. It was said that its predicate is omitted, its estimate being: "For the poor whose description is such-and-such is a due and an obligation." They are the poor among the Emigrants (Muhajirun), who numbered about four hundred men. They had no dwellings in Medina and no tribes, and they were in the mosque learning the Qur'an and cracking date-pits (yarda'un, "they crack") by day. They would go out with every expedition (sariyyah) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched, and they were the People of the Suffah (Ashab al-Suffah). So Allah, the Exalted, urged the people on their behalf, and whoever had surplus would bring it to them in the evening.

﴿Who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾. Concerning this there are several opinions. Qatadah said, and it is the best of them: they confined themselves to jihad in the way of Allah ﴿they cannot go about in the land﴾, meaning they have no leisure for trade and seeking livelihood, and they are the People of the Suffah whom we mentioned. It was said: they confined themselves to obedience to Allah. It was said: its meaning is that poverty and want restrained them from jihad in the way of Allah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are a people who were struck by wounds with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in jihad in the way of Allah, so they became disabled; illness and chronic disability restricted them from going about in the way of Allah for jihad. Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is that, because of how much they fought, the whole earth became a war against them, so they cannot go about in the land because of the multitude of their enemies.

﴿Whom the ignorant one thinks to be rich﴾ — Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Hamzah read yahsabuhum with a fatha on the sin, and the others read it with a kasra. ﴿Because of their abstinence﴾, meaning because of their restraint from asking and their contentment. Whoever does not know their condition thinks they are rich. Al-ta'affuf is the tafa"ul form from al-'iffah, which is restraint. One says "'affa 'an al-shay'" when he refrains from it, and "ta'affafa" when he exerts effort in withholding.

﴿You recognize them by their mark﴾. Al-simaa, al-simiyaa and al-simah all mean the sign by which a thing is known. The scholars differed about its meaning here. Mujahid said: it is humility and modesty. Al-Suddi said: the trace of hardship from need and poverty. Al-Dahhak said: the yellowness of their complexions from hunger and harm. It was also said: the shabbiness of their garments. ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾. 'Ata' said: if they have lunch, they do not ask for dinner, and if they have dinner, they do not ask for lunch. It was also said: its meaning is that they do not ask people at all, because He said "from abstinence," and abstinence is the leaving of asking; and because He said "you recognize them by their mark," and if asking were part of their conduct, recognizing them by a sign would not be necessary. So the meaning of the verse is: there is no asking from them in which persistence would occur. Al-ilhaf is insistence and obstinacy.

We were informed by Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri, who was informed by Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Isma'ili, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, who was informed by Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam, who was informed by Anas ibn 'Iyad, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "For one of you to take his rope, go and bring a bundle of firewood on his back, and Allah thereby keeps his face (from asking), is better for him than to ask people, whether they give him or refuse him." (ﷺ) [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Zakat, chapter: Seeking to abstain from asking, 3/335. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 6/112-113.]

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi, who was informed by Zahir ibn Ahmad, who was informed by Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi, who was informed by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The needy one is not this wanderer who goes around among people, whom a morsel or two morsels turn away, or a date or two dates." They said: "Who then is the needy one, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who does not find sufficiency so that it suffices him, and who is not noticed so that charity is given to him, and who does not stand up and ask people." (ﷺ) [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Zakat, chapter: The saying of Allah, the Exalted (They do not ask people persistently), 3/340, and in al-Tafsir. And Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter: The needy one who does not find sufficiency and is not noticed so that charity is given to him, no. (1039), 2/719. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/86.]

It is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyyah or its equivalent, has asked persistently." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Zakat, chapter: Who is given from charity and the limit of sufficiency, 2/229, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri with the wording "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyyah has been persistent," and al-Mundhiri remained silent on it. And al-Nasa'i in al-Zakat, chapter: If he does not have dirhams but has their equivalent, 5/98-99. And Ahmad: 4/36 and 5/430, the wording being his, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar from a man of Banu Asad. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/84, and its chain is sound.]

We were informed by Abu Sa'id 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri, who was informed by my grandfather Abu Sahl 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ibn 'Adafir, who was informed by Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abbad al-Dabari, who was informed by 'Abd al-Razzaq, who was informed by Ma'mar, from Harun ibn Riyab, from Kinanah al-'Adawi, from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq, who said: I undertook a guarantee (himalah) among my people, so I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have undertaken a guarantee among my people, and I came to you so that you might help me with it." He said: "Rather, we will bear it on your behalf, O Qabisah, and pay it to them from the charity." Then he said: "O Qabisah, asking is forbidden except in one of three cases: a man struck by a calamity (jaihah), which destroyed his wealth, so he may ask until he attains a means of livelihood, then he withholds; and a man struck by need until three men of sound judgment from his people testify that he has been struck by need and that asking has become lawful for him, so he may ask until he attains a means of livelihood, then he withholds; and a man who undertook a guarantee, so he may ask until he has completed it, then he withholds. Anything other than that is unlawful gain (suht), which its possessor consumes as unlawful gain." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter: Whom asking is lawful for, no. (1044), 2/722, with similar wording. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/122 with the wording: "Asking is not lawful except for three: a man who undertook a guarantee between people; a man struck by a calamity that destroyed his wealth, so he may ask until he attains a sufficiency of livelihood; and a man struck by poverty until three men of sound judgment from his people testify that he has been struck by need and that asking has become lawful for him. Whatever other than this of requests is unlawful gain."]

We were informed by Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi, who was informed by Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who was informed by Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi, who was informed by Abu 'Isa Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, who was informed by Qutaybah, who was informed by Shurayk, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever asks people while he has what suffices him, will come on the Day of Resurrection with scratches (khumush) or abrasions (khudush) or lacerations (kudut) on his face." [Al-khumush is like al-khudush in meaning, and al-kudut are the traces of abrasions; every trace of scratching, biting or the like is kudut.]

It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what suffices him? He said: "Fifty dirhams, or their value in gold." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Zakat, chapter: Who is given from charity and the limit of sufficiency, 2/226; see what al-Mundhiri said in his abridgment. And al-Tirmidhi in al-Zakat, chapter: Who is lawfully given zakat, 3/313-314, from Ibn Mas'ud, and he said: the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud is a hasan hadith, and Shu'bah spoke about Hakim ibn Jubayr on account of this hadith. Ibn Hajar said: weak, accused of Shi'ism, of the fifth tier (Taqrib). And Ibn Majah in al-Zakat, chapter: Who asks while having a means of support, 1/589, and al-Albani authenticated it in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah, no. (499), and in Sahih Ibn Majah, no. (1490). And al-Darimi in al-Zakat, chapter 15: Who is lawfully given charity, 1/386. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/83.]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever good you spend﴾, of wealth, ﴿indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾, and He will reward it. [The phrase "wa 'alayhi majaz" is noted here.]

﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly﴾. It was narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: This verse was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. He had four dirhams and owned nothing else; he gave one dirham by night, one by day, one secretly and one openly. [Narrated by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 86, with a sound chain.]

And from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: When ﴿For the poor who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾ was revealed, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf sent many dinars to the People of the Suffah, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, sent a wasq of dates in the middle of the night. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning both of them ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day﴾, the verse. By "by day, openly" is meant the charity of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and by "by night, secretly" is meant the charity of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Umamah, Abu al-Darda', Makhul and al-Awza'i said: it was revealed concerning those who tie horses for jihad, for they are fed by night and by day, secretly and openly. [Al-Tabarani and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uraib, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: this verse was revealed concerning the people of horses; Yazid and his father are unknown. And 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated with a weak chain from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: this verse was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: he had four dirhams... And Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn al-Musayyib that he said: the verse was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan in their spending in the army of hardship (jaysh al-'usrah). (See: Lubab al-Nuqul of al-Suyuti, p. 118, in the margin of al-Jalalayn; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 84-85.)]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was informed by 'Ali ibn Hafs, who was informed by Ibn al-Mubarak, who was informed by Talhah ibn Abi Sa'id, who said: I heard Sa'id al-Maqburi narrate that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever keeps a horse in the way of Allah, out of faith in Allah and belief in His promise, then its satiety, its watering, its dung and its urine are in his scales on the Day of Resurrection." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter: Whoever keeps a horse in the way of Allah, 6/57, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 10/388.]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then for them is their reward with their Lord﴾. Al-Akhfash said: the predicate was introduced with the fa' because "alladhina" carries the meaning of "man," and the response of "man" is introduced with the fa' as the response of a conditional. Or the meaning of the verse is: whoever spends such-and-such, then for him is his reward with his Lord. ﴿And no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 273–274:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For the poor who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾. The scholars differed concerning the position of this lam (the particle "li-," "for"). It was said that it is connected to the position of the lam in His saying "then it is for yourselves," as if He said: "And whatever good you spend, it is for the poor, and you only spend for yourselves." It was also said that its meaning is the charities mentioned earlier. It was said that its predicate is omitted, its estimate being: "For the poor whose description is such-and-such is a due and an obligation." They are the poor among the Emigrants (Muhajirun), who numbered about four hundred men. They had no dwellings in Medina and no tribes, and they were in the mosque learning the Qur'an and cracking date-pits (yarda'un, "they crack") by day. They would go out with every expedition (sariyyah) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched, and they were the People of the Suffah (Ashab al-Suffah). So Allah, the Exalted, urged the people on their behalf, and whoever had surplus would bring it to them in the evening.

﴿Who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾. Concerning this there are several opinions. Qatadah said, and it is the best of them: they confined themselves to jihad in the way of Allah ﴿they cannot go about in the land﴾, meaning they have no leisure for trade and seeking livelihood, and they are the People of the Suffah whom we mentioned. It was said: they confined themselves to obedience to Allah. It was said: its meaning is that poverty and want restrained them from jihad in the way of Allah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are a people who were struck by wounds with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in jihad in the way of Allah, so they became disabled; illness and chronic disability restricted them from going about in the way of Allah for jihad. Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is that, because of how much they fought, the whole earth became a war against them, so they cannot go about in the land because of the multitude of their enemies.

﴿Whom the ignorant one thinks to be rich﴾ — Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Hamzah read yahsabuhum with a fatha on the sin, and the others read it with a kasra. ﴿Because of their abstinence﴾, meaning because of their restraint from asking and their contentment. Whoever does not know their condition thinks they are rich. Al-ta'affuf is the tafa"ul form from al-'iffah, which is restraint. One says "'affa 'an al-shay'" when he refrains from it, and "ta'affafa" when he exerts effort in withholding.

﴿You recognize them by their mark﴾. Al-simaa, al-simiyaa and al-simah all mean the sign by which a thing is known. The scholars differed about its meaning here. Mujahid said: it is humility and modesty. Al-Suddi said: the trace of hardship from need and poverty. Al-Dahhak said: the yellowness of their complexions from hunger and harm. It was also said: the shabbiness of their garments. ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾. 'Ata' said: if they have lunch, they do not ask for dinner, and if they have dinner, they do not ask for lunch. It was also said: its meaning is that they do not ask people at all, because He said "from abstinence," and abstinence is the leaving of asking; and because He said "you recognize them by their mark," and if asking were part of their conduct, recognizing them by a sign would not be necessary. So the meaning of the verse is: there is no asking from them in which persistence would occur. Al-ilhaf is insistence and obstinacy.

We were informed by Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri, who was informed by Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Isma'ili, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, who was informed by Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam, who was informed by Anas ibn 'Iyad, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "For one of you to take his rope, go and bring a bundle of firewood on his back, and Allah thereby keeps his face (from asking), is better for him than to ask people, whether they give him or refuse him." (ﷺ) [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Zakat, chapter: Seeking to abstain from asking, 3/335. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 6/112-113.]

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi, who was informed by Zahir ibn Ahmad, who was informed by Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi, who was informed by Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The needy one is not this wanderer who goes around among people, whom a morsel or two morsels turn away, or a date or two dates." They said: "Who then is the needy one, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who does not find sufficiency so that it suffices him, and who is not noticed so that charity is given to him, and who does not stand up and ask people." (ﷺ) [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Zakat, chapter: The saying of Allah, the Exalted (They do not ask people persistently), 3/340, and in al-Tafsir. And Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter: The needy one who does not find sufficiency and is not noticed so that charity is given to him, no. (1039), 2/719. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/86.]

It is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyyah or its equivalent, has asked persistently." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Zakat, chapter: Who is given from charity and the limit of sufficiency, 2/229, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri with the wording "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyyah has been persistent," and al-Mundhiri remained silent on it. And al-Nasa'i in al-Zakat, chapter: If he does not have dirhams but has their equivalent, 5/98-99. And Ahmad: 4/36 and 5/430, the wording being his, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar from a man of Banu Asad. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/84, and its chain is sound.]

We were informed by Abu Sa'id 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri, who was informed by my grandfather Abu Sahl 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ibn 'Adafir, who was informed by Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abbad al-Dabari, who was informed by 'Abd al-Razzaq, who was informed by Ma'mar, from Harun ibn Riyab, from Kinanah al-'Adawi, from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq, who said: I undertook a guarantee (himalah) among my people, so I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have undertaken a guarantee among my people, and I came to you so that you might help me with it." He said: "Rather, we will bear it on your behalf, O Qabisah, and pay it to them from the charity." Then he said: "O Qabisah, asking is forbidden except in one of three cases: a man struck by a calamity (jaihah), which destroyed his wealth, so he may ask until he attains a means of livelihood, then he withholds; and a man struck by need until three men of sound judgment from his people testify that he has been struck by need and that asking has become lawful for him, so he may ask until he attains a means of livelihood, then he withholds; and a man who undertook a guarantee, so he may ask until he has completed it, then he withholds. Anything other than that is unlawful gain (suht), which its possessor consumes as unlawful gain." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter: Whom asking is lawful for, no. (1044), 2/722, with similar wording. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/122 with the wording: "Asking is not lawful except for three: a man who undertook a guarantee between people; a man struck by a calamity that destroyed his wealth, so he may ask until he attains a sufficiency of livelihood; and a man struck by poverty until three men of sound judgment from his people testify that he has been struck by need and that asking has become lawful for him. Whatever other than this of requests is unlawful gain."]

We were informed by Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi, who was informed by Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi, who was informed by Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi, who was informed by Abu 'Isa Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, who was informed by Qutaybah, who was informed by Shurayk, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever asks people while he has what suffices him, will come on the Day of Resurrection with scratches (khumush) or abrasions (khudush) or lacerations (kudut) on his face." [Al-khumush is like al-khudush in meaning, and al-kudut are the traces of abrasions; every trace of scratching, biting or the like is kudut.]

It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what suffices him? He said: "Fifty dirhams, or their value in gold." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Zakat, chapter: Who is given from charity and the limit of sufficiency, 2/226; see what al-Mundhiri said in his abridgment. And al-Tirmidhi in al-Zakat, chapter: Who is lawfully given zakat, 3/313-314, from Ibn Mas'ud, and he said: the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud is a hasan hadith, and Shu'bah spoke about Hakim ibn Jubayr on account of this hadith. Ibn Hajar said: weak, accused of Shi'ism, of the fifth tier (Taqrib). And Ibn Majah in al-Zakat, chapter: Who asks while having a means of support, 1/589, and al-Albani authenticated it in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah, no. (499), and in Sahih Ibn Majah, no. (1490). And al-Darimi in al-Zakat, chapter 15: Who is lawfully given charity, 1/386. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/83.]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever good you spend﴾, of wealth, ﴿indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾, and He will reward it. [The phrase "wa 'alayhi majaz" is noted here.]

﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly﴾. It was narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: This verse was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. He had four dirhams and owned nothing else; he gave one dirham by night, one by day, one secretly and one openly. [Narrated by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 86, with a sound chain.]

And from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: When ﴿For the poor who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾ was revealed, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf sent many dinars to the People of the Suffah, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, sent a wasq of dates in the middle of the night. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning both of them ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day﴾, the verse. By "by day, openly" is meant the charity of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and by "by night, secretly" is meant the charity of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Umamah, Abu al-Darda', Makhul and al-Awza'i said: it was revealed concerning those who tie horses for jihad, for they are fed by night and by day, secretly and openly. [Al-Tabarani and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uraib, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: this verse was revealed concerning the people of horses; Yazid and his father are unknown. And 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated with a weak chain from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: this verse was revealed concerning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: he had four dirhams... And Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn al-Musayyib that he said: the verse was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan in their spending in the army of hardship (jaysh al-'usrah). (See: Lubab al-Nuqul of al-Suyuti, p. 118, in the margin of al-Jalalayn; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 84-85.)]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was informed by 'Ali ibn Hafs, who was informed by Ibn al-Mubarak, who was informed by Talhah ibn Abi Sa'id, who said: I heard Sa'id al-Maqburi narrate that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever keeps a horse in the way of Allah, out of faith in Allah and belief in His promise, then its satiety, its watering, its dung and its urine are in his scales on the Day of Resurrection." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter: Whoever keeps a horse in the way of Allah, 6/57, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 10/388.]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then for them is their reward with their Lord﴾. Al-Akhfash said: the predicate was introduced with the fa' because "alladhina" carries the meaning of "man," and the response of "man" is introduced with the fa' as the response of a conditional. Or the meaning of the verse is: whoever spends such-and-such, then for him is his reward with his Lord. ﴿And no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 275–277:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who consume interest (riba)﴾, meaning: those who deal in it. He specified consuming because it is the main purpose of wealth. ﴿Will not stand﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, ﴿except as one stands whom Satan has driven to madness﴾, meaning: whom Satan throws down (yasra'uhu). The origin of khabt (striking, trampling) is striking and treading, and it is striking without evenness. It is said: "a khabut camel," for the one that tramples people and strikes the ground with its legs. ﴿From the touch﴾, meaning from madness. It is said: "the man was mass (mussa)," and he is "mamsus" if he is mad. Its meaning: the one who consumes interest will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as one who has been thrown down.

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Abdullah ibn Yahya informed us; Ya'qub ibn Sufyan informed us; Isma'il ibn Salim informed us; Abbad ibn Abbad informed us, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the account of the Night Journey, that he said: "Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, took me to many men, each of whom had a belly like a great house, arranged along the path of the people of Pharaoh—and the people of Pharaoh are exposed to the Fire morning and evening." He said: "They approach like thirsty camels, trampling the stones and trees, not hearing and not understanding. When the owners of those bellies sense them, they rise, and their bellies tilt them, and they are thrown down. Then one of them rises, and his belly tilts him, and he is thrown down. They cannot move until the people of Pharaoh overtake them and drive them back and forth. That is their punishment in the barzakh between this world and the Hereafter." ﴿Said﴾ and the people of Pharaoh say: "O Allah, never establish the Hour." ﴿He said﴾: And on the Day of Resurrection it is said: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾ (40:46). I said: "O Gabriel, who are these?" He said: "These are those who consume interest; they will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness from the touch." [[Narrated by al-Asbahani through the route of Abu Harun al-Abdi, who is weak. See: al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib by al-Mundhiri: 3/9.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because they said, "Trade is only like interest."﴾ meaning: that which befell them was because of this saying of theirs and their deeming it lawful. That is because the people of the Jahiliyyah, when one of them had a debt due from his debtor and demanded it, the debtor would say to the creditor: "Extend the term for me and I will increase the amount for you." So they would do that, and they would say: "It is all the same to us whether the increase is at the outset of the sale as profit or at the due date in exchange for delay." So Allah, exalted is He, refuted them and said: ﴿But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest﴾. Know that riba in the language means increase. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what you give in interest to increase the wealth of people﴾, meaning to multiply it, ﴿does not increase with Allah﴾ (30:39). Seeking increase by way of trade is not forbidden in general; what is forbidden is an increase upon a specific attribute in a specific property, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained. Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Abd al-Wahhab informed us, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Muslim ibn Yasar and another man, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not sell gold for gold, nor silver for silver, nor wheat for wheat, nor barley for barley, nor dates for dates, nor salt for salt, except like for like, hand to hand. But sell gold for silver and silver for gold, wheat for barley and barley for wheat, dates for salt and salt for dates, hand to hand, however you wish—and one of them mentioned salt or dates and the other added: whoever increases or seeks increase has committed riba." [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musaqat, chapter: exchange and selling gold for silver in cash, no. 1587, 3/1210. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/56.]] This hadith was also narrated by Mutarrif from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Muslim ibn Yasar and Abd Allah ibn Atik, from Ubadah; so the Prophet (ﷺ) specified six items.

The majority of scholars held that the ruling of riba applies to these six items by their attributes, and extends to every property in which those attributes are found. Then they differed regarding those attributes. One group held that the meaning in all of them is one, namely value (naf'), and they established riba in all property. Most held that riba applies to dirhams and dinars by one attribute and to foodstuffs by another attribute, and they differed about that attribute. One group said: in dirhams and dinars it is established by the attribute of monetary value (naqdiyyah), which is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. Another group said: it is established by the illah of weight, which is the view of the Ashab al-Ra'y (the Hanafis), and they established riba in all weighed items such as iron, copper, cotton and the like.

As for the four remaining items, one group held that riba is established in them by the illah of measure, which is the view of the Ashab al-Ra'y, and they established riba in all measured items, whether foodstuff or not, such as lime, plaster and the like. A group held that the illah in them is food together with measure or weight, so every foodstuff that is measured or weighed is subject to riba, and it is not subject to riba in what is neither measured nor weighed. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and al-Shafi'i stated it in his old opinion (al-Qadim). In his new opinion (al-Jadid) he said that riba is established in them by the attribute of food, and he established riba in all foodstuffs—fruits, produce, vegetables and medicines—whether measured or weighed, on the basis of what was narrated from Ma'mar ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I used to hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: food for food, like for like."  [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musaqat, chapter: selling food like for like, no. 1592, 3/1214. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 8/58.]]

Thus the subject of riba according to al-Shafi'i is whatever is a price (thaman) or foodstuff. Riba is of two kinds: riba al-fadl (excess) and riba al-nasa' (delay). If one sells an item of riba for the same kind in equal amounts—such as selling one of the two precious metals for its own kind, or selling a foodstuff for its own kind, like wheat for wheat and the like—both kinds of riba apply to it, so it is permitted only when equal by the standard of the Shari'ah. If it is weighed, like dirhams and dinars, equality by weight is required; if it is measured, like wheat and barley, it is sold for its own kind with equality by measure, and mutual handover in the session of the contract is required. If one sells an item of riba for a different kind, one considers: if he sells for something not sharing the attribute of riba, such as selling a foodstuff for one of the two precious metals, there is no riba in it, just as if he sold it for something other than an item of riba; or if he sells for something sharing the attribute, such as selling dirhams for dinars, or wheat for barley, or selling one foodstuff for a different foodstuff, then riba al-fadl does not apply to it, so it is permitted with difference or by estimation (juzaf) [[Selling a thing whose measure or weight is not known; it is a Persian loanword, arabized.]], but riba al-nasa' does apply to it, so mutual handover in the session is required. The Prophet's (ﷺ) saying, "Do not sell gold for gold—" up to "except like for like" contains the requirement of equality and the prohibition of excess when the kind is the same; his saying "in cash" contains the prohibition of delay; and his saying "hand to hand, however you wish" contains the permission of excess when the kind differs together with the requirement of mutual handover in the session. This is regarding riba of exchange (riba al-mubaya'ah).

Whoever lends something on condition that more is returned to him, it is a loan that brings benefit, and every loan that brings benefit is riba.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord﴾, meaning a reminder and a warning. He used the verb in the masculine because it refers to the admonition (al-wa'z). ﴿And desists﴾ from consuming interest; ﴿for him is what has passed﴾, meaning what has gone before of his sin prior to the prohibition is forgiven for him; ﴿and his affair is up to Allah﴾ after the prohibition: if He wills, He protects him so that he remains steadfast in desisting, and if He wills, He forsakes him until he returns. It was also said: ﴿what has passed, and his affair is up to Allah﴾ concerning what He commands him and forbids him, and makes lawful for him and unlawful for him, and nothing of his own affair is in his hands. ﴿And whoever returns﴾ after the prohibition to consuming interest, considering it lawful, ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally﴾.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ghundar informed us; Shu'bah informed us, from Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, that he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the price of blood, the price of the dog, and the earnings of a prostitute, and cursed the one who consumes interest, the one who pays it, the woman who tattoos and the one who is tattooed, and the painter. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-Buyu', chapter: the one who pays interest, 4/314, and in al-Libas and al-Talaq. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/25.]]

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us; Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us; Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us; Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us; Zuhayr ibn Harb informed us; Hushaym informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the one who consumes interest, the one who pays it, its scribe, and its two witnesses, and said: "They are all alike." [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musaqat, chapter: cursing the one who consumes interest and the one who pays it, no. 1598, 3/1218. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/54.]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; Abu Muhammad al-Makhladi informed us; Abu Hamid ibn al-Sharqi informed us; Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us; al-Nadr ibn Muhammad informed us; Ikrimah ibn Ammar informed us; Yahya, that is Ibn Abi Kathir, informed us, who said: Abu Salamah narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Riba has seventy categories, the lightest of which in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is like a man who has intercourse with his mother." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Tijarat, chapter on the severity regarding riba, 1/764. He said in the Zawa'id: its chain includes Najih ibn Abd al-Rahman Abu Ma'shar, on whose weakness there is agreement. Ibn Hajar said: Najih ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Sindi, Abu Ma'shar, a client of Banu Hashim, well known by his kunyah, weak, of the sixth generation, aged and confused, died in 170 (Taqrib). See also Fayd al-Qadir 4/51 and Kashf al-Khafa 1/508, as it is attributed to al-Hakim and al-Tabarani.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾, meaning He diminishes it, destroys it, and removes its blessing. Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾: meaning He does not accept from it charity, nor jihad, nor hajj, nor kinship ties. ﴿And He causes charities to increase﴾, meaning He multiplies them and blesses them in this world, and multiplies the reward and recompense in the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾, by making interest lawful, ﴿sinful﴾, a wrongdoer by consuming it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 275–277:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who consume interest (riba)﴾, meaning: those who deal in it. He specified consuming because it is the main purpose of wealth. ﴿Will not stand﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, ﴿except as one stands whom Satan has driven to madness﴾, meaning: whom Satan throws down (yasra'uhu). The origin of khabt (striking, trampling) is striking and treading, and it is striking without evenness. It is said: "a khabut camel," for the one that tramples people and strikes the ground with its legs. ﴿From the touch﴾, meaning from madness. It is said: "the man was mass (mussa)," and he is "mamsus" if he is mad. Its meaning: the one who consumes interest will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as one who has been thrown down.

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Abdullah ibn Yahya informed us; Ya'qub ibn Sufyan informed us; Isma'il ibn Salim informed us; Abbad ibn Abbad informed us, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the account of the Night Journey, that he said: "Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, took me to many men, each of whom had a belly like a great house, arranged along the path of the people of Pharaoh—and the people of Pharaoh are exposed to the Fire morning and evening." He said: "They approach like thirsty camels, trampling the stones and trees, not hearing and not understanding. When the owners of those bellies sense them, they rise, and their bellies tilt them, and they are thrown down. Then one of them rises, and his belly tilts him, and he is thrown down. They cannot move until the people of Pharaoh overtake them and drive them back and forth. That is their punishment in the barzakh between this world and the Hereafter." ﴿Said﴾ and the people of Pharaoh say: "O Allah, never establish the Hour." ﴿He said﴾: And on the Day of Resurrection it is said: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment﴾ (40:46). I said: "O Gabriel, who are these?" He said: "These are those who consume interest; they will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness from the touch." [[Narrated by al-Asbahani through the route of Abu Harun al-Abdi, who is weak. See: al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib by al-Mundhiri: 3/9.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because they said, "Trade is only like interest."﴾ meaning: that which befell them was because of this saying of theirs and their deeming it lawful. That is because the people of the Jahiliyyah, when one of them had a debt due from his debtor and demanded it, the debtor would say to the creditor: "Extend the term for me and I will increase the amount for you." So they would do that, and they would say: "It is all the same to us whether the increase is at the outset of the sale as profit or at the due date in exchange for delay." So Allah, exalted is He, refuted them and said: ﴿But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest﴾. Know that riba in the language means increase. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what you give in interest to increase the wealth of people﴾, meaning to multiply it, ﴿does not increase with Allah﴾ (30:39). Seeking increase by way of trade is not forbidden in general; what is forbidden is an increase upon a specific attribute in a specific property, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained. Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Abd al-Wahhab informed us, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Muslim ibn Yasar and another man, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not sell gold for gold, nor silver for silver, nor wheat for wheat, nor barley for barley, nor dates for dates, nor salt for salt, except like for like, hand to hand. But sell gold for silver and silver for gold, wheat for barley and barley for wheat, dates for salt and salt for dates, hand to hand, however you wish—and one of them mentioned salt or dates and the other added: whoever increases or seeks increase has committed riba." [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musaqat, chapter: exchange and selling gold for silver in cash, no. 1587, 3/1210. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/56.]] This hadith was also narrated by Mutarrif from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Muslim ibn Yasar and Abd Allah ibn Atik, from Ubadah; so the Prophet (ﷺ) specified six items.

The majority of scholars held that the ruling of riba applies to these six items by their attributes, and extends to every property in which those attributes are found. Then they differed regarding those attributes. One group held that the meaning in all of them is one, namely value (naf'), and they established riba in all property. Most held that riba applies to dirhams and dinars by one attribute and to foodstuffs by another attribute, and they differed about that attribute. One group said: in dirhams and dinars it is established by the attribute of monetary value (naqdiyyah), which is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. Another group said: it is established by the illah of weight, which is the view of the Ashab al-Ra'y (the Hanafis), and they established riba in all weighed items such as iron, copper, cotton and the like.

As for the four remaining items, one group held that riba is established in them by the illah of measure, which is the view of the Ashab al-Ra'y, and they established riba in all measured items, whether foodstuff or not, such as lime, plaster and the like. A group held that the illah in them is food together with measure or weight, so every foodstuff that is measured or weighed is subject to riba, and it is not subject to riba in what is neither measured nor weighed. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and al-Shafi'i stated it in his old opinion (al-Qadim). In his new opinion (al-Jadid) he said that riba is established in them by the attribute of food, and he established riba in all foodstuffs—fruits, produce, vegetables and medicines—whether measured or weighed, on the basis of what was narrated from Ma'mar ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I used to hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: food for food, like for like."  [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musaqat, chapter: selling food like for like, no. 1592, 3/1214. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 8/58.]]

Thus the subject of riba according to al-Shafi'i is whatever is a price (thaman) or foodstuff. Riba is of two kinds: riba al-fadl (excess) and riba al-nasa' (delay). If one sells an item of riba for the same kind in equal amounts—such as selling one of the two precious metals for its own kind, or selling a foodstuff for its own kind, like wheat for wheat and the like—both kinds of riba apply to it, so it is permitted only when equal by the standard of the Shari'ah. If it is weighed, like dirhams and dinars, equality by weight is required; if it is measured, like wheat and barley, it is sold for its own kind with equality by measure, and mutual handover in the session of the contract is required. If one sells an item of riba for a different kind, one considers: if he sells for something not sharing the attribute of riba, such as selling a foodstuff for one of the two precious metals, there is no riba in it, just as if he sold it for something other than an item of riba; or if he sells for something sharing the attribute, such as selling dirhams for dinars, or wheat for barley, or selling one foodstuff for a different foodstuff, then riba al-fadl does not apply to it, so it is permitted with difference or by estimation (juzaf) [[Selling a thing whose measure or weight is not known; it is a Persian loanword, arabized.]], but riba al-nasa' does apply to it, so mutual handover in the session is required. The Prophet's (ﷺ) saying, "Do not sell gold for gold—" up to "except like for like" contains the requirement of equality and the prohibition of excess when the kind is the same; his saying "in cash" contains the prohibition of delay; and his saying "hand to hand, however you wish" contains the permission of excess when the kind differs together with the requirement of mutual handover in the session. This is regarding riba of exchange (riba al-mubaya'ah).

Whoever lends something on condition that more is returned to him, it is a loan that brings benefit, and every loan that brings benefit is riba.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord﴾, meaning a reminder and a warning. He used the verb in the masculine because it refers to the admonition (al-wa'z). ﴿And desists﴾ from consuming interest; ﴿for him is what has passed﴾, meaning what has gone before of his sin prior to the prohibition is forgiven for him; ﴿and his affair is up to Allah﴾ after the prohibition: if He wills, He protects him so that he remains steadfast in desisting, and if He wills, He forsakes him until he returns. It was also said: ﴿what has passed, and his affair is up to Allah﴾ concerning what He commands him and forbids him, and makes lawful for him and unlawful for him, and nothing of his own affair is in his hands. ﴿And whoever returns﴾ after the prohibition to consuming interest, considering it lawful, ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally﴾.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ghundar informed us; Shu'bah informed us, from Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, that he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the price of blood, the price of the dog, and the earnings of a prostitute, and cursed the one who consumes interest, the one who pays it, the woman who tattoos and the one who is tattooed, and the painter. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in al-Buyu', chapter: the one who pays interest, 4/314, and in al-Libas and al-Talaq. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/25.]]

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us; Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us; Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us; Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us; Zuhayr ibn Harb informed us; Hushaym informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the one who consumes interest, the one who pays it, its scribe, and its two witnesses, and said: "They are all alike." [[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musaqat, chapter: cursing the one who consumes interest and the one who pays it, no. 1598, 3/1218. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/54.]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; Abu Muhammad al-Makhladi informed us; Abu Hamid ibn al-Sharqi informed us; Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us; al-Nadr ibn Muhammad informed us; Ikrimah ibn Ammar informed us; Yahya, that is Ibn Abi Kathir, informed us, who said: Abu Salamah narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Riba has seventy categories, the lightest of which in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is like a man who has intercourse with his mother." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Tijarat, chapter on the severity regarding riba, 1/764. He said in the Zawa'id: its chain includes Najih ibn Abd al-Rahman Abu Ma'shar, on whose weakness there is agreement. Ibn Hajar said: Najih ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Sindi, Abu Ma'shar, a client of Banu Hashim, well known by his kunyah, weak, of the sixth generation, aged and confused, died in 170 (Taqrib). See also Fayd al-Qadir 4/51 and Kashf al-Khafa 1/508, as it is attributed to al-Hakim and al-Tabarani.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾, meaning He diminishes it, destroys it, and removes its blessing. Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning ﴿Allah destroys interest﴾: meaning He does not accept from it charity, nor jihad, nor hajj, nor kinship ties. ﴿And He causes charities to increase﴾, meaning He multiplies them and blesses them in this world, and multiplies the reward and recompense in the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾, by making interest lawful, ﴿sinful﴾, a wrongdoer by consuming it.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 278–281 (part 1 of 2):

The Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of riba (usury, interest)﴾. ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrimah said: It was revealed concerning al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with them both. The two had extended a loan (aslafa) in dates. When the time of harvesting (al-judhādh) arrived, the owner of the dates said to them: "If you take your full due, nothing will remain for me to support my dependants. Would you take half now, defer the other half, and I will double it for you?" They agreed. When the term came due, they demanded the increase. This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he forbade them. Then Allah revealed this verse, and they heard and obeyed, and they took only the principal of their money.[[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 87.]]

Al-Suddī said: It was revealed concerning al-ʿAbbās and Khālid ibn al-Walīd. They had been partners in the Jāhiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance), lending at riba to the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr, a people of Thaqīf. When Islam came, they still had large sums out at riba. Allah then revealed this verse. The Prophet ﷺ, in his sermon on the Day of ʿArafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ), said: "Behold, everything of the affairs of the Jāhiliyyah is under my feet, placed (abolished). The blood of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished. The first blood I abolish from our blood is the blood of Ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith, who was nursed among the Banū Saʿd and was killed by Hudhayl. And all the riba of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished. The first riba I abolish is the riba of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; it is abolished entirely."[[See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 87; the sermon of the Day of ʿArafah was cited previously on pp. (219) and (229) in the footnotes.[[See Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyūṭī, pp. 119, 121.]]]]

Muqātil said: It was revealed concerning four brothers from Thaqīf: Masʿūd, ʿAbd Yālīl, Ḥabīb and Rabīʿah, who were the sons of ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr ibn ʿAwf al-Thaqafī. They used to lend money to the Banū al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr ibn Makhzūm, and they took riba. When the Prophet ﷺ prevailed over al-Ṭāʾif, these brothers embraced Islam and demanded their riba from the Banū al-Mughīrah. The Banū al-Mughīrah said: "By Allah, we will not pay riba in Islam, since Allah the Exalted has removed it from the believers." They brought their dispute before ʿAttāb ibn Usayd, who was the governor (ʿāmil) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over Makkah. ʿAttāb ibn Usayd wrote to the Prophet ﷺ about the case of the two parties, and the sum was a large one. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of riba﴾.[[2]]

﴿If you are believers﴾.

﴿But if you do not do it﴾, that is: if you do not give up what remains of riba, ﴿then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾. Ḥamzah and ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr, recite fa-ādhanū with a long vowel (al-madd), on the pattern of āminū, meaning: inform others that you are at war with Allah and His Messenger. Its root is from al-udhun (the ear), meaning: place it in the ears. The others recite fa-udhanū, short (maqṣūr), with a fatḥah on the dhāl, meaning: know for yourselves and be certain of a war from Allah and His Messenger. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: On the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to the one who consumed riba: "Take your weapon for the war." The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: The war of Allah is the Fire, and the war of the Messenger of Allah is the sword.

﴿And if you repent﴾, that is, you give up regarding riba as permissible and turn back from it, ﴿then you shall have your principal; you shall not wrong﴾ by seeking an increase, ﴿nor be wronged﴾ by a reduction below the principal. When the verse was revealed, the Banū ʿAmr al-Thaqafī and others among those who dealt in riba said: "Rather, we repent to Allah, for we have no strength for a war with Allah and His Messenger." They accepted the principal. The Banū al-Mughīrah then complained of hardship and said: "Give us respite until the crops come in." They refused to grant a delay. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And if someone is in hardship﴾.

That is: if the debtor is in difficulty. The word is in the nominative as the subject of kāna (was), and no predicate has been given for it, which is permissible with an indefinite noun. You say: "If there is a righteous man, then honour him." It is also said that kāna here means waqaʿa (occurred), and in that case it needs no predicate. Abū Jaʿfar read ʿusrah with a ḍammah on the sīn. ﴿Then let there be postponement﴾: this is an imperative in the form of a statement, its implied sense being: "then for him is postponement." ﴿Until a time of ease﴾. Nāfiʿ read maysarah with a ḍammah on the sīn, while the others read it with a fatḥah. Mujāhid read maysurah with a ḍammah on the sīn in the construct form, and its meaning is affluence and ease. ﴿But that you remit it as charity﴾, that is: that you leave your principal to the one in hardship, ﴿is better for you, if you only knew﴾. ʿĀṣim read taṣaddaqū with a light ṣād, while the others read it with a doubled ṣād.

Al-Imam Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Qāḍī informed us: Abū al-Ṭayyib Sahl ibn Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān informed us: Abū al-ʿAbbās Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Mīkālī informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Mūsā ibn ʿAbdān, the ḥāfiẓ, informed us: Abū Ṭāhir Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Sarḥ informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Jarīr, from Ḥāzim, from Ayyūb, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qatādah, from his father, that he was seeking a man for a debt that was due, and the man hid from him. He said: "What kept you from this?" He said: "Hardship." So he made him swear to that, and he swore. Then he called for his sakk (written debt document) and gave it to him, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits it for him, Allah will save him from the distress of the Day of Resurrection.'"[[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: The virtue of granting respite to the one in hardship, no. (1563), 3/1196. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/196 with the same wording.]]

Abd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad al-Malīḥī informed us: Abū Manṣūr Muḥammad ibn Samʿān informed us: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rayyānī informed us: Ḥumayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā informed us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Manṣūr, from Rib‘ī, from Abū Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The angels met the soul of a man who had lived before you. He said: 'No, except that I was a man who lent money to people, and I would tell my servants to grant respite to the one who is well-off and to overlook the one in hardship.' Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: The virtue of granting respite to the one in hardship, from Ḥudhayfah, no. (1560), 3/1194. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/197.]]

(3006), 4/2301–2302. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/198.]]

**Chapter on debt, the goodness of repaying it, and the severity of its matter.**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾. The people of Basra read the verb with a fatha on the ta', meaning "you will arrive (taṣīrūna) at Allah," while the others read it with a damma on the ta' and a fatha on the jim, meaning "you will be sent back (turaddūna) to Allah." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: This is the last verse revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Place it at the top of two hundred and eighty verses of Surat al-Baqarah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lived after it twenty-one days. Ibn Jurayj said: nine nights. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: seven nights. He died on Monday, two nights having passed from the month of Rabiʿ al-Awwal, when the sun had passed its zenith, in the eleventh year after the Hijrah.

Al-Shaʿbi related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): The last verse revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the verse on riba (usury). [[Regarding knowing what was revealed last, there is disagreement. Al-Shaykhan related from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: The last verse revealed was "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah" [al-Nisa': 176]. And the last surah revealed was Surat Bara'ah. Al-Bukhari related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The last verse revealed was the verse on riba. Al-Bayhaqi related the same from ʿUmar. In Ahmad and Ibn Majah, from ʿUmar: among the last things revealed was the verse on riba. Al-Nasa'i related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The last thing revealed of the Qur'an was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281]. Ibn Jarir and al-Firyabi related the like of it, and it is also narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr... etc. There are other opinions. The views can be reconciled by saying that some of them refer to the last of the surahs revealed, some to the last of the verses, and some to the last subject matter of the verses, so they are relative "lasts." For a detailed treatment, see al-Suyuti's al-Itqan fi ʿUloom al-Qur'an: 1/101–106, edited by Muhammad Abu al-Fadl Ibrahim.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 278–281 (part 1 of 2):

The Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of riba (usury, interest)﴾. ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrimah said: It was revealed concerning al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with them both. The two had extended a loan (aslafa) in dates. When the time of harvesting (al-judhādh) arrived, the owner of the dates said to them: "If you take your full due, nothing will remain for me to support my dependants. Would you take half now, defer the other half, and I will double it for you?" They agreed. When the term came due, they demanded the increase. This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he forbade them. Then Allah revealed this verse, and they heard and obeyed, and they took only the principal of their money.[[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 87.]]

Al-Suddī said: It was revealed concerning al-ʿAbbās and Khālid ibn al-Walīd. They had been partners in the Jāhiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance), lending at riba to the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr, a people of Thaqīf. When Islam came, they still had large sums out at riba. Allah then revealed this verse. The Prophet ﷺ, in his sermon on the Day of ʿArafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ), said: "Behold, everything of the affairs of the Jāhiliyyah is under my feet, placed (abolished). The blood of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished. The first blood I abolish from our blood is the blood of Ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith, who was nursed among the Banū Saʿd and was killed by Hudhayl. And all the riba of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished. The first riba I abolish is the riba of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; it is abolished entirely."[[See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 87; the sermon of the Day of ʿArafah was cited previously on pp. (219) and (229) in the footnotes.[[See Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyūṭī, pp. 119, 121.]]]]

Muqātil said: It was revealed concerning four brothers from Thaqīf: Masʿūd, ʿAbd Yālīl, Ḥabīb and Rabīʿah, who were the sons of ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr ibn ʿAwf al-Thaqafī. They used to lend money to the Banū al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr ibn Makhzūm, and they took riba. When the Prophet ﷺ prevailed over al-Ṭāʾif, these brothers embraced Islam and demanded their riba from the Banū al-Mughīrah. The Banū al-Mughīrah said: "By Allah, we will not pay riba in Islam, since Allah the Exalted has removed it from the believers." They brought their dispute before ʿAttāb ibn Usayd, who was the governor (ʿāmil) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over Makkah. ʿAttāb ibn Usayd wrote to the Prophet ﷺ about the case of the two parties, and the sum was a large one. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of riba﴾.[[2]]

﴿If you are believers﴾.

﴿But if you do not do it﴾, that is: if you do not give up what remains of riba, ﴿then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾. (1885), 3/1501. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/200.]]

[[Regarding knowing what was revealed last, there is disagreement. Al-Shaykhan related from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: The last verse revealed was "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah" [al-Nisa': 176]. And the last surah revealed was Surat Bara'ah. Al-Bukhari related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The last verse revealed was the verse on riba. Al-Bayhaqi related the same from ʿUmar. In Ahmad and Ibn Majah, from ʿUmar: among the last things revealed was the verse on riba. Ibn Jarir and al-Firyabi related the like of it, and it is also narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr... etc. There are other opinions. The views can be reconciled by saying that some of them refer to the last of the surahs revealed, some to the last of the verses, and some to the last subject matter of the verses, so they are relative "lasts." For a detailed treatment, see al-Suyuti's al-Itqan fi ʿUloom al-Qur'an: 1/101–106, edited by Muhammad Abu al-Fadl Ibrahim.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verses 278–281 (part 1 of 2):

The Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of riba (usury, interest)﴾. ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrimah said: It was revealed concerning al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with them both. The two had extended a loan (aslafa) in dates. When the time of harvesting (al-judhādh) arrived, the owner of the dates said to them: "If you take your full due, nothing will remain for me to support my dependants. Would you take half now, defer the other half, and I will double it for you?" They agreed. When the term came due, they demanded the increase. This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he forbade them. Then Allah revealed this verse, and they heard and obeyed, and they took only the principal of their money.[[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 87.]]

Al-Suddī said: It was revealed concerning al-ʿAbbās and Khālid ibn al-Walīd. They had been partners in the Jāhiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance), lending at riba to the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr, a people of Thaqīf. When Islam came, they still had large sums out at riba. Allah then revealed this verse. The Prophet ﷺ, in his sermon on the Day of ʿArafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ), said: "Behold, everything of the affairs of the Jāhiliyyah is under my feet, placed (abolished). The blood of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished. The first blood I abolish from our blood is the blood of Ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith, who was nursed among the Banū Saʿd and was killed by Hudhayl. And all the riba of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished. The first riba I abolish is the riba of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; it is abolished entirely."[[See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 87; the sermon of the Day of ʿArafah was cited previously on pp. (219) and (229) in the footnotes.[[See Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyūṭī, pp. 119, 121.]]]]

Muqātil said: It was revealed concerning four brothers from Thaqīf: Masʿūd, ʿAbd Yālīl, Ḥabīb and Rabīʿah, who were the sons of ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr ibn ʿAwf al-Thaqafī. They used to lend money to the Banū al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr ibn Makhzūm, and they took riba. When the Prophet ﷺ prevailed over al-Ṭāʾif, these brothers embraced Islam and demanded their riba from the Banū al-Mughīrah. The Banū al-Mughīrah said: "By Allah, we will not pay riba in Islam, since Allah the Exalted has removed it from the believers." They brought their dispute before ʿAttāb ibn Usayd, who was the governor (ʿāmil) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over Makkah. ʿAttāb ibn Usayd wrote to the Prophet ﷺ about the case of the two parties, and the sum was a large one. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of riba﴾.[[2]]

﴿If you are believers﴾.

﴿But if you do not do it﴾, that is: if you do not give up what remains of riba, ﴿then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾. Ḥamzah and ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr, recite fa-ādhanū with a long vowel (al-madd), on the pattern of āminū, meaning: inform others that you are at war with Allah and His Messenger. Its root is from al-udhun (the ear), meaning: place it in the ears. The others recite fa-udhanū, short (maqṣūr), with a fatḥah on the dhāl, meaning: know for yourselves and be certain of a war from Allah and His Messenger. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: On the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to the one who consumed riba: "Take your weapon for the war." The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: The war of Allah is the Fire, and the war of the Messenger of Allah is the sword.

﴿And if you repent﴾, that is, you give up regarding riba as permissible and turn back from it, ﴿then you shall have your principal; you shall not wrong﴾ by seeking an increase, ﴿nor be wronged﴾ by a reduction below the principal. When the verse was revealed, the Banū ʿAmr al-Thaqafī and others among those who dealt in riba said: "Rather, we repent to Allah, for we have no strength for a war with Allah and His Messenger." They accepted the principal. The Banū al-Mughīrah then complained of hardship and said: "Give us respite until the crops come in." They refused to grant a delay. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And if someone is in hardship﴾.

That is: if the debtor is in difficulty. The word is in the nominative as the subject of kāna (was), and no predicate has been given for it, which is permissible with an indefinite noun. You say: "If there is a righteous man, then honour him." It is also said that kāna here means waqaʿa (occurred), and in that case it needs no predicate. Abū Jaʿfar read ʿusrah with a ḍammah on the sīn. ﴿Then let there be postponement﴾: this is an imperative in the form of a statement, its implied sense being: "then for him is postponement." ﴿Until a time of ease﴾. Nāfiʿ read maysarah with a ḍammah on the sīn, while the others read it with a fatḥah. Mujāhid read maysurah with a ḍammah on the sīn in the construct form, and its meaning is affluence and ease. ﴿But that you remit it as charity﴾, that is: that you leave your principal to the one in hardship, ﴿is better for you, if you only knew﴾. ʿĀṣim read taṣaddaqū with a light ṣād, while the others read it with a doubled ṣād.

Al-Imam Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Qāḍī informed us: Abū al-Ṭayyib Sahl ibn Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān informed us: Abū al-ʿAbbās Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Mīkālī informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Mūsā ibn ʿAbdān, the ḥāfiẓ, informed us: Abū Ṭāhir Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Sarḥ informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Jarīr, from Ḥāzim, from Ayyūb, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qatādah, from his father, that he was seeking a man for a debt that was due, and the man hid from him. He said: "What kept you from this?" He said: "Hardship." So he made him swear to that, and he swore. Then he called for his sakk (written debt document) and gave it to him, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits it for him, Allah will save him from the distress of the Day of Resurrection.'"[[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: The virtue of granting respite to the one in hardship, no. (1563), 3/1196. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/196 with the same wording.]]

Abd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad al-Malīḥī informed us: Abū Manṣūr Muḥammad ibn Samʿān informed us: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rayyānī informed us: Ḥumayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā informed us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Manṣūr, from Rib‘ī, from Abū Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The angels met the soul of a man who had lived before you. They said: 'Have you ever done any good?' He said: 'No.' They said: 'Think.' He said: 'No, except that I was a man who lent money to people, and I would tell my servants to grant respite to the one who is well-off and to overlook the one in hardship.' Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Overlook it﴾."[[Narrated by al-Bukhārī: in al-Buyūʿ, chapter: Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, 4/307. Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: The virtue of granting respite to the one in hardship, from Ḥudhayfah, no. (1560), 3/1194. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/197.]]

Abd al-Wāḥid al-Malīḥī informed us: Abū Manṣūr al-Samʿānī informed us: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rayyānī informed us: Ḥumayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Zāʾidah informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Rib‘ī, from Abū al-Yusr, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits it for him, Allah will shade him in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His shade."[[Narrated by Muslim in full: in al-Zuhd, chapter: The long hadith of Jābir and the story of Abū al-Yusr, no. (3006), 4/2301–2302. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/198.]]

**Chapter on debt, the goodness of repaying it, and the severity of its matter.**

Abd al-Wāḥid al-Malīḥī informed us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī informed us: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf informed us: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl informed us: Abū al-Walīd informed us: Shuʿbah informed us: Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed us, saying: I heard Abū Salamah at Minā narrate from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man demanded payment from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke harshly to him. His companions moved to confront him, but he said: "Leave him, for the one who is owed has a right to speak. Buy a camel for him and give it to him." They said: "We find nothing but one better than his age." He said: "Buy it and give it to him, for the best of you are those who are best in repaying."[[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Wakālah, chapter: Agency in repaying debts, 4/483, and in al-Istiqrāḍ and al-Hibah. Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: Whoever borrows something and repays better than it (and the best of you are those who are best in repayment), no. (1601), 3/1229. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Sarakhsī informed us: Zāhir ibn Aḥmad al-Sarakhsī informed us: Abū Isḥāq al-Hāshimī informed us: Abū Muṣʿab informed us, from Mālik, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Delaying payment by the wealthy is injustice. And when one of you is referred to a wealthy person, let him accept the referral."[[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Ḥawālāt, chapter: Referral (ḥawālah), and whether one may return to it, 4/464. Ibn Mājah in al-Ṣadaqāt, chapter: Severity regarding debt, 2/806. Aḥmad 2/440, 475, 508 from Abū Hurayrah. al-Dārimī in al-Buyūʿ, 2/262. al-Shawkānī said: its narrators are trustworthy except ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who is truthful but makes errors (Nayl al-Awṭār 5/14).
