Then he called for his sakk (written debt document) and gave it to him, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits it for him, Allah will save him from the distress of the Day of Resurrection.'"[[Narrated by Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: The virtue of granting respite to the one in hardship, no. (1563), 3/1196. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/196 with the same wording.]]

Abd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad al-Malīḥī informed us: Abū Manṣūr Muḥammad ibn Samʿān informed us: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rayyānī informed us: Ḥumayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā informed us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Manṣūr, from Rib‘ī, from Abū Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The angels met the soul of a man who had lived before you. They said: 'Have you ever done any good?' He said: 'No.' They said: 'Think.' He said: 'No, except that I was a man who lent money to people, and I would tell my servants to grant respite to the one who is well-off and to overlook the one in hardship.' Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Overlook it﴾."[[Narrated by al-Bukhārī: in al-Buyūʿ, chapter: Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, 4/307. Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: The virtue of granting respite to the one in hardship, from Ḥudhayfah, no. (1560), 3/1194. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/197.]]

Abd al-Wāḥid al-Malīḥī informed us: Abū Manṣūr al-Samʿānī informed us: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rayyānī informed us: Ḥumayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us: Zāʾidah informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Rib‘ī, from Abū al-Yusr, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits it for him, Allah will shade him in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His shade."[[Narrated by Muslim in full: in al-Zuhd, chapter: The long hadith of Jābir and the story of Abū al-Yusr, no. (3006), 4/2301–2302. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/198.]]

**Chapter on debt, the goodness of repaying it, and the severity of its matter.**

Abd al-Wāḥid al-Malīḥī informed us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī informed us: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf informed us: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl informed us: Abū al-Walīd informed us: Shuʿbah informed us: Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed us, saying: I heard Abū Salamah at Minā narrate from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man demanded payment from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke harshly to him. His companions moved to confront him, but he said: "Leave him, for the one who is owed has a right to speak. Buy a camel for him and give it to him." They said: "We find nothing but one better than his age." He said: "Buy it and give it to him, for the best of you are those who are best in repaying."[[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Wakālah, chapter: Agency in repaying debts, 4/483, and in al-Istiqrāḍ and al-Hibah. Muslim: in al-Musāqāh, chapter: Whoever borrows something and repays better than it (and the best of you are those who are best in repayment), no. (1601), 3/1229. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/194.]]

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Sarakhsī informed us: Zāhir ibn Aḥmad al-Sarakhsī informed us: Abū Isḥāq al-Hāshimī informed us: Abū Muṣʿab informed us, from Mālik, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Delaying payment by the wealthy is injustice. And when one of you is referred to a wealthy person, let him accept the referral."[[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Ḥawālāt, chapter: Referral (ḥawālah), and whether one may return to it, 4/464. Muslim in al-Musāqāh, chapter: The prohibition of the wealthy delaying payment and the validity of referral, no. (1564), 3/1197. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/210.]]

Abd al-Wahhāb ibn Muḥammad al-Khaṭīb informed us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Aḥmad al-Khallāl informed us: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Aṣamm informed us: al-Rabīʿ informed us: al-Shāfiʿī informed us: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd ibn Ibrāhīm informed us, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The soul of the believer is suspended by his debt until it is paid on his behalf."[[Narrated by al-Shāfiʿī 2/226; al-Tirmidhī in al-Janāʾiz, chapter: What has come that the soul of the believer is suspended by his debt until it is repaid, 4/193, and he said: this is a ḥasan (fair) ḥadīth. Ibn Mājah in al-Ṣadaqāt, chapter: Severity regarding debt, 2/806. Aḥmad 2/440, 475, 508 from Abū Hurayrah. al-Dārimī in al-Buyūʿ, 2/262. al-Shawkānī said: its narrators are trustworthy except ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who is truthful but makes errors (Nayl al-Awṭār 5/14). The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/202 and said: this is a ḥasan ḥadīth.]]

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Sarakhsī informed us: Zāhir ibn Aḥmad al-Sarakhsī informed us: Abū Isḥāq al-Hāshimī informed us: Abū Muṣʿab informed us, from Mālik, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qatādah al-Anṣārī, from his father, that he said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I am killed in the way of Allah, patient and seeking reward, advancing and not turning back: will Allah expiate my sins for me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes." When the man turned away, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him, or had him called, and said: "How did you say that?" He repeated his statement to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, except for debt. So Jibrīl said to me."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Imārah, chapter: Whoever is killed in the way of Allah, his sins are expiated except debt, no. (1885), 3/1501. The author cites it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah 8/200.]]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾. The people of Basra read the verb with a fatha on the ta', meaning "you will arrive (taṣīrūna) at Allah," while the others read it with a damma on the ta' and a fatha on the jim, meaning "you will be sent back (turaddūna) to Allah." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: This is the last verse revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Place it at the top of two hundred and eighty verses of Surat al-Baqarah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lived after it twenty-one days. Ibn Jurayj said: nine nights. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: seven nights. He died on Monday, two nights having passed from the month of Rabiʿ al-Awwal, when the sun had passed its zenith, in the eleventh year after the Hijrah.

Al-Shaʿbi related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): The last verse revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the verse on riba (usury). [[Regarding knowing what was revealed last, there is disagreement. Al-Shaykhan related from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: The last verse revealed was "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah" [al-Nisa': 176]. And the last surah revealed was Surat Bara'ah. Al-Bukhari related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The last verse revealed was the verse on riba. Al-Bayhaqi related the same from ʿUmar. In Ahmad and Ibn Majah, from ʿUmar: among the last things revealed was the verse on riba. Al-Nasa'i related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The last thing revealed of the Qur'an was: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281]. Ibn Jarir and al-Firyabi related the like of it, and it is also narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr... etc. There are other opinions. The views can be reconciled by saying that some of them refer to the last of the surahs revealed, some to the last of the verses, and some to the last subject matter of the verses, so they are relative "lasts." For a detailed treatment, see al-Suyuti's al-Itqan fi ʿUloom al-Qur'an: 1/101–106, edited by Muhammad Abu al-Fadl Ibrahim.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 282:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: When Allah prohibited ribā (usury), He permitted salam (advance sale), and said: "I testify that advance payment for a specified term has been made lawful by Allah, Exalted is He, in His Book, and He has permitted it." Then He said: "O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down."

His saying: ﴿When you contract﴾, that is, when you deal with one another in debt. It is said: "Dāyantuhu" when one deals with another on credit. He said ﴿a debt﴾ after His saying "you contract" because contracting (mudāyanah) may be a reward (mujāzāh) or an exchange (muʿāṭāh), so He restricted it with "debt" so that the meaning of the word would be known. It was also said that He mentioned it for emphasis, like His saying: ﴿nor any bird that flies with its two wings﴾ (6:38). ﴿For a specified term﴾: the term (ajal) is a known period with a known beginning and end. The term is required in the price in sale and in salam, so that the creditor may not demand payment before its due time. In a loan (qarḍ), according to most scholars of knowledge, a term is not required. ﴿Write it down﴾, that is, write down that which you have contracted, whether it is a sale, a salam, or a loan.

They differed regarding this writing. Some of them said it is obligatory, but most of them hold that it is a command of recommendation (istiḥbāb); if it is left out, there is no harm, like His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land﴾ (62:10). Some of them said that writing the debt, calling witnesses, and taking a pledge were obligatory, and then all of that was abrogated by His saying: "But if one of you entrusts another, let the one who is entrusted discharge his trust." This is the view of al-Shaʿbi. Then He explained the manner of writing, saying, Majestic is His remembrance: ﴿And let a scribe write it between you﴾, that is, let a scribe write the document of the debt between the creditor and the debtor. ﴿With justice﴾, that is, with truth, without addition or reduction, and without advancing or delaying the term. ﴿And let not the scribe refuse to write﴾, that is, let him not refrain. They differed regarding whether it is obligatory upon the scribe to write and upon the witness to bear testimony. Some people held that it is obligatory when he is asked to do so; this is the view of Mujahid. Al-Hasan said it is obligatory if there is no other scribe. Others said it is a matter of recommendation and desirability. Al-Dahhak said it was an obligatory binding command upon the scribe and the witness, and it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾ (2:282). ﴿As Allah has taught him﴾, that is, as Allah has legislated and commanded him. ﴿So let him write, and let the one who owes the debt dictate﴾, meaning the debtor acknowledges with his tongue what is upon himself, so that he knows what he owes. Al-Imlal and al-Imla' (both dictation) are two eloquent forms with the same meaning, both brought by the Qur'an. So al-Imlal is here, and al-Imla' is in His saying: ﴿And it is dictated to him morning and evening﴾ (25:5). ﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord﴾, meaning the one dictating. ﴿And let him not diminish anything from it﴾, that is, let him not reduce anything from it, that is, from the right that is upon him.

﴿But if the one who owes the debt is weak-minded﴾, that is, ignorant of dictation; Mujahid said this. Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: a small child. Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the safih is the squanderer who corrupts his wealth or his religion.

His saying ﴿or weak﴾, that is, an elderly old man. It was also said he is weak in intellect due to imbecility or madness. ﴿Or unable to dictate himself﴾ due to muteness, or inability to speak, or foreignness of language, or confinement, or absence, such that he cannot have the scribe present, or ignorance of what is his and what is upon him. ﴿Then let his guardian dictate﴾, that is, his trustee (qayyim), ﴿with justice﴾, that is, with honesty and truth. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and Muqatil said: by "the guardian" he meant the holder of the right, meaning if the one owing the right is unable to dictate, then the holder of the right and the creditor should dictate with justice, because he knows best his own right. ﴿And call to witness﴾, that is, and have witnesses called, ﴿two witnesses﴾, that is, two testifiers, ﴿from among your men﴾, meaning free Muslims, not slaves, children, or unbelievers; this is the view of most scholars. Shurayh and Ibn Sirin permitted the testimony of slaves. ﴿And if there are not two men﴾, that is, if the witnesses are not two men, ﴿then a man and two women﴾, that is, then let a man and two women testify.

The jurists agreed that the testimony of women alongside men is permissible in matters of property, such that a right may be established by one man and two women. They differed regarding matters other than property. A group held that their testimony is permissible alongside men in matters other than punishments (ḥudūd); this is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri and the Companions of opinion (Aṣḥāb al-Raʾy). Another group held that what is other than property is not established except by two just men. Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, held that what women commonly witness, such as birth, breastfeeding, loss of virginity, virginity, and the like, is established by the testimony of one man and two women, or by the testimony of four women. They agreed that the testimony of women is not permissible in punishments.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿From those whom you accept as witnesses﴾, meaning whoever is acceptable in his religion and trustworthiness. The conditions for the acceptance (qabūl) of testimony are seven: Islam, freedom, sanity, puberty, justice (ʿadālah), good character (murūʾah), and the absence of accusation (intifāʾ al-tuhmah). The testimony of a disbeliever is rejected, because those known for lying among people are not permitted to testify, so one who lies against Allah, Exalted is He, is more deserving of having his testimony rejected. The Companions of opinion permitted the testimony of dhimmis against one another. The testimony of slaves is not accepted, though Shurayh and Ibn Sirin permitted it, and it is the view of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him. A madman has no statement until he has reason. The testimony of children is not permitted. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, was asked about this and said: It is not permitted, because Allah, Exalted is He, says: "From those whom you accept as witnesses," and justice is a condition. Justice means that the witness avoids major sins and does not persist in minor sins. Good character is a condition, and it is what relates to the refinement of the self, such that one whose abandonment of it is known to indicate little shame; it includes good appearance, conduct, companionship, and occupation. If a man shows of himself some of these things, which people of his kind would in general be ashamed to display, his lack of good character is known and his testimony is rejected. The absence of accusation is a condition, so that the testimony of an enemy against his enemy is not accepted, even if he is acceptable as a witness against others, because he is suspected regarding the right of his enemy. The testimony of a man for his son or his father is not accepted, even if he is acceptable as a witness against them. The testimony of one who draws benefit to himself by his testimony is not accepted, such as an heir testifying against a man who killed his testator; or one who averts harm from himself by his testimony, such as the accused testifying to discredit the one who testifies against him, because suspicion is firmly attached to his testimony.

We were informed by Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi, who was informed by Abu al-ʿAbbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Siraj al-Tahhan, who was informed by Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Quraysh ibn Sulayman, who was informed by ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-Makki, who was informed by Abu ʿUbayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, who was informed by Marwan al-Fazari, from a shaykh from the people of al-Hirah called Yazid ibn Ziyad, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, raising it (to the Prophet ﷺ): "The testimony of a treacherous man or treacherous woman is not permitted, nor of one who harbors enmity toward his brother, nor of a suspect in matters of clientage (walāʾ) or kinship, nor of a servant (qāniʿ) with the members of the household." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Testimonies, chapter on those whose testimony is not permitted, 6/580-582, and he said: this is a strange hadith which we know only through the hadith of Yazid ibn Ziyad al-Dimashqi, and Yazid is weak in hadith; this hadith from al-Zuhri is not known except through him. It was also transmitted by al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi, where it reads "nor one who harbors grudge against his brother," and in its chain is Yazid ibn Ziyad al-Dimashqi, who is abandoned, as you know. Abu Zurʿah said in al-ʿIlal: "It is a munkar hadith." It was declared weak by ʿAbd al-Haqq, Ibn Hazm and Ibn al-Jawzi. Ibn Majah, in the Book of Rulings, chapter on whose testimony is not permitted, 2/2366; in the addenda it is said: its chain contains Hajjaj ibn Artah, who used tadlis and transmitted it with ʿanʿanah, and this is the narration of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb from his father from his grandfather. (Ghamr: ghamr means rancor and enmity.) Ahmad, 2/204, 208, 225, 226, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 10/123, said: this is a strange hadith, and Yazid ibn Ziyad al-Dimashqi is munkar al-hadith.]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That if one of them errs, the other will remind her﴾. Hamzah read "in tadilla" with a kasrah on the alif, ﴿fa-tudhakkira﴾ with raf` on the ra'. Its meaning is the conditional and the beginning (of a new sentence). The position of "tadilla" is jussive by the conditional, but this is not apparent in the doubled form; "fa-tudhakkiru" is in the nominative because what follows the fā' of the conditional is a new sentence (mubtada'). The reading of the majority is with a fatḥah on the alif and naṣb on the ra', connected to the earlier statement; "tadilla" is in the accusative position with "an," and "fa-tudhakkira" is coordinated with it. The meaning of the verse: "then a man and two women, so that one of them may remind the other." "Tadilla" means "to forget": it means that if one of them forgets her testimony, the other reminds her, saying, "Did we not attend such-and-such gathering and hear such-and-such?" Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read "fa-tudhakkira" with a light (mukhaffaf) form, and the rest read it with a doubled (mushaddad) form. "Dhakara" and "adhdhakara" have the same meaning, and both are transitive from dhikr, which is the opposite of forgetting. It is related from Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah that he said: it is from dhikr, meaning one makes the other a remembrance, that is, their testimony becomes like the testimony of a male. The first view is more sound, because it is coordinated with forgetting.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾. It was said he meant when they are called to bear testimony; He called them "witnesses" in the sense that they will be witnesses. For some this is a command of obligation. Some said that the response is obligatory if no one else is available; if others are available, one has a choice; this is the view of al-Hasan. Others said it is a command of recommendation, and one has a choice in all circumstances. Some said this applies to establishing and giving testimony, so the meaning of the verse is: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called" to give the testimony they have borne; this is the view of Mujahid, ʿAtaʾ, ʿIkrimah and Saʿid ibn Jubayr. Al-Shaʿbi said: the witness has a choice as long as he has not testified. Al-Hasan said: the verse applies to both matters together, bearing and establishing, when he is free.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 283:

﴿And do not be weary﴾, i.e., do not grow tired, ﴿of writing it﴾, and the pronoun refers to the debt, ﴿whether it is small﴾, whether the debt was small, ﴿or large﴾, whether it was little or much, ﴿for its term﴾, i.e., to its due time. ﴿That﴾, i.e., the writing, ﴿is more just﴾, more equitable, ﴿with Allah﴾, because He commanded it, and following His command is more just than abandoning it, ﴿and more upright for testimony﴾, because writing reminds the witnesses. ﴿And more likely﴾, and more fitting and closer to ﴿that you will not doubt﴾, meaning that you will not be uncertain about the testimony. ﴿Except when it is a present trade﴾. ʿĀṣim read both of these with the accusative (naṣb) as the khabar (predicate) of kāna (the verb "to be"), with the ism (subject) omitted, its meaning being: "except that the trade be a present trade," or "the sale be a present trade." The rest read them in the nominative (rafʿ), and it has two interpretations:

The first: you make kawn (being) mean wuqūʿ (occurring), so the meaning is "except that a present trade occur."

The second: you make the ism (subject) the trade and the khabar (predicate) the verb, which is His saying ﴿that you conduct among yourselves﴾. Its estimate is: "except that there be a present trade, circulating among you." The meaning of the verse is: "except that it be a present trade, hand to hand, that you conduct among yourselves, with no term attached to it." ﴿There is no blame upon you that you do not write it﴾, meaning the trade. ﴿And take witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this is a firm command from Allah, the Exalted, and calling witnesses is obligatory for small and large debts, whether in cash or deferred. Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the matter in it is left to trustworthiness, based on His saying, the Exalted, ﴿but if one of you trusts another﴾, to the end of the verse. Others said it is a command of recommendation (amr nadb).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾. This is a prohibition in the passive form (lil-ghāʾib), and its original form is yuḍārir. One of the two rāʾs was assimilated into the other and it was put in the accusative because of the doubling, due to the meeting of two sukūns. They differed about it. Some of them said: its original form is yuḍārir, with the first rāʾ kasra, and the verb is attributed to the scribe and the witness. Its meaning: the scribe should not be harmed so that he refuses to write, nor the witness so that he refuses to testify; and the scribe should not be harmed so that he adds, subtracts, or alters what was dictated to him, nor the witness so that he testifies to what he was not called to testify about. This is the view of Ṭāwūs, al-Ḥasan, and Qatādah. Others said: its original form is yuḍārar, with the rāʾ fatḥa as a passive verb, and they made the scribe and the witness the objects. Its meaning is that a man calls upon the scribe or the witness while they are occupied with an important task, and they say: "We are occupied with an important task, so seek someone other than us." The caller then says: "Indeed Allah has commanded you both to respond," and he insists on them, thereby distracting them from their need. So He forbade this and commanded that others be sought instead. ﴿And if you do﴾, what I have forbidden you of harm, ﴿then indeed it is defiance in you﴾, i.e., disobedience and departure from the command. ﴿And fear Allah. And Allah teaches you, and Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

﴿And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken in hand﴾. Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it as fa-ruhunun, with ḍamma on the hāʾ and the rāʾ. The rest read it as fa-rihān, which is the plural of rahn, like baghl and baghāl, and jabal and jibāl. The ruhun is the plural of rihān, the plural of the plural, as al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī said. Abū ʿUbayd [in manuscript B: Abū ʿUbayda] and others said: it is also the plural of rahn, like saqf and suquf. Abū ʿAmr said: we read it as fa-ruhun only so that it would be a distinction between them and rihān al-khayl (the racing of horses). ʿIkrima read it as fa-ruhn, with ḍamma on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ. The lightening and the heavying of ruhn are two dialects, like kutb and kutub, and rusl and rusul. The meaning of the verse: if you are on a journey and do not find the means of writing, then take pledges from those to whom you incur debt, as a security for your wealth. They agreed that the pledge is not complete except by possession (qabḍ). His saying "fa-rihān maqbūḍa" means: take pledges and take possession. So if he pledges but does not hand it over, the pledgor is not compelled to hand it over. Once he hands it over, it becomes binding on the pledgor, so that he may not reclaim it as long as any part of the debt remains. Taking a pledge is permitted in a settled place also, when a scribe is present. Mujāhid said: taking a pledge is not permitted except on a journey when no scribe is available, based on the apparent meaning of the verse. According to the others, the statement in the verse came out in terms of the more general and more common case, not as a condition.

The evidence for this is what is narrated: that the Prophet ﷺ pledged his coat of mail with Abū al-Shaḥm the Jew, and that was neither on a journey nor when no scribe was available. [Narrated by al-Bukhārī, in Jihād, chapter on what has been said about the coat of mail and shirt of the Prophet ﷺ in war, 6/99, with the text: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while his coat of mail was pledged to a Jew for thirty ṣāʿ of barley," from ʿĀʾisha. And Muslim, in Musāqāt, chapter: The pledge and its permissibility in settled places and on journeys, no. 1603, 3/1226, from ʿĀʾisha, with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought food from a Jew on credit, and he gave him a coat of mail as a pledge." And the author in Sharḥ al-Sunna, 8/182.] ﴿But if one of you trusts another﴾. In the codex of Ubayy it reads "fa-in ītaman", meaning: if the one owing the debt is trustworthy with the creditor, so that he does not take any pledge from him, because of the creditor's good opinion of him.

﴿Then let him who has been entrusted discharge his trust﴾, i.e., let him pay it with fidelity to the trust. ﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord﴾, in discharging the right. Then he returned to addressing the witnesses and said: ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾ [51/b] when you are called to establish it. He forbade concealing testimony and threatened for it, saying: ﴿And whoever conceals it, indeed his heart is sinful﴾, i.e., his heart is wicked. It has been said: Allah has threatened nothing like His threat concerning the concealing of testimony, when He said: "indeed his heart is sinful," and He meant by it the distortion of the heart. We seek refuge in Allah from that. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾, the explanation of the testimony and its concealment, ﴿Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 284:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, [dominion], [and its inhabitants are His servants, and He is their Owner] [[Omitted from B.]] ﴿Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. The scholars differed concerning this verse. Some said: it is specific [in its application], then they differed over the manner of its specificity [[In B: its specification (takhsis)]]. Some of them said: it is connected to the previous verse and was revealed concerning the concealing of testimony [[In B: its meaning is: "Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, O witnesses"]], or concealing the concealment. Allah will call you to account for it. This is the view of al-Sha'bi and Ikrimah. Others said: it was revealed concerning one who allies with the disbelievers rather than the believers, meaning: whether you disclose what is in yourselves of allegiance to the disbelievers, or keep it secret, Allah will call you to account for it. This is the view of Muqatil, as mentioned in surah Al 'Imran: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers﴾ up to His saying ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or disclose it, Allah knows it﴾ (3:29).

Al-Baghawi's Commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 285–286 (part 1 of 2):

The majority of scholars held that the verse is general (ʿāmm), but then they differed regarding it. A group said: it has been abrogated (mansūkh) by the verse that follows it [see: al-Nāsikh wa'l-Mansūkh by Abu'l-Qasim ibn Salama, pp. 27–28].

The evidence for this is what Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Qahir related to us: ʿAbd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to me: Muhammad ibn al-Minhal al-Darir and Umayya ibn Bistam al-ʿAyshi, and the wording is his, both said: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us: Rawh, who is the son of al-Qasim, related to us, from al-ʿAla', from his father, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:

When Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ) "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it," [the verse] — he said: this was hard upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then knelt down on their knees and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have been charged with deeds we can bear: prayer, fasting, jihad and charity; and this verse has been revealed to you, which we cannot bear." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you want to say what the People of the Two Books said before you: 'We hear and we disobey'? Rather say: ﴿We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord; and to You is the final return.﴾" When the people recited it and their tongues submitted to it, Allah sent down after it: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers. "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say: "We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord; and to You is the final return."﴾ When they did that, Allah abrogated it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it has earned, and it bears what it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make errors."﴾ He said: Yes. ﴿"Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us."﴾ He said: Yes. ﴿"Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear."﴾ He said: Yes. ﴿"And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."﴾ He said: Yes [Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Iman, bab bayan annahu subhanahu wa-ta'ala lam yukallif illa ma yutaq, no. 199, 1/115].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) its meaning [see Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Iman, bab bayan annahu subhanahu wa-ta'ala lam yukallif illa ma yutaq, no. 200, 1/116], except that in all of these he said "Qad fa'altu" ("I have done it") instead of "Na'am" ("Yes"). This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them), and Muhammad ibn Sirin, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Qatada and al-Kalbi held it too.

Al-Imam Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi related to us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Asfahani related to us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih related to us: Yaʿqub ibn Yusuf al-Qazwini related to us: al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam al-ʿUrani related to us: Mis'ar ibn Kidam related to us, from Qatada, from Zurara ibn Awfa, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper, so long as they do not speak it or act upon it" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, bab idha hanitha nasiyan, and in al-ʿItq and al-Talaq; and Muslim in al-Iman, bab tajawuz Allah ʿan hadith al-nafs wa'l-khawatir bi'l-qalb idha lam tastaqarr, no. 202, 1/116–117. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna, 1/108].

Some said: the verse is not abrogated, because abrogation does not apply to information (khabar); it applies only to commands and prohibitions. And His saying ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾ is information to which abrogation does not apply. Then they differed about its interpretation. A group said: Allah has affirmed that the heart earns, when He said ﴿for what your hearts have earned﴾ [2:225]. So there is no servant who conceals or openly does any deed, or any movement of his limbs, or any whisper in his heart, except that Allah informs him of it and calls him to account for it, then forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan, and it is indicated by His saying ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned﴾ [17:36].

Others said: the meaning of the verse is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls His creatures to account for all that they have displayed of their deeds or concealed, and punishes them for it. However, His punishment for what they concealed, which they did not know of, is through what befalls them in this world of calamities, afflictions and matters over which they grieve. This is the view of ʿA'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this verse, and he said: "O ʿA'isha, this is Allah's reproach to the servant for what afflicts him of fever and misfortune, even a thorn, or goods he places in his sleeve and then loses, and is alarmed over them, until the believer emerges from his sins as red gold emerges from the furnace" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir Surat al-Baqara, 8/338, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith from ʿA'isha, which we know only through the narration of Hammad ibn Salama; and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, p. 221. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, and Ahmad, 6/218, from ʿA'isha (may Allah be pleased with her)].

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi related to us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani related to us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayani related to us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yazid ibn Abi Habib related to me, from Sa'id ibn Sinan, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "When Allah wishes good for His servant, He hastens his punishment in this world; and when Allah wishes evil for His servant, He holds back his sin for him until He meets him with it on the Day of Resurrection" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, bab fi'l-sabr ʿala'l-bala', 7/77, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna, 5/245. Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-ʿArzami, who is weak – Majma' al-Zawa'id, 10/191–192; Mizan al-I'tidal, 2/585].

Some said: ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves﴾ means what is in your hearts of resolve, ﴿or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, and if you do not display it while you are resolved upon it, Allah will call you to account for it. As for what your souls whisper of that which you have not resolved upon, that is among what Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity with, and He does not hold you accountable for it. Its evidence is His saying: ﴿Allah will not call you to account for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned﴾ [2:225].

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: I said to Sufyan: Is a servant held accountable for an intention? He said: If it is a firm resolve, he is held accountable for it.

It was also said that the meaning of "muhasaba" (reckoning) is informing and making known. The meaning of the verse: "And whether you show what is within yourselves, so that you act upon it, or conceal what you harbour and intend, Allah will call you to account for it, and will requite you for it, and make you know it. Then He will forgive the believers, to manifest His bounty, and punish the disbelievers, to manifest His justice." This is the meaning of the saying of al-Dahhak, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both). It is indicated by his saying "yuhasibkum bihi Allah" and not "yu'akhidhkum bihi", and reckoning is other than taking to account. The evidence for this is what Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Zarrad related to us: Abu'l-Qasim ʿAli ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i related to us: Abu Sa'id al-Haytham ibn Kulayb related to us: ʿIsa ibn Ahmad al-ʿAsqalani related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: Hammam ibn Yahya related to us, from Qatada, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: I was holding the hand of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them both), when a man came to him and said: How did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about private conversation (najwa)? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, brings the believer near on the Day of Resurrection until He places His covering (kanaf) upon him, shielding him from the people, and says: 'O My servant, do you recognise the sin of such and such?' He says: 'Yes, my Lord.' Then He says: 'O My servant, do you recognise the sin of such and such?' He says: 'Yes, my Lord.' Until, when He has made him confess his sins and he sees in himself that he is ruined, He says: 'I have concealed them for you in the world, and I have forgiven them for you today.' Then he is given the book of his good deeds. As for the disbeliever and the hypocrites, the witnesses will say: 'These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Mazalim, bab qawlihi ta'ala (alā la'nat Allahi ʿala'l-zalimin), 5/96] (11:18).

The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿So He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾: Abu Ja'far, Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim and Yaʿqub put the "ra'" and the "ya'" in the nominative (raf'), while the others read them in the jussive (jazm). The nominative is on the basis of a new sentence (ibtida'), and the jussive is on the basis of conjunction (nasaq). Tawus related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "He forgives whom He wills" refers to the great sin, and "He punishes whom He wills" refers to the small sin. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [21:23].

The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ means he affirmed (ṣaddaqa) ﴿in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers, each believes in Allah﴾, meaning each one of them; for this reason the verb is in the singular. ﴿His angels, His books and His messengers﴾: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "kitabihi" in the singular, meaning the Qur'an. It was also said that its meaning is plural even though it is mentioned with a singular form, as in His saying: ﴿So Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good news and warners, and sent down with them the Book﴾ [2:213]. The others read "wa-kutubihi" in the plural, as in His saying: ﴿His angels, His books and His messengers﴾ [4:136]. ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾, so that we believe in some and disbelieve in others as the Jews and Christians did. There is an implied element in it, its estimated form being "they say: we make no distinction." Ya'qub read "la yufarriqu" with the "ya'", so that it is a report about the Messenger; or its meaning is that all of them do not make distinction. He said "bayna ahad" and did not say "bayna aḥad" (plural), because "aḥad" applies to both the singular and the plural. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Not one of you could withhold from Him﴾ [69:47]. ﴿And they said: We hear﴾ your words, ﴿and we obey﴾ your command.

Narrated from Hakim, from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with them both), that Jibril (peace be upon him) said to the Prophet (ﷺ) when this verse was revealed: "Indeed Allah has praised you and your Ummah, so ask, and you will be given." So he asked, at Allah's inspiration, and said, ﴿Forgiveness, [our Lord]﴾ [[Al-Tabari, Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Hakim ibn Jabir: "When ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ was revealed, Jibril said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has praised you and your Ummah well, so ask, and you will be given.' So he asked: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, until he concluded the surah with the request of Muhammad (ﷺ)." See Tafsir al-Tabari 6/129 and al-Durr al-Manthur 2/133.]] This is in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning "forgive us, forgiveness," or "we ask You for forgiveness." ﴿Our Lord, and to You is the final return. Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is the fulfilling of a need, and in it the question is implied, as if it said: "And they said: Do not burden us beyond our capacity." And He responded: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity," meaning beyond its strength. Al-Wus' is the name for what is within a person's ability and does not constrict him. The scholars differed in its interpretation. Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), 'Ata', and most of the exegetes held that it refers to the whispers of the soul mentioned in His saying: ﴿Whether you reveal what is in your souls or conceal it﴾, as we have mentioned. It is also reported from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: "They are the believers specifically: He made their religious affairs easy for them and did not burden them with anything except what they are able to bear, as Allah says: ﴿Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you﴾ (2:185), and Allah says: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ (22:78)." Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah was asked about His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, and he said: "Except its ease, and He does not burden it beyond its capacity." This is a good opinion, because al-Wus' is less than al-Taqah (capacity).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It has what it earned﴾, meaning: for the soul is what it did of good; for it is its reward and recompense. ﴿And against it what it earned﴾ of evil; upon it is its burden. ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task﴾, meaning do not punish us, ﴿if we forget﴾. Some of them took it to mean forgetting, which is heedlessness. Al-Kalbi said: The Children of Israel, when they forgot something they had been commanded or erred, the punishment was hastened upon them, and something of food or drink was forbidden to them according to the measure of that sin. So Allah commanded the believers to ask Him to abandon taking them to account for that. It was also said that it is from forgetting in the sense of abandoning, as in His saying: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ (9:67).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or we err﴾. It was said its meaning is intention and deliberateness; it is said: "So-and-so erred," if he did it intentionally. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin﴾ (17:31). 'Ata' said: "If we forget or err," meaning: if we are ignorant or do it deliberately. Most of them took it to be from error, which is ignorance and heedlessness, because whatever is done deliberately of sin is not pardoned but is in the Will of Allah, whereas error is pardoned. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Error and forgetfulness have been lifted from my Ummah, and what they have been compelled to do."

[[This wording is well known in the books of fiqh and usul. What is best known is what Ibn Majah reported in the Book of Divorce, chapter on the divorce of one compelled and one forgetful, through the route of al-Walid ibn Muslim from al-Awza'i from 'Ata' from Ibn Abbas with the wording: "Indeed Allah has removed from my Ummah error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do." All its narrators are trustworthy, but there is a break (inqita') between Ibn Abbas and 'Ata'; al-Busiri pointed to this in al-Zawa'id, saying: its isnad is sound if the break is set aside. It has been narrated with other wordings, some of which strengthen others. See Irwa' al-Ghalil of Shaykh al-Albani 1/123, al-Mu'tabar fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Minhaj, and al-Zarkashi's al-Mukhtasar p. 154.]].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden (isr)﴾, meaning a heavy covenant and a pact that we cannot uphold, so that You punish us for breaking and abandoning it. ﴿As You laid it upon those before us﴾, meaning the Jews, who did not uphold it, so You punished them. This is the saying of Mujahid, 'Ata', Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and a group. It is indicated by His saying: ﴿And you took upon that My covenant (isri)﴾ (3:81), meaning My covenant. It was also said: its meaning is: do not make the matter strict or harsh upon us as You made it strict upon those before us of the Jews. That is because Allah obligated upon them fifty prayers, commanded them to pay a quarter of their wealth in zakat, and whoever had a najasah on his garment would cut it off, and whoever committed a sin would wake up to find his sin written on his door, and similar burdens and shackles. This is the meaning of the saying of 'Uthman, 'Ata', Malik ibn Anas, Abu 'Ubaydah and a group. It is indicated by His saying: ﴿And He removes from them their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾ (7:157). It was also said: al-Isr is a sin for which there is no repentance; its meaning is: protect us from the like of it. Its root meaning is restraint and firmness.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no power to bear﴾, meaning do not impose upon us of deeds what we cannot endure. It was also said it refers to the whispers and the inner suggestions. It is related from Makhul that he said: it is ghulmah; it was said: ghulmah is intensity of desire. From Ibrahim he said: it is love. From Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab he said: it is ishq (passionate love). Ibn Juraij said: it is the transformation into apes and pigs. It was also said it is the gloating of enemies, and it was said: it is separation and severance; we seek refuge in Allah from it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And pardon us﴾, meaning overlook and erase our sins. ﴿And forgive us﴾, meaning cover our sins and do not disgrace us. ﴿And have mercy on us﴾, for we cannot attain righteous deeds except by Your obedience, and we cannot abandon Your disobedience except by Your mercy. ﴿You are our Protector﴾, our Helper, our Guardian and our Ally. ﴿So give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Forgiveness, our Lord﴾. He said: Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿I have forgiven you﴾. And concerning His saying: ﴿Do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾, he said: "I will not take you to task." ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden﴾, he said: "I will not lay upon you a burden." ﴿And do not burden us with what we have no power to bear﴾, he said: "I will not burden you." ﴿And pardon us﴾ to the end, he said: "I have pardoned you, forgiven you, shown you mercy, and given you victory over the disbelieving people." [[Mentioned by al-Tabari at the tafsir of the verse: 6/142-143, and see Mahmud Shakir's note in the margin.]].

Mu'adh ibn Jabal, when he finished Surah al-Baqarah, would say: "Amin."

We were told by Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir, from 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan, from Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Abu Usamah, who said: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to me from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Talhah ibn 'Ali ibn Musarrif, from Murrah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached Sidrat al-Muntaha, which is in the sixth heaven; to it ends what ascends from the earth and is taken from it, and to it ends what descends from above it and is taken from it. He said: ﴿When there covers the lote tree that which covers﴾ (53:16). He said: "A cloth of gold." He said: "And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given three things: the five prayers, and he was given the final verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and whoever of his Ummah does not associate anything with Allah will be forgiven the great sins." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Faith, chapter on the mention of Sidrat al-Muntaha, no. 173: 1/157.]]

We were told by the Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, from Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfara'ini, from Abu 'Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz, from Yunus and Ahmad ibn Shaybān, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abu Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two verses from the end of Surah al-Baqarah: whoever recites them at night, they will suffice him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter 12, 7/317-318, and in Fada'il al-Qur'an; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the virtue of al-Fatihah and the final verses of al-Baqarah and encouragement to recite the two verses at the end of al-Baqarah, nos. (255) and (256), 1/554-555. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/464. Its meaning is disputed: it was said they sufficed him instead of night prayer; it was said they sufficed him as reward and virtue; it was said they sufficed him from every devil or from every calamity.]]

We were told by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, from Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani, from Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani, from Humayd ibn Zanjawayh, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from al-Ash'ath ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jarmi, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, wrote a Book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and from it He sent down two verses with which He concluded Surah al-Baqarah. They are not recited in a house for three nights, and a devil will come near it." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the virtues of the Qur'an, chapter on what has come concerning the end of Surah al-Baqarah, 8/190, and he said: this is a gharib hadith. Ibn Hibban in al-Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah al-Baqarah, no. 1726, p. 427 of Mawarid al-Zam'an. Ahmad 4/274 from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir. al-Darimi in al-Fada'il, chapter on the virtue of the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah and Ayat al-Kursi: 2/449. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/467, and he said: this is a gharib hadith; see the margin of Sharh al-Sunnah.]]

Al-Baghawi's Commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 285–286 (part 1 of 2):

The majority of scholars held that the verse is general (ʿāmm), but then they differed regarding it. A group said: it has been abrogated (mansūkh) by the verse that follows it [see: al-Nāsikh wa'l-Mansūkh by Abu'l-Qasim ibn Salama, pp. 27–28].

The evidence for this is what Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Qahir related to us: ʿAbd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to me: Muhammad ibn al-Minhal al-Darir and Umayya ibn Bistam al-ʿAyshi, and the wording is his, both said: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us: Rawh, who is the son of al-Qasim, related to us, from al-ʿAla', from his father, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:

When Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ) "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it," [the verse] — he said: this was hard upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then knelt down on their knees and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have been charged with deeds we can bear: prayer, fasting, jihad and charity; and this verse has been revealed to you, which we cannot bear." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you want to say what the People of the Two Books said before you: 'We hear and we disobey'? Rather say: ﴿We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord; and to You is the final return.﴾" When the people recited it and their tongues submitted to it, Allah sent down after it: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers. "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say: "We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord; and to You is the final return."﴾ When they did that, Allah abrogated it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it has earned, and it bears what it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make errors."﴾ He said: Yes. ﴿"Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us."﴾ He said: Yes. ﴿"Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear."﴾ He said: Yes. ﴿"And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."﴾ He said: Yes [Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Iman, bab bayan annahu subhanahu wa-ta'ala lam yukallif illa ma yutaq, no. 199, 1/115].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) its meaning [see Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Iman, bab bayan annahu subhanahu wa-ta'ala lam yukallif illa ma yutaq, no. 200, 1/116], except that in all of these he said "Qad fa'altu" ("I have done it") instead of "Na'am" ("Yes"). This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them), and Muhammad ibn Sirin, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Qatada and al-Kalbi held it too.

Al-Imam Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi related to us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Asfahani related to us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih related to us: Yaʿqub ibn Yusuf al-Qazwini related to us: al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam al-ʿUrani related to us: Mis'ar ibn Kidam related to us, from Qatada, from Zurara ibn Awfa, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper, so long as they do not speak it or act upon it" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, bab idha hanitha nasiyan, and in al-ʿItq and al-Talaq; and Muslim in al-Iman, bab tajawuz Allah ʿan hadith al-nafs wa'l-khawatir bi'l-qalb idha lam tastaqarr, no. 202, 1/116–117. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna, 1/108].

Some said: the verse is not abrogated, because abrogation does not apply to information (khabar); it applies only to commands and prohibitions. And His saying ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾ is information to which abrogation does not apply. Then they differed about its interpretation. A group said: Allah has affirmed that the heart earns, when He said ﴿for what your hearts have earned﴾ [2:225]. So there is no servant who conceals or openly does any deed, or any movement of his limbs, or any whisper in his heart, except that Allah informs him of it and calls him to account for it, then forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan, and it is indicated by His saying ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned﴾ [17:36].

Others said: the meaning of the verse is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls His creatures to account for all that they have displayed of their deeds or concealed, and punishes them for it. However, His punishment for what they concealed, which they did not know of, is through what befalls them in this world of calamities, afflictions and matters over which they grieve. This is the view of ʿA'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this verse, and he said: "O ʿA'isha, this is Allah's reproach to the servant for what afflicts him of fever and misfortune, even a thorn, or goods he places in his sleeve and then loses, and is alarmed over them, until the believer emerges from his sins as red gold emerges from the furnace" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir Surat al-Baqara, 8/338, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith from ʿA'isha, which we know only through the narration of Hammad ibn Salama; and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, p. 221. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, and Ahmad, 6/218, from ʿA'isha (may Allah be pleased with her)].

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi related to us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani related to us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayani related to us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us: al-Layth related to me: Yazid ibn Abi Habib related to me, from Sa'id ibn Sinan, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "When Allah wishes good for His servant, He hastens his punishment in this world; and when Allah wishes evil for His servant, He holds back his sin for him until He meets him with it on the Day of Resurrection" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, bab fi'l-sabr ʿala'l-bala', 7/77, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna, 5/245. Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-ʿArzami, who is weak – Majma' al-Zawa'id, 10/191–192; Mizan al-I'tidal, 2/585].

Some said: ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves﴾ means what is in your hearts of resolve, ﴿or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, and if you do not display it while you are resolved upon it, Allah will call you to account for it. As for what your souls whisper of that which you have not resolved upon, that is among what Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity with, and He does not hold you accountable for it. Its evidence is His saying: ﴿Allah will not call you to account for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned﴾ [2:225].

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: I said to Sufyan: Is a servant held accountable for an intention? He said: If it is a firm resolve, he is held accountable for it.

It was also said that the meaning of "muhasaba" (reckoning) is informing and making known. The meaning of the verse: "And whether you show what is within yourselves, so that you act upon it, or conceal what you harbour and intend, Allah will call you to account for it, and will requite you for it, and make you know it. Then He will forgive the believers, to manifest His bounty, and punish the disbelievers, to manifest His justice." This is the meaning of the saying of al-Dahhak, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both). It is indicated by his saying "yuhasibkum bihi Allah" and not "yu'akhidhkum bihi", and reckoning is other than taking to account. The evidence for this is what Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Zarrad related to us: Abu'l-Qasim ʿAli ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i related to us: Abu Sa'id al-Haytham ibn Kulayb related to us: ʿIsa ibn Ahmad al-ʿAsqalani related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: Hammam ibn Yahya related to us, from Qatada, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: I was holding the hand of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them both), when a man came to him and said: How did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about private conversation (najwa)? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, brings the believer near on the Day of Resurrection until He places His covering (kanaf) upon him, shielding him from the people, and says: 'O My servant, do you recognise the sin of such and such?' He says: 'Yes, my Lord.' Then He says: 'O My servant, do you recognise the sin of such and such?' He says: 'Yes, my Lord.' Until, when He has made him confess his sins and he sees in himself that he is ruined, He says: 'I have concealed them for you in the world, and I have forgiven them for you today.' Then he is given the book of his good deeds. As for the disbeliever and the hypocrites, the witnesses will say: 'These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Mazalim, bab qawlihi ta'ala (alā la'nat Allahi ʿala'l-zalimin), 5/96] (11:18).

The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿So He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾: Abu Ja'far, Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim and Yaʿqub put the "ra'" and the "ya'" in the nominative (raf'), while the others read them in the jussive (jazm). The nominative is on the basis of a new sentence (ibtida'), and the jussive is on the basis of conjunction (nasaq). Tawus related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "He forgives whom He wills" refers to the great sin, and "He punishes whom He wills" refers to the small sin. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [21:23].

The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ means he affirmed (ṣaddaqa) ﴿in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers, each believes in Allah﴾, meaning each one of them; for this reason the verb is in the singular. ﴿His angels, His books and His messengers﴾: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "kitabihi" in the singular, meaning the Qur'an. It was also said that its meaning is plural even though it is mentioned with a singular form, as in His saying: ﴿So Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good news and warners, and sent down with them the Book﴾ [2:213]. The others read "wa-kutubihi" in the plural, as in His saying: ﴿His angels, His books and His messengers﴾ [4:136]. ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾, so that we believe in some and disbelieve in others as the Jews and Christians did. There is an implied element in it, its estimated form being "they say: we make no distinction." Ya'qub read "la yufarriqu" with the "ya'", so that it is a report about the Messenger; or its meaning is that all of them do not make distinction. He said "bayna ahad" and did not say "bayna aḥad" (plural), because "aḥad" applies to both the singular and the plural. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Not one of you could withhold from Him﴾ [69:47]. ﴿And they said: We hear﴾ your words, ﴿and we obey﴾ your command.

Narrated from Hakim, from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with them both), that Jibril (peace be upon him) said to the Prophet (ﷺ) when this verse was revealed: "Indeed Allah has praised you and your Ummah, so ask, and you will be given." So he asked, at Allah's inspiration, and said, ﴿Forgiveness, [our Lord]﴾ [[Al-Tabari, Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Hakim ibn Jabir: "When ﴿The Messenger believes﴾ was revealed, Jibril said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has praised you and your Ummah well, so ask, and you will be given.' So he asked: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, until he concluded the surah with the request of Muhammad (ﷺ)." See Tafsir al-Tabari 6/129 and al-Durr al-Manthur 2/133.]] This is in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning "forgive us, forgiveness," or "we ask You for forgiveness." ﴿Our Lord, and to You is the final return. Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is the fulfilling of a need, and in it the question is implied, as if it said: "And they said: Do not burden us beyond our capacity." And He responded: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity," meaning beyond its strength. Al-Wus' is the name for what is within a person's ability and does not constrict him. The scholars differed in its interpretation. Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), 'Ata', and most of the exegetes held that it refers to the whispers of the soul mentioned in His saying: ﴿Whether you reveal what is in your souls or conceal it﴾, as we have mentioned. It is also reported from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: "They are the believers specifically: He made their religious affairs easy for them and did not burden them with anything except what they are able to bear, as Allah says: ﴿Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you﴾ (2:185), and Allah says: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ (22:78)." Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah was asked about His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, and he said: "Except its ease, and He does not burden it beyond its capacity." This is a good opinion, because al-Wus' is less than al-Taqah (capacity).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It has what it earned﴾, meaning: for the soul is what it did of good; for it is its reward and recompense. ﴿And against it what it earned﴾ of evil; upon it is its burden. ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task﴾, meaning do not punish us, ﴿if we forget﴾. Some of them took it to mean forgetting, which is heedlessness. Al-Kalbi said: The Children of Israel, when they forgot something they had been commanded or erred, the punishment was hastened upon them, and something of food or drink was forbidden to them according to the measure of that sin. So Allah commanded the believers to ask Him to abandon taking them to account for that. It was also said that it is from forgetting in the sense of abandoning, as in His saying: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ (9:67).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or we err﴾. It was said its meaning is intention and deliberateness; it is said: "So-and-so erred," if he did it intentionally. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin﴾ (17:31). 'Ata' said: "If we forget or err," meaning: if we are ignorant or do it deliberately. Most of them took it to be from error, which is ignorance and heedlessness, because whatever is done deliberately of sin is not pardoned but is in the Will of Allah, whereas error is pardoned. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Error and forgetfulness have been lifted from my Ummah, and what they have been compelled to do."

[[This wording is well known in the books of fiqh and usul. What is best known is what Ibn Majah reported in the Book of Divorce, chapter on the divorce of one compelled and one forgetful, through the route of al-Walid ibn Muslim from al-Awza'i from 'Ata' from Ibn Abbas with the wording: "Indeed Allah has removed from my Ummah error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do." All its narrators are trustworthy, but there is a break (inqita') between Ibn Abbas and 'Ata'; al-Busiri pointed to this in al-Zawa'id, saying: its isnad is sound if the break is set aside. It has been narrated with other wordings, some of which strengthen others. See Irwa' al-Ghalil of Shaykh al-Albani 1/123, al-Mu'tabar fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Minhaj, and al-Zarkashi's al-Mukhtasar p. 154.]].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden (isr)﴾, meaning a heavy covenant and a pact that we cannot uphold, so that You punish us for breaking and abandoning it. ﴿As You laid it upon those before us﴾, meaning the Jews, who did not uphold it, so You punished them. This is the saying of Mujahid, 'Ata', Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and a group. It is indicated by His saying: ﴿And you took upon that My covenant (isri)﴾ (3:81), meaning My covenant. It was also said: its meaning is: do not make the matter strict or harsh upon us as You made it strict upon those before us of the Jews. That is because Allah obligated upon them fifty prayers, commanded them to pay a quarter of their wealth in zakat, and whoever had a najasah on his garment would cut it off, and whoever committed a sin would wake up to find his sin written on his door, and similar burdens and shackles. This is the meaning of the saying of 'Uthman, 'Ata', Malik ibn Anas, Abu 'Ubaydah and a group. It is indicated by His saying: ﴿And He removes from them their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾ (7:157). It was also said: al-Isr is a sin for which there is no repentance; its meaning is: protect us from the like of it. Its root meaning is restraint and firmness.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no power to bear﴾, meaning do not impose upon us of deeds what we cannot endure. It was also said it refers to the whispers and the inner suggestions. It is related from Makhul that he said: it is ghulmah; it was said: ghulmah is intensity of desire. From Ibrahim he said: it is love. From Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab he said: it is ishq (passionate love). Ibn Juraij said: it is the transformation into apes and pigs. It was also said it is the gloating of enemies, and it was said: it is separation and severance; we seek refuge in Allah from it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And pardon us﴾, meaning overlook and erase our sins. ﴿And forgive us﴾, meaning cover our sins and do not disgrace us. ﴿And have mercy on us﴾, for we cannot attain righteous deeds except by Your obedience, and we cannot abandon Your disobedience except by Your mercy. ﴿You are our Protector﴾, our Helper, our Guardian and our Ally. ﴿So give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Forgiveness, our Lord﴾. He said: Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿I have forgiven you﴾. And concerning His saying: ﴿Do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾, he said: "I will not take you to task." ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden﴾, he said: "I will not lay upon you a burden." ﴿And do not burden us with what we have no power to bear﴾, he said: "I will not burden you." ﴿And pardon us﴾ to the end, he said: "I have pardoned you, forgiven you, shown you mercy, and given you victory over the disbelieving people." [[Mentioned by al-Tabari at the tafsir of the verse: 6/142-143, and see Mahmud Shakir's note in the margin.]].

Mu'adh ibn Jabal, when he finished Surah al-Baqarah, would say: "Amin."

We were told by Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir, from 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan, from Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Abu Usamah, who said: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to me from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Talhah ibn 'Ali ibn Musarrif, from Murrah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached Sidrat al-Muntaha, which is in the sixth heaven; to it ends what ascends from the earth and is taken from it, and to it ends what descends from above it and is taken from it. He said: ﴿When there covers the lote tree that which covers﴾ (53:16). He said: "A cloth of gold." He said: "And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given three things: the five prayers, and he was given the final verses of Surah al-Baqarah, and whoever of his Ummah does not associate anything with Allah will be forgiven the great sins." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Faith, chapter on the mention of Sidrat al-Muntaha, no. 173: 1/157.]]

We were told by the Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, from Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfara'ini, from Abu 'Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz, from Yunus and Ahmad ibn Shaybān, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abu Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two verses from the end of Surah al-Baqarah: whoever recites them at night, they will suffice him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter 12, 7/317-318, and in Fada'il al-Qur'an; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the virtue of al-Fatihah and the final verses of al-Baqarah and encouragement to recite the two verses at the end of al-Baqarah, nos. (255) and (256), 1/554-555. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/464. Its meaning is disputed: it was said they sufficed him instead of night prayer; it was said they sufficed him as reward and virtue; it was said they sufficed him from every devil or from every calamity.]]

We were told by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, from Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani, from Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani, from Humayd ibn Zanjawayh, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from al-Ash'ath ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jarmi, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted, wrote a Book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and from it He sent down two verses with which He concluded Surah al-Baqarah. They are not recited in a house for three nights, and a devil will come near it." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the virtues of the Qur'an, chapter on what has come concerning the end of Surah al-Baqarah, 8/190, and he said: this is a gharib hadith. Ibn Hibban in al-Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah al-Baqarah, no. 1726, p. 427 of Mawarid al-Zam'an. Ahmad 4/274 from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir. al-Darimi in al-Fada'il, chapter on the virtue of the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah and Ayat al-Kursi: 2/449. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/467, and he said: this is a gharib hadith; see the margin of Sharh al-Sunnah.]]
